# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project

Converts Point Blank (i3Engine) **Avatar V2 skins** into **V1 character files** so the skin uses the V1 skeleton,
ragdoll and weapon/helmet dummies. The user is an Indonesian-speaking PB modder: reply in Indonesian, and treat
their in-game test as the final verdict. `README.md` is the Indonesian user guide (options, error messages, CLI).
Not a git repository.

- `pindah_bone.py`: the whole engine (I3R2 reader, persist-chunk parsers, `convert()`, `verify()`, CLI `main()`).
- `I3Chara Convert Bone V3.pyw`: tkinter GUI over `pb.convert()` (worker thread + queue for log lines). With CLI args it runs
  `pb.main()` headless; when frozen, stdout is `None`, so it logs to `I3Chara Convert Bone V3.log`, and `HERE` is the exe folder.
  Since 2026-09-18 a successful conversion also writes `<name>\<name>.I3CHR` next to the `.I3S` and adds the character to
  `Base String\Character.txt`, both through `i3chr` (see "Character files the converter writes"); the exe therefore needs
  `--hidden-import i3chr`.
- `I3Chara Convert Bone V3.exe`: PyInstaller build of the `.pyw` (bundles `pindah_bone`).
- `i3chr.py` + `I3CHR Editor V3.pyw` + `I3CHR Editor V3.exe`: the **third tool**, an editor for `.I3CHR`
  animation/state files (tree view, per-state edits incl. filling empty states and picking an animation plus its
  duration from an `.i3AnimPack` through `i3anim`, adding states, copying a weapon branch under a new name, bulk
  path find & replace, CSV export/import). Since 2026-09-22 the **same window also edits a WEAPON `.I3CHR`**
  (the ninth tool's panel, `i3senjata`): the file type is detected on open. See "One editor for both" below.
  The `.exe` was rebuilt from the merged source on 2026-09-22 (old character-only build kept in
  `_backup_sebelum_gabung\`).
- `i3anim.py` + `I3Anim Editor V3.pyw` + `I3Anim Editor V3.exe`: the **fourth tool**, for `.i3AnimPack` animation
  packs (three lists: animations, tracks, keyframes; rename, retime, swap a motion from this or another pack, and
  export one animation as a standalone `.i3a`). Built 2026-09-13. It imports `i3anim`; `--skeleton` lazily imports `pindah_bone`
  to read the `.I3S`, so the exe is built with both hidden imports.
- `i3path.py` + `I3Path Editor V3.pyw` + `I3Path Editor V3.exe`: the **fifth tool** (2026-09-13), an editor for a map's AI
  walking path (`World\<Map>\Path.i3Path`): move/add/delete points, link/unlink, one-way/two-way, undo, CSV, and
  `--gambar` to write the render as PNG. Since 2026-09-24 it has the same **two tabs as the collision editor** -
  a textured OpenGL "Tampilan 3D" and the old top-down "Denah 2D". See "Map data" and "Path editor 3D view" below.
- `i3ins.py` + `I3INS Editor V3.pyw` + `I3INS Editor V3.exe`: the **sixth tool** (2026-09-13), a viewer/editor for a map's
  object placements (`World\Scene\<Map>\<Map>.i3INS`, GINS v3, and v4 from newer map builds such as `V3 Crackdown\`: respawns, glass, trigger boxes, light) over the same
  map render plus the AI path. It imports `i3path` for the render and, since 2026-09-14, `i3gl` for a textured 3D tab like
  the collision editor's, with each trigger box coloured and labelled by its event. It also adds, duplicates, renames and
  deletes objects, and imports glass/i3Obj objects (e.g. the Giran2 Golem) from another map's `.i3INS` + `.RSC`.
- `ikat_bone.py` + `I3Bone Weight V3.pyw` + `I3Bone Weight V3.exe`: the **seventh tool** (2026-09-13), binds bone weights
  to a model whose vertices have none (a head made from OBJ inside a mask template, `Avatar\Mask\M_M_Ucok\Ucok_Head_LOD1.i3s`),
  by transferring them from a skinned reference or to one bone, with a 3D preview and a per-bone pose test ("Uji gerak").
  Since 2026-09-19 that preview is drawn by `i3gl` (OpenGL) with the tkinter painter kept as the fallback, so the exe
  also needs `--hidden-import i3gl`. See "Binding bone weights" below.
- `i3senjata.py` (+ `I3CHR Weapon Editor V3.pyw`, superseded by the weapon panel inside
  `I3CHR Editor V3.pyw` but still present and still working): the **ninth tool** (2026-09-22), an editor for a WEAPON's
  `.I3CHR` (states, animations, durations, and the sound chain `i3TimeSequence` -> `i3TimeSequenceInfo` ->
  `i3SoundNode` -> `i3SoundPlayInfo` -> `i3Sound` that `i3chr.py` refuses), plus `konversi()`: take a V1
  weapon's state layout as the skeleton and fill it with a V3 weapon's animations and sounds. See
  "Weapon `.I3CHR`" below. No `.exe` yet.
- `i3col.py` + `i3gl.py` + `I3Collision Editor V3.pyw` + `I3Collision Editor V3.exe`: the **eighth tool** (2026-09-13), a
  viewer/editor for map collision (`World\<Map>\<Map>_Col_Hero.I3S` character collision and `_Col_Hit.I3S` bullet
  collision, PhysX 2.8.1 NXUSTREAM inside i3PhysixShapeSet): delete, add box, duplicate, move/rotate/resize, delete mesh
  triangles in an area. Two views: a textured OpenGL 3D tab (`i3gl.py`, 2026-09-14) and the 2D map render from `i3path`.
  See "Map collision" and "3D view" below.
- `pindah_senjata.py` + `pindah_karakter.py` + `I3Scene Convert v3.pyw` + `I3Scene Convert v3.exe`: the **second tool**,
  for new-client (`I3SN`) files. `pindah_senjata.py` main mode repairs a weapon so i3Viewer2 and the legacy client accept
  it (`Weapon\Harvest_Pitchfork\` is the sample); with `--base` it instead moves the mesh onto a V1 weapon
  (`Weapon\Kukrii\Kukrii.I3S`, CLI only since 2026-09-14). `pindah_karakter.py` (2026-09-14) converts new-client
  **character** files (skin LODs, mask, headgear) to the old V2 layout that i3Viewer2 and `pindah_bone` read. The GUI
  (user's layout, 2026-09-14): "1. File I3s" takes several files, `jenis_file()` routes each to character / weapon /
  already-old, output = `<name>_convert.i3s` in the input's folder, "Path tekstur" empty = keep the file's paths. With
  args the `.pyw`/exe runs `pindah_senjata.main()` for `--senjata/--base`, otherwise `pindah_karakter.main()`.
  Since 2026-09-24 it also routes **map collision** files (see "V3 collision -> V1"): `kenali()` asks
  `i3col.adalah_collision()` first, and the window icon comes from `Icon\Scene.ico` (`_pasang_ikon`,
  a folder next to the program wins over the bundled copy). The `.exe` was rebuilt that day with
  `--hidden-import i3col --hidden-import i3pack --icon Icon\Scene.ico --add-data "Icon;Icon"`;
  the 2026-09-14 build is kept in `_backup_sebelum_collision\`.
  See "New-client character files" below.
- `i3pack.py` + `I3Pack Editor V3.pyw` + `I3Pack Editor V3.exe`: the **tenth tool** (2026-09-23), an editor for the client's `.i3Pack`
  archives, written from scratch to replace `Desktop\Decode\i3PackEditor.exe` whose source the user lost (that exe is
  native C++/MFC from the `pbblow replica` kit, so it cannot be decompiled back to source). Library + CLI + tkinter GUI;
  its output is **byte-identical to the old exe's**, re-encryption of SECURE files included. See "`.i3Pack` format" below.
  Drag & drop from Explorer works without any extra package: `PenerimaTarikan` calls `DragAcceptFiles` and
  **subclasses the Tk window procedure** (`SetWindowLongPtrW(GWL_WNDPROC)`) to catch `WM_DROPFILES`. The `WNDPROC`
  object is kept on the instance (if the GC frees it Windows calls a dead address) and the old proc is restored on
  `WM_DESTROY`. **The wndproc must not touch tkinter at all**: a real drop is dispatched from inside the Tcl event
  loop, where Tcl has released the GIL, and calling `after_idle` (or any widget method) there kills the process with
  `Fatal Python error: PyEval_RestoreThread ... the GIL is released` - the user hit exactly this (WER: `pythonw.exe`
  faulting in `ucrtbase.dll`, `0xC0000409`). The callback therefore only does ctypes calls plus `queue.Queue.put`, and
  the existing `after()` pump in the window does the work, serialised by a busy flag because the confirmation dialog
  runs a nested Tk loop. **A test that uses `SendMessage` to deliver `WM_DROPFILES` passes even when the app is
  broken** (the callback then runs with the GIL held, from Python code); the test must `PostMessage` and let
  `mainloop()` dispatch it.
  Dropped files replace same-named entries keeping their cipher, new names are added plain, folders are recreated as
  nodes, and a lone `.i3Pack` opens instead.
  Two more things the user asked for (2026-09-23): a **File Browser** (`JendelaJelajah`, Ctrl+B) modelled on PB SDK's
  `Form3` - type to filter, prefix combo from the SDK's `fileTag` list, "show empty" hiding packs <= **313 bytes**
  (the SDK's own rule; a real empty pack this tool writes is 312), size/date columns, Enter opens the top hit - and
  **external tools per file type** (`Pengaturan` in `I3Pack Editor V3.ini` next to the program, auto-detected on first
  run: `.i3i` -> i3ImageViewer, `.i3s` -> i3Viewer2, `.rsc` -> RSCEditor, `.pef`/`.i3RegXML` -> PropertyEditor,
  `.I3CHR`/`.i3Path`/`.i3INS`/`.i3AnimPack` -> this repo's own V3 editors). A file opened that way is written to a
  temp dir under its own name, and the `after()` pump hashes it once a second: when the external tool saves, the user
  is asked whether to pull the new bytes back into the pack.
  The file list has the old exe's columns - **Nama, Ukuran, Tipe, Cipher, Encoding, Diubah**. `Cipher` is
  `Berkas.cipher_lengkap()`: the slot's own cipher (`no` / `V1` / `V2.<type>:<key>`) plus `int: IIA2(n) P8(n) TEX2(n)`
  from `periksa_internal()`, a byte scan for `IIA2` chunks whose cipher word at +20 is non-zero, `VA30` with format bit
  0x20000000, and TEX2/TEX3 tags (0.01 s on a 23 MB pack, cached per content). Checked against the notes above: the
  Dajeong skins read `IIA2(2)`/`IIA2(6)`, Priest is clean. `Encoding` is a heuristic (BINER/ASCII/UTF-8/UTF-16 LE),
  `Diubah` is the session edit time. Rows whose content was replaced are tagged red, newly added ones green
  (`Berkas.diubah` / `.status`, display-only fields the library never writes).
  The `.exe` was built 2026-09-23 with the PyInstaller 6.22.2 venv left in an earlier session's scratchpad
  (`--onefile --windowed --hidden-import i3pack`, 8.6 MB); `main()` calls `AttachConsole(-1)` and reopens
  `CONOUT$` when the frozen exe is given CLI arguments, otherwise a windowed build prints into NUL. Smoke test
  `scratchpad/uji_exe.py`: 8 checks in a folder holding no `.py` file (CLI list/extract-one/--help, window opens,
  a window carrying `WS_EX_ACCEPTFILES`, clean close, the `.ini` written with auto-detected tools). Note the window
  belongs to the **onefile child process**, so find it by title, not by the PID `Popen` returned. Drag & drop is
  registered on `winfo_id()` (the Tk client window, class `TkChild`) - `GetParent()` is timing-dependent at startup,
  and every Tk widget window is a descendant of that one, so the shell's parent walk always reaches it. Tests: `uji_i3pack.py` (29 checks incl. byte-comparison against the exe),
  `uji_i3vtex.py` (28), `uji_i3obj.py` (32), `uji_i3bersih.py` (31) and `uji_i3pack_gui.py` (147 GUI checks; the drag & drop ones build a real HDROP - `DROPFILES` header + double-NUL
  UTF-16 list in `GlobalAlloc` memory - `PostMessage` it and run `mainloop()` briefly, so the whole path is exercised.
  `GlobalAlloc.restype` must be set to `c_void_p` or the handle is truncated on 64-bit Python).
- `i3game.py` + `I3Game Editor V3.pyw` + `I3Game Editor V3.exe`: the **eleventh tool** (2026-09-24), an editor for
  the client's stage list `BC.i3Game` - the file that decides which maps the client knows at all. See
  "`BC.i3Game`" below. Built with `--icon Icon\IconExe.ico --add-data "Icon;Icon" --hidden-import i3game`.
- `i3rsc.py` + `I3RSC Editor V3.pyw` + `I3RSC Editor V3.exe`: the **thirteenth tool** (2026-09-25), an
  editor for the resource lists `.RSC`. Reads BOTH entry forms (`RSC2` per-map and `RSC1` global,
  which `i3ins.baca_rsc` could not open at all), edits entries, opens/saves straight from a `.i3Pack`,
  and **copies entries from another RSC** - see "`.RSC` fully decoded" below.
- `i3viewer.py` + `I3Viewer Editor V3.pyw` + `I3Viewer Editor V3.exe`: the **fourteenth tool** (2026-09-26), a 3D
  editor for a map's scene `.I3S` - list the models in a map, **copy a model out of another map**, and drag it into
  place. Works on V1 and V3 (`I3SN`) scenes. See "Moving models between maps" below.
- `i3bvh.py` + `I3BVH Convert V3.pyw` + `I3BVH Convert V3.exe`: the **fifteenth tool** (2026-09-26), a two-way
  bridge between **BVH motion capture** (what Blender exports from a Mixamo FBX) and a standalone **`.i3a`**.
  `BVH -> .i3a` retargets the motion onto a character's own skeleton read from its `.I3S`; `.i3a -> BVH`
  writes a PB animation out so it can be opened in Blender. No Blender needed for either direction.
  See "Mixamo -> `.i3a`" below. `Blender\mixamo_ke_bvh.py` is an optional shortcut script that
  runs inside Blender (import the FBX, export the BVH); the manual two-menu route is identical and is
  what the README documents. That script is the only piece here never executed - there is no Blender
  on this machine.
- `i3wrd.py` + `I3WRD Editor V3.pyw` + `I3WRD Editor V3.exe`: the **twelfth tool** (2026-09-24), an editor for a map's
  `.i3WRD` - the table of contents the client reads FIRST when loading a map (the five scene files, the map-sector and
  world-section tables, and the fog). See "`.i3WRD`" below. Its `--ganti-nama-map` is the fix for a copied map pack:
  the five paths inside still name the source map, which is what produces
  `i3ResourceManager::OnUpdate : Asserted : pNode != NULL`.
- Bases live in `Base Chara\` and are picked by gender (`--gender`, radio buttons in the GUI):
  `Female\REBEL_Female.I3S` and `Male\SWAT_Male.I3S`. The user dropped RicaWraith/Bella in 2026-09-12;
  `--base FILE` still takes any V1 character. `I3ToolsViewer\i3Viewer2.exe` is the user's engine viewer.
- Avatar V2 input comes in three folders and two categories the GUI has separate fields for:
  `Avatar\Skin\` (body) plus either `Avatar\Mask\` (face, for a skin with no face, e.g. `F_S_AR_Priest-Red`)
  or `Avatar\Headgear\` (hair, for a skin with no hair, e.g. `IF_S_Dajeong-Red`).

## Commands

There is no test suite, linter or build config; every conversion re-reads its output and checks every vertex.

```powershell
# skin tanpa rambut + headgear (rigid part)
$d = "Avatar\Skin\IF_S_Dajeong-Red"
python pindah_bone.py --gender female --skin $d\IF_S_Dajeong-Red_LOD0.i3s --skin $d\IF_S_Dajeong-Red_LOD1.i3s --skin $d\IF_S_Dajeong-Red_LOD2.i3s --skin $d\IF_S_Dajeong-Red_LOD3.i3s --headgear Avatar\Headgear\IF_H_Dajeong\IF_H_Dajeong.I3S --out $env:TEMP\pb\Dajeong_Red\Dajeong_Red.I3S --tex-prefix "Chara/Dajeong_Red/" --copy-tex --drop-mesh Teamband
# skin tanpa wajah + mask (skinned part, one file per LOD)
$d = "Avatar\Skin\F_S_AR_Priest-Red"; $m = "Avatar\Mask\F_M_Chou"
python pindah_bone.py --gender female --skin $d\F_S_AR_Priest-Red_LOD0.i3s --skin $d\F_S_AR_Priest-Red_LOD1.i3s --skin $d\F_S_AR_Priest-Red_LOD2.i3s --skin $d\F_S_AR_Priest-Red_LOD3.i3s --mask $m\F_M_Chou_Y_LOD1.i3s --mask $m\F_M_Chou_Y_LOD2.i3s --mask $m\F_M_Chou_Y_LOD3.i3s --out $env:TEMP\pb\Priest\Priest.I3S --tex-prefix "Chara/Priest/" --copy-tex --drop-mesh Teamband
python "I3Chara Convert Bone V3.pyw"          # GUI
# senjata client baru dibetulkan apa adanya (mode utama program kedua)
python pindah_senjata.py --senjata Weapon\Harvest_Pitchfork\Harvest_Pitchfork.I3S --out $env:TEMP\pb\Harvest_Pitchfork\Harvest_Pitchfork.I3S --tex-prefix "Weapon\Harvest_Pitchfork" --copy-tex
# mesh senjata baru dipindah ke bone senjata V1 (mode --base)
python pindah_senjata.py --base Weapon\Kukrii\Kukrii.I3S --senjata Weapon\Harvest_Pitchfork\Harvest_Pitchfork.I3S --out $env:TEMP\pb\HP_Kukrii\HP_Kukrii.I3S --tex-prefix "Weapon\HP_Kukrii" --copy-tex
python "I3Scene Convert v3.pyw"      # GUI senjata + karakter client baru
# karakter client baru (skin/mask/headgear) ke format V2 lama -> <nama>_convert.i3s di folder yang sama
python pindah_karakter.py --file Avatar\Skin\F_S_SX_HarvestFarmer-Red\F_S_SX_HarvestFarmer-Red_LOD1.i3s --copy-tex
```

Bisection (2026-09-17): `Uji\Harvest_ViperRed_ujiB_tanpaTopi.I3S` (fix2 minus `--drop-mesh A_H_FarmerHat`) **equips
and renders in game** - the A_H_FarmerHat_Harvest hat (a skinned 1-bone `Head` mesh plus an `_Alpha_` part with

Its attributes match the working IF_H_Dajeong_Shaman-Blue hat in Dasom_Red, its vertices are clean and its i3i
headers equal the working hair textures. **ujiD (fix2 with the `_Alpha_` nodes renamed `_Trans_`) equips and
renders with the hat in game**: the legacy client rejects AttrSet/Geometry names containing "Alpha" (ujiC/ujiE
were not needed). This is now in `pindah_bone` (see "Clean-up for the legacy client" below). The registry entry (`Character.i3RegXML`, key `Harvest_ViperRed`, _IDNumber 114, _Type 66) matches
Dasom_Red's; the I3CHR edits (`BShield`, 3PV `BalliicShield` path) reference nothing and Dasom_Red has the same.
`harvest_variant.py` (scratch) builds these via a patched `pb.I3R2` + `pb.RENAME`.

Client (`C:\Users\HYPERION\Documents\BlacklistPB V1 Remake`): `Chara\<name>\<name>.I3CHR` loose, the I3S and
textures in `Pack\Chara_<name>.i3Pack`. i3Pack = I3R2 v9 whose objects are `i3PackNode` (name + `TRN3` + 72-byte
header: child count @+8, child ids after it), then u32 0x90713282-ish marker + 4 bytes and 92-byte file entries.
Each entry is obfuscated by rotating the whole 92-byte block right by 2 bits as one big-endian integer: 64-byte name,
then offset = hi16 @+72 | lo16 @+80, size = hi16 @+74 | lo16 @+70 (other bytes unknown, maybe a checksum); file
data is stored plain at those absolute offsets. The I3CHR copies keep the 271081-byte string table by hand-editing
other strings (`BallisticShield` -> `BShield` / `Ballist313133icShield`, a 1PV anim path) - Dasom_Red works that way. The broken earlier file had been **re-saved by
an i3Engine tool** (resource path `C:\Users\HYPERION\Desktop\HeavyRain\Chara\Dasom_Red\Dasom_Red.I3S`):
header version 0x90001, BMA1->BMA2, objects re-laid out, orphans dropped, 0xCCCCCCCC padding, a pointer
value at i3LOD+44 - i3Viewer2 opens that, the legacy client does not. A full re-save is not the same as
i3Viewer2's "Quitar IIA2" strip, which keeps the 0x80001 layout (the working `Dasom_Blue.I3S`).

user in the GUI) renders correctly in the BlacklistPB client - hair seated on the head, face clear, animation normal.

Regression check after touching conversion code: run both commands above (`Verifikasi OK` + expected LOD pairing)
and load each result in i3Viewer2 — **the viewer is the only check that catches engine-level rejects**. The old
byte-identical MD5 baselines are gone with the RicaWraith inputs the user deleted; the 2-NUL string-table fix
(2026-09-12) changed every output anyway, so files converted before it should be re-converted.

Base choice: `Base Chara/Female/REBEL_Female.I3S` shares one skeleton between LOD0+LOD1 and its index/middle finger
bind differs from V2 skins (warning, no fix possible). `Base Chara/Male/SWAT_Male.I3S` is the male bone source (its
LOD0 has 56 bones, no legs); female skins and female masks are correctly refused against it (pose diff 0.33).

Rebuild the exe with PyInstaller 6.22.2 in a throwaway venv outside the project (downloading from PyPI needs the
user's OK first), then smoke-test it headless with the same args as the CLI:

```powershell
<venv>\Scripts\pyinstaller --noconfirm --clean --onefile --windowed --name "I3Chara Convert Bone V3" --paths . --hidden-import pindah_bone --hidden-import i3chr "I3Chara Convert Bone V3.pyw"
```

**Windows Defender deletes `--onefile` builds (2026-09-27)**. The user reported "I3Pack Editor saya tadi
tidak ada exe nya". It was not a failed build: `Get-MpThreatDetection` shows Defender removing
`I3Pack Editor V3.exe` **and** `I3Viewer Editor V3.exe` (plus their Start Menu shortcuts) at 23:46, and the
freshly built copy in the scratchpad at 23:55 - ThreatID `2147731849`, a machine-learning heuristic. A copy
attempt during quarantine fails with a bare `Permission denied`, which looks like a file-lock problem and is
not one. `I3BVH Convert V3.exe` was gone too.

This is the standard false positive on a PyInstaller **onefile** binary: one big self-extracting archive, the
shape packers have. The cure that does not depend on the heuristic's mood is `--onedir`:

    <venv>\Scripts\pyinstaller --noconfirm --clean --onedir --windowed --name "<Tool>" --paths . \
        <hidden imports as in the onefile command> --icon Icon\<X>.ico --add-data "Icon;Icon" "<Tool>.pyw"

Rebuilt that way 2026-09-27 and **not flagged**: `I3Pack Editor V3` (exe 1.4 MB + `_internal`, 21 MB total),
`I3Viewer Editor V3` (3.3 MB + 66 MB, numpy) and `I3BVH Convert V3` (3.2 MB + 66 MB). Each now lives in its
own folder `HeavyRain\<Tool>\<Tool>.exe`; all three open on a real pack and close cleanly.

Two consequences of onedir worth knowing: the program's `.ini` is written **next to the exe**, i.e. inside that
folder, so an existing `<Tool>.ini` in the project root must be copied in (done for I3Pack Editor); and
`folder_ikon()` still works because `sys._MEIPASS` is the `_internal` folder, where `--add-data` puts `Icon\`.
A folder next to the exe still wins, so icons stay replaceable without a rebuild.

**Settled 2026-09-28**: the user added the folder exclusion themselves - `(Get-MpPreference).ExclusionPath`
now lists `C:\Users\HYPERION\Desktop\HeavyRain` - and asked for the single-file form back, so all three were
rebuilt `--onefile` at their usual sizes (`I3Pack Editor V3` 8,698,459 B with `i3i`; `I3Viewer Editor V3`
23,040,039 B; `I3BVH Convert V3` 22,982,968 B), each smoke-tested (window opens, Pack Editor on a real pack,
all close cleanly) and the temporary onedir folders removed. **Changing Defender settings is the user's call,
never done from here.** Keep `--onedir` in mind as the fallback when an exclusion is not an option (another
machine, a handover copy). Note also that Defender took the **Start Menu shortcuts** for I3Pack Editor and
I3Viewer Editor with the exes; they were not recreated.

**Cloud build (2026-09-17)**, when no Windows shell is available: Wine 9 (`/usr/lib/wine/wine64`, WINEPREFIX of
its own), Windows CPython 3.10.15 from astral-sh/python-build-standalone (`cpython-3.10.15+20241016-x86_64-pc-
windows-msvc-install_only.tar.gz`, includes tkinter; python.org is blocked by the proxy, GitHub is not), and
PyInstaller 6.22.2 wheels fetched with `pip download --platform win_amd64 --python-version 3.10` (add `pefile` and

makes the isolated child fail with `init_sys_streams ... Invalid handle`. The resulting exe converts the Harvest

The orphan-texture placeholder counts embedded-texture sizes from `s.tertanam` (it used to depend on which files

`--add-data` and `--icon` paths are resolved against `--specpath`, so when the spec goes to the scratchpad
(as below) give them as ABSOLUTE paths or PyInstaller stops with "Unable to find ... when adding binary
and data files".

Onefile builds spawn a child process, so `Get-Process -Id` on the process `Start-Process` returned reports
`MainWindowHandle = 0`; enumerate by `-Name` instead to see the real window. Point `--distpath/--workpath/--specpath`
at the scratchpad so the project folder stays clean, then copy the exe in.

PowerShell 5.1 drops empty-string arguments to native programs: use `--head-exclude=`, not `--head-exclude ""`.

## How `convert()` works

1. Base must have exactly one `i3Body`; its LODs become `v1` (LOD0 = first-person arms with curled-finger pose,
   LOD1 = 63 bones + ragdoll, LOD2/LOD3 = 25 bones). All `--skin` files are pooled; `--part` files are handled separately.
2. `pair_lods` searches for the best one-to-one assignment of source (body, LOD) entries to V1 LODs:
   - a candidate **fits** a V1 LOD when its bone names are a superset of that LOD's names. Many V2 skins
     (Gowoon, Dasom, SpiderNatasha) use one 67-bone skeleton for every LOD, so equality would reject their
     LOD2/LOD3 against a 25-bone V1 LOD; the surplus bones are remapped to their nearest ancestor by `build_remap`
     (finger bones -> `R Hand`), which is how V1 LOD2 meshes are built anyway.
   - `pose_count(src, dst, tol=0.05)` then rejects a candidate when more than a third of the compared bones sit
     somewhere else entirely. A few bones may differ a lot (REBEL_Female's 12 grip fingers, 0.40) and every bone may
     differ a little (IF_S_Dasom-Red's whole skeleton is 2.5 mm lower), but a female skin on `SWAT_Male` differs on
     51 of 56 bones and is refused with a "pilih jenis kelamin yang sesuai" message. **Name equality alone does not
     separate male from female**: both skeletons use the same bone names, only the bind pose differs.
   - among the fitting candidates it first maximises the number of LODs whose **file-name LOD number** matches
     (`lodno` from `_LOD(\d).i3s`, set by `lod_entries` only for a file holding exactly one (body, LOD); added
     2026-09-17), then the number of LODs whose pose matches exactly (<1e-3; this is what picks the
     curled-finger LOD0 arms mesh), then minimises detail inversions, so the base LOD with the most original
     vertices gets the densest source mesh. Without the name term IF_S_Dasom-Red (LOD1-3 skeletons 2.4 mm lower,
     so only its LOD0 arms match exactly - and they match base LOD2 too) got LOD0<-LOD2 body and LOD2<-LOD0 arms.
     Checked against all 28 per-LOD skins in `Avatar\Skin\`: only Dasom-Red changed (the rest already paired by
     number; Gowoon_PBIC2026 is a new-client file and is refused before pairing). The log warns when a skin
     lands on a LOD other than its file-name number.
3. Parts (`--part`/`--mask`/`--headgear`) are split into a rigid pool and a skinned pool, **pooled across files** so a
   mask shipped as one file per LOD (`F_M_Chou_Y_LOD1/2/3.i3s`, 1 body 1 LOD each) can fill several V1 LODs.
   `spread_parts` walks the third-person LODs (lod > 0; LOD0 shows no head) and gives each the most detailed pool
   entry that still fits — `part_fit` = the part's weighted bone names exist in that LOD and their inverse binds match
   within 1e-3 (rigid parts skip the test). A LOD with nothing left gets a log line, leftovers get a warning, and if
   nothing fits at all the error names the closest miss ("pose bone-nya tidak cocok ... selisih 0.33" = female mask on
   the male base). A part file shaped like V1 (1 body, same LOD count, e.g. the old `Chou_Head.i3s`) still pairs by LOD
   index. `--mask`/`--headgear` also declare the expected kind, so a file in the wrong GUI field is refused by name.
3b. When pose cannot separate two V1 LODs (an old base such as `Base Chara/Female/REBEL_Female.I3S` shares one skeleton between
   LOD0 and LOD1), `pair_lods` falls back to detail ranking using the base's own per-LOD mesh vertex counts.
3c. Bind-pose fit: if the paired skin's inverse-bind matrices differ from the base LOD's (REBEL_Female's index/middle
   fingers differ by 0.4), the LOD's `i3MatrixArray` is patched in place with the skin's matrices. If that skeleton or
   matrix array is shared with another LOD, the fit is skipped with a warning - **never add a new i3Skeleton object**:
   the engine resolves an i3LOD's skeleton at load time and crashes (0xC0000005 in i3SceneDx) on a forward reference.
   `--no-fit-bind` disables the fit.
3d. Rigid V2 headgear/hair parts (`Avatar/Headgear/IF_H_*.I3S`): detected when every VA of the part has no blend
   index slot. Their shape node is an `i3BoneRef`, the skeleton holds one dummy bone and no matrix array, and the
   vertices live in the attach bone's local space. `ATTACH_OF` maps the dummy name to the skin skeleton's
   `Bone_HeadGearAttach`/`Bone_FaceGearAttach`; `rigid_to_skin()` moves the vertices with
   `mat_mul(local matrix of the part's dummy bone, inv4(invBind(attach)))` - **the dummy's local matrix comes first**:
   it carries the orientation (IF_H_Dajeong's is an axis permutation, local X→world Y, Y→Z, Z→X) while the attach
   bone's world bind is a pure translation (0, 0.0098, 1.741), so dropping it leaves the hair rotated ("rambut
   terbalik"). It also rotates normal/tangent/binormal, appends a 1-byte bone index (`fmt |= 1 << 14`, descriptor
   byte 19 |= 0xC0) and binds them to `Head`. They go to the third-person LODs (lod > 0) by detail order and are excluded from verify's
   byte comparison (their vertices change on purpose).
4. `--drop-mesh` removes mesh roots by node-name substring. `build_remap` maps bone indices by name; V2-only
   `Bone_*Attach` bones fall back to their nearest ancestor (parent derived from the depth field).
5. `droppable_tail` drops only a contiguous tail of mesh/attr/buffer objects before the SGI that nothing earlier
   references (nothing is droppable in the two Base Chara files: their meshes sit before the SGI, so they stay as orphans).
6. Output: base header → string table (base prefix up to the header string count + new strings) → object table →
   **base data region copied verbatim with offsets shifted** → appended rewritten LOD shape nodes, new objects
   (per source, in index order, IDs continuing after kept objects), optional V1-head wrapper AttrSets, SGI last.
7. Orphan base textures are repointed to the smallest new texture; otherwise the engine looks for the missing base
   textures (i3Viewer2 opens a Korean folder-picker dialog for each). Trailing NUL padding on the base string table is
   stripped: appending strings after a NUL-padded last entry puts NULs inside a class name and the engine asserts
   (0x80000003 in i3BaseDx).
6b. New `i3AlphaFuncAttr` objects are written with the ref masked to 0-255 (ref u32 + func u8); the
   IF_H_Dajeong_Shaman-Blue LOD1 attr carries `d2 00 72 00 05` and i3Engine itself saves it as `d2 00 00 00 05`.
7b. Clan logo: every V2 skin's `Model_Clan` binds `Avatar/Clan_PointBlank_Diff.i3i` (the V1 bases use `Chara/Clan/...`,
   repointed as orphans), which no skin folder ships, so i3Viewer2 asked for it on every result. The user keeps
   Diff/Norm/Spec in `Avatar\Clan\`. The GUI option "Salin tekstur clan" (default on, 2026-09-13; it replaced the removed
   "Pasang kepala asli" option - `--head` is CLI-only now) passes `clan_dir`, which only touches the texture copy step
   after the file is written: the clan folder joins the fallback search, and with copy-tex off only clan textures are
   copied. Output bytes are unchanged.
8. `verify()` checks SGI/root, skeleton names per LOD, a strict walk of every mesh reference, bone-index bounds,
   per-vertex bone-name equality against the source, and that non-index vertex bytes are untouched.

## Clean-up for the legacy client (2026-09-17)

`rapikan_sumber(s, folders, log)` runs on every skin/part source right after loading (in memory only), and
`nama_v1()` renames new AttrSet/Geometry objects:
- `nama_v1`: RENAME table, `Model_[Cc]lan_LOD\d(_Material)?` -> `Model_Clan(_Material)`, and `(?i)alpha` -> `Trans`.
  **In-game proven**: a node named `..._Alpha_...` makes the character fail to equip (Harvest hat).
- embedded `i3Texture` (data = whole .i3i) -> external: name from the i3i header (+26 u16 length, name at +60,
  basename), data kept in `s.tertanam` and always written next to the output (skipped by the copy step).
- NormalMapBind whose texture is i3i format 0x07 (byte 10; looked up in the source folder + `cadangan`) -> that
  AttrSet's NormalMapEnable/Bind go into `s.buang`; `dibuang(f, o)` (DROP_CLASSES or `s.buang`) is used by
  `mesh_refs` and the AttrSet rewrite.
- vertex colour dropped from every VA whose colours are all ffffffff (fmt &= ~8, 4 bytes after the normal removed).
  verify() compares against the cleaned source, so it still passes.
With these, the four HarvestFarmer LODs + female base + `--drop-mesh Teamband` give **byte for byte** the
in-game-tested `Uji\Harvest_ViperRed_ujiD_topiAlphaRename.I3S` (MD5 of 2,606,354 bytes). Regression over the 27
per-LOD skins in `Avatar\Skin`: 21 unchanged; changed only by the white-colour strip (Dasom Blue/Red,
SpiderNatasha, both Samurai Girls), by the clan rename (Element_Fire) and Harvest. Dasom_Red with the Shaman part
still verifies (formats 0x4483/0x8c483/0x8c4a7) but that new output is untested in game.

## How `pindah_senjata` works

Two modes. **`convert_mandiri()` (no `--base`) is the default and what the user wants**: it fixes the
new-client file in place, keeping its own skeleton, shape, size and LOD structure. Only the four things that
make a new-client weapon unusable are touched:

1. the `I3SN` wrapper (dropped by the reader),
2. VA30 **Platform 8** vertex arrays (`fmt & 0x20000000`, a `w` float after the tangent) -> `strip_platform8()`
   drops the `w` and clears the bit; the viewer's Cifrado panel calls these "layout pbbr120, no se modifica",
3. the new material (`i3SamplerAttr` + `i3RasterizerAttr` + `i3AlphaBlendAttr`) -> a V1-style AttrSet is
   appended (`i3TextureEnableAttr` + `i3TextureBindAttr` + `i3MaterialAttr`), the parent `i3BoneRef`'s kid list
   is repointed at it, and the three leftover objects are re-typed to `i3TextureEnableAttr` (1 byte) so no
   new-client class remains. **Only the `_Diff` texture is bound**: the new files are PBR, so feeding `_Norm`
   / `_Spec` into the old normal/specular slots renders the whole model red (`--peta-lengkap` to try anyway),
4. the 108-byte `MAT2` material -> `MATERIAL_V1`, the 68-byte V1 layout
   (ambient, diffuse, emissive, specular, shininess=12.8; taken from Kukrii - REBEL_Female is the same with a
   black specular). Without this the weapon renders dull/unlit: it is what the user meant by "ceklist"
   (the Propiedades panel's Diffuse/Specular/Emissive/Shininess).

IIA2 encryption is left alone - i3Viewer2 decrypts it for display and its **Cifrado > Quitar IIA2 (strip)**
button plus a save writes plain indices. `tulis()` writes patched objects **in place** when they fit
(no zero-fill: `i3PhysixShapeSet` keeps untabled data past its declared size), otherwise in the tail.

Patching a node means re-emitting `name + INF2 + the bytes after it` - an `i3BoneRef` stores its bone index
there, and dropping it asserts `i3BoneMatrixListAttr::getBone`.

## How `pindah_senjata.convert()` (mode `--base`) works

1. Both files are read with `pb.I3R2`, which now strips a leading **`I3SN`** container (4 bytes before the plain
   I3R2 image; that wrapper alone is why i3Viewer2 refuses new-client files).
2. `weapon_lods()` walks each LOD's `i3BoneRef` chain down to the material `i3AttrSet` -> `i3Geometry` ->
   `i3GeometryAttr` -> VA/IA, and records which bone the leaf `i3BoneRef` uses (bone index sits right after the
   INF2 block) plus the `bind attr -> texture` map. Kukrii's chain is `GunDummy > AnimationDummy`, the Pitchfork's
   `GunDummy > AniDummy > AniDummy_Scale`, and the two chains have **different orientations**, so vertices are
   moved with `mat_mul(world(source leaf bone), inv4(world(base leaf bone)))` - the same trick as the V2 hair.
   Verified by transforming both meshes into GunDummy space: max difference 0.000000 m.
3. LODs pair by index; extra base LODs reuse the coarsest source LOD, extra source LODs are ignored with a warning.
4. `rebuild_va()` rewrites the source vertices into the **base LOD's own vertex layout**: the 40-byte VA header is
   copied from the base (format word + descriptor), positions/normals/tangents are rotated, and tangent/binormal
   are re-encoded. V1 weapons store them as **16.16 fixed-point int32**, new-client files as float32 (plus a
   `w = -1.0` after the tangent when format bit 0x20000000 is set). Descriptor byte 17 tells which: `& 0x7F` is
   1 = float, 2 = fixed.
5. Mesh objects are written **in place over the base's VA/IA objects** (`patch[obj.idx] = new bytes`, the table
   entry is repointed into the tail). Appending new objects at the end and pointing the base's `i3GeometryAttr` at
   them does NOT work: the engine creates objects in file order, so a forward reference leaves the vertex buffer
   uncreated and i3Viewer2 dies on `i3VertexArrayDX::Lock` (`Asserted : m_pBuffer`).
6. The V1 material is kept as is (that is what makes the result legacy-safe: `NewClass=0`, no `i3SamplerAttr` /
   `i3RasterizerAttr` / `i3AlphaBlendAttr`). Only the texture path **strings** are rewritten per role
   (diffuse/normal/specular/refmask/emissive, detected from the source's own bind attrs first, then from the
   `_Diff`/`_Norm`/`_Spec`/`_Ref` suffix). Roles the source lacks are dropped from the AttrSet and their base
   texture string is repointed at the new diffuse so no file goes missing.
7. `verify()` re-reads the output: LOD count, per-LOD vertex/index counts against the source, vertex format equal
   to the base's, every material attribute resolvable, string table ending in 2 NULs.

## New-client character files -- `pindah_karakter.py`

Sample (2026-09-14): `Avatar\Skin\F_S_SX_HarvestFarmer-Red\` LOD0-3 (`I3SN` + I3R2 v9, 44/95/90/85 objects, one
i3Body/LOD per file, 67/29 bones, full character incl. face `F_M`, hair `F_H`, gloves `F_G`, clan and a hat) and the hat
`Avatar\Headgear\A_H_FarmerHat_Harvest\A_H_FarmerHat_Harvest.I3S` the user extracted. Only two classes are new
(`i3SamplerAttr`, `i3AlphaBlendAttr`; weapons also `i3RasterizerAttr`), plus `MAT2` materials, Platform 8 VAs and
encrypted IIA2 (type 2).

- `i3SamplerAttr` = `SPLA`, u8 count, 44-byte slots: u32 texture raw id, **u8 role (0 diffuse, 7 normal, 5 specular,
  11 ref, 10 emissive)**, `02 02 02`, 16 zeros, 3 x f32 1.0, `01 01`, 6 zeros.
- `MAT2` (108 B): +6 diffuse RGBA, +22 third colour, +38 fourth colour, +54 u16, **+56 shininess**, +60/+64 the two
  i3SpecHighlightsAttr values. Old 68-byte material = 16 zeros + MAT2[6:54] + MAT2[56:60]; the clan material and
  highlights come out identical to `M_S_BG_Berserker-Red`'s old ones.
- `i3AlphaBlendAttr` = `APBA` + 8 bytes: +4 alpha test on, +5 ref, +6 func (D3DCMP, 5 GREATER), +8 blend on, +9 src,
  +10 dst, +11 op (D3DBLEND/D3DBLENDOP). Hair `01 32 05 00 00 02 01 01`, transparent hat part `01 00 05 00 01 05 06 01`.
  Old equivalents (IF_H_Dajeong, F_M_Chou, BB_P90_Ext_Bike): `i3AlphaTestEnableAttr 01`, `i3AlphaFuncAttr` = u8 ref + 3
  junk bytes + u8 func, `i3BlendEnableAttr 01`, `i3BlendModeAttr` = src dst op (`05 06 01`), placed after the material.
- VA header f32 +36 is **-1.0 in every old file** (Base Chara REBEL_Female aside) and 0.0 in new-client files; it is
  written as -1.0. Platform 8 `w` is mixed +1/-1 per vertex while the stored binormal is n x t, so the handedness only
  lived in `w`; the old layout has none.
- `pindah_bone`'s reader refuses the originals (`i3SamplerAttr ... belum didukung`), so `periksa()` requires
  `pb.lod_entries()` to accept the result.
- The file is **rebuilt, not patched**: `baca()` turns every reference slot into a Python reference (known slots: node
  kids, i3Transform matrix + combiner, AttrSet attrs, Geometry attrs, SKN2 LOD ids, BLD1 u64 ids, SKT1/BMA ids, SGI root,
  bind textures, sampler slots, i3PhysixShapeSet PXA3 ids in its untabled tail), and unknown classes or data that does not
  tile the file are refused. Converted attributes and all textures are deferred and emitted right before their first
  user, which reproduces the stock V2 order (Enable, Texture, Bind, ..., Material, AttrSet); attrs, buffers and textures
  always precede their users, node kids may follow as in stock files. Unused textures and the new classes are dropped;
  the source string table is kept in order minus unused class names/texture paths. Unchanged read -> rebuild reproduces
  the four HarvestFarmer files byte for byte (minus `I3SN`). i3Transform in these files = name + INF2 + u32 matrix +
  u32 combiner; the chara i3TransformSourceCombiner is 9 bytes; i3BoneRef tail = u32 0, u32 bone index, 8 zeros.
- New-client normal maps are `.i3i` format `0x07` (1 byte/pixel, one mip, likely BC5), so only `_Diff` is bound unless
  `--peta-lengkap`. The skin also references `Avatar/Clan_PointBlank_Diff.i3i` and the hat textures in
  `Avatar/Headgear/...`; `cari_tekstur()` looks in the input folder, the game-relative path from every parent folder,
  the program folder and `Avatar\Clan`, and `--copy-tex` copies them next to the result.
- Results 2026-09-14: all four LODs and the hat open in i3Viewer2 with no log lines (`VA30 P8=0 TEX2=0 TEX3=0
  NewClass=0`, only `IIA2=n`) and render textured; `pindah_bone --gender female` on the four `_convert.i3s` gives
  Verifikasi OK (LOD1 warns about REBEL_Female's 12 finger binds, as for every skin) and the V1 character renders with
  the hat. The exe CLI writes byte-identical files. Not tested in game.

## How `i3chr.py` works

`.I3CHR` is a plain I3R2 container holding a character's animation state machine, not geometry:
`i3Chara` (root) -> `i3AIContext` tree (`Lower > Stand`, `Upper > 1PV > AssaultRifle > AK-47 > AttackIdle`)
-> `i3AI` (state machine + driver name such as `AIDriverCharaUpper_AssaultRifle`) -> `i3AIState` ->
external `i3Animation` objects whose path lives in the string table (`CHARA/SWAT_FEMALE/3PV/...I3A`).
SWAT_Female.I3CHR: 24449 objects, 1291 AIs, 16132 states, 4385 animations.

- `i3AI` = name + `AI_0` + ... + u32 count + count u32 state ids + the driver name as a trailing raw string;
  the count is found by testing which u32 is followed by that many valid `i3AIState` ids.
- `i3AIContext` = name + `GND1`(parent id at +12) + `AIC1`(AI id at +8); the parent of a root context is the
  `i3Chara`. That is what `pohon()` walks to build the tree.
- `i3AIState` = name + `AIS1` + ... + **animation raw id at +16**, speed float at +24, blend float at +28,
  a copy of the animation's duration (f32) at +44, and the **embedded animation path: u32 length at +64, the
  text at +120** (object size = name + 120 + path length). A state with no animation has all of those at 0 and
  no text; filling one means writing all of them, not just +16 (checked byte-for-byte against 870MCS).
- **Making a new character = copy the base `.I3CHR` and change only the scene path.** The `i3Chara` node name
  must stay the base character's name (`SWAT_Female`): the engine resolves the animation set through it, and
  stock files do the same - `Chou_HalloweenNurse.I3CHR` is still named `SWAT_Female` inside. Renaming it makes
  the client fail with `i3Chara.cpp(379) i3Chara::OnLoad` + `Asserted : pNewChara` (user hit this 2026-09-12).
  Animation paths may legitimately point at another character (`CHARA/SWAT_FEMALE/...`); do not "fix" them.
- The `i3SceneGraphInfo` of an `.I3CHR` is itself an **external object**: its raw id carries the string index of
  `Chara\SWAT_Female\SWAT_Female.I3S`, so `set_scene()` edits it like any animation path. The character name
  lives inside the `i3Chara` node data (`set_nama()` also rewrites the identical free string in the table, the
  one no object references).
- Editing a path only rewrites the string-table entry when that string has a single user; otherwise the object
  gets its own string and every 4-byte reference to the old raw id is patched (`_raw_id_baru`).
- **Per-state animation (2026-09-13)**: `set_anim_state(state_idx, path, durasi=None)` points ONE state at an
  animation - including states that have none (the empty `UI_IdleA`/`UI_IdleB` of the Saiga weapons) - by writing the
  raw id (+16), the duration copy (+44) and the embedded path (+64/+120). `objek_animasi()` reuses an `i3Animation`
  whose path matches case-insensitively, otherwise appends a new external object at the end of the table: all 4385
  stock `i3Animation` objects have size 0 (a table entry plus a path string), and states referencing later objects
  are normal (4385 such references in stock data). `durasi=None` copies the duration from another state using the
  same object. The GUI Animasi field and CSV import use it; `set_anim()` renames the path of the **object**, i.e.
  for every state sharing it (870MCS, CaneShotgun and the patched Saiga_BT all share `UI_IDLEA`), and is now only
  reached through the bulk find & replace. `periksa()` also compares every patched object byte for byte and every
  new animation object. Regression check: redoing the Saiga_BT fix with `set_anim_state` + `set_angka(blend=0.3)`
  from the stock file reproduces the in-game-confirmed `Uji I3CHR Saiga/SWAT_Female.I3CHR` byte for byte.
- The embedded path copy in a state is **not** what the engine uses: 3830 of 13817 stock states with an animation
  disagree with their object's path (case, even `SWAT_FEMALE` vs `SWAT_Male`) and still play. The object reference is
  authoritative; the copy is written only for tidiness.
- **Adding states (2026-09-13)**: `tambah_state(ai_idx, nama)`. `i3AI` = name + `AI_0` + 32 bytes (u32 driver-name
  length at +12, the rest 0 in all 1291 AIs) + u32 state count at `AI_0+36` + state ids + driver name. **All 766 state
  lists are sorted by name case-insensitively**, so the new id goes to its sorted position (`UI_IdleA` after
  `UI_Idle_Stand`, as in M-7). **In stock data every one of the 16132 states sits before its AI in the table** (every
  AI before its context, every parent context before its children), so a new state is NOT appended at the end: the
  nearest `i3Animation` slot before the AI becomes the new state, and that animation is re-created at the end of the
  table with its state(s) repointed. State -> later-animation references are normal (4385 in stock data), no object
  other than states references animations, and no other object id moves. Template (`_cari_contoh`): same name, same
  driver, most similar context path, prefer one that has an animation, lowest index - 1PV UI states carry flag `0x01`
  at AIS1+4 while the working 3PV ones carry `0x21` (UI_IdleA) / `0x09` (UI_IdleB), which is why a 1PV template was
  wrong in the first attempt. The copy gets animation, embedded text and event (+56) cleared and its next state (+48)
  remapped by name inside the target AI (0 if absent). When `set_anim_state` fills a state, the embedded text follows
  another state that uses the same animation if the paths match case-insensitively. Regression check: adding
  `UI_IdleA`/`UI_IdleB` to `Upper > 3PV > Knife > Baseball_Bat > AttackIdle` and filling them with M-7's Knife UI
  animations + blend 0.3 gives states byte-identical to M-7's, 0 states after their AI and no other object changed
  (`Uji I3CHR Baseball_Bat/SWAT_Female.I3CHR`). **In-game confirmed 2026-09-13**: Baseball_Bat plays the relaxed
  knife lobby idle on Info Detail, so the engine accepts states added with this layout.
- **Copying a branch (2026-09-13)**: `salin_cabang(ctx_idx, nama)` copies a whole weapon branch (e.g.
  `Upper > 1PV > Knife > 2023_U20_WC_Trophy`; GUI "Salin cabang ini...", CLI `--salin-cabang JALUR NAMA`) under the
  same parent with a new name - how a new weapon such as `Harvest_Pitchfork` gets its AI. A context stores only its
  own parent id (GND1+12) and AI id (AIC1+8), no child list, so the parent stays untouched and the copies are
  appended at the end of the table in stock order: per context, each state directly followed by its private helper
  `Idle` and its 21-byte `i3TimeSequence`, then the AI, then the context, parents before children. Remapped: state
  +48/+56, the AI's state list, context GND1+12 (not for the copy's root)/AIC1+8. Scanning every u32 of every stock
  AI/state/context/time-sequence object found no other object references and no name hash (Knife siblings differ
  only in the GND1+8/AIC1+4 flag and the AI id; no time sequence holds its state's id). Animations are shared, not
  copied: `ganti_path_cabang` swaps path text per state in the copy only (`ganti_teks` would also rename the
  original). The root AI is renamed only when its name equals the context's (1219 of 1291; 72 stock contexts carry
  another weapon's AI name, e.g. `Sword_TH` -> AI `Kunai`, `BB_Gatling` -> `G36C`, so PB's own tools copied branches
  the same way). `rencana_salin` validates without side effects - duplicate sibling name, top-level branch, unknown
  layout, and branches whose events carry sound or an effect USED to be refused here (that limit was lifted 2026-09-26, see below) - so the GUI checks 1PV and 3PV before copying either. Test: Trophy 1PV (24
  objects, 19 states) and 3PV (23, 18) -> `Uji I3CHR Harvest_Pitchfork/SWAT_Female.I3CHR`: byte-equal to the source
  apart from names and remapped ids, 0 stock-order violations, no old object changed; CLI, GUI and exe write the
  identical file. Not yet confirmed in game.
- More AIS1 fields: +48 u32 **next state** id (470 states: `Change -> Idle` 358, where that `Idle` is a **private
  helper state in no AI's list** - no animation, no +48/+56, 1-2 objects after its `Change` - so the by-name remap in
  `tambah_state` is only right for same-AI links like `UI_IdleB -> UI_IdleA` (110) and `JumpEnd -> Idle` (2); every
  weapon already has `Change`), +56 u32 **i3TimeSequence** id (events/sounds, 876 states, never shared, 1-6 objects
  after its state), +36/+40 always `ffffffff`,
  +52/+60 always 0. +4 flags: `0x20` = **loops** (`Idle`, `Move`, `UI_Idle_Stand` and 3PV `UI_IdleA` are `0x21`),
  `0x01` = plays once (`Change`, `Attack`, `Damage*`, `UI_Idle_Change`), `0x09` = once then back (`JumpEnd`,
  `UI_IdleB`). **A looping state needs an animation whose first and last pose match**: the user put
  `Baseball_Bat/UI/Idle_Change` (first vs last pose up to 92 degrees) in `UI_IdleA` and the lobby snapped back
  every 3.1 s (their video, 2026-09-13); knife `UI_IdleA`/`UI_IdleB` differ 0.1/0.0 degrees and loop cleanly, and
  switching back to loop-safe animations with matching durations fixed it in game.
- 16 `Upper > 3PV > * > * > AttackIdle` contexts have no `UI_IdleA`/`UI_IdleB` states at all (Knife 8, Mission 3,
  SMG 2, ShotGun/DualKnife/Shield 1) - the case `tambah_state` exists for.
- `simpan()` rebuilds header + strings + table + data (patched objects in place when they fit) and then
  `periksa()` re-reads the result and compares every AI/state/animation. Saving an unchanged file reproduces
  the input **byte for byte** (verified on SWAT_Female.I3CHR).
- CSV export writes floats with `%.9g` so a float32 survives the round trip; without that every row looks
  changed on import.

## Character files the converter writes (2026-09-18)

The user asked the converter to finish the job: after `convert()` the GUI also produces the character's `.I3CHR` and
its entry in the game's string list. Both helpers live in `i3chr.py`:

- `BASE_CHR` = `Base I3CHR\SWAT_Female\SWAT_Female.I3CHR` / `Base I3CHR\SWAT_Male\SWAT_Male.I3CHR` (4.2 MB each,
  24,452 / 24,511 objects, both named `SWAT_Female`/`SWAT_Male` inside). `base_chr_for(gender, here, base_i3s)` picks one;
  for a custom base it guesses from the base `.I3S` file name.
- `buat_karakter(base, nama, out)` = `I3CHR(base)` + `set_scene(path_scene(nama))` + `simpan()`. `path_scene` writes
  `Chara\<nama>\<nama>.I3S` with backslashes, like the base and like every working character in the user's client.
  **The `i3Chara` node name is deliberately left alone** (engine looks the animation set up by it). The output is the base
  plus exactly the string-length difference (4,250,618 -> 4,250,630 bytes for `Bella_FireFighter`), and `simpan()`
  re-reads and compares every AI/state/animation. The in-game files in `BlacklistPB V1 Remake\Chara` are not byte-equal
  to this (they came from a different SWAT_Female build), only structurally the same.
- `Base String\Character.txt` = **UTF-16LE with BOM, lines joined by CRLF, no CRLF after the last line**, one entry per
  line: `Character\<name>\_Name` TAB display name, `Character\<name>\Description` TAB description (26 lines /
  6,088 bytes on 2026-09-18). Colour markup is `{col:r,g,b,a}...{/col}`. `baca_daftar`/`isi_daftar` round-trip it;
  `tambah_daftar(path, nama, judul, keterangan)` replaces the two lines of that character case-insensitively or appends
  them, backs the file up once to `Character._backup.txt`, writes through a temp file and re-reads to compare.
  `nama_tampil('Dajeong_Red')` -> `Dajeong {col:255,153,51,255}(Red){/col}` is only the GUI's editable default.
- `Chara_Config\Character.i3RegXML` (3.6 MB, UTF-8, LF, no BOM) is PropertyEditor's registry export:
  `<ROOT Name="RegistryRoot">` > `<KEY_1 Name="Character|Misc|Mode">` > one `<KEY_2 Name="<character>">` per character
  (127 under Character, ~68 lines each) holding `<STRING_2|REAL32_2|INT32_2|VEC3D_2|VEC4D_2 Name="..."
  Value__Default_="..." Value_Brazil="..." ...>` for 16 nations, plus a nested `<KEY_3 Name="DamageRate">`.
  `baca_registry()` splits it into lines (join round-trips byte for byte) and returns the KEY_2 spans; `_set_reg()`
  rewrites every `Value_*` attribute of one KEY_2-level value; `nomor_registry()` gives the largest `_IDNumber` (465)
  and `UIShapeIndex` (205) for the GUI's suggestions. `tambah_registry(path, nama, id, ui, gender)` copies the whole
  KEY_2 block of `CONTOH_REG` (`Harvest_ViperRed` female / `Boarder_Ucok` male - the user's own recent entries;
  `_SexType` 0 male / 1 female / 2 Dino, `_Type` 66, 59, ...), renames the key, stamps `__Make Time`/`__Update Time`
  with the current unix time, sets `_ResPath` = `Chara/<nama>/<nama>.I3CHR`, `_IDNumber` and `UIShapeIndex`, and
  appends it right before the Character section's `</KEY_1>` (the stock file already has unsorted entries at the end).
  An existing character is updated in place instead of duplicated. A duplicate `_IDNumber` is refused, naming the other
  character; a duplicate `UIShapeIndex` only logs a note (the stock file has several). Backup once to
  `Character._backup.i3RegXML`, write through a temp file, then re-read: the XML must still parse
  (`ElementTree.fromstring` needs **bytes** - a str with the encoding declaration raises ValueError), every other
  character's block must be unchanged, and the new values must read back. The client reads the packed `.Pef`, not this
  XML, so the user still exports it themselves.
- GUI: rows "6. Nama di game (daftar)" + "Keterangan" (auto-filled, editable), row "7. ID karakter (_IDNumber)" +
  "UIShapeIndex" (auto-filled from `nomor_registry` at startup), three Opsi checkboxes, and a credit badge
  `i3SChara Converter by HeavyRain` bottom right (the user's mock-up). `_langkah()` runs each extra step so a failure
  there leaves the `.I3S` result intact and only logs the reason. Tested 2026-09-18 on scratch copies: helpers, and an
  end-to-end GUI conversion of the four HarvestFarmer LODs (`.I3S` verified, `.I3CHR` scene repointed and verified,
  `Character.txt` +2 lines with the old lines untouched and a backup, `Character.i3RegXML` 127 -> 128 characters with
  every old block unchanged) plus refusals (bad name, duplicate id, non-numeric). `FILE_DAFTAR` and `FILE_REGISTRY` in
  the `.pyw` are the paths the tests patch so the user's real files are never touched. Not tested in game.
  The user converted `Mermaid_Red` with the new build the same evening, which is what added it to their
  `Base String\Character.txt` (and made the backup there).

## OBJ import into `.I3S` -- the user's PB SKD tool (2026-09-18)

The user brings outside models in as OBJ with **`PB SKD - By Skript47`**, and they have its **C# source**:
`D:\My Project\Point Blank Developer Tools\PB SDK Skript47 C# By Hyperion\` (`PB SKD.sln`, `Application\*.cs`,
exe in `Application\bin\Debug`). Right-click a mesh in the mesh list -> Import -> `.obj`/`.pbg`.
Its model: `I3S._block` is a `Dictionary<int, Block>` keyed by 1-based ID = table position, each block holding raw
`data` + `line` (class string index); `CreateI3S()` writes entries in dictionary order, so **ID order = creation
order**. `_geometry` holds one entry per `i3Geometry` with its `geometryAttr`/`vertexArray`/`indexArray` block ids;
`ImportOBJ(g, lines)` overwrites the VA/IA blocks and rewrites the GeometryAttr from those ids.

- **The bug that broke `Apex_Wattson.I3S`** (2026-09-18): when the mesh's `i3VertexArray` is shared with another mesh,
  `Form1.importMenuItem_Click` asks "i3VertexArray N is not unique, do you want create new i3VertexArray?" and on Yes did
  `CreateBlock(1, nLine); _geometry[..].vertexArray = _block.Count;` - the new VA became the **last** block, i.e. after
  the GeometryAttr that uses it (and even after the SGI). The engine creates objects in file order, so
  `i3VertexArrayDX::Lock` fails: **`Asserted : m_pBuffer`** (the user's `i3Viewer2.log` shows exactly that line). Stock
  files never do this: `REBEL_Female`/`Dasom_Red` have 0 GeometryAttr -> later-buffer references, while forward
  `i3AttrSet -> i3Geometry` (21/40) and `i3Node -> i3AttrSet` are normal.
- **Fix in the source** (2026-09-18): new `I3S.CreateVertexArrayForMesh(int g, out string warning)` creates the block at
  the end and then **swaps its content with an `i3Geometry` block that lies before the mesh's GeometryAttr**, repointing
  the owning AttrSet's INF2 kid to the moved geometry (helper `I3S.KidOffset`). No renumbering is needed because the swap
  keeps every ID, and the resulting layout only adds one more normal `AttrSet -> Geometry` forward reference.
  `Form1` now calls it instead of `CreateBlock`. Sources backed up in `_backup_sebelum_perbaikan\`; rebuilt with
  MSBuild (`Application/Win.csproj`, .NET Framework 4.8, x86).
  Headless test (`scratchpad/uji_sdk`, a console project compiling the same SDK sources): importing
  `Desktop\Wattson\Body_LOD1.obj` into a shared-VA mesh of `Chara\Dasom_Astel_Blue` gives block 95 (before
  GeometryAttr 111), 290 -> 291 objects, 0 GeometryAttr -> later buffer, the same forward-reference profile as the
  template, and i3Viewer2 opens the result with no dialog and no log line.
- **Repairing a file that already has the bug**: swap each trailing VA slot with an earlier `i3Geometry` slot and swap the
  two references (GeometryAttr VA id at +9 of the 21-byte attr, AttrSet kid id at INF2+16). Done for
  `HeavyRain\Apex_Wattson_fix.I3S`: same size/object count/string table, LOD vertex counts unchanged
  (48,288 / 105,861 / 93,716 / 54,016), loads clean in i3Viewer2.
- Leftovers in that model, not related to the crash: 11 of 17 VAs are format `0x00000483` (**no blend indices**, so those
  meshes do not follow the skeleton - bind them with `ikat_bone.py`), their VA header f32 +36 is `+1.0` where stock files
  have `-1.0`, and all 16 texture references still point at `Chara/Dasom_Astel_Blue/...`.

## I3R2 format notes (reverse-engineered; the code is the reference)

- New-client files start with a 4-byte **`I3SN`** magic followed by the normal `I3R2` image; every offset inside is
  relative to the `I3R2` start, so dropping the first 4 bytes is all it takes to read them.
- Header is 0xB8 bytes: 0x0C string count, 0x10/0x18 string table offset/size, 0x20/0x24/0x2C object
  count/table offset/table size, 0x34 SGI id, 0x3C 16-byte code.
  **"not checked by the game" was WRONG for `.i3Pack` - corrected 2026-10-01**: for a map's main pack
  `Pack/<Map>.i3Pack` those 16 bytes are the "Encription Code" that `i3ResourceFile::CheckProtectionCode`
  reads, and a zero code kills the match with "Game data file rusak". See "Kode proteksi pack" below.
  For `.I3S`/`.I3CHR` the field still appears to be ignored (every tool here has zeroed it for weeks).
- Strings are `\r\n`-separated and **the table always ends with exactly 2 NUL bytes** (true of every original i3 file;
  the size field includes them). The engine takes the last entry as a C string, so without that padding it reads heap
  garbage past the buffer: `i3ResourceFile.cpp(784) "Unknown Class Meta .(i3AlphaFuncAttr<garbage>)"` and then
  `i3AttrSet::OnLoad` asserts `pAttr != nullptr` and the viewer dies. It only bites when the last string is a class
  name, and it is **non-deterministic** (it depends on the byte that happens to follow the buffer), which is why
  outputs written before 2026-09-12 sometimes loaded. Trailing NULs must be stripped when re-reading (mid-table NULs
  are what assert 0x80000003 in i3BaseDx). Object entry = 28 bytes: class string index, raw id,
  unk, u64 offset, u64 size. Raw id = 1-based id (table index + 1); external objects (textures) set bit 31 and put the
  path's string index in bits 16–30. References inside objects are raw ids.
- Declared sizes are unreliable: `i3NormalMapBindAttr` and `i3ReflectMaskMapBindAttr` write 4 bytes but declare 8
  (the converter writes `[normal][specular]` like V1 files); `i3PhysixShapeSet` has untabled trailing PhysX data.
  Never re-layout base objects; copy the region.
- Chunks: name = u8 length + bytes. `INF2`: flags, child count, pBound (non-zero → 24-byte bbox after the kids), kid ids.
  `ATS1`: count, priority 10, 0, attr ids (mod tools may pad zeros). `GEO2` (65 bytes): VA id @13, IA id @17.
  `VA30` vertex layout: `pos12 nrm12 [color4] uv8 [idx4] [4×weights] [tan12 bin12]` - **format bit 0x08 = a
  4-byte vertex colour right after the normal**, which shifts the blend-index block (`vidx_off()`); Dasom and
  SpiderNatasha use it (fmt 0x0008C4AF / 0x0008C48B).
  `IIA2`: count @4, 24-byte pad, u16 indices @32; the cipher word i3Viewer2 calls pad[0] is at **+20** (0 = plain, high byte 1 = PB 3.68+ type, low byte = key index). i3Viewer2's "Cifrado de la escena" panel decodes that word for you: `pad[0]=0x0000020E` = `cipher_type=2 key_idx=14`
  (it calls them IIA2 (PBM)); its **Cifrado > Quitar IIA2 (strip)** button decrypts and a save then writes plain
  indices - that is how the in-game-tested Dajeong_Red got clean index arrays (max index < vertex count). Dajeong skins and the Harvest_Pitchfork weapon are encrypted, Priest is not; convert() copies index data verbatim and warns. Only trust that field when 32 + 2*count == size (older files use a 12-byte header). **The IIA2 cipher IS the same PBM
  cipher as the `.i3Pack` V2 one** (proved 2026-09-24): harvest key 2:04 with `i3pack.pelajari_v2` and run
  `TabelV2.buka()` over the index bytes at +32 of `IF_S_Dajeong-Red_LOD1.i3s`'s 21,321-index array and the
  max index is 5656 against 5,657 vertices, while that file's five arrays whose keys are not harvested stay
  out of range. So the existing "Learning Encrypted Key" machinery unlocks scene index arrays too - which is
  what an OBJ exporter would need (the user asked about one 2026-09-24; answered, not built). `VA30`: format @4, count @8, descriptor @16..19,
  vertices @40; format 0x24 = tangent+binormal, `(fmt>>14)&7` blend indices, `(fmt>>18)&3` weights; vertex =
  pos12 nrm12 uv8 [idx4] [4×weights] [tan12 bin12]; V1 files have descriptor byte 19 |= 0xC0 (the converter sets it).
  `i3Body`: INF2 + `SKN2` (LOD count @+48, ids @+52). `BLD1` (i3LOD): u64 skeleton/shape/bone-map ids @8/@16/@24.
  `SKT1`: BMA2 id @8, shape-set count @12, ids @48. `BMA2`: bone count @4, matrix-array id @8, 128-byte bone records
  (name[32], depth @112; parent @32 is -1 in V2). `i3MatrixArray`: count + 64-byte inverse bind matrices.
  `SGI1`: root id 16 bytes after the tag.
- Older V1 characters (both bases in `Base Chara/`) use `BMA1` instead of `BMA2` (same layout) and
  an untagged 21-byte i3GeometryAttr (VA id @9, IA id @13). `i3SkinGeometryAttr` = that plus an `SGA1` chunk whose
  i3MemoryBuffer holds a per-submesh bone palette, so its vertex blend indices point into the palette, not the
  skeleton: such files work as `--base` but are rejected as `--skin`/`--part`.
- Headgear part files carry no inverse binds (`i3BoneMatrixListAttr` with matrix-array id 0), so `skeleton_bones`
  returns `inv: None` and `pose_diff` skips those bones; their orientation lives in the bone record's local matrix
  (@+48), which `skeleton_bones` returns as `local`.
- Classes unknown to legacy clients are stripped from AttrSets (`DROP_CLASSES`: `i3ReflectMap*`,
  `i3SpecHighlightsAttr`); `Model_clan` is renamed to V1's `Model_Clan`. i3Viewer2's status bar
  "Cifrado: limpio (sin hits)" means no new classes or index-array cipher were found.

User: "Program I3CHR Editor V3 juga tidak bisa menambahkan cabang baru atau salin cabang baru", with
`SWAT_Female_Emote.I3CHR` and the message *"state Emote di Zombie_Attack memakai event berisi suara -
cabang seperti ini belum bisa disalin"*. That refusal dated from before `i3senjata` decoded the sound
chain and before `i3chr` learned to carry the `SND1` tail; both have existed since 2026-09-22, so the
limit was simply stale. It is now lifted.

An `i3AIState`'s event (`+56`) is an `i3TimeSequence` = name + INF2 + `u32 n` + n x `u32` id of an
`i3TimeSequenceInfo`. Each info is 24 bytes - `f32` when, `f32` length, 0, **`u32` id of the thing to
fire** - and that thing is one of two kinds:

- an **`i3SoundNode`** (internal). Its `.wav` hangs off it as `SND1` -> `i3SoundPlayInfo` -> `+16`
  external `i3Sound`.
- an **external object**, and this is new: the emote file fires effects, e.g.
  `i3SceneGraphInfo` `Effect/H/Emote_Air_Kiss_Heart.i3s`.

`isi_event(t)` returns what a copy must duplicate, in file order - per event
`[i3SoundPlayInfo][i3SoundNode][i3TimeSequenceInfo]` for a sound, just the info for an effect. The
**external objects are shared, never duplicated**: the `.wav` path and the effect scene are the same
resource, and copying an external entry would only add a duplicate string.

`salin_cabang` remaps three more reference slots: the id list inside `i3TimeSequence`, the info's `+12`,
and the `SND1+4` inside a sound node. The copied node carries its 52-byte `SND1` **inside its declared
size** (`_snd1()` reads it from either place), which is the shape `i3senjata.periksa_suara` expects and
the one that avoids the "cannot shoot" bug.

`SWAT_Female_Emote.I3CHR` (the user's own 16-emote file, 116 objects) copies `Zombie_Attack` into 7 new
objects - state, play info, sound node, info, sequence, AI, context - and `Air_Kiss` (effect event) into
5. On `Base I3CHR\SWAT_Female.I3CHR` the branches this used to refuse now copy too:
`Upper > 1PV > Throwing > K-400 > AttackIdle` gives 30 new objects and the file verifies.

`uji_i3chr_cabang.py`: **25 checks** - the sound chain duplicated but the `.wav` shared, `SND1` inside
the copy's size and pointing at the copy's own play info, the original branch byte-identical, the effect
event shared, `tambah_state` on an emote branch, and the editor window driven through "Salin cabang
ini...". Regression: both `Base I3CHR` files still save **byte-identically** with all 37 / 60 `SND1`
tails intact, and an ordinary weapon branch still copies.

### Panel SENJATA akhirnya bisa menyunting penuh (2026-09-28)

User: "saya tidak bisa mengedit i3chr nya secara penuh. kenapa ??" Betul: panel karakter punya
"Tambah state ke cabang ini...", "Salin cabang ini...", dan kotak suara Tambah/Terapkan/Hapus,
sedangkan panel senjata cuma bisa MENYUNTING yang sudah ada - animasi, durasi, blend, dan isi tiap
peristiwa suara. Padahal pustakanya tidak membedakan keduanya: `i3chr.tambah_state`,
`tambah_suara` dan `hapus_suara` semuanya metode `I3CHR`, dan `i3senjata.Senjata` memang membungkus
satu `I3CHR` di `self.c`.

Jadi yang kurang hanya pemasangannya. `PanelSenjata` sekarang punya baris tombol di bawah pohon:

    Tambah state...     -> i3chr.tambah_state(self.s.ai['idx'], nama)
                           saran nama = i3senjata.STATE_V1 yang belum dimiliki file ini
    Tambah suara...     -> i3chr.tambah_suara(state.idx, wav, kapan, panjang)
                           lewat dialog TambahSuara (wav + detik + panjang, koma diterima);
                           saran wav = yang sudah dipakai senjata ini
    Hapus suara         -> i3chr.hapus_suara(state.idx, no), pakai konfirmasi

Yang penting: `Senjata` membaca daftar state sekali di `__init__`, jadi sesudah setiap perubahan
pembungkusnya harus dibuat ulang - `_muat_ulang()` memanggil `i3senjata.Senjata(self.jalur, self.s.c)`
dan **memakai ulang objek `I3CHR` yang sama**, supaya tambalan yang belum disimpan tidak hilang.

**Hapus state sudah ada sejak 2026-09-30** - lihat bagian berikutnya. Catatan lama di sini
("belum ada primitifnya") sudah tidak berlaku.

`uji_i3chr_senjata_penuh.py`: **19 pemeriksaan** - sisi pustaka (tambah state, tambah suara dengan
detik/panjangnya, hapus lagi, simpan + baca ulang, `periksa_suara` tetap lolos) dan jendelanya
digerakkan in-process (ketiga tombol ada, state baru muncul di pohon, suara bertambah lalu terhapus,
dan menekan Hapus tanpa memilih baris memberi pesan alih-alih meledak). Regresi `uji_i3chr_cabang.py`

### Hapus state -- yang dibuang keanggotaannya, bukan objeknya (2026-09-30)

User: "tambahkan untuk hapus state seperti UI_IdleB atau UI_IdleA. disana belum ada fitur hapus".

**Objeknya TIDAK dicabut dari tabel**, dan itu bukan jalan pintas: nomor objek di `.I3CHR` adalah
posisinya di tabel (raw id = indeks + 1) dan setiap rujukan memakai nomor itu, jadi membuang satu
baris akan menggeser ribuan rujukan lain. Yang dihapus adalah keanggotaannya di daftar id milik
`i3AI`.

Bentuk hasilnya sah karena berkas bawaan sudah memakainya - diukur, bukan diduga:

- **`SWAT_Female.I3CHR` punya 358 `i3AIState` yang tidak ada di daftar AI mana pun** (state
  penolong `Idle` milik `Change`), `SWAT_Male` 360. Jadi state yatim adalah bentuk bawaan.
- **525 dari 1.291 `i3AI` bawaan memang berisi 0 state** (simpul pengelompok `Lower`, `Upper`,
  `1PV`, `ShotGun`, `870MCS`), dan `ai_list()` sepakat dengan `_ai_info()` di ke-1.291 AI - jadi
  daftar yang mengecil tidak merusak pembacaan.
- Tidak ada satu pun state yang terdaftar di **lebih dari satu** AI (0 dari 16.135), jadi membuang
  dari satu daftar selalu berarti state itu benar-benar lepas.

`I3CHR.hapus_state(state_idx, ai_idx=None, putus_lanjut=True)` -> `{nama, ai_idx, pos, sisa, putus}`:

- membuang id state dari daftar `i3AI`; urutan id yang lain tidak bergeser;
- **mengosongkan tautan `+48` ("state berikutnya") dari state yang MASIH terdaftar** ke state yang
  dibuang - kalau tidak, state yang katanya sudah dihapus tetap diputar sesudah state itu. Tautan
  milik state yatim sengaja dibiarkan supaya pasangan bawaan `Change -> Idle` tidak ikut terusik.
  Ukurannya di `SWAT_Female`: **112 tautan `+48` menunjuk state SE-AI** (110 `UI_IdleB -> UI_IdleA`,
  2 `JumpEnd -> Idle`) dan **358 menunjuk state di luar daftar**;
- menolak state terakhir sebuah AI ("satu-satunya state di cabang ini");
- rantai suaranya (`+56`) dan animasinya ikut jadi yatim bersama state-nya; tidak ada objek lain
  yang menunjuk mereka. `pemilik_state(idx)` melaporkan AI mana saja yang masih memuatnya.

GUI: **"Hapus state ini"** di panel KARAKTER (baris tombol di bawah pohon AI; butuh satu baris STATE
yang dipilih, bukan nama cabangnya) dan **"Hapus state"** di panel SENJATA. Keduanya memakai
konfirmasi yang menyebutkan bahwa objeknya tetap ada di berkas. CLI: `--hapus-state JALUR NAMA`,
mis. `--hapus-state "Upper>1PV>ShotGun>870MCS>AttackIdle" UI_IdleB`.

Catatan ukuran: karena objek `i3AI` justru MENGECIL 4 byte, `simpan()` menulisnya di tempat dan
berkas hasilnya tetap 4.250.618 byte - sama persis dengan aslinya.

`uji_i3chr_hapus_state.py`: **45 pemeriksaan** - hapus state bawaan (hilang dari daftar, jumlah objek
tetap, objeknya tetap `i3AIState`), tautan `+48` diputus sementara `Change -> Idle` tidak tersentuh,
tambah lalu hapus lagi mengembalikan daftar id **persis** seperti semula, simpan + baca ulang dengan
**37/37 chunk SND1 selamat**, empat penolakan, berkas senjata (`Senjata` dibaca ulang, driver utuh,
`periksa_suara` lolos), dan **kedua panel jendelanya digerakkan in-process** (tombolnya ada, barisnya
hilang dari pohon, jawab "Tidak" tidak menghapus apa pun, memilih baris cabang atau tanpa pilihan
memberi pesan alih-alih meledak). Regresi: `uji_i3chr_cabang.py` 25, `uji_i3chr_senjata_penuh.py` 19,
dan simpan-tanpa-ubah tetap **byte-identik** untuk kedua `Base I3CHR`.

Exe dibangun ulang 2026-09-30: `I3CHR Editor V3.exe` **9.292.853 byte** dan - karena membundel
salinan `i3chr`-nya sendiri - `I3Tools V3.exe` **23.959.090 byte** (uji exe-nya 7 dan 21 pemeriksaan
di folder tanpa satu pun `.py`). Yang lama ada di `_backup_sebelum_hapus_state\`.

**Belum ada: mengganti NAMA state.** Nama tersimpan sebagai `u8 panjang + teks` di depan chunk
`AIS1`, jadi mengubahnya menggeser seluruh isi state itu dan `_nama()` - yang membaca `o.data`, bukan
daftar tambalan - akan memberi offset yang salah untuk objek yang sudah ditambal. Belum dikerjakan.

### Menyunting rantai suara dari panel KARAKTER (2026-09-27)

User: "saya mau tambah path sound nya ... di program nya belum ada tambah path suara".
Berkas emote (`SWAT_Female_Emote.I3CHR`, 20 AI) terdeteksi sebagai KARAKTER, dan panel
karakter dulu tidak punya medan suara sama sekali - rantai suara hanya bisa disunting lewat
`i3senjata.Senjata`, yang menolak file dengan lebih dari 1 AI. Jadi emote tidak bisa disentuh.

API-nya sekarang ada di `i3chr.I3CHR` supaya kedua panel bisa memakainya:

- `suara_state(state_idx)` -> `[{no, kapan, panjang, node, wav, efek, idx_info, idx_node,
  idx_spi, idx_suara}]`. `efek` terisi kalau peristiwanya memanggil objek eksternal
  (mis. `Effect/H/Emote_Air_Kiss_Heart.i3s`) dan bukan `i3SoundNode`.
- `objek_suara(path)` - pakai ulang / buat `i3Sound` eksternal. Lewat `_buat_eksternal(kelas, path)`
  yang sekarang dipakai bersama `i3Animation` (bentuknya sama: entri tabel + satu string, ukuran 0).
- `set_wav_state(state_idx, no, path, kapan=, panjang=)` - ganti path SATU peristiwa.
- `tambah_suara(state_idx, path, kapan, panjang)` - bikin rantai baru; membuatkan `i3TimeSequence`
  juga kalau state-nya belum punya (dan menulis id-nya ke `+56` state).
- `set_waktu_suara`, `set_nama_suara`, `hapus_suara`, `pemakai_suara(idx_suara)`.

**Kenapa satu peristiwa bisa diganti tanpa mengganggu yang lain**: objek `i3Sound` memang dipakai
bersama - di `SWAT_Female_Emote.I3CHR` keempat state Zombie_Attack / HipHop / Gangnam_Luna /
Dance_Felipe menunjuk raw id `0x80390069` yang sama (sisa `salin_cabang`, yang menggandakan
`i3SoundPlayInfo` + `i3SoundNode` tapi BERBAGI `.wav`). Karena tiap peristiwa punya
`i3SoundPlayInfo` sendiri, `set_wav_state` cukup menulis ulang `+16` di play info milik
peristiwa itu. `i3senjata.set_wav` sengaja tetap berperilaku lama (mengubah semua pemakai),
karena untuk senjata itu justru yang diinginkan.

Cetakan objek baru (diukur dari berkas bawaan, `SPI_CETAKAN` di `i3chr.py`):

    i3SoundPlayInfo  136 byte, tanpa nama, 'SPI1' ... +16 = raw id EKSTERNAL i3Sound
    i3SoundNode      u8 len + nama (= nama dasar .wav) + 'INF2' + 12 nol
                     + 'SND1' + u32 id play info + 44 nol   <- DI DALAM data objeknya
    i3TimeSequenceInfo  24 byte: f32 kapan, f32 panjang, u32 0, u32 id node, 8 nol
    i3TimeSequence   u8 0 (nama kosong) + 'INF2' + 12 nol + u32 jumlah + id tiap info

Objek dibuat berurutan **[i3SoundPlayInfo][i3SoundNode][i3TimeSequenceInfo]** - `i3senjata.
_baca_peristiwa` memang memeriksa ketiganya berurutan dan menolak file yang tidak begitu.

**`periksa()` dulu mematok kelas**: `for idx in asli.baru` membandingkan dengan `'i3Animation'`,
jadi `i3Sound` baru selalu ditolak ("animasi baru ... tidak tertulis benar"). Sekarang
dibandingkan dengan kelas objek aslinya.

GUI: panel karakter dapat kotak **"Suara di state terpilih"** (daftar Detik / Panjang /
File .wav, isian File .wav + Detik + Panjang, tombol Tambah / Terapkan / Hapus). Ditaruh di
baris sendiri selebar jendela - waktu ditumpuk di dalam kotak "State terpilih" tombolnya
