### URUTAN OBJEK rantai suara -- satu-satunya aturan yang tidak boleh dilanggar (2026-09-30)

Log client user, sesudah menambahkan suara ke `UI_IdleA` lewat alat ini::

    i3ResourceFile::LoadHeader : Chara/Harvest_ViperRed/Harvest_ViperRed.I3CHR
    m_StringTableSize : 271286
    i3TimeSequence::AddSequence : Asserted : pNode != NULL
    i3Node::AddChild            : Asserted : pChild != NULL

**Engine membuat objek BERURUTAN TABEL.** `i3TimeSequence::OnLoad` mencari tiap
`i3TimeSequenceInfo`-nya lewat nomor objek, dan objek yang letaknya di BELAKANGNYA belum ada -
jadi `pNode` NULL dan seluruh `.I3CHR` ditolak. Ini keluarga yang sama dengan jebakan
`i3VertexArrayDX::Lock Asserted : m_pBuffer` di scene.

Diukur di berkas bawaan - **0 dari 100 peristiwa** pernah terbalik:

| | peristiwa | info di depan urutannya | jarak |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SWAT_Female.I3CHR` | 37 | 37/37 | tepat 1 objek |
| `SWAT_Male.I3CHR` | 60 | 60/60 | tepat 1 objek |
| `BB_P90_Ext_Bike.I3CHR` | 3 | 3/3 | 1..9 objek |

Jadi urutan wajibnya `[i3SoundPlayInfo][i3SoundNode][i3TimeSequenceInfo][i3TimeSequence]`.

**Yang TIDAK termasuk pelanggaran**: `i3AIState` -> `i3TimeSequence` di belakangnya. Itu justru
bentuk bawaan - 876 kali di `SWAT_Female`, selalu 1-6 objek sesudah state-nya. Sama seperti
state -> animasi di belakangnya (4385 kali). Rupanya hanya `i3TimeSequence` yang menyelesaikan
rujukannya saat OnLoad.

**Bug yang bikin ini terjadi**: `tambah_suara` (fitur 27/09/2026) memanggil
`urutan_state(state_idx, buat=True)` LEBIH DULU - yang membuat `i3TimeSequence` di ujung tabel -
lalu menempel ketiga objek isinya di belakangnya. Untuk state yang sudah punya urutan hasilnya
sama buruknya: urutannya ada di awal berkas, info barunya di ujung. `salin_cabang` tidak kena
(`rencana_salin` memang menulis `isi_event(t)` dulu baru `masuk('i3TimeSequence', t)`).

Perbaikannya, dan kenapa begitu:

- keempat objek selalu dibuat **berurutan di ujung tabel**;
- state yang SUDAH punya urutan pun dibuatkan `i3TimeSequence` **baru** berisi daftar peristiwa
  lama + yang baru, lalu `+56` state diarahkan ke sana. Nomor objek tidak boleh bergeser, jadi
  menyelipkan objek di depan urutan lama mustahil - dan `state -> urutan di belakangnya` memang
  sah (lihat tabel di atas). Urutan lamanya ditinggal jadi yatim.

**`perbaiki_urutan()`** menyelamatkan berkas yang terlanjur rusak: urutannya dibuat ulang di ujung
tabel, setiap state yang memakainya diarahkan ulang, dan **daftar urutan yang lama DIKOSONGKAN** -
bukan sekadar ditinggalkan. Ini salah dulu sekali: engine membuat SEMUA objek di tabel, termasuk
yang tidak dirujuk siapa pun, jadi `AddSequence` tetap dipanggil untuk objek yatim dan assert-nya
tetap meledak. `simpan()` sekarang **menolak** menulis berkas yang masih punya rujukan mundur
(lewat `urutan_salah()` di dalam `periksa()`), dan jendelanya menawarkan perbaikan begitu berkas
semacam itu dibuka. CLI: `--perbaiki-urutan`.

Berkas user (`D:\Data C\BlacklistPB\Chara\Harvest_ViperRed\Harvest_ViperRed.I3CHR`) diperbaiki
di tempat 30/09/2026 - 24.459 -> 24.460 objek, 4.251.733 byte, cadangan sekali di
`Harvest_ViperRed._backup_urutan.I3CHR`. Isinya: `UI_IdleA` (#23462) memanggil
`Sound/Emotion/WM_SalsaDance.wav` di detik 0,000.

**IN-GAME CONFIRMED 30/09/2026** (user: "Oke sudah bisa"): sesudah urutannya dibetulkan client
menerima berkasnya - tidak ada lagi `AddSequence : pNode != NULL`. Yang terbukti di sini adalah
berkasnya DIMUAT; apakah wav-nya benar-benar berbunyi di layar Info Detail belum dilaporkan
terpisah.

`uji_i3chr_urutan_suara.py`: **36 pemeriksaan** - lima berkas bawaan bersih, `tambah_suara` ke state
yang belum punya urutan dan yang sudah punya, simpan + baca ulang dengan 37/37 SND1 selamat,
penjaga menolak berkas rusak dengan pesan client yang sebenarnya, `perbaiki_urutan` (termasuk daftar
lama benar-benar kosong), simpan-tanpa-ubah byte-identik, dan jendelanya digerakkan in-process untuk
kedua jawaban Ya/Tidak.

**Pelajarannya, dan ini yang ketiga kalinya di proyek ini**: uji Python yang membaca ulang berkasnya
sendiri TIDAK bisa menangkap pelanggaran urutan - berkasnya terbaca sempurna, cuma client yang
menolak. Setiap kali alat ini membuat objek yang dirujuk objek lain, tanyakan dulu: **siapa
menunjuk siapa, dan siapa lahir duluan?**

### `.I3CHR` senjata V1 lama memakai bentuk raw-id eksternal LAMA (2026-09-27)

`set_scene` pada `Weapon/P90_Ext/P90_Ext.I3CHR` mati dengan `IndexError` di `_set_ext`. Sebabnya
berkas itu memakai bentuk raw id eksternal yang lama - bentuk yang sudah tercatat di file ini untuk
`.i3WRD` dan scene golem, tapi belum ditangani `i3chr.py`:

    0xFFFF0000 | nomor_string          bentuk LAMA  (nomor objek disiratkan dari posisi tabel)
    bit31 | nomor_string<<16 | id      bentuk BARU

`pindah_bone.I3R2` sudah membaca keduanya (baris 140-145), jadi `o.ext` benar; yang salah cuma
`_set_ext`, yang menghitung `si = (raw >> 16) & 0x7FFF` -> 0x7FFF untuk `0xFFFF0001`. Akibatnya
**setiap `.I3CHR` senjata V1 lama tidak bisa diganti scene-nya**, termasuk dipakai sebagai `dasar`
oleh `i3senjata.konversi()`.

Penolong `_si_ext(raw)` sekarang mengenali kedua bentuk dan dipakai di `_set_ext`, di pencarian
pemakai string, dan di penandaan string terpakai oleh `set_nama`; `_raw_id_baru` **mempertahankan
bentuk lama** (`0xFFFF0000 | si`) kalau objeknya memang bentuk lama, jadi berkas tidak berpindah
bentuk diam-diam.

Regresi: simpan-tanpa-ubah tetap **byte-identik** untuk `Base I3CHR\SWAT_Female.I3CHR` (4.250.618 B),
`SWAT_Male.I3CHR` (4.219.525 B), `P90_Ext.I3CHR` dan `BB_P90_Ext_Bike.I3CHR` - 4 dari 4.
Berkas lama di `_backup_sebelum_ext_lama\i3chr.py`.

## `.i3AnimPack` (APF3) notes -- `i3anim.py`

Kumpulan animasi karakter/senjata. Header 0xA4: `0x04` jumlah animasi, **`0x08` jumlah kunci posisi**,
**`0x0C` jumlah kunci rotasi**, `0x14` awal wilayah data (= `0xA4 + jumlah*284`), `0x1C` ukuran wilayah data.
Tabel isi 284 byte/baris: u32 tipe (1 = penuh, 3 = badan atas), u64 jumlah trek, **u64 offset RELATIF terhadap
`0x14`**, `char[264]` nama virtual (`chara/swat_female/1pv/.../Reload_A.i3a`).

Wilayah data = **kolam kunci** lalu **deskriptor tiap animasi** (urut offset):

- Kolam kunci di awal wilayah data, **lima kelompok berurutan**: posisi penuh 12B (jumlah di header 0x08), rotasi
  penuh 16B (0x0C), skala 12B (jumlahnya **tidak dicatat** -- `_siapkan_kolam()` menghitungnya dari sisa kolam),
  posisi mampat 6B = 3 fp16 (0x24), rotasi mampat 8B = 4 fp16 (0x28). Trek dengan bendera **`0x80`** mengambil
  kunci dari kelompok mampat, bukan yang penuh -- itulah yang dulu bikin paket `Chara_*_Throw_*` dan senjata melee
  ditolak. Totalnya harus persis sama dengan `min(offset)`; itu ujinya (748 dari ~785 paket APF3 lolos).
  **Kunci dipakai bersama**: satu kunci bisa ditunjuk banyak trek dan banyak animasi, jadi kolamnya jauh lebih
  kecil dari jumlah kunci semua animasi (Assault: 63.052 kunci unik untuk 6.202 trek).
- Deskriptor satu animasi = `trek*36` tabel nama (u32 + `char[32]` nama tulang Biped: `IK`, `Spine1`, `R Hand`...)
  + `trek*72` rekaman + tabel telunjuk (daftar u32 nomor kunci di kolam, panjangnya berubah-ubah).
- Rekaman 72 byte = `i3TransformSequence` hasil dump memori: `+0x00` u32 bendera kanal, `+0x04` u32 jumlah kunci,
  `+0x08` f32 jarak waktu antar kunci (0 = tidak tetap), `+0x0C/+0x10/+0x14/+0x18` penunjuk memori tiap kanal
  (sampah runtime, abaikan), `+0x20` f32 durasi detik.
- **Bendera kanal** -- nibble bawah = kanal yang dipakai, bit atas = kanal itu *tetap* (menulis 1 nilai saja walau
  kuncinya banyak): `0x01` posisi (tetap kalau `0x10`), `0x02` rotasi (tetap kalau `0x20`), `0x04` skala
  (tetap kalau `0x40`), `0x08` waktu tiap kunci. **`0x80` = kuncinya dari kolam mampat** (tidak mengubah panjang
  tabel telunjuk, cuma kelompok kolam yang dibaca).
- **Tabel telunjuk** = per trek, berurut kanal, `panjang_kanal()` u32 tiap kanal. Kanal posisi/rotasi berisi nomor
  kunci di kolam; kanal waktu berisi f32 detik (bukan nomor). Rumus ini **cocok untuk 19.995 animasi di 778 paket,
  tanpa satu pun meleset** -- itu ujinya kalau susunan rekaman diubah.

Akibat praktisnya: `kunci()` mengembalikan isi animasi sebenarnya (waktu + posisi + quaternion tiap trek).
Menyalin animasi di dalam paket yang sama = salin blok deskriptornya. Antar paket, `salin_dari()` memetakan ulang
nomor kuncinya: tiap kunci dicari di kolam tujuan, kalau belum ada ditambahkan **di belakang kelompoknya**
(`kolam_baru()`), lalu `n_pos`/`n_rot` di header diperbarui -- dengan begitu semua nomor kunci lama tetap sah.
`simpan()` menulis kolam lalu deskriptor berurutan tanpa lubang: ukuran deskriptor tidak dicatat di tabel,
dihitung dari jarak ke offset berikutnya, jadi lubang akan merusak tetangganya.

**In-game confirmed 2026-09-12** on the BlacklistPB client, both by the user: (1) swapping `Reload_A` with
`Reload_B` inside `Chara_SWAT_Female_Assault.i3AnimPack` changed the AK-47 reload motion, other weapons unaffected;
(2) copying `Attack_A` from `Chara_SWAT_Female_Mars_Saber.i3AnimPack` onto that same slot **across packs** - the
AK-47 reload plays the sword swing. So the relative-offset layout, the channel-flag model and the key remapping
are all correct against the real engine, not just against the reader. `--durasi` matters: a copied animation keeps
its own duration and looks wrong until it is retimed to the destination slot's duration.

`ekspor_i3a()` menulis satu animasi sebagai **`.i3a` mandiri**: I3R2 biasa berisi satu `i3TransformSequence` per
trek plus satu `i3Animation` sebagai objek akar (id di header 0x34). Susunan sequence = `u8 panjang + nama`, header
18 byte (`u16 2`, u8 bendera kanal, `01 01 01`, u32 0, u32 jumlah kunci, u32 0), f32 durasi, lalu array tiap kanal
berurut posisi/rotasi/skala/waktu. **Loader `.i3a` mengabaikan bendera kanal itu dan selalu membaca keempat
array sebanyak jumlah kunci** -- menulis lebih sedikit (mis. bendera 0x0E untuk trek tanpa posisi) bikin engine
membaca offset yang salah: `i3Skeleton::Traverse` mengeluh "Invalid value of matrix in Skeleton Bone (Root)" plus
`i3Math::div Asserted : val2`, dan animasinya cuma bergerak sedikit (dialami user 2026-09-13). Jadi ekspor selalu
menulis bendera `0x0F` dan mengisi kanal yang tidak ada di paket: **posisi diambil dari posisi bind skeleton**
(`posisi_bind()` membaca `.I3S`, baris terakhir matrix lokal tulang @+48), waktu dihitung dari `+0x08` atau dibagi
rata sepanjang durasi, skala selalu (1,1,1). Tanpa `--skeleton` posisinya jadi (0,0,0) dan model rusak. `i3Animation` = `u8 0 + u32 jumlah + (u32 id + char[32]
nama)` tiap sequence; ukurannya persis `5 + 36*jumlah`. Diuji dengan membongkar-pasang ulang 77 sequence di
`Effect/H/*.i3a`: identik byte-per-byte. Kunci yang di paket disimpan sekali (kanal tetap) diulang sebanyak jumlah
kunci, dan skala selalu ditulis identitas (1,1,1) seperti file bawaan. **Confirmed 2026-09-13**: i3Viewer2 memuat `.i3a` lepas lewat
kotak Animation di panel i3Body, dan `Idle_Stand.i3a` hasil ekspor (dari
`Chara_SWAT_Male_Baseball_Bat.i3AnimPack` + `Chou_Mermaid.I3S`) berjalan mulus tanpa satu pun baris di
`i3Viewer2.log`. Jadi rute paket -> `.i3a` mandiri sudah lengkap dan terbukti.

**Idle lobby yang "tegang" (2026-09-13, Saiga_BlackTortoise)**: bukan file rusak dan bukan paket animasi. Layar
Info Detail memutar state `UI_IdleA`/`UI_IdleB` di context `Upper > 3PV > <kelas> > <senjata> > AttackIdle` milik
`.I3CHR`. Untuk `Saiga` dan `Saiga_BlackTortoise` kedua state itu ada tapi **kosong** (rujukan animasi 0, panjang
path 0), jadi karakter diam di pose terakhir. Uji game user: mengganti gerakan `UI/Idle_Stand` di paket Saiga_BT
tidak berpengaruh sama sekali - itu yang membuktikan layarnya tidak memakai `Idle_Stand`. Perbaikannya: salin utuh
byte state `UI_IdleA`/`UI_IdleB` milik 870MCS (#12188/#12190, menunjuk `SHOTGUN/UI/UI_IDLEA.I3A` dan
`UI_IDLEB.I3A`, blend 0,3) ke state kosong Saiga_BT (#12846/#12847) -> `Uji I3CHR Saiga/SWAT_Female.I3CHR`.
**In-game confirmed 2026-09-13**: karakter bergerak di Info Detail sambil memegang Saiga_BT. Artinya **engine
mencari animasi lewat path di semua paket** - animasinya tetap ditemukan di `Chara_SWAT_Female_ShotGun.i3AnimPack`
walau senjata yang dipegang punya paket sendiri. Catatan `--salin`: `UI_IdleA/B`
shotgun punya 63 trek (+`Pivot`) sedangkan paket Saiga_BT 62, jadi jalur paket tidak bisa dipakai untuk itu.

`cek_kolam()` menolak paket yang ukuran kolamnya tidak sama dengan jumlah kelima kelompok (sekitar 37 paket APF3
tersisa, pola selisihnya kecil seperti 54 byte -- belum dipecahkan). Membaca daftar, menukar animasi sepaket, dan
mengubah durasi tetap jalan di semua paket APF3.

Magic `APF1`/`APF2`/`APF3` **wadahnya sama persis** - tabel isi 284 byte, offset relatif, kolam lima kelompok -
jadi ketiganya dibaca dengan kode yang sama (dicek 2026-09-13 dengan `KrissSuperV.i3AnimPack`, APF1, yang lolos
penuh; header 0x10 di situ berisi jumlah kunci skala, cocok dengan yang dihitung `_siapkan_kolam()` dari sisa).
Cakupan sekarang: **APF1 108/108 lengkap, APF3 748/784, APF2 cuma 2/93** (yang lain tabel telunjuknya meleset -
pola APF2 belum dipecahkan). `.i3a` mandiri (mis. `Effect/H/DTown_Boss_Door.i3a`)
bukan APF3 melainkan **I3R2 biasa** berisi objek `i3TransformSequence` + `i3Animation`; satu sequence =
`u8 panjang + nama`, header 18 byte (u32 jumlah kunci @+10), f32 durasi, lalu `N*float3` posisi, `N*float4` rotasi,
`N*float3` skala, `N*float` waktu (44 byte per kunci).


## Weapon `.I3CHR` -- `i3senjata.py` + `I3CHR Weapon Editor V3` (2026-09-22)

User: "Buatkan saya alat untuk mengedit I3CHR untuk weapon ... BB_PinkDragon.I3CHR yang dari V3 ...
sinkronisasi animasinya tidak tepat untuk V1 ... ambil animasi, sound, idle, load animasi ... tapi saya
tetap menggunakan file AKS74U.I3CHR". The **ninth tool**. Samples: `Weapon\Aks74u\AKS74U.I3CHR` (V1,
86 objects, 11 states) and `Weapon\BB_PinkDragon\BB_PinkDragon.I3CHR` (V3, 98 objects, 17 states),
both driver `AIDriverMasterGun_Type`, plus their `.i3AnimPack`s.

A weapon `.I3CHR` is the same I3R2 container as a character's but tiny: **one** `i3AIContext`, one `i3AI`,
11-17 `i3AIState`. What characters do not have is the **sound chain** hanging off `i3AIState+56`, which
`i3chr.py` deliberately refuses (`rencana_salin` rejects branches whose time sequences reach `i3SoundNode`).
Decoded here:

- `i3TimeSequence` = name + `INF2` (no kids) + `u32 n` + n x `u32` raw id of `i3TimeSequenceInfo`.
  The empty one is 21 bytes (n = 0), a 3-sound one is 33.
- `i3TimeSequenceInfo` = **24 bytes, no name**: `+0 f32` WHEN the sound fires (seconds into the state),
  `+4 f32` the sound's own length, `+8` 0, `+12 u32` raw id of `i3SoundNode`, `+16`/`+20` 0.
- `i3SoundNode` = name (always the `.wav` basename) + `INF2`, and **no reference at all**.
- `i3SoundPlayInfo` = 136 bytes, no name, starts `SPI1`; **`+16` is an EXTERNAL raw id** (bit 31 set,
  string index in bits 16-30) pointing at the `i3Sound` that carries the `.wav` path. Rest is volume 100,
  3.0 / 50.0 distances, pitch 1.0, 360/360 cone, `ffffffff`.
- `i3Sound` = external object, size 0, ext = the `.wav` path.

Because `i3SoundNode` stores no id, its `i3SoundPlayInfo` is found **by order**: every event is three
consecutive objects `[i3SoundPlayInfo][i3SoundNode][i3TimeSequenceInfo]`. `_baca_peristiwa` checks that and
refuses a file that breaks it rather than guessing. **One `i3Sound` is shared by many events** - a weapon has
3 wavs (remove/load/reload) for 18 events - so `set_wav` changes every event using it and renames all their
`i3SoundNode`s too; it returns how many, and the GUI says so.

Writing goes through `i3chr.I3CHR`, so `simpan()` is the proven path: strings + object table rebuilt, objects
that grow move to the tail, **no object id ever shifts**, then the result is re-read and compared.

**Why the V3 file was out of sync in V1** - three separate things, all visible in the decoded data:

| | AKS74U (V1) | BB_PinkDragon (V3) |
|---|---|---|
| states | 11 | 17 (extra Change1PV/3PV, Fire/Idle 1PV/3PV_Zoom) |
| reload Master | **2.000 s** | 2.500 s |
| reload animation | 6 different `.i3a` (Female/Male x 1PV/3PV + Master) from `AK-47_DualMag` | one `Reload.i3a` for all six |
| sound order in a reload | 0.398 remove, 1.196 **load**, 1.992 **reload** | 0.000 remove, 0.855 **reload**, 1.880 **load** |

The `_Load` / `_Reload` names are **swapped between the two builds**, so matching sounds by file name puts the
cocking sound at the magazine-insert moment. `konversi()` therefore defaults to `cocok_suara='urutan'`
(pair them by time order, which preserves "which sound at which moment"); `'nama'` is the other option.

`konversi(dasar, donor, out, nama, scene, durasi, cocok_suara)`: state list, flags, speed, blend and the
per-event times stay from the **dasar** (the V1 skeleton); animation paths, wav paths and wav lengths come
from the **donor**. Missing donor states fall back through `CADANGAN` (e.g. `LoadMagMaster1PV` <- `LoadMag1PVMale`).
`durasi='pintar'` (default) keeps the base's seconds for `LoadMag*` (they must match the V1 character's hands)
and takes the donor's for everything else - V1 files often have Fire/Idle at 0.033 s (one frame, the weapon
does not move), which would be wrong on a weapon that has a real idle. Existing `i3Animation` objects are
**repointed** instead of new ones being appended, so the result has the same 86 objects and no orphan still
naming the base weapon.

What it cannot fix: the engine plays an animation for its **own** length; `+44` is only a copy. So a 2.0 s
Master state pointing at a 2.5 s `Reload.i3a` is still 0.5 s out. `periksa_durasi()` reads the weapon's
`.i3AnimPack` (through `i3anim`) and reports exactly that; the GUI marks those rows red. Fixing it means
retiming the animation in **I3Anim Editor V3**.

- `i3senjata.py` - `Senjata` (read/edit), `konversi()`, CLI (`--donor --out --nama --scene --durasi
  --cocok-suara`; with no `--donor` it just prints the file).
- `I3CHR Weapon Editor V3.pyw` - tree of states with their sounds as children, edit panel (animation,
  duration, blend / wav, when, length), weapon name + scene, "Periksa durasi", and "Konversi dari senjata
  lain..." which fills name/scene/output from the donor automatically.
- Tests: `scratchpad/uji_senjata/uji_senjata.py` (8 groups: parsing both files, unchanged save byte-identical
  for both, every editor writing survives a save+reload, the conversion's state list/animations/sounds/object
  count/durations, both sound-matching modes, both duration modes, the `.i3AnimPack` check finding exactly the
  two Master mismatches, and a character `.I3CHR` being refused with a useful message) and
  `scratchpad/uji_senjata/uji_gui.py` (window driven in-process: tree fills 17 states + 20 sounds, edit panel,
  a duration typed with a **comma** applied, red marking, sound row edit, save + reload, the conversion dialog
  auto-fill and its refusal to overwrite the base). All pass.
### One editor for both -- the merge (2026-09-22)

User: "Apakah anda bisa menggabungkan I3CHR Editor ini ?? Karena sama-sama format chr, untuk
senjata dan charakter pun bisa di edit i3chr nya". Done: `I3CHR Editor V3.pyw` is now one
window for both. Originals in `_backup_sebelum_gabung\` (both `.pyw`, `i3chr.py`,
`i3senjata.py`, `README.md`).

- `kenali(path)` reads the file **once** with `i3chr.I3CHR` and hands that object to
  `i3senjata.Senjata(path, chr_)` when `len(ai_list()) == 1`, so a 4 MB character file is not
  parsed twice. A 1-AI file whose sound chain will not parse falls back to character mode with a
  note in the log instead of an error.
- Both old `App(tk.Tk)` classes became `ttk.Frame`s (`PanelKarakter`, `PanelSenjata`) inside one
  `App`. They are created lazily and hidden with `grid_remove`, never destroyed, so switching
  between a character and a weapon keeps each panel's log and state. The file row + the
  bold KARAKTER/SENJATA line live in the `App`; everything else is the proven code unchanged.
  `tk.Toplevel(frame)` and `frame.wait_window()` work exactly as before (test 10 covers it).
- **The real reason this is worth doing**: the character editor used to open a weapon file happily
  and then save it through `i3chr.simpan()`, which drops the untabled `SND1` chunk - the bug that
  made BB_PinkDragon unable to shoot. So the tail-carrying moved **from `i3senjata.Senjata` into
  `i3chr.I3CHR`**: `_hitung_ekor()` is now a method of `I3CHR`, `simpan()` folds each tail into
  `self.patch` before laying the file out, and `periksa()` additionally requires every
  `i3SoundNode` that had a tail to still have it. `Senjata._ekor` is a property onto `self.c.ekor`.
  `simpan()` must mutate `self.patch` (not a local copy): `periksa()` compares `asli.patch` against
  what was written, and after the fold the written object legitimately includes the 52 bytes.
- **Character files have 37 such nodes** (`Base I3CHR\SWAT_Female\SWAT_Female.I3CHR`; the
  Throwing / HK45 dual / Bow branches), so the character editor had the identical latent bug.
  Proved by running the pre-fix `i3chr.py` from the backup: renaming one `i3SoundNode` longer and
  saving loses its chunk. With the fix all 37 survive.
- **Bug found while testing the merge**: an EXTERNAL object (`size == 0`, e.g. `i3Animation` /
  `i3Sound`) carries **another object's offset**, so including them when computing "where does the
  next object start" can put the boundary at the current object's own offset. `periksa_suara` then
  died with `IndexError` and, worse, `_hitung_ekor` silently recorded **no tail** - the SND1 bug
  would have come back. It only shows up once a new `i3Animation` is appended (its offset landed on
  an `i3SoundNode`'s). Both now filter on `if o.size`. No file delivered so far is affected
  (`_hasil_V1/BB_PinkDragon.I3CHR` patches only `i3AIState`, and the converted file was verified at
  18/18 nodes).
- Smaller fixes that came out of the GUI test: `PanelSenjata.isi_pohon()` now restores the selected
  row (pressing Terapkan rebuilt the tree and emptied the edit panel, so two edits in a row needed
  a re-click); the weapon panel gained **"Pilih..."** next to the animation field (pick an animation
  plus its true duration from the weapon's own `.i3AnimPack` - the character panel always had this,
  and it is the direct cure for the duration mismatch the tool warns about) and its own
  **Simpan** / **Simpan sebagai...** buttons; the log got `width=52` and the tree columns were
  trimmed, because `ScrolledText`'s default 80 characters pushed Kecepatan/Blend/Ulang out of view.
- **The `.exe` was rebuilt** (PyInstaller 6.22.2 in `scratchpad/venv_build`, hidden imports
  `i3chr i3senjata i3anim pindah_bone`, 9.25 MB). Smoke-tested by
  `scratchpad/uji_gabung/uji_exe.py` in a folder holding **no `.py` files at all**, so the bundle is
  proven self-contained: CLI mode, then the window opened on a weapon and on a character, captured
  with PrintWindow and closed with `WM_CLOSE`. Note that PyInstaller's FrozenImporter wins over
  `sys.path`, so the exe uses its BUNDLED modules even when the `.py` files sit next to it -
  editing `i3chr.py` only affects the `.pyw` until the exe is rebuilt.
- **`if sys.stdout is None` no longer detects a windowed exe**: PyInstaller 6 wires stdout to `NUL`
  instead of leaving it None, so `batch()` silently wrote nothing (found by the exe test, fixed with
  `getattr(sys, 'frozen', False)`). **The same idiom is still in the other `.pyw` files**
  (`I3Chara Convert Bone V3` and friends), so their exes have the same silent-CLI bug.
- Tests: `scratchpad/uji_gabung/uji_gui_gabung.py` (12 groups, window driven in-process: type
  detection incl. a junk file, both panels appearing and being hidden rather than rebuilt, the
  weapon edit path with a comma decimal, the new animation picker, a weapon save keeping 18/18
  SND1 chunks, the V1 flag fix through the button, a character edit + save keeping 37/37 chunks,
  the three dialogs opening with a Frame as parent, `tambah_state` through the panel, and an
  unreadable file leaving the window intact). `scratchpad/uji_senjata/uji_senjata.py` (12 groups)
  and the old `uji_gui.py` still pass unchanged, and saving without editing is still byte-identical
  for both `SWAT_Female.I3CHR` (4.25 MB) and `BB_PinkDragon.I3CHR`.

### Why a V3 weapon cannot shoot in a V1 client: one flag bit (2026-09-22, IN-GAME PROVEN)

`BB_PinkDragon` (V3) would not fire in the user's V1 client and its `Idle` animation was frozen.
**The whole cause is bit `0x00200000` of `i3AIState+4`** on the states that carry it -
`Idle`, `Idle1PV_Zoom`, `Idle3PV_Zoom`, `LoadBullet`. Clearing it is a **4-byte** edit and the
weapon fires with a working idle, keeping all 17 states including the V3-only Change/Zoom ones.

This was settled by single-variable files tested in game by the user, not by reasoning:

| test | what was changed | result |
|---|---|---|
| converted file (AKS74U skeleton, 11 states) | everything | **fires** |
| `UJI1` working file, `+8` set back to `0` | 44 B | still fires -> `+8` irrelevant |
| `UJI2` working file, `CHR1+4` set to `0x0019dcf4` | 3 B | still fires -> irrelevant |
| `_lengkap` original with the V1 11 states moved to the front of `i3AI` | 17 B | **still dead** -> state ORDER irrelevant |
| **`UJI4` original, loop bit cleared on 4 states** | **4 B** | **fires, idle works** |

So: state count, state order, `+8` and `CHR1+4` are all harmless; only the flag matters. An
earlier guess in this file that the driver picks states by position was **wrong** and is
disproved by `_lengkap`.

Also corrected: the nine weapons with `+8 = 0` (`AS_Val`, `ApexK_EtheriumHand`, `BB_Gatling`,
`BB_P90_Ext_Bike`, `Baseball_Bat`, `Hunter_Sword_Basic`, `Kriss_Vector_SV`, `KrissSuperV_CRB`,
`AWP_VermilionBird`) are all modern imports and all also carry a non-zero `CHR1+4`
(`0x0019dcXX`); they are markers of the V3 tool, not proof that either value is safe. Across 470
client weapons `CHR1+4` is 0 in 437 and the `Idle` flag is `0x00010000` in 413, `0x00210000` in
25 (mostly event/import weapons) and `0x00410000` in 2.

In `i3senjata.py`: `BIT_BERULANG`, `StateSenjata.berulang`, `Senjata.set_berulang()`,
`periksa_bendera()`, and `perbaiki_v1(jalur, out)` which clears the bit everywhere and touches
nothing else. `konversi()` and `urutkan_v1()` now clear it automatically; the CLI has
`--perbaiki-v1` and reports the bit when just reading a file; the GUI has a **"Perbaiki untuk V1"**
button and says so in "Periksa durasi". Test 12 covers it.

**V1 still has no weapon zoom states**: of 470 client weapons only `BB_P90_Ext_Bike` (another V3
import) has `*_Zoom`, and the V1 snipers `Cheytac` / `L115A1` have 13 states with none. Keeping the
zoom states costs nothing now that the flag is fixed, but the V1 driver is not expected to play
them.

### BB_P90_Ext_Bike: the working recipe is the STOCK base file with its own NAME kept (2026-09-28)

Found by the user, in game. Clearing the loop bit (above) was **not enough** for this weapon: the flag
came out clean (`periksa_bendera` empty, 4 bytes changed) and it still would not fire - the trigger did
nothing at all, no sound, no animation, no recoil.

    stock P90_Ext.I3CHR, name left as 'P90_Ext', scene repointed at
    Weapon\BB_P90_Ext_Bike\...I3S, animations + sounds swapped to the bike's   -> FIRES
    the bike's OWN .I3CHR (17 states, AIDriverMasterGun_Type) renamed to 'P90_Ext'
                                                                               -> crash / the memory error

Be careful about what that proves: in the working case **two things** differ from the bike's own file -
the file itself (6 states, `AIDriverGunDefault`, both Extension states filled with `Idle.i3a`) and the
`i3Chara` name. It is not established that the name alone does it. What IS established: the recipe.

The name half fits the survey already in this file - of 220 V1 weapons the `i3Chara` name is **another
weapon's in 134**, empty in 70, and its own in only 16 - and it matches the character rule ("the
`i3Chara` node name must stay the base character's name; the engine resolves the animation set through
it"). So for a weapon converted onto a V1 base, **keep the base weapon's name** unless there is a reason
not to; `konversi()` defaults to `nama or donor.nama`, i.e. the donor's, which is the minority shape.

Note the earlier `BB_PinkDragon` conversion fired while named after itself, so this is not universal -
`Weapon.pef`'s `LinkedToCharaAI` for both weapons names the weapon itself and the character `.I3CHR`
files do carry that context (76 of 81). The difference between the two cases is not pinned down.

Everything else was eliminated by measurement before the user found this: `Weapon.pef` differs from stock
P90_Ext in only 3 fields (`LinkedToCharaAI`, `_ResName`, `_Number`); `_Number` 670 is unique and inside
its class range (1..675, neighbour `BB_PinkDragon` 673 works); `Weapon/Weapon.RSC` declares the `.I3CHR`
and `Sound.RSC` all four wavs; the `.I3CHR` loads with no error line and 12 intact `SND1` nodes; `Fire`
really is in the `i3AI` id list; and the `.i3AnimPack` table (8 animations, 17/17/17/17/14/14/14/14
tracks) is identical to the Dev original.

### (superseded) state order theory -- kept for the elimination data


After the SND1 fix the converted file **shoots in game** (user confirmed) while the original V3
`BB_PinkDragon.I3CHR` still does not. Diffing the two, `Fire` itself is identical (same
`Attack.i3a`, 0.667 s, same flags); only five things differ, and three are ruled out by the
user's own client packs (`scratchpad/i3pack.py` over 400-470 weapons):

- `+8` `0` vs `0xffffffff` - **not it**: 9 of 400 stock weapons use `0` (`AS_Val`, `Baseball_Bat`,
  `Kriss_Vector_SV`, `KrissSuperV_CRB`, ...) and work.
- `Idle`/`LoadBullet` looping for 7.567 s - **not it**: stock `AUG_A3_Cupid`, `Cheytac_M200_Dolphin`,
  `KrissSuperV_Dolphin` loop `Idle` for 6-10 s.
- Master duration and sound times - cannot stop a gun firing.

What is left is the **six extra states** (`Change1PV/3PV`, `Fire/Idle 1PV/3PV_Zoom`). The state id
list inside `i3AI` is stored alphabetically, so those names push everything down and `Fire` moves
from index 2 to index 4; index 2 becomes `ExtensionActivate` (0 s, no animation, no sound). That
matches the symptom exactly, so `AIDriverMasterGun_Type` in this client appears to pick states by
**position, not name**. It could not be proved from the binary: `PointBlank.exe` is packed and
contains none of the state names in ASCII or UTF-16.

`urutkan_v1(jalur, out)` acts on that: it rewrites only the u32 id array inside `i3AI` so the 11
V1 states come first and the V3 extras follow. Same object count, same size, **17 bytes differ**
in the whole file. Nothing is dropped - unlike `konversi()`, which builds on a V1 base and
therefore loses the extra states. CLI `--urutkan-v1`; test 11.

**V1 has no weapon zoom states at all.** Out of 470 weapons in the user's client only
`BB_P90_Ext_Bike` (the other V3 import) has `*_Zoom`; the V1 snipers `Cheytac` and `L115A1` - guns
that obviously zoom - carry 13 states and none of them is a zoom state. `BB_OA93_Dragon`, a V3-era
weapon already converted for this client, also has no zoom states (11 states, empty `i3Chara`
name). So aiming in V1 is a camera/scope effect plus the character's own animation, and a weapon
`.I3CHR` cannot drive a zoom pose: while zoomed the weapon keeps playing `Idle`. Expect
"animasi Zoom tidak bekerja" to stay true however the file is built.

### The `SND1` chunk -- why a converted weapon loads but cannot shoot (2026-09-22)

User: "Saya menggunakan file original BB_PinkDragon.I3CHR tapi tidak bisa menembak."
**It was a bug in this tool**, found from the user's own `BC.log`:

    LoadHeader : Weapon/BB_PinkDragon/BB_PinkDragon.I3CHR
    m_StringTableSize : 904
    [F] i3SoundNode.cpp(276) i3SoundNode::OnLoad : Could not read data.
        i3ResourceManager::__LoadResource i3Chr <gagal> : Weapon/BB_PinkDragon/BB_PinkDragon.I3CHR
        i3ResourceFile_i3Chara::LoadOrClone  Asserted : pChara != NULL

`m_StringTableSize : 904` identified the file: not the original V3 one (929) but a converted
copy. **When the `.I3CHR` fails to load the weapon has no state machine at all** - the model
still renders from the `.I3S`, so the gun is visible and reloads-by-registry work, but there is
no `Fire` state: it cannot shoot. That is the signature to look for.

Cause: **`i3SoundNode` keeps 52 bytes OUTSIDE its declared size** -
`'SND1' + u32 raw id of its i3SoundPlayInfo + 44 zeros` - sitting in the gap before the next
object. `i3chr.simpan()` writes a patched object in place only while it still fits, otherwise it
appends it to the tail of the file **using only the declared bytes**. Renaming a sound node
(`WM_AKS74U_Load.wav` 18 chars -> `WM_BB_PinkDragon_Load.wav` 25) makes it grow, so all 18 nodes
moved to the tail and every `SND1` chunk was left behind. Scan of gaps per class: only
`i3SoundNode` (52, real data), `i3Chara` (7-14) and `i3AIContext` (8) have untabled bytes; the
last two are zero padding.

Fixed in `i3senjata.py`:
- `_hitung_ekor()` records, per object, the untabled bytes that start with a 4-char chunk tag
  (`SND1`-style: 3 letters + a digit), so zero padding is ignored; `simpan()` appends that tail to
  any patch before writing, which pushes the object to the file tail **with** its chunk.
- `periksa_suara()` runs after every save: each `i3SoundNode` must still have `SND1` right after
  `name + INF2`, resolving to an `i3SoundPlayInfo`. It finds the chunk by position, because after
  the fix it lives *inside* the declared size. Stock AKS74U/BB_PinkDragon pass; the user's broken
  copy is correctly refused.
- Two further bugs surfaced while fixing it: `set_nama_node` took the name length from the
  **original** object instead of the current patched data, so renaming the same node twice cut
  into the new name; and the converter re-ran `set_wav` because the donor's float32 sound lengths
  differ between states by ~3e-6 (tolerance is now 1e-4, and `set_wav` skips a rename when the
  node name is already right).
- Tests 9 and 10 in `scratchpad/uji_senjata/uji_senjata.py` guard all of it.

**Evidence base**: `scratchpad/i3pack.py` reads `.i3Pack` (the CLAUDE.md layout confirmed: node
`name + TRN3 + 72-byte header + kid ids`, then `u32 0x90713282` + 4 bytes, then 92-byte entries
rotated right 2 bits as one big-endian integer). Surveying **220 V1 weapons** out of the user's
client `Pack\`:
- the `i3Chara` name is **empty in 70**, another weapon's name in **134** (`AK-47_DualMag` ->
  `AK-47`, every `AK-47_SOPMOD_*` -> `AK-47`) and its own in only **16** (base guns such as
  `AKS74U`). So a weapon `.I3CHR` naming itself is unusual but not fatal.
- `+8` in `i3AIState` is `0xffffffff` in 213 of 220 weapons and `0` in 7 - and character files use
  `0` everywhere, so neither value is broken.
- `BB_P90_Ext_Bike`, shipped in this V1 client and working, has **exactly BB_PinkDragon's profile**:
  17 states with Change/Zoom, its own name, `+8 = 0`, `Idle`/`LoadBullet` looping (`0x00210000`).
  That is what ruled the state layout out as the cause and pointed at the file itself.

- Delivered `Weapon\BB_PinkDragon\_hasil_V1\BB_PinkDragon.I3CHR` (86 objects, 12,580 bytes,
  rebuilt after the SND1 fix below): 11 V1 states,
  everything pointing at BB_PinkDragon, reload sounds at V1 timings (0.398 / 1.196 / 1.992 and Master
  0.390 / 0.696 / 1.390). The user's own `BB_PinkDragon.I3CHR` was not touched. **Not tested in game yet.**
  No `.exe` built - PyInstaller is not installed and downloading it needs the user's OK.

### Putting a `.i3a` back INTO a pack -- `impor_i3a` / `tambah_i3a` (2026-09-26)

User: "i3Anim Editor kalau bisa saya ingin menambahkan file i3a saya. bisa ??" This closes the loop:
a motion can now go Mixamo -> BVH -> `.i3a` -> **into a `.i3AnimPack`**, which is where the engine
looks for the animations a `.I3CHR` state names.

Two operations, both in `i3anim.AnimPack`:

- **`impor_i3a(no, jalur)`** replaces the motion of an existing slot, matching **by bone name**. The
  slot's track count and track names are never touched, so the animation still fits the skeleton that
  pack is for; a track whose name is not in the `.i3a` keeps its original record and index values.
  This is the route that needs no `.I3CHR` edit at all - overwrite an animation a state already
  points at (a lobby `UI_IdleA`, say) and the character plays it.
- **`tambah_i3a(jalur, nama)`** appends a **new** animation to the pack, `nama` being the virtual
  path a `.I3CHR` state will reference (`chara/swat_female/3pv/common/emote_gangnam.i3a`).

`_rekam_trek()` builds the 72-byte record plus its slice of the index table. Flags are derived from
the data: a channel whose value never changes is marked FIXED (one value written), and the time
channel is left out when the keys are evenly spaced and start at 0 (the engine then derives the times
from `langkah` at +8). Every shape this produces - **0x03, 0x0B, 0x13, 0x1B, 0x3B** - occurs in the
stock packs, and the `u32` in front of each track name is 0 there in all 20,219 tracks measured.

Two details that matter:

- **The position channel follows the destination.** A `.i3a` ALWAYS carries all four channels (its
  loader ignores the flags), while **95 % of pack tracks have no position channel at all** - 936 of
  20,219. So `impor_i3a` drops a constant position when the slot it is replacing had none, which is
  what makes export-then-import reproduce the original **exactly**. A position that actually varies
  is always kept. `tambah_i3a` has no slot to copy, so it writes both channels in full: dropping a
  constant position there would be betting that the value equals the bind pose, and that is not proven.
- **The two new handlers did not mark the pack as changed** (user hit this immediately): `_tulis`
  refuses to rewrite the same path while `self.ubah == 0`, so "Simpan" answered "Tidak ada perubahan"
  after an import while "Simpan sebagai..." worked, because its path differs. Both handlers now
  bump `self.ubah`, and the GUI test presses **Simpan** and checks the file on disk really changed.
- **`simpan()` never wrote the animation count** at header +4. Nothing had changed it before
  `tambah_i3a` existed, so the omission was invisible; with a new entry the result could not be
  reopened ("awal data tidak cocok dengan jumlah animasi").

Key values go through the existing `_cari_tambah()`, so an identical key is reused and only genuinely
new ones grow the pool - a pack-to-`.i3a`-to-pack round trip does not grow the file at all.

GUI: **I3Anim Editor V3** gained "Ganti dari .i3a..." and "Tambah .i3a..." next to "Ekspor .i3a...";
the second asks for the virtual path and preselects the folder of the pack's first animation.
CLI: `--impor-i3a NO FILE` and `--tambah-i3a FILE NAMA`.

`uji_i3anim_i3a.py`: **43 checks** - export animation 0 to `.i3a`, import it back and get the keys
back **bit for bit** (max difference 0.000000000), the other animations untouched, adding a new entry
(count, name, duration, old animations intact, duplicate name refused), a real `Emote\*.i3a` going
into a pack with 32 of 43 tracks matched and rotations identical to the source, three refusals, and
the editor window driven in-process through both buttons plus a save.

Regression: of the 21 `.i3AnimPack` on this machine an unchanged save is **byte-identical for 19**;
the two refusals (`Chara_*_Throw_Skull_Grenade`) are the known key-pool-formula gap (`cek_kolam`),
not new. **Not tested in game.**

## Emote di client V1 -- apa yang sudah ada dan apa yang hilang (2026-09-27)

User: "apakah V1 ini bisa menggunakan emote?? emote ini hanya berfungsi di V3". Ditelusuri dari
dua sisi: client `D:\Data C\BlacklistPB` dan server `SERVER BLACKLIST V42 EN VERSION`.
**Analisis saja - tidak ada berkas yang diubah.**

### Rantai emote, lengkap

    Emotion.Pef  EmoteList\<Emote>\LinkedToCharaAI   (nama konteks)
        -> konteks di  Chara\<Base>\<Base>_Emote.I3CHR   (akar "Emote", driver AIDriverCharaWhole)
            -> state tunggal bernama "Emote"
                -> .i3a di  Chara\<Base>\Chara_<Base>_Emote.i3AnimPack

`<Base>_Emote.I3CHR` adalah **karakter tersendiri**: node `i3Chara`-nya bernama `SWAT_Male_Emote`
(bukan `SWAT_Male`) sementara SGI-nya tetap menunjuk `Chara\SWAT_Male\SWAT_Male.I3S`. Jadi polanya
`<nama base>_Emote`, dan paket animasinya ikut nama itu (`Chara_SWAT_Male_Emote.i3AnimPack`).

### Yang SUDAH ADA di client V1 (semua terverifikasi, bawaan)

- **4 paket animasi emote**, 16 Juli 2024: `Chara_SWAT_Male_Emote`, `Chara_SWAT_Female_Emote`,
  `Chara_REBEL_Male_Emote`, `Chara_REBEL_Female_Emote` (masing-masing 15 animasi, 43 trek).
- **`SWAT_Male_Emote.I3CHR`** (16 Juli 2024): akar konteks `Emote` + 15 konteks anak
  `Air_Kiss, Arm_Wave, Boxing_Idle, Bye_Bye, Crying, Drunk_Idle, Kill_You, Salsa_Dance, Salute,
  Shuffling, Sitting_Clap, Swing_Dance, Victory, Warming_Up, Zombie_Attack`. Semua 15 rujukan
  animasinya **resolve** ke paketnya (0 hilang).
- **Deklarasi sumber daya bawaan**: `Chara.i3pack` -> `Chara/AnimPack.RSC` (4 entri emote) dan
  `Chara/Character.RSC` (2 entri `*_Emote.I3CHR`). File ini **MD5-identik dengan update resmi
  V1 1.15.42** (`a416aa873e5ffd0b405e03cb8e22c638`, 278.599 byte), jadi ini bawaan Zepetto, bukan
  tambahan user. Revisi yang lebih lama (`Change Logs/V1.15.42`, 206.956 byte) dan V3 `Pack 3.88`
  (45.962 byte) sama-sama **tidak** punya entri emote.
- **15 dari 18** emote di daftar V3 animasinya sudah ada di client V1. Yang belum: `Felipe`,
  `HipHop`, `Luna` - dan ketiganya ada di `HeavyRain\Emote\` (`Dance_Felipe.i3a`, `HipHop.i3a`,
  `Gangnam_Luna.i3a`).

### Yang HILANG

**1. `config/Emotion.Pef`** - ini intinya. Ada di `Script.i3Pack` V3 (52.184 byte), TIDAK ada di
`Script.i3pack` V1 (19 berkas, Juni 2018). Isinya I3R2 biasa (v0x90001, 739 objek) berisi kunci
`EmoteList` dengan 18 emote. Susunan nilai registry di berkas ini **bukan** bentuk 15-kolom nasional
seperti `Weapon.pef`, melainkan sederhana:

    u8 panjang + nama + u32 tipe + nilai
    tipe 0 = i32, 1 = f32, 2 = 'RGS3' + u32 aksara + UTF-16LE

Medan tiap emote: `ItemID`, **`LinkedToCharaAI`** (nama konteks di `.I3CHR`), `PlayTime` (detik),
`_UIShapeIndex`, `_UITemplateIndex`. ItemID-nya satu blok berurutan **4120003..4120022**
(`ByeBye` 4120003 ... `HipHop` 4120022) - 7 digit, jadi BUKAN ruang id senjata 9 digit, dan
`ComDiv.getIdStatics(id,1)` memberi 0 (UNKNOWN) di server.
Nama `LinkedToCharaAI` cocok **satu-satu** dengan 15 konteks di `SWAT_Male_Emote.I3CHR`.
Berkas ini juga memuat daftar Spray (`Mode_Bomb`, `PopArt_OK`, `Rica_GGEZ`, ...).

**2. UI emote.** Nol. Sapuan seluruh 37.378 berkas di 3.565 pack client: 0 hit untuk
`emote/emoti/dance/salute/gangnam/taunt/gesture`. `UI_Re2_Script.i3pack` berisi 156 skrip Lua
(`.luab`) untuk lobby/inventori/klan - tidak satu pun untuk emote. `_UIShapeIndex` 0..22 menunjuk
ikon yang tidak ada di client ini.

**3. Dukungan server: nol.** 150 handler paket di `pbserver_game/global/clientpacket/`, tidak ada
satu pun emote. `ITEM_CLASS` punya 17 nilai (UNKNOWN..TEMP) tanpa kelas emote. Slot perlengkapan
`PlayerEquipedItems` = `_primary, _secondary, _melee, _grenade, _special, _red, _blue, _helmet,
_beret, _dino` - tidak ada slot emote.

### `.gantirank` - kenapa lobby bisa bergerak

`BASE_CHATTING_REC` -> `ChangePlayerRankDev.SetPlayerRankDev` -> **`BASE_RANK_UP_PAK` (opcode 2614)**,
isinya cuma `u32 rank, u32 rank, u32 exp`. Client-lah yang memainkan upacara naik pangkat sendiri;
suaranya bawaan di `Sound_Character_Action.i3pack`: `CH_Ceremony_SWAT_Female.wav`,
`CH_Ceremony_SWAT_Male.wav`, `CH_Ceremony_Rebel_Female/Male.wav`. Jadi **client V1 memang sanggup
memainkan animasi seluruh badan di lobby atas perintah server** - tapi paket itu tidak bisa menyebut
animasi mana pun, jadi bukan jalan menuju emote sembarang. Tidak ada animasi bernama "ceremony"
atau "salute" di 299 `.i3AnimPack` / 2.702 `.I3CHR` client (kecuali `Salute` di paket emote).

### Yang TIDAK bisa dibuktikan dari sini

`PointBlank.exe` (= `PointBlank.i3Exec`, 10.031.944 byte, isinya sama) **terbungkus**. Uji kontrol:
string yang pasti dipakai - `CStageBattle`, `CGameCharaBase`, `CEquipShapeManager`, `AIDriverCharaUpper`,
`UI_IdleA` - **tidak satu pun** muncul di dalamnya, padahal `BC.log` mencetak `CEquipShapeManager::
SetMapShape` dan `StageBattle.cpp`. Jadi "tidak ada string Emote di exe" **bukan bukti** exe tidak
mendukung emote. Bukti terkuat ke arah sebaliknya: update resmi 1.15.42 mengirim animasi + `.I3CHR`
+ deklarasi RSC-nya, yang tidak masuk akal kalau exe-nya tidak memakainya.

Catatan: `BC.log` memang mencatat registry yang hilang (`LocaleValue::GetInt32 [YouTubePlayer] -
LocaleValue.pef`), tapi tidak ada keluhan soal `Emotion.Pef` - bisa berarti exe tidak membacanya,
bisa juga berarti baru dibaca saat UI emote dibuka (yang memang tidak ada).

### Jalur yang masuk akal kalau mau dicoba

- **Jangan sentuh `Script.i3pack`** - anti-tamper (`STR_TBL_GLOBALDEF_GAMEINTERFACE_DATA_CRACKED1/2`).
  Menukarnya dengan `Script.i3Pack` V3 juga akan mengganti seluruh basis data item V1
  (`Weapon.pef` 44 MB -> 65 MB, `Character.Pef` 1,2 MB -> 4,4 MB).
- **`Blacklist_Script_Config.i3pack` adalah pack config kedua yang menang atas `Script.i3pack`**
  (15 berkas, termasuk `BC.i3Game` - itulah cara stage BioLab didaftarkan). Menaruh `Emotion.Pef`
  di situ adalah uji termurah untuk melihat apakah exe V1 membacanya, tanpa menyentuh yang protected.
- In-game: medan Animation (bendera `2`) sampai ke client lain tanpa diubah isinya. **KOREKSI
  30/09/2026**: kalimat lama di sini - "server meneruskan blok aksi apa adanya" - **salah**.
  `WriteActionBytes` membongkar blok itu medan per medan lalu MENYUSUNNYA ULANG, termasuk menulis
  sendiri panjang dan kata flags-nya; lihat bagian "Memicu animasi dari server" di bawah. Artinya
  server bisa mengubah, menambah, atau membuat sendiri blok aksi - yang belum diketahui hanya arti
  angkanya bagi client.

Skrip analisis ada di scratchpad sesi ini: `cari_emote.py`, `cari_ceremony.py`, `uji_kontrol.py`,
`periksa_emote.py`, `banding_rsc.py`, `banding_script.py`, `urai_emotion.py`.

## Map data, `.i3Path` and `.i3INS` notes -- `i3path.py`

The user's map sample (2026-09-13) is `World\Crackdown\` (`Crackdown.i3WRD`, `Crackdown_World.I3S`, `Crackdown_Sky.i3s`,
`Crackdown_Ref.dds`, `Path.i3Path`) plus `World\Scene\Crackdown\` (`Crackdown.i3INS`, `Crackdown.RSC`,
`_Generated\Box*.i3s`, `_Generated\*.i3Evt`). Everything there except the RSC/i3INS is I3R2 **version 7**
(`01 00 07 00`); the game packs in `D:\Data C\Downloads\Point Blank Dev\Pack 3.88` are version 9.

- `Crackdown_World.I3S`: 190 objects, `i3Node` root -> `i3AttrSet` -> 24 `i3Geometry`, **no transform nodes**, so
  vertices are already in world space (y up). VA30 vertices are 40 bytes with the position first; `i3IndexArray` =
  u32 count, u32 0, u16 indices; the untagged 21-byte `i3GeometryAttr` has the primitive type at @0 (4 = triangle
  list), primitive count at @1, VA id @9, IA id @13. 48,704 vertices, 28,278 triangles; the play area is about ±18 m,
  but skyline pieces reach ±290 m.
- `Crackdown.RSC`: `RSCF` + `RSC2` entries (type, two name lengths, offset, the path twice, `ffffffff`, `0` + `0xCC`
  padding), listing every map resource including `World/Crackdown/Path.i3Path`. `Box*.i3s` are unit cubes (±0.5) under
  an `i3Transform2`; the i3INS scale is the box size. `Cb03.i3Evt` = `i3TimeEventGen` + `i3TimeEventInfo` "World-Section
  설정" + `i3ActionSetWorldSection`.
- **`Path.i3Path`** (AI walking path) = I3R2 with two objects: `i3MemoryBuffer` (u32 size + payload) and `i3GamePath`
  (empty name + GND1 of 44 zero bytes + `GPT1`: u32 buffer object id, u32 point count, u32 link count, rest 0; declared
  192 bytes, and the file ends with one extra 0 byte that must be kept). Payload = points x 88 + links x 76 + a u32
  adjacency list, exactly 10,016 bytes for Crackdown's 48 points / 69 links:
  - point: +0 u32 0, +4 f32 x/y/z, +16 u32 value (Crackdown: 20 on 8 points, 70 on the centre point 19, meaning
    unknown), +20 f32 RGBA editor colour (1, 0.4, 0, 1), +36 u32 first adjacency index, +40 u32 adjacency count, rest 0.
  - link: +0 u32 **1 = two-way, 0 = one-way**, +4 u32 0, +8 u32 from, +12 u32 to, +16 f32 unit direction =
    normalize(to - from) (true for all 69), rest 0.
  - adjacency, per point in point order: sorted link indices = every link leaving the point plus every two-way link
    arriving at it. Verified on Crackdown and `Map\SweetCrackdown\Path.i3Path` (same data; only the colour float and the
    header version differ); the only one-way link is 15 -> 16, a 1.42 m drop from a ledge.
  `GamePath` holds links as references to point objects, so deleting a point renumbers everything; `simpan()` rebuilds
  the adjacency, the GPT1 counts and the directions (kept bit-exact while both endpoints are unmoved) and rewrites the
  object table. An unchanged save and a CSV export -> import -> save reproduce the file byte for byte; editing,
  one-way/two-way, reversing, deleting, emptying and refilling all re-read cleanly. **Not yet tested in game.**
- `Denah` renders a map mesh top-down in pure Python (no Pillow, so the exe stays small): highest surface per cell
  (10 cm), bright edges where the height jumps more than 0.35 m, crop = 3-97 % triangle-centroid percentiles joined
  with the path points + 3 m. **Columns run along -X** (`ke_piksel` = `(x1 - x) / sel`): the world is right-handed Y-up,
  and the decoded game minimap (`Images\mini_Crackdown.i3i`, DXT5) and the container text in the 3D view both put +Z up
  and +X to the **left**. Until 2026-09-14 all three map editors drew +X to the right, i.e. mirrored; their
  `ke_layar`/`ke_dunia` now anchor on `x1` instead of `x0`. Crackdown: 436x454 px in about 1 s, and the official path runs exactly along the
  corridors between the obstacles. Official path points sit a median 0.25 m above that surface (under a roof the
  highest surface is the roof, which is why "Y ikut permukaan" is off by default).
- **`Crackdown.i3INS`** (magic `GINS`, version 3, 76 objects, parse ends exactly at EOF): 32-byte header ('GINS', u32 3,
  u32 count, 20 zero bytes); each object = 92-byte body (+0 u32 A, +4 u32 B = class code, +8 f32 position, +20 f32
  quaternion xyzw, +36 f32 scale, +48 1, +52 0, +56 0/3, +60 0/1, +76 flags, +80 12-byte hash) + u32 extra size + u32
  name length + extra bytes + name. Contents: `World` root, 12 unnamed B=`4CE77B33` objects (the respawn points: the
  v4 file names them `Respawn0`; +60 splits them 6/6, probably the team), `Element` (the light, 27 m up, tilted), 35
  `Crackdown_Glass*`, `Path`, 26 `Box*` (trigger volumes; 8 carry a 48-byte extra whose first u32 is 50/61/66). The
  game's `Pack 3.88\Crackdown_Scene.i3Pack` stores **GINS v4** instead (a layer table of 80-byte names such as
  `Glass`, `Default`, `HitMap`, then 41 objects = the same list without the glass), so the user's v3 file is a
  different build.
- **The 26 `Box*` objects are `i3Trigger`s** (decoded 2026-09-14 when the user asked what they are for): entering one runs
  its `_Generated\*.i3Evt` (I3R2: `i3TimeEventGen` + `i3TimeEventInfo` + one action). 7 are **World Section** triggers
  (`i3ActionSetWorldSection`, `AWS1` + u32 section: `Cd01` 1, `Cd02` 2, `Cb03` 3; `Cd04`-`Cd07` exist but no box uses them)
  and 19 are **Map Sector** triggers (`i3ActionSetMapSector`, `AMS1` + u32 sector: `map1`, `m2`-`m7`, `M8`-`M11`, `M13` =
  1-12). Body +0 "A" is equal for boxes sharing an event (the RSC lists each event right before the first box using it).
  **SOLVED 2026-09-24**: `A` is `nHashCodeResPath` = the first 4 bytes of the MD5 of the resource path and `B` is
  `nHashCodeInstClass` = `class_crc()` of the spawned C++ class - see "ROOT CAUSE of every failed map copy" below.
  (CRC32/FNV/djb2 were tried and failed because it is MD5, and of the UPPER-CASED path.) The 48-byte extra's first u32 is the **owner trigger's
  object index** (`i3Trigger::setOwner`): 50/61/66 in the 76-object files and 15/26/31 in the pack's 41-object list, i.e.
  Box, Box_7, Box_602 in both. `InstanceFile.gandakan()`/`hapus()` shift these indices since 2026-09-14 (before, a
  duplicated respawn left every owner pointing one object too early). `i3ins.info_kotak()` pairs boxes with events
  that way and returns {} unless every box pairs. `Crackdown.i3WRD` holds the tables: `i3MapSectorTable` (`MST1`, u32 count 13 at +4,
  148-byte records from +40, name[128] in cp949: `-`, `RED 컨테이너/갈림길/언덕/앞마당`, `중앙`, `컨테이너B`, `컨테이너A`,
  `BLUE 앞마당/컨테이너/언덕/갈림길`, `중앙 컨테이너`; the RED areas are in the -Z half with the flag-0 respawns) and
  `i3WorldSectionTable` (`WST1`, 4 x 176-byte records: name[128], u32 mask, u32 0, u32 0xFF: `world` 0xD, `컨테이너1` 3,
  `컨테이너2` 5, `컨테이너3` 9). Section 1 boxes are container-sized at floor level (y 1.7-4.1) at the centres of the five
  container-named sectors; sections 2/3 sit right above two of them (roofs). Client names (`update_map_sector::
  _UpdateMapSector`, radio text `[Radio] %s {col:98, 180, 253, 255}[%s]{/col}`, `i3Framework::SetCurrentPortalMask`,
  `i3GameObj::OnUpdateWorldSectionMask`) suggest map sector = the player's location name and world section = a portal /
  visibility mask; neither is tested. The 3.2 m tall map-sector boxes cover every corridor, so they do not block movement.
  Stock oddities: Box_61 duplicates Box_6, and Box_601/Box_6001 (sector 1) lie on Box_60/Box_600 (sectors 4/3).
- **`_Generated\Box_N.i3s` repeats each box's placement**: PhysX actor pose = i3INS position + rotation and box half
  extents = i3INS scale / 2 for 24 boxes; Box_600 and Box_6002 differ in Z by 0.19/0.30 m (their actors sit at the Z of
