### Path editor 3D view (2026-09-24)

User: "Untuk I3Path Editor V3 buatkan versi 3D nya dengan menggunakan GPU OpenGL". Built on the same
`i3gl` pattern as the collision and I3INS editors, so the camera, picking and drag idioms are identical
(right-drag rotate, middle/Shift-right pan, wheel zoom to the point under the cursor, WASDQE walk,
F = focus on the selected point, Home = fit).

- The path is drawn as **lit cubes** (immediate mode, one per point: orange, purple when `Nilai` is not 0,
  cyan when selected, magenta for the pending link start) plus `GL_LINES` for the links - yellow two-way,
  red with a screen-facing arrowhead for one-way - and the point numbers through `GLFrame.tulis_di`
  with the depth test off. Marker radius grows with camera distance (`max(0.28, jarak*0.006)`) so far
  points stay visible and clickable.
- **All four tools work in 3D**, not only selection: tool 2 puts a new point on the map surface under
  the cursor (depth buffer; falls back to the plane of the current point when there is no mesh), tool 3
  links two clicked points, tool 4 deletes. Dragging moves the point on its own height plane, **Shift**
  drags it up/down in the camera-facing vertical plane, and "Tinggi (Y) ikut permukaan" makes it stick
  to the map surface. Picking is ray-sphere for points and ray-segment for links (`_sinar_bola` /
  `_sinar_ruas`), points first, and anything more than 0.3 m behind the map surface goes last unless
  "Titik tembus pandang" is on.
- **"Potong atap di atas Y"** (new, on by default, prefilled with the highest path point + 3 m) clips the
  MAP ONLY with one `glClipPlane`. Without it a covered map is useless from above: SweetCrackdown spans
  Y 1.5..27.2 while its path sits at Y 1.6..3.3, so the whole screen is just the roof.
- `_batas_y3d()` fits the camera to the **path's** Y range, not the mesh's, for the same reason.
- Both tabs stay in sync: `_gambar_ulang()` redraws the 2D canvas and schedules a 3D frame; the 2D denah
  is only fitted when its tab is actually opened (`pas_2d_tertunda`), and `_muat_dunia` now loads the
  `PetaGL` mesh first (fast) and the 2D denah after, in the same worker thread.
- The window icon is set from `_pasang_ikon()` **after** the GL context exists - `iconbitmap` before that
  deadlocks `update_idletasks()` inside `i3gl._buat_konteks` (see the collision editor note).
- `i3gl.py` gained three things for this: `GL_QUADS`/`GL_TRIANGLE_FAN`, `glNormal3f`/`glColor3f`, and
  **IIA2 decryption**: `buka_indeks()` opens an encrypted index array with the tables in `Cipher V2\`
  (the same PBM cipher as the `.i3Pack` V2 one, exactly as `i3obj.py` does), rejects a key whose result
  has an index past the vertex count, and records unlearned masks in `PetaGL.kunci_perlu`. Before this a
  map taken straight out of a `.i3Pack` usually failed with "tidak ada mesh yang bisa digambar" - the
  pack copy of `SweetCrackdown_World.I3S` needs **37 different type-1 keys**, one per mesh. This helps
  the collision and I3INS 3D views too.
- Tests: `scratchpad/path3d/uji_gui.py` - 25 checks driving the real window (tabs, mesh load, a frame that
  actually draws, click-to-select, horizontal drag keeping Y, Shift drag keeping X/Z, full undo restoring
  the file **byte for byte**, tools 2/3/4 through 3D clicks, camera rotate/zoom/fit/walk, and switching to
  the 2D tab and back). Not tested in game (the file format is unchanged - only the view is new).

## Binding bone weights -- `ikat_bone.py`

The user's OBJ importer (2026-09-13) swaps only the mesh of a mask template: `Ucok_Head_LOD1.i3s` is
`M_M_RedBulls_X_LOD1.i3s` object for object (same 63-bone skeleton, node names `M_M_RedBulls_X`), but its VA is fmt
`0x00000483` (pos nrm uv only; 13,140 unwelded vertices = 4,380 triangles), descriptor `118111c1`, header f32 +36 = +1.0
(every stock VA has -1.0), `CJHead.i3i` is embedded as an internal `i3Texture` (the file bytes plus the absolute path as
the name in its I3IB header), and NormalMap/SpecularMap Enable = 1 with bind texture 0. Without blend indices
`pb.menempel()` classes it as rigid headgear, so the converter's Mask field refuses it.

- Stock V2 mask VAs (RedBulls/AcidPol): LOD1 fmt `0x0008C4A7` (3 blend indices + 2 weights + tangents), LOD2/3
  `0x0008C483`; descriptor `11811101` (AcidPol LOD2/3 `11821102`); +36 = -1.0. Blend block = 3 index bytes + 1 zero byte
  + 2 f32 weights, third implied; unused slots are index 0 / weight 0 and slot order is arbitrary (`06 07 05` = Neck,
  Head, Spine3). RedBulls X LOD1: 544 of 567 vertices 100 % Head, the bottom ring blends Neck/Head/Spine3. LOD3 masks
  carry only TextureEnable/Bind + Material - the diffuse-only layout written when a normal map has no texture.
- Tangent convention (checked on `F_S_AR_Priest-Red`, plain IA): binormal = normal x tangent exactly and points along -V;
  `hitung_tangen()` reproduces the stored tangents with mean dot 0.92-0.99.
- `ikat()` per mesh: weld identical pos+nrm+[colour]+uv bytes (IA rewritten, needs a plain IA), group vertices by position
  so seams share one weight, k nearest skinned source vertices (grid, 1/d^2, optional same-facing normal filter), source
  bone names mapped onto the model skeleton (missing -> nearest ancestor), neighbour smoothing, top 3 weights >= 0.01.
  Material: NormalMap/Specular Enable+Bind with texture 0 are dropped from the AttrSet (objects stay as orphans);
  tangents only while a normal map stays bound. `rakit()` splices the changed objects into the original data region and
  shifts later offsets, so overlapping declared sizes and untabled bytes survive (an empty change reproduces the file).
  `periksa()` re-reads: other objects identical, vertex bytes unchanged, indices/weights valid, triangles identical,
  `pb.menempel()` false.
- Results: Ucok head from RedBulls X LOD1 -> Head 99.0 %, Neck 0.6 %, Spine3 0.4 %, 3,896 vertices, 233,664 bytes.
  Re-binding RedBulls X from RedBulls Y gives the same dominant bone on 567/567 vertices (max weight diff 0.015).
  `part_fit` 2.8e-6 on SWAT_Male LOD1-3 (female base 0.33). One part file fills only one V1 LOD in `spread_parts`, so
  `--lod23` writes identical copies `_Bone_LOD2/3`; a 25-bone LOD accepts the 63-bone part because only used bones are
  checked. Berserker skin + the three copies convert with Verifikasi OK and render in i3Viewer2 with no log lines.
  Not yet tested in game.
- Character forward is +Y (SWAT_Male toes y 0.077, feet -0.05); the preview's "Depan" uses the Foot->Toe direction.
- **OpenGL preview (2026-09-19, the user asked for it because rotating the view was heavy)**: the `.pyw` now stacks an
  `i3gl.GLFrame` over the old `tk.Canvas` in the same grid cell and `grid_remove`s the canvas; the canvas comes back
  (`_gl_gagal`) if the context cannot be created or `i3gl` is missing, so the tkinter painter `_gambar()` is untouched
  and still works. `_lukis()` picks the backend, `_ikat_gambar(w)` binds the same mouse handlers to both widgets, and
  `_tekan/_seret/_roda` branch on `self.gl`.
  **Model space is Z-up, OpenGL is Y-up**, so every point is written as `(x, z, -y)` and the front view is computed
  twice: `_arah_depan()` returns (canvas yaw, GL yaw), the GL one being `degrees(atan2(fx, -fy))` = 180 for a SWAT
  skeleton. Camera = `i3gl.Kamera` with `fov = 35` (the default 55 bends a character's proportions) and `kam.pas()`
  on the mapped bounding box.
  One display list per mesh (`_siapkan_daftar` / `_buat_daftar` -> new `i3gl.daftar_warna`, which compiles
  `glVertexPointer` + `glNormalPointer` + `glColorPointer` + `glDrawElements` into a list; `i3gl` gained
  `glColorPointer`, `glPointSize`, `glShadeModel`, `glColorMaterial` and the matching constants). The cache key is
  `(position-list identity, colour mode, selected bone)`: **rotating the camera rebuilds nothing**, and only the meshes
  whose vertices actually moved are rebuilt when the "Uji gerak" slider moves - `_hitung_tampilan` hands back the very
  same list object for a mesh it does not pose, so `is` is the test (checked on Apex_Wattson: only the 3 weighted
  `Model_Clan` meshes change, the 11 unweighted ones stay). Normals are posed alongside positions (`_pose_normal`,
  same weight blend as `ib.pose_titik`) so the lighting follows a rotated limb.
  A mesh whose index array is unreadable (encrypted IIA2) is drawn as `GL_POINTS`, unlit, like the dots the canvas drew.
  `GL_CULL_FACE` stays off with `GL_LIGHT_MODEL_TWO_SIDE` on, because OBJ imports have mixed winding. Bones and the
  selected-bone label are drawn with the depth test off so they stay visible inside the mesh as before, and the status
  text plus the 0-100 % legend are drawn in an ortho pass (`glOrtho(0, W, H, 0, -1, 1)`, text via `GLFrame.tulis`).
  Measured on `Desktop\Wattson\Apex_Wattson_fix.I3S` (14 meshes, 298,173 vertices, 32,916 triangles, RTX 3050):
  **13 ms per frame drawing everything**, against 553 ms for the canvas at its decimated "pratinjau cepat" setting
  (8,000 triangles) and 928 ms for a full canvas draw; the pose slider costs 31 ms per step. Tested from source (three
  colour modes, bone pick, pose test, Depan/Samping/Pas ke layar, drag/pan/wheel, a forced `_gl_gagal` and a missing
  `i3gl` both falling back to the canvas with the old output) and in the rebuilt exe, which reports the renderer name
  and draws its GL text through `wglUseFontBitmapsW`. Not yet used by the user.

## Map collision (`_Col_Hero` / `_Col_Hit`) -- `i3col.py`

`V3 Crackdown\World\Crackdown\Crackdown_Col_Hero.I3S` (character collision, 227 shapes: 41 boxes, 184 convex, 2 meshes)
and `Crackdown_Col_Hit.I3S` (bullet collision, 14 triangle meshes, one per material). Both load in i3Viewer2 (it draws
nothing for them). `Crackdown.i3WRD` references them only as whole external SGIs, never their nodes.

- Scene: `i3Transform` root (matrix rows (-1,0,0),(0,0,1),(0,1,0) = Z-up -> Y-up) > `i3Transform` "Scene Root" (identity,
  kids sorted by name) > one `i3Transform2` per collision: name + INF2 (flags 8, no kids) + u32 i3MatrixObject + u32
  i3TransformSourceCombiner, then **24 untabled bytes** `TXM2` + u32 i3PhysixShapeSet id + 16 zeros. Combiner = `TSC2`,
  u32 1, u8 0, u32 i3Animation id, u32 index into that animation's list, `01 00`. The single i3Animation lists every
  node's i3TransformSequence (Hero 11 constant keys over 3.33 s, Hit 1 key); keys, matrix and actor pose always agree.
- Object order per node: terrain i3MemoryBuffer, (face buffer + i3Vector3Array for meshes), shape set, matrix, combiner,
  transform2; all sequences + the animation sit right after the first node's matrix. Every object is referenced; the
  string table = class names + names of Transform/Transform2/ShapeSet/Sequence in object order + 2 NULs.
- `i3PhysixShapeSet` = name only, then **untabled**: 68-byte `PXA3` (+4 flags 0, 4 = mesh; +12 NXU size; +16 terrain
  buffer id; +20 1; +24 face buffer id; +28 face count; +32 i3Vector3Array id; +36 f32 0.3 1 1; zeros) + a PhysX 2.8.1
  binary **NXUSTREAM** ("NXUSTREAM\0\0" + u32 281 + u32 103; headers 0x00ABCDEF, id, size incl. the 16-byte header,
  0x01234567; strings u32 len + chars + NUL, empty = u32 0). Tree: 0x00 > 0x6A collection (id "ShapeSetXXXXXXXX", unique)
  > 0x69, [0x05 convex desc | 0x09 mesh desc (+0x07)], 0x66 scene (identical bytes in all 241) > 0x2A actor ("Actor_0",
  name = node, 16-float world pose, rows with translation in column 4 = transpose(node * SceneRoot * root), exact) >
  shape 0x21 box (3 f32 half extents) / 0x26 convex / 0x27 mesh > 0x20 base (name, 16-float local pose, flags 0x120040 box
  and mesh, 0x40 convex) > 0x11; then 0x6C end.
- Cooked CVXM: `ICE\x01CLHL` (empty) + `ICE\x01CVHL` v5: nbVerts @+40, nbHullTris @+44, vertices @+64, u32 max index +
  u8 triangles. Cooked MESH v1: flags @+12 (0x02 face remap, 0x08 8-bit, 0x10 16-bit indices), nv @+28, nt @+32,
  vertices @+36, triangles, remap, OPCODE model, and it ends with u32 nt + nt edge-flag bytes. Cooked triangle order
  differs from the i3 face buffer (u32 bytes + 16-byte faces: u32 x3, u16 terrain index, u16 junk) and the remap does not
  explain it; match by vertex positions (11 of ~20k do not match: cooking added vertices in MET_00 and TH_MET_90).
- Terrain buffer (u32 24, u32 type, i32 -1 or 0, u32 penetration, 12 zeros): CCR_ 1 concrete, MET_ 2 metal, GND_ 3
  ground, WOOD_ 4, TH_MET_90 13/90, TH_WOOD_50 14/50, PAP_ 16, GLASS_ 17, PLASTIC_ 18, RUB_ 19, CLOTH_ 20,
  TH_BARBEDWIRE_10 31/10; Hero all type 0 (194 with -1, 33 with 0). The node name is only a label.
- `ColFile` keeps objects with Python references and rebuilds the whole file with new ids; an unchanged save is
  byte-identical for both files and every save is re-read and compared (`periksa`). Delete = the node's 6-8 objects +
  its animation entry + the Scene Root kid. New box = embedded SM_00 NXU template (`KOTAK_NXU`) with a new collection id,
  names, pose and half extents (local pose identity, so the box's local frame is the node frame), terrain buffer copied
  from a chosen node, the new sequence inserted after the last sequence and the other objects before the SGI.
  Duplicate copies every object. Moving writes matrix, sequence keys and actor pose (rotation bytes kept when only
  translating); yaw is relative to the file's base orientation. Deleting mesh triangles sets the cooked indices to
  (a,a,a), the edge flag to 0 and the matching i3 face to (a,a,a): counts stay, rays cannot hit a point.
- Verified 2026-09-13: delete, add box (Hero; Hit with CCR_ / TH_MET_90 material), duplicate convex/mesh, move/yaw/resize,
  undo, delete triangles and the CLI all re-read with every other collision unchanged, and the outputs load in i3Viewer2
  without log lines. Not tested in game; the client may read `Crackdown_Col.i3Pack` instead of the loose files.

### Three newer collision variants (2026-09-24)

User: "File Crackdown_Col_Hero.I3S dan SweetCrackdown_Col_Hero tidak bisa di buka" (the SweetCrackdown
map they had just unpacked to `Desktop\SweetCrackdown\`). Three separate causes, all fixed in `i3col.py`:

- **Collision that never moves.** `i3TransformSourceCombiner` = `TSC2` + **u32 source count** + u8, then
  10 bytes per source (u32 i3Animation id, u32 index, u16). Old maps always have 1 source (19 bytes); these
  files have **0** (9 bytes), no `i3Animation` and no `i3TransformSequence` at all, and most `i3Transform2`
  nodes carry **no combiner** (67 of 89 in that file). The old parser demanded `len == 19` and
  `_kenali` demanded exactly one `i3Animation`. Now `self.anim` may be None, a node may have no combiner,
  `_tulis_pose` skips the sequence, and a new box copies whatever shape its template has.
  `Glass_Lab_Col_Hero.i3s` is the same kind, so it is not a one-off.
- **Shape set `PXA4`** (56-byte header instead of PXA3's 68): `+12` NXUSTREAM size, **`+16` size of a second
  blob**, `+20` terrain buffer id, `+24` 1, `+28/+32/+36` the three f32, `+40..55` kept as is. The three
  PXA3 fields that are gone are the i3 face buffer id, its count and the `i3Vector3Array` id - in PXA4 there
  are no such objects; instead a **second cooked PhysX mesh (`NXS\x01MESH`)** follows the NXUSTREAM, same
  triangle count but different vertex order and a different coordinate space (the NXU copy is the local one
  that `_cooked()` already reads, so the 3D view is right). Also note the **declared object size is not just
  the name** for PXA4 - part of the blob falls inside it, and how much differs per file (`o.dalam` remembers
  it, which is what keeps an unchanged save byte-identical). Because the second copy cannot be matched
  triangle-for-triangle, **`hapus_segitiga` refuses PXA4 collisions** instead of half-deleting them.
- **Unreferenced strings.** A collision file re-saved by an i3Engine tool carries its source path
  (`C:\Users\...\Crackdown_Col_Hero.I3S`) in the string table with **no object using it**; `isi()` rebuilt
  the table from objects only and dropped it, so even an unchanged save differed. `ColFile` now records those
  strings (`str_ekstra`) and puts them back at the same index.
- **A file that is still encrypted** now opens anyway: `i3col.buka_isi()` tries every table in `Cipher V2\`
  when the bytes do not start with `I3R2`/`I3SN`, and saving writes the plain file (with a log line saying so,
  since it goes back into the pack through I3Pack Editor V3, which re-applies the slot's cipher). The probe
  must decrypt **the first 65536-byte chunk**, not 64 bytes: the PBM tables are chosen by chunk length.
- Regression: all 8 collision files on this machine (both Crackdown_Col_Hero builds, both Col_Hit, SweetCrackdown
  Hero+Hit, Glass_Lab, SpacePort 981 collisions) open and rewrite **byte-identically**, and add/duplicate/
  move/rotate/resize/delete/undo/save pass on the animation-less, the PXA4 and the still-encrypted file.
  Scripts in this session's scratchpad: `col/uji_semua.py`, `col/uji_edit.py`, `col/uji_gui.py`.
- **`iconbitmap` before the OpenGL context deadlocks the app** (cost an hour 2026-09-24): calling
  `self.iconbitmap(...)` inside `App.__init__` makes the `update_idletasks()` inside `i3gl._buat_konteks`
  never return - the window appears half drawn with a black right side and cannot be closed (WER logs
  `AppHangB1`; the user hit exactly this). `I3Collision Editor V3.pyw` sets the icon from `_pasang_ikon()`,
  scheduled with `after(300, ...)` and re-scheduled until `self.gl.ctx` exists. The exe was rebuilt
  2026-09-24 with `--icon Icon\IconExe.ico --add-data "Icon;Icon"` plus `--hidden-import i3pack`, and its
  `batch()` now uses `getattr(sys, 'frozen', False)` (PyInstaller 6 points a windowed exe's stdout at NUL,
  so the CLI used to write nothing at all). Old exe in `_backup_sebelum_col_tanpa_animasi\`.

### Kotak MIRING untuk ramp dan tangga (2026-10-08)

User: "untuk I3Collision Editor V3, tambahkan fungsi untuk kotak miring / bisa edit kotak
miring (trapesium untuk tangga)."

Jalan tulisnya sudah ada sejak awal - `_tulis_pose(t2, W, putar=True)` menerima matriks dunia
APA SAJA. Yang membatasi cuma lapis di atasnya: `Collision.yaw` memberi **None** begitu
putarannya tidak murni sumbu Y, dan `pindahkan()` menolak dengan "hanya bisa digeser",
sementara `set_ukuran()` menolak lewat `permutasi()`.

- `mat_putar(yaw, pitch, roll, pos)` dan `euler_dari(W)` - pitch di sumbu X lokal, lalu roll
  di sumbu Z, lalu yaw di sumbu Y. Bolak-balik tepat di 420 kombinasi (selisih matriks
  0,000000000) **termasuk gimbal roll +-90**. Dan `mat_putar(yaw)` tanpa pitch/roll
  mengembalikan `mat_yaw(yaw)` lewat jalan pintas - BUKAN sekadar nilai yang sama: perkalian
  dengan 0.0 bisa menghasilkan **-0.0**, yang bit-nya berbeda, jadi berkas yang seharusnya
  tidak berubah akan berubah. Diuji byte-identik di 73 sudut.
- `Collision.putaran` -> (yaw, pitch, roll), selalu angka. `Collision.miring` -> bool.
  `pindahkan(node, posisi, yaw, pitch, roll)`; sudut yang tidak diberi dipertahankan, jadi
  memutar ramp mendatar tidak menghilangkan kemiringannya.
- `set_ukuran(node, ukuran, lokal=True)` membaca ukuran di sumbu KOTAK sendiri. Itu
  satu-satunya yang punya arti untuk ramp - "tinggi di sumbu Y dunia" tidak ada artinya,
  sedangkan "lebar x tebal x panjang" ada.
- `rangka_ramp(bawah, atas, lebar, tebal)` -> (matriks dunia, setengah-ukuran lokal), dan
  `tambah_ramp()` memakainya. Dua titik itu tengah tepi bawah dan tengah tepi atas
  **permukaan yang dijalani**; tebalnya menggantung ke BAWAH supaya undakan aslinya tertutup.
  Sumbu lokal: X = lebar, Y = tegak lurus permukaan, Z = panjang lereng.
- `rangka_undakan` / `tambah_tangga(bawah, atas, lebar, jumlah)` - alternatif dari beberapa
  kotak TEGAK, bentuk yang persis seperti kotak collision map bawaan.

GUI: kolom **Miring X/Z (derajat)**, tombol **Tegakkan**, dan **"Kotak miring / tangga..."**
yang terisi otomatis dari diagonal kotak yang sedang dipilih - jadi alur kerjanya: gambar
kotak kasar di atas tangganya dengan alat 2, pilih, buka kotak itu, pilih ramp atau undakan.
Label kolom ukuran berganti sendiri jadi `Ukuran lokal L/T/P:` begitu kotaknya miring, dan
Enter di kolom mana pun = Terapkan.

**Ctrl+seret SENGAJA tidak dipakai untuk memutar di editor ini** - Ctrl+klik sudah dipakai
pivot kamera (lihat catatan 3D view). Di I3INS Editor V3 Ctrl memang bebas, jadi di situ
dipakai.

#### Buktinya engine menerima kotak miring: satu kotak bawaan

Disapu 161 berkas collision di client (**71.069 kotak**, 36.728 convex, 3.022 mesh):
**tepat SATU kotak yang miring** - `SM_box1256` di `AngkorRuins_Col_Hero`, tulang 30,53
derajat, di map bawaan yang bisa dimainkan. Satu dari 71.069 memang tipis, tapi itu bukti
yang tepat jenisnya: engine memuat dan memainkannya.

Kotak itu juga yang membongkar cacat lama: **`permutasi()` TIDAK mendeteksi kemiringan yang
disimpan di matriks NODE.** Ia hanya melihat `pose_lokal` x arah dasar file, jadi untuk
SM_box1256 (dan untuk setiap ramp buatan alat ini) ia mengembalikan permutasi yang kelihatan
sah. Akibatnya label "(miring)" tidak muncul DAN `set_ukuran` menulis ukuran ke sumbu yang
salah tanpa mengeluh. Yang benar `Collision.arah_lokal()` - kolom `kali_nxu(pose, pose_lokal)`,
yaitu arah SEBENARNYA sumbu lokal shape di dunia - dan `miring` memakai itu. `set_ukuran` dan
`ukuran_dunia` sekarang berpatokan `miring`, bukan `permutasi() is None`.

#### Trapesium sungguhan (convex wedge) TIDAK bisa dibuat - dan ini angkanya

Map bawaan memang punya wedge: dari 4.053 convex yang disapu, **391 bertopologi (6 titik, 8
segitiga)** = prisma segitiga, dan 33.257 bertopologi kotak (8, 12). Jadi bentuknya nyata.
Yang tidak mungkin **menulisnya**: data cooked `CVXM` PhysX 2.8.1 bukan sekadar titik +
segitiga. Diukur dengan mem-diff dua convex 892-byte bertopologi sama:

    575 dari 892 byte berubah mengikuti geometri, tersebar di 30+ rentang
    (termasuk medan satu-byte dan tabel terkemas - SVM/Gauss map, valency)
    panjang blob-nya pun ikut berubah: 892 / 941 / 990 / 1039 / 1088 / 1137 / 1186
    - selisihnya tepat 49 byte, jadi ada tabel yang panjangnya ikut geometri

Membuatnya berarti membongkar serialisasi `InternalConvexMesh` PhysX secara penuh, dan convex
yang SALAH akan terbaca sempurna oleh Python lalu merusak client - kelas kegagalan yang sudah
berkali-kali mahal di proyek ini. Jadi tidak dikerjakan, dan itu disampaikan ke user apa adanya.

**Kotak miring menggantikannya dengan baik untuk tangga**: yang disentuh pemain permukaan
ATASNYA, dan `tambah_ramp` menaruh permukaan itu tepat di garis bawah-atas. Bedanya cuma alas
kotaknya menembus ke bawah tangga - di dalam geometri, tidak terasa. Kalau nanti benar-benar
perlu wedge, rute yang TIDAK berisiko: pakai ulang blob cooked wedge bawaan apa adanya dan
hanya mengubah POSE-nya (391 wedge tersedia di map bawaan), bukan membentuknya ulang.

#### Uji dan regresi

`uji_i3col_miring.py` **63 pemeriksaan** (matematika, rangka ramp/undakan, berkas sungguhan,
sunting kotak yang sudah miring, jalur lama tidak berubah, dan kotak bawaan AngkorRuins) dan
`uji_i3col_miring_gui.py` **40** (jendelanya digerakkan in-process; `messagebox` dipatok sejak
awal supaya kotak modal tidak menggantung uji).

Dua cacat yang ketangkap uji dan diperbaiki - dua-duanya nyata, bukan salah uji:

* `rangka_undakan` MEMBUANG satu undakan diam-diam untuk tangga MENURUN (undakan terakhir
  tingginya nol). Puncak potongan sekarang `max(y di t0, y di t1)`, bukan `y di t1`.
* `set_ukuran(lokal=False)` tidak menolak kotak yang benar-benar miring - lihat soal
  `permutasi()` di atas.

**Regresi yang menentukan**: ke-161 berkas collision di client dibaca dan ditulis ulang dengan
kode BARU dan kode PRA-PERUBAHAN berdampingan - **161 byte-identik, 0 beda, dan ke-151
penolakan pesannya sama persis** (71.069 kotak diperiksa). Ditambah `tambah_kotak` +
`gandakan` + `pindahkan` + `set_ukuran` + `hapus` berurutan: hasilnya **byte-identik** dengan
kode lama. `uji_i3tools.py` 38, `uji_i3objin.py` 35 lolos. (`uji_mapbsp.py` 19/22 - ketiga
kegagalannya berkas contoh `.bsp` yang sudah dihapus user, bukan dari ronde ini.)

### I3INS Editor V3: tombol Terapkan TERTIMBUN, jadi respawn tidak bisa diputar (2026-10-08)

User: "posisi, rotate spawn tidak bisa di edit. saya sudah ubah 180 derajat spawn tidak
berputar." Betul, dan sebabnya satu angka di tata letak - bukan di pustakanya:

```python
tb = ttk.Frame(po); tb.grid(row=11, ...)   # Terapkan, Pusatkan
tb = ttk.Frame(po); tb.grid(row=11, ...)   # Tambah..., Duplikat, Ganti nama..., Hapus
```

**Dua frame di sel grid yang SAMA saling menimbun, dan yang dibuat belakangan menang.** Diukur
di jendela sungguhan: titik tengah tombol "Terapkan" dikembalikan `winfo_containing()` sebagai
tombol **"Tambah..."**. Jadi tombolnya kelihatan tapi tidak bisa diklik, dan karena tidak ada
ikatan Enter di kolomnya, SELURUH panel (posisi, putaran, quaternion, skala, bendera) tidak
bisa diterapkan sama sekali. Posisi masih bisa diubah dengan menyeret di 3D - itu jalur lain -
sedangkan putaran tidak punya jalur lain, jadi putaran memang mustahil.

Pustakanya sendiri bersih: `pindah()` dan `set_quat()` jalan untuk respawn, dan hasilnya
bertahan sesudah simpan + baca ulang (diuji).

Perbaikannya baris tombol dipindah ke row 12 dan 13, ditambah:
* **Enter di kolom mana pun = Terapkan** (`en.bind('<Return>')`).
* **Ctrl + seret mendatar di 3D = putar sumbu Y**, Shift mengancingnya ke kelipatan 15 derajat.
  Rotasinya DIKALIKAN ke quaternion lama lewat `i3ins.kali_quat` (hasil kali Hamilton), bukan
  menulis yaw baru - jadi objek yang rotasinya tidak murni sumbu Y tetap mempertahankan
  kemiringannya. Penanda 3D memang ikut quaternion (`_matriks`), jadi hasilnya terlihat sambil
  diseret.

`uji_i3ins_putar_gui.py` **33 pemeriksaan**, dan yang paling menjaga yang pertama: tiap tombol
panel harus dikembalikan `winfo_containing()` sebagai DIRINYA SENDIRI. Uji yang hanya memanggil
`app._terapkan()` langsung tidak akan pernah menangkap bug ini - itulah sebabnya ia lolos
berminggu-minggu.

Tiga jebakan uji di ronde itu, ketiganya salah uji bukan salah produk:
* **`event_generate('<Return>')` hilang kalau widgetnya tidak FOKUS** - Tk mengarahkan event
  tombol ke widget yang fokus. Pakai `focus_force()` lalu `when='now'`.
* `_urungkan()` mengganti daftar objek dengan salinan dari riwayat dan **mengosongkan pilihan**,
  jadi Terapkan sesudah urungkan memang memberi pesan "Pilih dulu" - sekarang itu diuji sebagai
  perilaku, bukan dianggap kegagalan.
* `putar()` mengandaikan quaternion PANJANG 1; quaternion uji yang tidak ternormalkan membuat
  perbandingan "a lalu b" vs "kali_quat(a, b)" meleset 0,0016 dan terbaca seperti cacat.

## 3D view -- `i3gl.py`

Added 2026-09-14 to I3Collision Editor V3 (tab "Tampilan 3D"; the old canvas is tab "Denah 2D"). No extra packages:
OpenGL 1.x fixed function through ctypes (`opengl32.dll`, a `gdi32` pixel format, `wglCreateContext`) on a `tk.Frame(bg='')`.

- `GLFrame` draws on demand (`jadwalkan` -> `after_idle`); `segera()` flushes a pending draw; `kedalaman_sekarang()` reads
  one depth pixel of the last frame (**the depth buffer survives SwapBuffers**: equal to a re-render at three pixels on
  the RTX 3050); `tangkap()` = glReadPixels of a fresh frame; text = `wglUseFontBitmapsW` lists + `glBitmap` offsets
  (`tulis_di`, colour must be set before `glRasterPos`). `saat_gagal` reports a failed context and the editor switches to
  the 2D tab. GL >= 1.3 entry points (`glActiveTexture`, `glClientActiveTexture`, `glCompressedTexImage2D`) come from
  `wglGetProcAddress` with a current context. **`GL_COMPILE` is 0x1300** (0x1F00 is `GL_VENDOR`: with it every display
  list silently draws nothing, GL error 1280).
- `PetaGL` walks the world I3S from the SGI root: i3Transform matrices (`i3MatrixObject`, D3D row-major = GL column-major,
  so the 16 floats go to `glMultMatrixf` unchanged), AttrSets (`ATS1` or the old untagged u16 list), TextureBind /
  LuxMapBind + their Enable attrs, AlphaTestEnable/AlphaFunc (ref = byte 0), BlendEnable/BlendMode (D3D blend enums).
  VA offsets come from the format word (`0x2` normal, `0x8` colour, `(fmt>>10)&3` UV sets); GEO2 or 21-byte geometry attr;
  IIA2 (plain only) or old index arrays; lists and strips. `.i3i` DXT data is uploaded as is with its mip chain: byte 10
  `0x80`/`0x81` = DXT1, `0x04` = DXT5 (survey of 624 project `.i3i`; `0x07` on `Harvest_Pitchfork_Norm` is unhandled).
  Rows are top-first like D3D, so UVs need no flip. Lightmap on unit 1 (uv1, V -0.99..0 with REPEAT), `GL_COMBINE` RGB
  scale 2. V3 Crackdown: 24 batches, 28,289 triangles, 26/26 textures, read 0.03 s, upload 0.03 s; a full frame with all
  collisions 12-14 ms.
- **Handedness**: the world is right-handed Y-up, raw coordinates go to OpenGL with no Z flip (container text "NF.U"
  reads correctly, the top view matches the minimap). Initial camera yaw 180 / pitch 55 = seen from -Z like the minimap.
- Collisions are display lists in **shape-local space** keyed by content (box size, or length + hash of the cooked data)
  and drawn with `transpose(kali_nxu(pose, pose_lokal))`: moving swaps only the matrix, duplicates share lists, deleted
  triangles (a,a,a) drop out. Fills are translucent without depth writes, so the depth buffer holds only the world
  mesh (cursor readout, zoom to cursor, box base height, occluded picks). The selected shape is drawn again with
  `GL_GREATER` to show its hidden part dimmed. The Y filter is two `glClipPlane`s on world and collisions.
- Picking = CPU ray casting (AABB, then Moller-Trumbore on `geometri_dunia`), ~50 ms on the Hit file. **Order = the 2D
  rule**: non-mesh shapes smallest first (largest face of the bbox), meshes last by distance, hits more than 0.3 m behind
  the world surface last; a click without dragging on an already selected shape cycles. Nearest-first was wrong:
  Crackdown Hero has a ceiling box `SM_226` (Y 10-18.7) over the whole map, and every click from above selected it.
- No `<Double-Button-1>` binding: a quick second click (to cycle, or to start a drag) arrives as a double click, skips
  the ButtonPress handler and jumped the camera. Pivot = middle click or Ctrl+click.
- Box tool in 3D takes its base height from the world depth under the press (and writes it into "Tinggi bawah");
  triangle tool = screen rectangle over triangle centroids (`kam.ke_layar`), red preview after 120 ms idle.
- Test pattern: load the `.pyw` with `SourceFileLoader`, drive `event_generate` with an explicit `state` (0x100 Button1,
  0x1 Shift, 0x4 Control), capture the GL view with `GLFrame.tangkap()` and the window with PrintWindow flag 2 (it
  includes the GL content). Regression run 2026-09-14: pick, drag, Shift-drag, cycle, new box on the floor,
  middle/Ctrl pivot, triangle delete (1,905 previewed = 1,905 deleted), undo, unchanged save byte-identical; the old
  I3Path/I3INS GUI tests still pass with the mirrored denah. Not tested in game.
- **`GLFrame.siap()` re-entrancy** (fixed 2026-09-14): the `update_idletasks()` inside context creation can run the
  scheduled `gambar_sekarang()`, which called `siap()` again and built a second context that the outer call then
  replaced. Display lists made during that nested first frame lived in the lost context and the map upload reused
  their numbers, so the I3INS markers drew map batches scaled to box size (the view covered in one colour). Nested
  calls are now refused. The collision editor never showed it because it builds lists only after a file is open; its
  GUI regression run gives the same results after the fix. The I3INS editor also rebuilds its lists when `gl.ctx` changes.
- Embedded textures: the old `World\Crackdown\Crackdown_World.I3S` keeps all 26 textures (lightmap included; 21 DXT1,
  5 DXT5) as internal `i3Texture` objects whose data is a whole `.i3i`; `_tekstur` reads them with
  `baca_i3i(data=...)` under the key `#tertanam<idx>`, so that map renders textured too.

## The login bot -- `BOT PB\` (WinForms, 2026-09-18/19)

A decompiled Point Blank login bot the user owns (`BOT PB.sln`, .NET Framework 4.8, x86, build output in
`bin\Debug`). It was a console program; the window version added 2026-09-18 keeps the bot logic and routes
`Console.WriteLine` / `Console.ReadLine` through `UiConsole.cs` (`Ui.Pasang()` swaps `Console.Out`/`Console.In`;
every `ReadLine` waits on a `BlockingCollection<string>` that the buttons fill with `Ui.Jawab`).

- State machine: `Program.Tarefa()` switches on **`Program.Result - 1`**, so every case label is the enum member
  *one below* the state that triggers it (`case Result.ListarSala` runs when `Program.Result == EntrarNaSala`).
  Packet handlers in `Conection\Packages\PROTOCOL\REQ\` set `Program.Result` to drive it. Each received packet is
  handled on its own thread (`ClientSync.ProcessorPacote` -> `new Thread(receivePacket.Run)`), so a handler blocking
  in `Console.ReadLine` (the login prompt) does not stall reception.
- Flow after login: `BASE_USER_ENTER_REQ` -> CHANNEL prompt -> `BASE_CHANNEL_ANNOUNCE_REQ` -> LOBBY_ENTER_ACK ->
  `LOBBY_ENTER_REQ` -> **DECISION prompt** (1 = chat bot, 2 = rooms) -> LOBBY_GET_ROOMLIST_ACK ->
  `LOBBY_GET_ROOMLIST_REQ` -> ROOM prompt -> LOBBY_JOIN_ROOM_ACK. So "Masuk room" is only reachable through
  **Decision 2 (room)**; an empty room list sends the bot to the chat prompt instead
  ("no rooms created you will be redirected to chat").
- **"Tombol masuk room tidak berfungsi" (user, 2026-09-19) -- cause found and proved**: the window enabled its
  action buttons from `Program.Result`, but `LOBBY_CHATTING_REQ.Receptado()` set `Program.Result = Result.Chat`
  for **every chat line of every other player in the lobby**. Proof by building the pre-fix sources in a scratch
  copy and driving `Form1.timer1_Tick` by reflection: with `Result = EntrarNaSala` the "Masuk room" button is
  enabled, and after feeding one crafted chat packet `Result` is `Chat` and the button is disabled; the same kills
  "Decision 2 (room)", which is why the user could never even reach the room list.
- **Fix**: `Ui` now tracks the question the bot is actually blocked on. `Ui.Tanyakan(Tanya.X)` is called right
  before each `Console.ReadLine` (9 prompts in `Tarefa` plus User/Password in `BASE_SCHANNEL_SERVER_REQ`), and
  `UiReader.ReadLine()` publishes it as `Ui.Pertanyaan` for the duration of the wait. `timer1_Tick` enables
  buttons from `Ui.Pertanyaan`, never from `Program.Result`, so incoming packets cannot grey a button out.
  Other players' chat no longer touches `Program.Result` (only the bot's own echo still runs `Comanndos`).
  "Masuk lobby" / "Daftar room" poke `Program.Result` directly, which is lost when `Tarefa` sits in a `ReadLine`,
  so they are enabled only while no question is pending; "Kirim chat" / "Chat GM" fall back to sending
  `LOBBY_CHATTING_ACK` directly when the bot is not at the chat prompt. The Decision answer is read with
  `int.TryParse` (a blank answer used to throw `FormatException` on the `Tarefa` thread = process killed by
  Windows, which is what pressing "Keluar dari server" at that prompt did), and the ROOM / CHANNEL PASSWORD /
  AUTO-KILL inner loops now check `Program.Sesi` after each answer so a disconnect cannot leave an old `Tarefa`
  thread waiting on the queue and stealing the next session's first answer.
  Originals in `BOT PB\_backup_sebelum_perbaikan_tombol\`.
- **Test rig** (`scratchpad/uji_alur_room.py`): a fake server on 127.0.0.1:39190 that speaks the plain inbound
  framing `[u16 len][u16 opcode][body]` (`ClientSync` reads the length then `len + 2` bytes, and the opcode is the
  first u16 of that buffer; outbound packets are encrypted, but the bot logs `Send: <class>` so that is what the
  test asserts). It walks 2049 -> 2564 -> 2566 -> 2049 -> 2580 -> 2574 -> 3080 -> 3074, injects a 3093 chat from
  "PemainLain" while the bot waits for CHANNEL, for DECISION and for ROOM ID, and ends with a real click on
  "Masuk room": all buttons stay enabled and the bot sends `LOBBY_JOIN_ROOM_ACK` with room id 7. Window automation
  notes: WinForms classes are `WindowsForms10.EDIT.app...` / `.BUTTON.` / `.RICHEDIT...`, `BM_CLICK` works
  cross-process, and a `NumericUpDown` is driven by `WM_SETTEXT` on the Edit that sits just left of its button
  (its `Value` getter validates the typed text). `scratchpad/uji_tombol/` is the same check without a server,
  driving `Form1` by reflection. The rig rewrites `bin\Debug\config\settings.ini` (the user's real account is in
  it) and restores it from a backup at the end - always restore it.
- Still true of the bot: a room with a password cannot be joined, `LOBBY_JOIN_ROOM_ACK(id, "")` always sends an
  empty one; room ids must be 0-254 (`numRoom.Maximum` matches).
- **"Di dalam permainan bot tidak muncul dan tidak bergerak" (user, 2026-09-19)**. Two separate things:
  - **Not visible**: `BATTLE_RESPAWN_ACK` (opcode 3337, "I spawn now, this is my loadout": 11 item ids + 1 class
    byte) exists in the sources but **was never sent by anything**. Without it the server never places the
    character in the map, so the bot sits in the room invisible. It is now sent automatically from
    `BATTLE_STARTBATTLE_REQ` right after " * you entered the battle." (checkbox "Auto spawn", `Program.AutoSpawn`)
    and by the new button "Spawn (muncul di map)". The ids moved to `BATTLE_RESPAWN_ACK.Item` / `.Kelas` and can be
    overridden from `config/settings.ini` line `Spawn=` (11 ids + class, comma separated) when the server's item ids
    differ; defaults are the stock `100003445,601002003,702001001,803007001,904007002,0,1001001005,1001002006,`
    `1102003001,0,1006003043,9` (1001001005 / 1001002006 are red/blue characters, the same `1001`+team+id shape as
    `Character.i3RegXML`'s `_IDNumber`).
  - **Not moving**: the bot has **no movement packet at all** - the only coordinates it ever sends are the three
    hardcoded floats inside `BATTLE_DEATH_ACK`. The opcode for a position update is unknown and cannot be guessed.
    Tool added for finding it: `ClientSync`'s unknown-opcode branch now calls `Program.CatatTakDikenal`, which logs
    the opcode, the length and up to 70 bytes of the payload as hex, **at most 3 times per opcode** (reset on
    disconnect by `Putus`). Inbound packets are plaintext (only outbound are rotated by `Use.Encrypt`), so those
    lines are directly readable. Plan: park the bot in a room, let a real player run around, and the server's
    position broadcast shows up as an unknown opcode; the client->server opcode is that number **minus one**
    (the convention holds throughout: 3079/3080 lobby enter, 3081/3082 join room, 3333/3334 start battle,
    3337/3338 respawn, 3354/3355 death).
- `BATTLE_PRESTARTBATTLE_REQ` read the battle-server port with `ReadU()` (**signed** int16), so a port above 32767
  threw `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` inside the handler and `BATTLE_STARTBATTLE_ACK` was never sent - the bot
  would silently fail to enter the battle. Changed to `ReadUH()`.
- Test for all of this: `scratchpad/uji_alur_battle.py` drives the fake server one step further than
  `uji_alur_room.py` (3082 join room -> 3426 ready -> 3349 prestart -> 3334 start) and asserts the bot sends
  `BATTLE_RESPAWN_ACK`, that the manual Spawn button works, and that two unknown opcodes are logged with their hex.
  It runs the exe built into the scratchpad, so the user's own running bot is not disturbed.
- **On the user's real server (2026-09-19)**: the spawn is **accepted** - every `BATTLE_RESPAWN_ACK` the bot sends
  is answered by the server with `BATTLE_RESPAWN_REQ`, and `BATTLE_ROOM_INFO_REQ` / `BATTLE_SENDPING_REQ` follow.
  The character still does not show up for other players, which fits the remaining gap: PB renders a player from
  its position broadcasts, and the bot never sends one. The repeated `BATTLE_RESPAWN_ACK` lines in the user's log
  were the Spawn button being pressed by hand (the auto path is guarded by `room.IsBattle` and fires once); the log
  now says "otomatis" or "lewat tombol" so the two can be told apart.
- **Packet recorder (`Rekam.cs`, 2026-09-19)** - the tool for finding the movement packet. Checkbox "Rekam paket ke
  file" writes every packet to `rekaman\paket_<tanggal>.log` next to the exe: `waktu MASUK|KELUAR opcode len=N : hex`.
  Inbound is logged in `ClientSync.ProcessorPacote` right after the opcode is read (plaintext), outbound in
  `ArrayProcess.AditionalByte` **before** `Use.Encrypt`, so both directions are readable. `Rekam.Rahasia()` hides the
  payload of opcodes **2561** (`BASE_LOGIN_ACK`: user + password in clear) and **2644** (channel password) - the file
  is meant to be handed over for analysis, so credentials must never land in it. Recording stops on disconnect
  (`Putus`). The old "3 or 4 digit opcode" filter around `Program.CatatTakDikenal` is gone, so no unknown opcode is
  missed any more. Test: `scratchpad/uji_rekam.py` (both directions, 2/4/5-digit opcodes, masked login packet).
- What to look for in a recording: a `MASUK` opcode that repeats many times per second while a real player walks,
  whose payload changes smoothly - that is the position broadcast. The packet the bot must send is that opcode
  **minus one**. If nothing of the sort appears while a player moves, the position sync does not run over this TCP
  connection at all (PB also has a separate battle-server endpoint, the IP:port printed by
  `BATTLE_PRESTARTBATTLE_REQ`, which this bot never connects to).
- **The server's own source settles it (2026-09-19)**: the user has the full C# server at
  `HeavyRain\SERVER BLACKLIST V42 EN VERSION\` (`pbserver_auth` / `pbserver_game` / `pbserver_battle` /
  `pbserver_data`, plus `Bin\Release\config\*.ini`). In-battle movement does **not** use the TCP game
  connection at all - it is **UDP to the battle server**, so no amount of TCP recording would ever have shown it.

### Battle UDP protocol (read from `pbserver_battle`)

- Endpoint: `battle.ini` `udpIp` / `udpPort` (192.168.199.239:40009 here); the client learns it from TCP packet
  **3349** (`BATTLE_PRESTARTBATTLE_PAK.cs`), whose real layout is
  `u32 isPreparing | u32 slot | u8 udpType | leaderPublicIP+u16 | leaderLocalIP+u16 | u8 0 |`
  `myPublicIP+u16 | myLocalIP+u16 | u8 0 | battleIP+u16 | u32 UniqueRoomId | u32 gen2` (+35 hitpart bytes when asked).
  The bot used to read only the leader's IP and skip 63 bytes, throwing away exactly the three values it needed.
  `udpType=3` (game.ini) = RELAY: the server relays, so `dedicationSlot` must be **255**.
- Header, 13 bytes, **plaintext** (`BattleHandler.BeginReceive`):
  `u8 opcode | u8 slot | f32 seconds | u8 round | u16 totalLength | u8 respawnNo | u8 roundNo | u8 accountId | u8 0`.
  Body = bytes 13..totalLength, scrambled by `AllUtils.encrypt(body, totalLength % 6 + 1)` - **the same rotate cipher
  as `Use.Encrypt` on the TCP side**, so the bot reuses it.
- `accountId` is the **low byte of the account id** (`BitConverter.GetBytes(slot._playerId)[0]` in
  `Game_SyncNet.SendUDPPlayerSync`), which the bot already knows from `BASE_LOGIN_REQ`. The battle server stores the
  byte the client sends in opcode 65 as `_playerIdByUser` and the one the game server sends (triggered by the TCP
  `BATTLE_RESPAWN_ACK`!) as `_playerIdByServer`; **sync packets are only relayed when the two match**, which is why
  the spawn packet and the UDP client are both needed.
- Bodies: **65** = `u32 1012 | u32 12 | u32 roomId | u32 gen2 | u8 255` (the version must equal `battle.ini`
  `UDPVersion`, here 1012.12, or `Room.AddPlayer` refuses); server answers **66**. **97** = `u32 roomId | u8 255 |
  u32 gen2` (ping, refreshes `LastPing`). **3** = `[action blocks] u32 roomId | u8 255 | u32 gen2`.
- Action block: `u8 type (0 = USER) | u16 slot | u16 blockLength | u32 flags (Events) | data`, blockLength counts the
  whole block (9 + data). The `Events` flags are read in ascending order, each adding a fixed record:
  `1 ActionState` 4 bytes, `2 Animation` u16, **`4 PosRotation` 6 x u16 = X, Y, Z as half floats + camX, camY, area**,
  `8 OnLoadObject` u8+u16, `0x20 RadioChat`, `0x40 WeaponSync`, ... (`network/actions/user/a*_*.cs`).
  Despite the field names, `a4_PositionSync._rotationX/Y/Z` **are the position** (`BattleHandler.cs:466` stores them
  as the player's `Half3 Position`).
- `BattleUdp.cs` in the bot implements all of it: opcode 65 on entering the battle, opcode 3 every 100 ms with
  ActionState+Animation+PosRotation, opcode 97 once a second, plus a reader that decrypts incoming relays and logs
  other players' coordinates (`Ikuti` then anchors the bot on the last player seen, `Gerak` walks it in a 3 m circle).
  Checkbox "Gerak di map (sinkron UDP battle)" (`UdpGerak` in settings.ini), stopped by `Putus`.
### Memicu animasi dari server -- mekanismenya ADA, artinya belum diketahui (2026-09-30)

User: "Ada tidak ya untuk trigger gerakan animasi ?? melalui command dari server ??"

**Server battle tidak meneruskan paket mentah.** `BattleHandler.WriteActionBytes` membaca tiap blok
aksi medan per medan lalu menulis ulang semuanya::

    s.GoBack(2);
    s.writeH((ushort)(result.Length + 9));   // panjang DIHITUNG ULANG
    s.writeD((uint)ac._flags);               // kata flags DITULIS ULANG
    s.writeB(result);

`CheckDataFlags` membuktikan server memang sudah mengubah flags saat berjalan
(`ac._flags -= Events.WeaponSync`). Jadi menambahkan sebuah medan ke paket pemain lain bukan hal
yang mustahil secara format.

**Dan server sudah MEMBUAT blok aksi sendiri atas nama sebuah slot.**
`Packet4Creator.getCode4SyncData`::

    syncType 4: writeC(STAGEINFO_CHARA) writeH(slot) writeH(11) writeD(256)    writeH(life)
                                                                 Events.LifeSync
    syncType 5: writeC(USER)            writeH(slot) writeH(11) writeD(524288) ...
                                                                 SufferingDamage

`syncType 4` dikirim tiap ~2,5 detik dari `Room.SyncInfo` untuk tiap pemain yang nyawanya berubah,
`syncType 5` dari `DamageManager.SetHitEffect`. Bentuk `tipe + slot + panjang + flags + isi` itu
sudah diproduksi server dan diterima client. Maka bentuk untuk animasi tinggal::

    writeC(USER)  writeH(slot)  writeH(11)  writeD(2)  writeH(nilai)
                                      9+2   Events.Animation

`Events.Animation = 2` ditangani `a2_unk`: **satu `ushort`**, dibaca lalu ditulis lagi tanpa
ditafsirkan sama sekali.

**Yang belum diketahui: arti `ushort` itu bagi client.** Enum-nya menamainya `Animation`; baris log
bawaan di `a2_unk` sendiri menyebutnya *"moving the crosshair position"* - tebakan penulis server,
tidak pernah diuji. Tidak ada apa pun di server yang menafsirkannya.

**Di lobby tidak ada jalan sama sekali**: nol hit untuk "anim" di seluruh
`pbserver_game/global/serverpacket/`. Satu-satunya pemicu animasi server->client yang terbukti tetap
`BASE_RANK_UP_PAK` (2614), isinya cuma `rank, rank, exp` - client memainkan upacaranya sendiri dan
paket itu tidak bisa menyebut animasi mana pun.

#### Pencatat `logAnimasi` -- baca dulu sebelum menulis

Dipasang 30/09/2026 supaya artinya bisa diukur dari client sungguhan, bukan ditebak.
`pbserver_battle/data/sync/LogAnimasi.cs` + `battle.ini` `logAnimasi=false` (bawaan MATI).

  yang melompat ke angka tetap saat lompat/jongkok/reload = animasi.

- **Berhenti sendiri di 1000 baris** dan menulis laju baris/detik. Kalau batas itu tercapai dalam
  hitungan detik, itu sendiri sudah jawabannya.
- Seluruh jalurnya di belakang `if (!Aktif)`, jadi permainan normal cuma membayar satu cek bool.

keluaran keduanya untuk anim 0 / 1 / 0x1234 / 0xFFFF - **byte identik, 4 dari 4**.
