#### Percobaan pertama: 9 baris lalu senyap - mode NPC memakai jalur paket LAIN

Kamar `Combat with NPC` (Team_DeathMatch + Challenge, TD_PORTAKABA, `Used spawn count: 15`).
Hasilnya cuma 9 baris, semuanya dalam 60 milidetik di awal pertandingan, lalu tidak ada apa-apa
lagi selama ~2 menit bermain::

    [20.36.34.292] slot 13 anim 8176 (0x1FF0) <- NILAI BARU  state 00-08-22-00
    [20.36.34.295] slot 0  anim 8176 (0x1FF0)                state 00-08-91-00  pos -8,4/0,6/-31,5
    ... slot 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 15 - semuanya 8176

Isinya sendiri sudah menarik: **nilainya SAMA (8176) untuk kesembilan slot** dan hanya slot 0 yang
punya posisi - jadi slot 0 pemain sungguhan, sisanya NPC. `ActionState` justru BERBEDA per slot
(`00-08-22-00`, `00-08-91-00`, `00-08-11-00`), yang menunjukkan medan itu memang per-karakter
sedangkan 8176 lebih mirip nilai awal/tetap.

**Tapi "senyap" itu ternyata bukan berarti nilainya tetap.** Sebabnya:
`Packet132Creator.getBaseData132` - jalur mode bot, opcode **131/132** - menyalin blok USER
**bulat-bulat** tanpa memisah medannya::

    ac._flags = (Events)p.readUD();
    ac._data  = p.readB(ac._lengthData - 9);
    s.writeD((uint)ac._flags);
    s.writeB(ac._data);          // tidak ada a1/a2/a4/a8 sama sekali

Jadi kail di `getNewActions` (opcode 3/4) tidak pernah jalan begitu pertandingan NPC berjalan.
Kesembilan baris itu datang dari paket opcode 3 di awal saja.

**Pelajaran rancangan, dan ini yang diperbaiki**: pencatat yang hanya menulis saat nilai BERUBAH
membuat "tidak ada baris baru" punya dua arti yang tidak bisa dibedakan - nilainya tetap, atau
flag-nya memang tidak dikirim. Sekarang **setiap blok dihitung** dan ringkasannya ditulis tiap 15
detik::

    == ringkasan 20:41:03 (120 detik) : 7412 blok aksi, 0 (0,0%) membawa medan Animation,
       9 perubahan, 1 nilai berbeda
       jalur  : aksi 9, bot 7403
       flags  : 0x7=5200, 0xF=2203, 0x2007=9
       CATATAN: tidak satu pun blok membawa flag Animation - client tidak mengirim medan ini
       di jalur paket tersebut.

Ditambah kail **hanya-catat** di `Packet132Creator` (`LogAnimasi.CatatMentah` mengurai medannya
sendiri dari `ac._data`; byte yang ditulis tidak disentuh), supaya kamar NPC maupun kamar biasa
sama-sama terpantau. `room` di jalur itu null - kuncinya jadi per slot saja, cukup untuk uji satu
kamar.

Bukti relay tidak berubah diperluas ke KEDUA jalur: bangun sumber pra-perubahan ke folder kedua,
lalu banding keluaran `WriteActionBytes` **dan** `getBaseData132` untuk anim 0 / 1 / 0x1234 /
0xFFFF - **byte identik, 8 dari 8**. `UjiAnim.cs` jadi **21 pemeriksaan**.

Binari kedua terpasang 30/09/2026: `PBBattleServer.exe` **112.128 B**, md5
`778f932394212dd3afa4b6467e34cb99`. Cadangan ASLI (105.472 B, md5 `d2a23541...`) tetap yang di
`_backup_binari_sebelum_log_animasi/` - dicek hash-nya dulu supaya tidak tertimpa binari tahap
pertama.

Jebakan di sisi uji: `battle.ini` sungguhan sudah `logAnimasi=true`, jadi kelompok uji ke-2
terlanjur membuat berkas log dan kelompok ke-3 yang menghapus foldernya menemukan `_berkas`
masih terisi - nol berkas, tiga pemeriksaan gagal. `ResetPencatat()` mengosongkan keadaan statis
pencatat di awal tiap kelompok.

#### Percobaan kedua (kamar biasa, 2 pemain): medannya DIKIRIM, tapi NILAINYA TETAP

Kamar `Feel The Headshot!!` (Team_DeathMatch, SWEETCRACKDOWN), 2 client di satu PC, 3 menit main::

    1975 blok aksi, 1494 (75,6%) membawa medan Animation, 2 perubahan, 1 nilai berbeda
    nilai : 8176 (0x1FF0)

Kedua "perubahan" itu cuma kemunculan pertama slot 0 dan slot 1. Jadi hasilnya tegas:
**medan Events.Animation DIKIRIM terus-menerus oleh client V1 ini, tapi isinya konstan 0x1FF0** -
tidak bergerak saat jalan, lompat, tembak, reload, mati, apa pun.

Sebaran kata flags-nya (dari ringkasan yang sama) menunjukkan medan mana yang sebenarnya hidup::

    0x6    1146x  Animation + PosRotation        <- paket paling umum, anim selalu 0x1FF0
    0x47    178x  ActionState + Animation + PosRotation + WeaponSync
    0xD      74x  ActionState + PosRotation + MoveSync
    0x4      70x  PosRotation
    0x5      68x  ActionState + PosRotation
    0x1      66x  ActionState
    0x2045   62x  ActionState + PosRotation + WeaponSync + FireSync

**`ActionState` (flag 1, 4 byte) yang berubah-ubah per karakter**, bukan Animation - di log
terlihat `00-08-22-00`, `00-08-91-00`, `00-08-11-00` untuk slot berbeda pada saat yang sama.
Kode yang dikomentari di `BattleHandler` membongkarnya sebagai medan terkemas
(`all & 3`, `(all >> 2) & 1`, `(all >> 10) & 0xF`, `(all >> 14) & 1`, `(all >> 15) & 1`,
`(all >> 16) & 0xF`, `(all >> 20) & 0xFF`).

Dua bacaan yang TIDAK bisa dipisahkan hanya dengan mendengarkan:

1. medannya memang tidak terpakai di build client ini - menulis apa pun ke situ tidak ada efeknya;
2. medannya SELEKTOR animasi, tapi client cuma pernah mengirim "tidak ada animasi" = 0x1FF0,
   sedangkan penerimanya tetap punya penanganan untuk nilai lain.

#### `animPaksa` -- menimpa nilainya, karena mendengarkan sudah habis

`battle.ini`: `animPaksa=off` (bawaan) | sebuah angka (`0`, `255`, `0x1FF1`) | `sapu`, dengan
`animPaksaDetik=10`. Kalau menyala, nilai yang direlay ke client lain diganti - **panjang bloknya
tidak berubah** (tetap satu ushort), jadi paketnya tetap sah, dan diukur: hanya **2 byte** dari 30
yang berbeda.

Daftar `sapu` sengaja bukan sapuan 65536 kemungkinan melainkan penguji SUSUNAN `0x1FF0`
(`0001 1111 1111 0000`) - mematikan tiap bagiannya satu per satu::

    0x0000 0x0001 0x0010 0x0100 0x1000 0x0FF0 0x2FF0 0x1FF1 0x1F00 0x00F0 0x1FFF 0xFFFF

12 nilai x 10 detik = satu pertandingan 2 menit menutup semuanya, dan tiap pergantian ditulis
`>>> MEMAKSA medan Animation = ... [sapu n/12] mulai HH:MM:SS` di log supaya bisa dicocokkan
dengan apa yang terlihat di layar. Hanya jalur `aksi` (opcode 3/4) yang ditimpa - jalur bot
(131/132) menyalin blok bulat-bulat dan sengaja tidak disentuh.

`UjiAnim.cs` jadi **32 pemeriksaan**; yang baru: `off` tidak menimpa apa pun, angka desimal dan
heksa terbaca, panjang blok tetap, hanya 2 byte berubah, `sapu` memutar 12 nilai lalu berulang,
dan setelan ngawur diabaikan alih-alih meledak. Banding lama-vs-baru dengan `animPaksa=off` tetap
**byte identik, 8 dari 8** di kedua jalur.

Binari ketiga terpasang 30/09/2026: `PBBattleServer.exe` **113.152 B**, md5
`52336e1a366585aa8fe7b8c206d68e4d`. Cadangan asli (105.472 B) tetap di
`_backup_binari_sebelum_log_animasi/`.

#### Percobaan ketiga: ada glitch, tapi belum bisa disebut bukti (2026-09-30)

Sapu 12 nilai dijalankan dua putaran (21.32.19 - 21.35.10) dengan 2 client di satu PC. User:
"kenapa pergerakan lawan dengan saya berbeda ya, kek glitch gitu".

**Log tidak bisa menjawab itu, dan penting tahu kenapa**: nilai yang MASUK dari kedua client
tetap `0x1FF0` sepanjang percobaan (`2 perubahan, 1 nilai berbeda` di tiap ringkasan) - client
tidak pernah mengubah apa yang dia KIRIM hanya karena menerima nilai lain. Jadi log cuma tahu apa
yang dipaksa, bukan apa yang terlihat di layar. Yang bisa menghubungkan keduanya hanya mata user.

Dan ada penjelasan tandingan yang harus disingkirkan lebih dulu: **2 client di satu PC memang
sering desync sendiri**. "Ada glitch saat memaksa" tidak sama dengan "glitch karena memaksa" -
rancangan sapu yang pertama tidak punya pembanding sama sekali, jadi bukti apa pun darinya lemah.

**Rancangan yang menjawab sendiri**, dipasang sesudah itu:

- **Sapu berselang-seling dengan periode KONTROL**: nilai (10 dtk) - tanpa timpa (10 dtk) - nilai
  berikutnya - tanpa timpa, dan seterusnya. Kalau yang terlihat ikut BERDENYUT mengikuti giliran,
  penyebabnya memang medan ini; kalau glitch-nya terus-menerus, itu desync biasa dan medan ini
  tidak bersalah. Tiap giliran ditulis `>>> MEMAKSA ...` / `>>> KONTROL - tidak menimpa apa pun`
  lengkap dengan jamnya.
- **`animPaksaSlot`** (-1 = semua): isi satu slot saja, supaya SATU karakter ditimpa dan satunya
  lagi jadi pembanding yang tidak tersentuh. Diuji sampai byte: dengan `animPaksaSlot=1`, blok
  relay slot 0 keluar identik dengan masukannya.

`UjiAnim.cs` jadi **35 pemeriksaan**. Banding lama-vs-baru dengan `animPaksa=off` tetap byte
identik di kedua jalur. Binari keempat: `PBBattleServer.exe` **113.664 B**, md5
`bb817d6377ec391fd3ca1fbd7be93bbc`.

**Pelajaran rancangan percobaan, dan ini yang kedua kalinya di ronde ini**: percobaan tanpa
pembanding menghasilkan pengamatan yang tidak bisa dipakai. Yang pertama - pencatat yang hanya
menulis saat nilai berubah - membuat "senyap" ambigu; yang kedua - sapu tanpa periode kontrol -
membuat "glitch" ambigu. Dua-duanya baru ketahuan sesudah user menjalankannya di game.

#### Tidak perlu diam - dan server ini memang tidak punya AFK-kick

User: "kalau saya idle / diam selama itu, saya bisa-bisa otomatis keluar room". Diperiksa:
**tidak ada AFK-kick otomatis di server ini sama sekali.** Yang ada cuma perintah GM manual
`.kickAFK <jam>` / `.countAFK <jam>` (`pbserver_game/data/chat/AFK_Interaction.cs` ->
`GameManager.KickActiveClient(hours)`), dan patokannya LAMA KONEKSI dalam jam, bukan diam di
pertandingan. Satu-satunya pengusir otomatis yang ada berkaitan dengan hole punching
(`Battle_First_Hole`, 30 detik sebelum battle). Jadi kalau client terlempar karena diam, itu
perilaku client-nya sendiri, bukan server.

Tapi yang lebih penting: **diam memang rancangan yang keliru.** Keluhan aslinya adalah
*pergerakan* yang terlihat aneh, jadi karakter yang diamati harus BERGERAK dengan pola sederhana
dan berulang (lari bolak-balik menyusur dinding). Yang dicari bukan "ada glitch atau tidak",
melainkan apakah glitch-nya **muncul-hilang mengikuti irama 10 detik** giliran MEMAKSA / KONTROL.

Ditambah mode **`animPaksa=denyut:<nilai>`** - satu nilai saja tapi tetap diselingi periode
kontrol, untuk dipakai sesudah sapu menunjuk satu nilai yang mencurigakan. Nilai tetap tanpa
`denyut:` tetap berlaku terus-menerus (berguna nanti, sesudah artinya diketahui).

`UjiAnim.cs` jadi **38 pemeriksaan**; binari kelima `PBBattleServer.exe` **114.176 B**, md5
`d118b31ff5bae92df2fb12814012b965`. Banding lama-vs-baru dengan `animPaksa=off` tetap byte
identik.

#### Percobaan keempat: "karakter menghilang lalu muncul" - menarik, tapi BELUM bukti

18 menit, **52 giliran MEMAKSA + 52 KONTROL**, `animPaksaSlot=-1`. User: "tidak ada pergerakan,
cuma karakter menghilang, lalu muncul tiba-tiba".

Apa yang PASTI dari log:

- **Server tidak mengeluh sama sekali** - nol `BUF ANORMAL`, nol pengecualian, nol peringatan di
  seluruh `logs/battle` selama 18 menit itu. Paket yang ditimpa tetap sah secara susunan.
- **Client tetap tidak mengubah apa yang dia KIRIM**: 2.864 blok, 2.701 (94,3%) membawa medan
  Animation, `1 nilai berbeda` = `0x1FF0`. Menerima nilai lain tidak membuatnya mengirim lain.

Apa yang BELUM pasti, dan ini intinya: **apakah hilang-munculnya mengikuti irama 10 detik.** Dua
penjelasan masih sama-sama cocok - (a) client menolak nilai yang tidak dikenalnya lalu berhenti
memperbarui karakter itu, atau (b) desync biasa 2 client di satu PC. Periode 10 detik terlalu
pendek untuk dibedakan dengan mata tanpa stopwatch, dan itu kelemahan rancangan, bukan
kelemahan pengamatan user.

Putaran penentu berikutnya karena itu **satu nilai, 30 detik menyala / 30 detik mati**::

    animPaksa=denyut:0
    animPaksaDetik=30

"Hilang persis setengah menit lalu kembali persis setengah menit" tidak mungkin disalahartikan
sebagai desync. Ini murni ubahan ini, tanpa bangun ulang.

#### Bug di pencatatnya sendiri: 8 menit baris lenyap diam-diam

Berkas `logs/animasi/2026-09-30--21-55-19.log` dimulai pada 22:03:53 **tanpa baris judul** -
delapan menit pertama hilang. Sebabnya: `Mulai()` cuma jalan sekali (saat `_berkas == null`),
sedangkan `Tulis()` menelan semua pengecualian. Begitu folder `logs/animasi` lenyap di tengah
jalan - dalam hal ini karena pembersihan sesudah menjalankan `UjiAnim` di `Bin/Release` -
setiap penulisan gagal tanpa suara sampai ada yang membuat foldernya lagi.

Untungnya tidak ada data yang benar-benar hilang: tiap baris juga masuk `logs/battle` lewat
`Logger`, dan dari situlah ke-52 giliran itu dihitung. Tapi pencatat yang bisa mati diam-diam
adalah jebakan untuk ronde berikutnya, jadi `Tulis()` sekarang membuat ulang foldernya dan
melaporkan kegagalan PERTAMA lewat `Logger.error`. `UjiAnim.cs` jadi **43 pemeriksaan**, termasuk
kelompok 9 yang menghapus folder log di tengah jalan lalu menuntut baris berikutnya tetap tercatat
di berkas yang sama.

Binari keenam: `PBBattleServer.exe` **114.176 B**, md5 `92d9a16242dc5dd6b38413b61bb37cf2`.

#### KESIMPULAN: medan Animation MATI di client V1, dan semuanya DIKEMBALIKAN (2026-09-30)

Putaran penentu - `animPaksa=denyut:0`, **30 detik menyala / 30 detik mati, 10 menit,
10 giliran paksa** - hasilnya nihil. User: "tidak ada pergerakan sama sekali". Dengan irama
sepanjang itu desync tidak mungkin menyamarkan pola, jadi hilang-muncul yang terlihat di putaran
sapu 10 detik sebelumnya memang **desync biasa 2 client di satu PC**, bukan akibat menimpa.

Ringkasan seluruh ronde, semuanya terukur:

| | |
|---|---|
| medan dikirim client | 94-97% blok aksi, di **semua** sesi |
| nilainya | `0x1FF0` - **satu nilai, tidak pernah berubah** dalam ~8.000 blok |
| server saat ditimpa | nol galat, nol `BUF ANORMAL`, 52 giliran/18 menit |
| client saat ditimpa | tidak bereaksi, dan tidak mengubah apa yang dia kirim |

Jadi **`Events.Animation` tidak bisa dipakai memicu animasi dari server di client V1 ini.**
Yang masih hidup dan belum dicoba: **`ActionState` (flag 1, 4 byte)** - di log jelas berbeda-beda
per karakter pada saat yang sama (`00-08-22-00`, `00-08-91-00`, `00-08-11-00`) dan `BattleHandler`
sudah punya pembongkar bit-nya dalam bentuk komentar.

**Dikembalikan penuh atas permintaan user.** Terverifikasi satu per satu:

- 5 berkas sumber (`a2_unk.cs`, `Config.cs`, `BattleHandler.cs`, `Packet132Creator.cs`, `.csproj`)
  md5-identik dengan cadangan; `LogAnimasi.cs` dihapus; nol jejak `LogAnimasi`/`animPaksa`/
  `logAnimasi` tersisa di seluruh sumber dan config.
- `Bin/Release/PBBattleServer.exe` kembali **105.472 B, md5 `d2a23541ccad59aeaa908a2d0b7f675a`**
  (binari 22/09). `PBCoreData.dll`, `PBGameServer.exe`, `PBAuthServer.exe` tidak pernah disentuh.
- `battle.ini` **byte-identik** dengan aslinya. Penting: tulisan ulang Python saya sempat mengubah
  akhir-barisnya dari **CRLF jadi LF** - kalau hanya barisnya yang dihapus, berkasnya akan tetap
  berbeda 25 baris. Diff dulu, lalu kembalikan berkasnya utuh.
- Bangun ulang dari sumber yang sudah dikembalikan menghasilkan relay yang **identik byte per
  byte** dengan binari pra-percobaan (uji `--hex-saja`, 8 dari 8).

Seluruh percobaan disimpan di `_hasil_log_animasi_dibatalkan/` - `LogAnimasi.cs`, kelima berkas
yang ditambal, `UjiAnim.cs` (43 pemeriksaan), binari ber-log, dan `log_percobaan/` berisi kedua
log mentahnya. Kalau `ActionState` nanti dikerjakan, kerangkanya tinggal dipakai lagi.

#### Kalau ternyata itu memang animasi: jalur command-nya

Sudah ditelusuri dan ketiga potongannya ada:

1. **Perintah chat** di `pbserver_game/global/clientpacket/Base/BASE_CHATTING_REC.cs` - polanya
   `gantirank` (baris 1144, `(int)player.access >= 6`).
2. **Kanal game -> battle**: `Battle_SyncNet.LoadPacket` menerima opcode **1** (RespawnSync),
   **2** (RemovePlayerSync), **3** (round) dari `Game_SyncNet`. Rantai opcode 1 sudah terbukti
   jalan di game, jadi menambah opcode 4 adalah perubahan sebentuk.
   (Catatan: `Game_SyncNet.SendHPMortalIndividual` menulis opcode **40** ke port UDP battle, tapi
   switch di `BattleHandler` tidak punya `case 40` - kode mati, jangan dijadikan contoh.)
3. **Penyuntik blok**: satu `ObjectHitInfo` bertipe baru di `Packet4Creator.getCode4SyncData`,
   sebentuk dengan syncType 4/5 yang sudah ada.

- Verified by `scratchpad/uji_udp.py`, whose UDP server **reimplements the server's own parsing** (header split,
  `AllUtils.decrypt`, action-block walk): every packet the bot sends parses cleanly - 65 with version 1012.12,
  roomId, gen2, dedication 255, slot and the account-id byte; 3 with a 27-byte USER block, flags 0x7 and a sane
  half-float position; 97 ping - and a relayed position the fake server sends back is decoded by the bot to exactly
  X 10.50 / Y 2.00 / Z -7.25.
- **First run against the real server (2026-09-19)**: the bot is fully registered - the battle server **relays the
  real player's position to it** (` * posisi pemain slot 0: X -31.92 Y 4.93 Z -3.52` and so on, Y 4.70 being the
  floor), and the relay loop only sends to players whose `AccountIdIsValid()` holds, so the TCP spawn and the UDP
  handshake both took. Relaying the bot's own packets is not gated by the respawn counters (`RespawnIsValid` is
  never called) and `CheckDataFlags` only touches `WeaponSync`, so nothing else blocks it server-side.
- **Mimic mode** (`BattleUdp.Tiru`, on by default): since the bot receives the real client's action blocks, it keeps
  the last one whose flags are a subset of `ActionState|Animation|PosRotation|OnLoadObject` (0xF) as a template and
  re-sends it with only the slot and the three position half-floats replaced - so the block's length, flag set and
  state bytes are exactly what a real client produces. The round byte is likewise mirrored from received packets
  (it used to be a constant 0), each new flag combination is logged once (` * bentuk paket client: bendera 0x...`),
  and UDP packets now go into the recorder too (`UDP-K` / `UDP-M` lines).
  `uji_udp.py` proves it: after the fake server relays a block with flags 0xF, 30 bytes and state `AA BB CC DD`, the
  bot's next packet carries flags 0xF, 30 bytes, the same state bytes, its own slot, and a position within 6 m of
  the player it is following.
- **In game 2026-09-19 (user's screenshot)**: the bot's character is visible and moves. It circles the player because
  `Ikuti` anchors on the last player seen and `Gerak` walks a 3 m circle; `UdpIkuti` / `UdpMutar` / `UdpJari` /
  `UdpJeda` in settings.ini change that.
- **Shooting** (`BattleUdp.Tembak`, checkbox "Tembak pemain yang diikuti", off by default). The shot is one USER
  block with flags `ActionState|Animation|PosRotation|FireSync|NormalDamage` = 0xA007, 75 bytes:
  `a2000_FireSync` = `u16 shotId | u16 shotIndex | u16 camX | u16 camY | u16 camZ | u32 itemId` (14 bytes), then
  `a8000_NormalHitData` = `u8 count` + per hit `u32 hitInfo | u16 boomInfo | u16 weaponInfo | u8 equipSlot |
  3xf32 bullet start | 3xf32 bullet end` (33 bytes). `hitInfo` packs `ObjectType (2 bits, 1 = User) |
  victim << 2 | hitPart << 11 | HitType << 17 | damage << 21` (`AllUtils.getHitType` / `getHitWho` / `getHitPart` /
  `getHitHelmet` / `getHitDamageNORMAL`), and `weaponInfo` = `weaponNumber << 6 | weaponClass`. The weapon fields
  come from the spawn loadout's primary item by inverting `AllUtils.createItemId`: 100003445 -> slot 0 (PRIM),
  class 3 (Assault in **the server's** ClassType enum, which differs from the bot's own), number 445.
  Settings: `Tembak`, `TembakDamage` (0 = fire effect only, no damage), `TembakJeda`, `TembakBagian` (2 body,
  29 headshot), `SenjataItem`.
  Server-side gate worth remembering: damage is applied only when `pl.RespawnLogicIsValid()` holds
  (`_respawnByServer == _respawnByLogic`), and every extra TCP `BATTLE_RESPAWN_ACK` bumps `_respawnByLogic`, so
  **pressing the Spawn button repeatedly can desync those counters and silently drop all damage** - spawn once.
  `uji_udp.py` step 6 checks the whole block field by field with the server's own decoders: flags 0xA007, 75-byte
  block, item 100003445, victim slot, damage 30, part 2, class 3 / number 445 / slot 0, bullet end = player position.
- **Walking the map's AI path** (the user's suggestion, 2026-09-19): instead of circling, the bot now follows
  `World\<Map>\Path.i3Path` - the same file `i3path.py` edits. `JalurAI.cs` is a small C# reader for it: parse the
  I3R2 object table (0x20 count, 0x24 table offset, 28-byte entries with u64 offset/size), find the object holding
  the `GPT1` chunk, read `u32 bufferRawId | u32 points | u32 links` after it, take the buffer object at
  `rawId & 0xFFFF - 1`, then read 88-byte points (`+4` x/y/z) and 76-byte links (`+0` 1 = two-way, `+8` from,
  `+12` to) and build the neighbour lists from the links rather than trusting the stored adjacency table.
  Axes match the battle position packets exactly (X/Z horizontal, Y height), so path coordinates go straight into
  `PosRotation`. All `World\*\Path.i3Path` are loaded once and the map is chosen automatically: the one whose
  nearest point is closest to the player the bot can see - no mapId table needed (the server source has none).
  Walking: step towards the target point at `Kecepatan` m/s, on arrival pick the next neighbour - the one nearest the
  player when following, otherwise a random one that is not where it came from. Settings: `PakaiJalur`,
  `JalurFolder`, `Kecepatan`; the status bar shows `jalur titik <dari>-><ke>`.
  Checked against `i3path.py` on `World\BurningHall\Path.i3Path` (146 points, 237 links): same count, same
  coordinates to 0.002, **same neighbour list for every single point**, and `uji_udp.py` re-run with that file next
  to the exe shows the bot walking real path positions instead of the circle.
- **Patrol, auto-respawn and the map panel** (user, 2026-09-19: "bergerak sesuai keinginan BOT, jangan mengelilingi
  saya", "saat bot mati usahakan respawn lagi", "tampilkan option pembacaan map di winform"):
  - `BattleUdp.Ikuti` now defaults to **false**, so the bot patrols the whole path on its own (random neighbour that
    is not where it came from) and its starting point is a random path node instead of the one nearest the player.
    With it on, it walks toward the player through the corridors as before. Shooting is independent of it - it only
    needs a player position from a relayed packet, so a patrolling bot still fires.
  - `PilihJalur()` picks the map from `MapPilihan` (the window's dropdown) first, then the single loaded path, then
    the one nearest a seen player - so a patrolling bot no longer needs to see anyone before it can start walking.
  - **Auto-respawn**: `BATTLE_DEATH_REC` now reads every victim in the packet and recognises the bot's own slot -
    the victim byte is wrapped, `Use.VictmSlot(victm, 1) = (48 + victm) & 15`. On its own death it sets
    `BattleUdp.Mati` (which stops the shooting) and calls `Program.RespawnNanti(alasan)`, a background thread that
    waits `RespawnJeda` seconds (checking `Program.Sesi` so a disconnect cancels it) and sends `BATTLE_RESPAWN_ACK`
    again - the same packet the real client sends, which is also what makes the game server re-issue `RespawnSync`
    to the battle server so damage and sync start being accepted again.
  - **Window panel "Peta dan gerak bot"** (new `grpPeta`, the form grew to 1004x842): folder World + "Pilih..." +
    "Baca jalur map", a map dropdown ("(otomatis)" or a specific map), a green line showing the loaded path
    (`BurningHall: 146 titik | X -28.1..27.3 ...`), "Pakai jalur AI map", the radio pair "Bot jalan sendiri (patroli
    map)" / "Ikuti pemain terdekat", Kecepatan, "Respawn otomatis saat bot mati" and its delay. All of it is saved to
    settings.ini (`JalurFolder`, `JalurMap`, `PakaiJalur`, `UdpIkuti`, `Kecepatan`, `AutoRespawn`, `RespawnJeda`) and
    the paths are read once at window load.
  - `uji_udp.py` steps 7-9 cover it: the map list reads BurningHall and the log says "patroli sendiri"; over 5 s the
    bot's own position packets move 9.2 m and reach 10.9-19.9 m from the player (proof it is not circling); and a
    crafted `BATTLE_DEATH_REC` whose victim resolves to the bot's slot produces " * bot mati (dibunuh slot 5)"
    followed by the automatic `BATTLE_RESPAWN_ACK`.
- **Standing still and facing the player** (user, 2026-09-19: "ada sesi dia diam, buatkan optionnya", "buat bot
  menghadap ke player, jangan membelakangi player"):
  - `BattleUdp.Diam` (checkbox "Diam di tempat (berhenti berjalan)", settings key `Diam`): `HitungPosisi()` returns
    early **after** `PilihJalur()` in the path branch and before the circle fallback, so the bot keeps sending its
    position packet every 100 ms - it stays visible, keeps facing the player and keeps shooting - but stops stepping.
    Unchecking it resumes from where it stood.
  - **Facing**: `pbserver_battle` only relays `camX`/`camY` (`a4_PositionSync`), it never interprets them, so the
    encoding the client uses cannot be read from the server source. The bot therefore **learns it from the real
    player's own packets** at runtime: `CatatContohHadap(bx, bz, cam)` stores (heading from the position delta,
    raw camX) each time a relayed player moves more than 0.25 m, and after 20 samples `PelajariHadap()` tests six
    hypotheses - half float radian, half float radian reversed, half float degree, degree reversed, u16 full circle,
    u16 reversed - taking the circular-mean offset per hypothesis and keeping the one with the lowest mean residual,
    accepted only below 0.45 rad. `HitungHadap()` then writes `atan2(px - X, pz - Z) + geserHadap` (encoded with
    `SandiSudut` in the learned mode) into camX of the position packet - including the mimic-template path, where it
    patches `offPos + 6` - and of the shooting packet. Checkbox "Hadapkan badan ke pemain" (`Hadap`, on by default),
    label `lblHadapInfo` shows the learned mapping and the status bar says "hadap ok"; until it is learned the bot
    simply does not touch camX, so nothing gets worse while it is still collecting samples.
  - `uji_udp.py` steps 10-11: a fake player walking a circle while sending half-radian camX teaches the bot
    ("half radian, geser 0.05 rad, selisih 0.14 rad") and its next packet aims within 0.05 rad of the player; with
    "Diam" checked 22 position packets drift 0.000 m and the bot keeps sending them, and after unchecking it moves
    6.70 m again.
  - **In game 2026-09-19 (user's screenshot)**: the bot does face the player, so the self-calibration works against
    the real client. Two follow-ups the same evening: the character looked like it was floating, and they asked for a
    button plus the **F5** key for the stand-still toggle.
- **Bot height and the F5 hotkey** (user, 2026-09-19: "posisi bot bisa di turunkan sedikit lagi, soalnya kelihatan
  melayang", "buatkan tombol fungsi diam di tempat, kalau bisa fungsinya tombol keyboard F5"):
  - `BattleUdp.GeserY` (default **-0.5 m**) is added to Y through the private `Ykirim` property, which is what all
    three position writes use (mimic template, plain packet, shooting packet) plus the bullet start and the status
    bar. Raw `Y` stays the path/anchor height, so walking logic is untouched. Spinner "Tinggi bot (m)" in `grpPeta`
    (-5..+5, step 0.1, live) and settings key `GeserY`, written and read with InvariantCulture.
    Why an offset is needed: `.i3Path` points sit a median 0.25 m above the map surface, and the real client's own Y
    for a standing player is only about 0.23 m above the floor - but the exact gap depends on the map, so it is a
    knob rather than a constant. No map mesh for BurningHall/Library is in the project, so it cannot be computed.
  - **F5** is a Windows hotkey (`RegisterHotKey(Handle, 0xB0D1, 0, VK_F5)` in `PasangHotkey()` from `OnLoad`,
    `WM_HOTKEY` in an overridden `WndProc`, `UnregisterHotKey` in `OnFormClosing`) - **not** `KeyPreview`, because the
    point is to work while the game window has focus. It and the new button `btnDiam` both just flip
    `chkDiam.Checked`, so all three routes share one code path and the button text follows the state
    ("Diam di tempat (F5)" / "Jalan lagi (F5)"). A failed registration (another program owns F5) is logged and the
    window button still works. Note the trade-off: while the bot runs, the game itself no longer receives F5.
  - The window grew to **1004x898** and `grpPeta` to 980x166 (new row at y=128).
  - `uji_udp.py` steps 12-13: the button stops the bot and its text flips; typing -1,50 into the spinner drops the
    Y sent by exactly 1.00 m with X/Z unchanged; the bot logs "tombol F5 siap", the test's own `RegisterHotKey(F5)`
    is refused (proof the bot holds it), and a posted `WM_HOTKEY` sets it walking again (8.6 m).
    **Windows here is Indonesian, so `NumericUpDown` parses a comma as the decimal separator** - the test reads the
    box's current text to find the separator instead of assuming a dot. Two test-harness bugs fixed while at it:
    a leftover `BOT PB.exe` from an aborted run polluted the fake server's UDP stream (the rig now kills leftovers
    first), and step 6's local `kelas` shadowed the `kelas()` window helper for every later step.


## Ranked mode (`room.BattleAce`) -- the server's weapon progression (2026-09-19)

The user's own feature in `SERVER BLACKLIST V42 EN VERSION\`: in a Ranked room the player's primary weapon is
replaced with a random, stronger one each time their kill count hits a threshold, and the same weapon must come
back on every respawn. A room becomes Ranked when `LOBBY_CREATE_ROOM_REC` sees `room_type == 13`
(`room.special = 2; room.BattleAce = true`); `/` chat commands in `BASE_CHATTING_REC` toggle it too.

Flow: `Net_Room_Death.RegistryFragInfos` (per frag, after `killer.allKills++`) ->
`Weapon_List_Ranked.Load_Weapon_Ranked(killer, player, frag)` -> `A_3415_PAK(slotId, account)` to that player;
then `BATTLE_RESPAWN_REC.CheckEquipment` decides the loadout of every respawn.
Weapon ids per tier live in `Bin\Release\data\weapon\rankedweaponlist.ini`
(`Assault`..`Assault9`, `SubMachine`..`9`, `Sniper`..`9`, `Shotgun`..`9`, `Mg`..`9`, `Special`; 2-21 ids each).
Thresholds and tiers, unchanged by the repair: kill **3,6** -> tier 1, **9,11** -> 2, **14,17** -> 3, **21** -> 4,
**25** -> 5, **28** -> 6, **33,37** -> 7, **43** -> 8, **50** -> 9, **55** -> `Special`.

Bugs found and fixed (originals in `_backup_sebelum_perbaikan_ranked\`; all four projects build clean with
VS 2026's MSBuild -- the .NET 4.0 MSBuild in `C:\Windows\Microsoft.NET\Framework` cannot, it rejects
`langversion=preview`; build to the scratchpad, `OutputPath` points at the live `Bin\Release`):

- **The respawn handler re-rolled the weapon on every death** (`BATTLE_RESPAWN_REC.CheckEquipment`), from five
  hardcoded ids below 55 kills and from `Special` above, so a player lost the weapon they had just earned the
  moment anyone killed them - the exact thing the user reported. Now the weapon lives in the new
  **`SLOT.AceWeapon`** (int, cleared by `SLOT.ResetSlot()`, i.e. one battle): the first spawn rolls it once
  (`Weapon_List_Ranked.SenjataAwal()`, tier 1), every later respawn simply re-applies it, and only
  `Load_Weapon_Ranked` changes it.
- **`Weapon_List_Ranked` wrote the weapon to the wrong object**: it set `player._equip._primary` (the Account),
  but `BATTLE_RESPAWN_REC` does `slot._equip = equip` with a **new** object built from the client's packet, so
  after the first respawn `slot._equip` and `account._equip` are different objects and the battle never saw the
  award. `Pakai(slot, player, weapon)` now writes `slot.AceWeapon`, `slot._equip._primary` and
  `player._equip._primary`, then sends the 3415 packet.
- **`int caseSwitch = rnd.Next(1, 4)`** gives 1..3 only, so `case 4` (Shotgun) and `default` (Mg) were dead code:
  two of the five weapon classes could never be awarded.
- **`Assaultx3` .. `Assaultx9` read `values2[...]`** instead of `values3..values9`, so every assault award from
  tier 3 upward handed out a **tier-2** weapon. (It never threw only because all nine Assault lists happen to hold
  18 ids; a shorter `Assault2` would have been an `IndexOutOfRangeException` inside the death handler.)
- **`new Random()` per call, twice per call** (`random` and `rnd`): .NET Framework seeds from `Environment.TickCount`,
  so two players killing in the same tick got identical weapons. One shared `static readonly Random` behind a lock
  (`Weapon_List_Ranked.Acak`) replaces both.
- `player` (`AccountManager.getAccount(killer._playerId, true)`) can be null for a bot/GM slot -> the call site is
  guarded, and it now also requires `killer._team != victimSlot._team` so a suicide or team kill at exactly a
  threshold cannot re-roll the weapon.
- The ini is read **once and cached** (re-read when the file's timestamp changes) instead of `File.ReadAllText` plus
  ~45 `foreach` scans on every single kill, and a missing key is logged instead of throwing `NullReferenceException`
  on `listValue.Split`. `Weapon_List_Ranked.cs` went 1213 -> 167 lines and is now table-driven
  (`TANGGA` thresholds x `KELAS` names); the ini format and the public signature are unchanged.
- Behaviour change worth knowing: the **first** weapon of a battle is now drawn from the tier-1 ini lists instead of
  the five hardcoded ids. Four of those five are in the lists anyway; only the old MG starter `50010001` is not one
  of the two ids in `Mg=`.
- Still open (asked the user): the award only becomes the weapon **in hand** at the next spawn, because PB swaps the
  model on respawn - 3415 updates the client's equipment record. Making it instant would mean forcing a
  `BATTLE_RESPAWN_PAK` right after the kill, which also teleports the player to a spawn point.
- Orphan file `pbserver_game\global\serverpacket\Battle\A_3415_LONG_PAK.cs` declares a second
  `A_3415_LONG_PAK` whose constructor is misnamed `A_3415_PAK`; it is not in the `.csproj`, so it never compiles.
- **`rankedweaponlist.ini` was wrong too** (checked 2026-09-19 when the user asked): **all 18 ids on the nine
  `Mg`..`Mg9` lines were missing a digit** - `50010002` instead of `500010002`. The server's own decoder
  `ComDiv.getIdStatics(id, 1) = id / 100000000` is the `ITEM_CLASS` (1 ASSERT, 2 SMG, 3 SNIPER, 4 SHOTGUN,
  **5 MACHINE**), so the 8-digit form decodes to 0 = UNKNOWN. Four independent confirmations that 9 digits is
  right: the `WeaponList` enum holds *both* spellings for the same guns (`MK46_SILVER = 50010002` next to
  `MK_46_Silver = 500010002`); `tourneyitem.ini` (the user's own whitelist of legal weapons) is **entirely**
  9-digit and lists MGs `500010012`/`500010013`; the tournament check inside `BATTLE_RESPAWN_REC.cs` compares
  against `500010012`/`500010013`; and the `Special=` line of the very same ini already uses `500010017`.
  17 of the 18 corrected ids are in the enum (`500010016` is not, but neither is `500010017`, which `Special`
  uses - the enum is hand-maintained and incomplete). **The `rnd.Next(1, 4)` bug had been masking this**: MG
  could never be drawn, so the broken ids never reached a client. Fixing the range would have exposed them.
  Fixed in place with a one-time `rankedweaponlist._backup.ini`, together with three within-line duplicate ids
  the user asked to drop (`Assault9` 100003438, `SubMachine3` 200004108, `Special` 100003131). Checker
  `scratchpad/cek_ranked_ini.py` (override the path with `INI_UJI`) went 30 problems -> 10; the 10 left are ids
  absent from the `WeaponList` enum, which only costs the chat line a name (`(WeaponList)id` prints the number).
  Not fixed, reported to the user as balance rather than bugs: `Sniper6`/`Sniper7` share 11 of 19 ids,
  `Shotgun2`/`Shotgun5` share 9, and every MG tier holds only 2 ids with `Mg7` and `Mg8` identical, so MG
  progression effectively stops at tier 7.
- **Installed 2026-09-19** with the user's server shut down and their explicit go-ahead: solution rebuilt straight
  into `Bin\Release` (`PBGameServer.exe`, `PBCoreData.dll`, `PBBattleServer.exe`, `PBAuthServer.exe`), old binaries
  kept in `Bin\Release\_backup_binari_sebelum_perbaikan_ranked\`. Not started by me - launching it opens ports and
  touches the database, which is the user's call.
- Test: `scratchpad/uji_ranked/UjiRanked.cs`, a console program that loads the freshly built `PBGameServer.exe` /
  `PBCoreData.dll` and drives the real code by reflection (`Weapon_List_Ranked` is internal), with
  `FormatterServices.GetUninitializedObject` for `Room`/`Account`/`BATTLE_RESPAWN_REC` - `Account.SendPacket` is
  null-safe, and every other branch of `CheckEquipment` is behind a `Room.<flag>` that defaults to false, so the
  BattleAce path can be called offline. It checks all 14 thresholds against the ini sets, that all five classes
  appear, that kill 50 never yields an `Assault2` id, that 60 back-to-back draws are not identical, that
  `ResetSlot()` clears `AceWeapon`, that 12 consecutive respawns keep one weapon, and that an award then shows up
  on the next respawn. All pass.

## A sound for the "WEAPON UPDATE" HUD -- what the server can and cannot do (2026-09-29)

User: "saya ingin menambahkan sound effect ketika otomatis ganti senjata ... bagaimana caranya
metrigger suara seperti notice MEAT CHOPPER?" and then pinned it precisely:
`frag.killFlag = KillingMessage.Intercept;`.

### Where those notices actually come from

Everything - the HUD notice AND the announcer voice - is chosen **by the client** from two
fields of **packet 3355 `BATTLE_DEATH_PAK`**:

- `writeH((short)frag.killFlag)` per frag, a bitmask (`Core.models.enums.room.KillingMessage`):
  `PiercingShot 1, MassKill 2, ChainStopper 4, Headshot 8, ChainHeadshot 16, ChainSlugger 32,
  Suicide 64, ObjectDefense 128, Intercept 256`. **`Intercept` is the WEAPON UPDATE HUD**, set in
  `Weapon_List_Ranked.Load_Weapon_Ranked`.
- a trailing byte built from the killer's streak: `killsOnLife == 2 -> 1, == 3 -> 2, > 3 -> 3`.
  That is the starred notice (the MEAT CHOPPER with 1-3 stars in the user's video).

The voices themselves are ordinary client resources - `Sound.i3pack` -> `Voice.RSC` lists 169
entries including `SOUND/VOICE/ANNOUNCE/MV_ANN_{PIERCING, MASSKILL, CHAIN_STOPPER, HEADSHOT,
CHAIN_HEADSHOT, CHAIN_SLUGGER, DOUBLE_KILL, TRIPLE_KILL, CHAIN_KILLER, KILL, HELMETPROTECTION}.WAV`.
**There is no `MV_Ann_Intercept.wav`** - which is exactly why the weapon upgrade is silent.

### The server can never name a sound, and the mapping is not in the packs

Measured, not assumed: a content sweep of **3,564 packs / 37,394 files** in
`D:\Data C\BlacklistPB\Pack` finds the strings **"MEAT CHOPPER", "WEAPON UPDATE" and
"CHAIN KILLER" nowhere at all**, in UTF-8 or UTF-16, and a filename sweep finds no
intercept/weapon-update texture and no meat-chopper sound. So the notice art, its text and its
notice->sound table all live inside the packed `PointBlank.exe` (which, per the note above, does
not even contain `CStageBattle` as a readable string). There is nothing editable there with the
tools in this repo.

Consequence, and it is the whole answer: **the only lever the server has is which FLAGS it sets**,
and the client plays a sound only for a flag that already owns a notice. Any sound you add brings
its notice with it.

Checked and rejected as alternatives: no server packet names a sound (`BASE_USER_EFFECTS_PAK`,
`INVENTORY_ITEM_EFFECT_REC` are lobby item effects); `Sound.i3pack -> Interface.RSC` holds only UI
clicks; the one voice channel the battle server touches, `a20_RadioSync` (`_radioId`, `_areaId`),
is relayed between clients and never originated server-side, and it would print a radio chat line.

### The bug found while looking

`Load_Weapon_Ranked` did `frag.killFlag = KillingMessage.Intercept` - an **assignment**, running
after `Net_Room_Death.RegistryFragInfos` had already set that kill's natural flag. So a headshot
that happened to earn a weapon upgrade **lost its HEADSHOT notice and its announcer voice**, and
lost it from `kills.GetAllKillFlags()` too, which `AllUtils.CompleteMission` reads afterwards
(`Game_SyncNet.cs:431`, after `:417`) for mission cards. Score was never affected -
`getKillScore()` is computed earlier in the same loop.

Now `frag.killFlag |= KillingMessage.Intercept | BenderaSuara();`.

### `SoundFlag` in rankedweaponlist.ini

New optional line in `data/weapon/rankedweaponlist.ini`, read by `Weapon_List_Ranked.BenderaSuara()`:

    SoundFlag=None          ; bawaan - tidak ada suara tambahan
    SoundFlag=MassKill      ; atau PiercingShot / ChainStopper / Headshot / ChainHeadshot /
                            ; ChainSlugger, atau angkanya (1 2 4 8 16 32)

It is OR-ed into the weapon-upgrade kill, so the client plays that flag's `MV_Ann_*.wav`.
**Default is `None`**, i.e. behaviour is unchanged except for the `|=` fix, because the chosen
flag also draws its own HUD notice and counts toward that mission card - a trade the user has to
judge in game. The ini is re-read whenever its timestamp changes (the existing `Daftar()` cache
rule), so `SoundFlag` can be tried **without restarting the server**. The parser now also skips
`;` comment lines and keeps every line's raw text in a second dictionary, which is how a
non-numeric value survives a reader that otherwise only accepts integer lists.

Tests in this session's scratchpad (`srv/`), both driving the freshly built binaries by
reflection: `UjiSuara.cs` **16 checks** (the nine SoundFlag spellings incl. a number, a bad name
and a missing line; Headshot surviving as 264 where it used to be flattened to 256;
Intercept|MassKill = 258; a non-threshold kill leaving `killFlag` untouched; a null frag; and the
hot reload) and `UjiIniAsli.cs` **11 checks** that the REAL ini still parses with the new reader -
all eight weapon lists, all 14 kill thresholds, and kill 4 correctly not a threshold.

**Installed 2026-09-29** at the user's request ("Iya bantu pasangkan") with all three servers
stopped: only `Bin\Release\PBGameServer.exe` changed (585,216 B); `PBCoreData.dll` has no source
change and was not touched. Sources in `_backup_sebelum_suara_weapon_update\`, rollback binary +
the original ini in `Bin\Release\_backup_binari_sebelum_suara_weapon_update\`.

**The rollback binary had to be REBUILT, and that is worth remembering.** By the time the install
step ran, `Bin\Release\PBGameServer.exe` was already the new build - its mtime matched the staged
copy in `_hasil_suara_weapon_update\` to the second, which is what a plain Explorer copy does
(it preserves the source timestamp). So the `cp -p` that was meant to save the previous binary
saved a copy of the new one, and the 584,192-byte original existed nowhere on disk afterwards.
The fix: swap the backed-up `Weapon_List_Ranked.cs` back in, rebuild to the scratchpad, restore
the source. That produces a 584,192-byte binary (same size as the original, different MVID) with
no `BenderaSuara()` - verified by reflection. **Check the hash of what you are about to back up,
not just that a file is there.**

Also measured while fixing it: `MSBuild /p:OutputPath=<scratch>` really does keep the build out of
`Bin\Release` - the hash there was identical before and after a full rebuild - even though both
`.csproj` files declare `<OutputPath>..\Bin\Release\</OutputPath>`. The earlier worry in this file
about builds landing in the live folder does not apply when the override is passed.

## Multi-client cannot enter battle -- UDP port 29890 (2026-09-19)

User: "kenapa saya menggunakan multi client saat mau battle tidak bisa masuk ke dalam permainan". Cause found
and **confirmed on the user's own machine**: the PB client binds `UDP 0.0.0.0:29890` (their `netstat -ano -p UDP`
showed the socket owned by the process named `PointBlank`, and across samples it was held by one client PID at a
time), while the server hands **the same constant 29890 to every player**. A UDP port is exclusive, so the second
client on one machine never finishes its UDP setup; 30 s later `Room.StartCounter(1, ...)` fires
`BaseCounter(EventErrorEnum.Battle_First_Hole)` - the enum's own comment reads `//Out by hole punching` - and the
player is kicked back to the room. Nothing to do with accounts, HWID or per-IP limits (there are none).
This also explains why the login bot coexists fine with a real client: `BattleUdp` uses `new UdpClient()`, an
ephemeral port.

The constant was written in four packet builders (all now read `udpClientPort` from the ini instead, default 29890
so behaviour is unchanged until the value is edited; originals in `_backup_sebelum_perbaikan_udpport\`):
`pbserver_auth` `BASE_SERVER_LIST_PAK` (2049, sent from `LoginClient.init()` **on connect, before login**),
`pbserver_game` `BASE_SERVER_LIST_PAK` (2049), `BATTLE_PRESTARTBATTLE_PAK` (3349, 4 places: leader public/local and
the player's own public/local) and `BATTLE_GIVEUPBATTLE_PAK` (2 places, per slot).
`ConfigGA.udpClientPort` / `ConfigGS.udpClientPort`, keys added to `auth.ini` and `game.ini`.

**`udpClientPort` MUST be a multiple of 7.** Found the hard way 2026-09-19: setting auth 29895 / game 29896 made
the login bot fail instantly with the auth server logging `Connection destroyed due to Unknown first packet. [17441]`
(17441 = opcode 2561 decrypted with the wrong shift). Both servers derive the packet cipher as
`Shift = SessionId % 7 + 1` (`LoginClient.cs:63`, `GameClient.cs:64`), but the client protocol derives it as
**`(sessionId + udpPort) % 7 + 1`** - see the bot's decompiled `BASE_SCHANNEL_SERVER_REQ.cs:16-21`, which reads the
2049 packet's sessionId and udpPort and computes `p.Encrypt = (num + num2) % 7 + 1`. The two agree only while
`udpPort % 7 == 0`, and the stock 29890 is exactly 7 x 4270, which is why nobody ever noticed. The user's own game
client logged in fine with 29895, so the real client apparently does not use the field that way - only the bot does.
Note also that in the bot that field feeds **only** the cipher shift; nothing binds a socket from it, so the auth
2049 value is probably not what makes the client bind 29890.

**PROVEN 2026-09-19, then fixed**: with `game.ini udpClientPort=29904` the user's client bound
`0.0.0.0:29904` (netstat, process `PointBlank`), while the login bot sat on an ephemeral 58115. So the client takes
its UDP port from the **game server**, and multi-client is fixable server-side. Note the client binds nothing while
in the lobby - it only binds on entering a battle, so the test must be run in-game, not at the lobby.
Fix: `Game.data.utils.PortUdp` hands every `GameClient` its own port on connect
(`GameClient.Start()` -> `PortUdp.Ambil(ip)`, released in `Close()`), keyed by the client's IP so each machine gets
its own series: 29890, 29897, 29904 ... 29995 (16 per IP, **step 7** to keep `udpPort % 7 == 0`; a 17th connection
from one IP falls back to the base). `GameClient.UdpPort` is then written by the game's `BASE_SERVER_LIST_PAK`
and, per player, by `BATTLE_PRESTARTBATTLE_PAK` (leader + own, via `Account._connection`) and
`BATTLE_GIVEUPBATTLE_PAK`. The auth server keeps the plain config value: there the field only seeds the cipher.
Tested by `scratchpad/uji_port/UjiPort.cs` (reflection over the built `PBGameServer.exe`): 16 distinct ports per IP
all congruent to 0 mod 7, a second IP starting over at the base, a released port being reused, no throw past the
16th, and the series following `udpClientPort`.
**IN-GAME CONFIRMED 2026-09-19** (the user's screenshot: two Point Blank windows side by side, both inside the same
Library match, same 09:38 timer): `PID 304 -> 0.0.0.0:29890` and `PID 1208 -> 0.0.0.0:29897`, i.e. base and base+7,
exactly as designed. Multi-client now enters battle.

**The client's single-instance mutex** (2026-09-19, the user was closing it by hand in Process Hacker): the client
creates the named mutex `\Sessions\<n>\BaseNamedObjects\PointBlank` at startup and refuses to run when it already
exists. Closing that handle in an already-running client lets the next one start - this is separate from the UDP
port fix above; **both** are needed for multi-client (mutex to launch, per-client port to enter battle).
`TutupMutexPB.exe` + `Multi Client.bat` + the C# source now sit in the client folder
(`C:\Users\HYPERION\Documents\BlacklistPB V1 Remake`, nothing overwritten). It enumerates handles with
`NtQuerySystemInformation(SystemExtendedHandleInformation=64)`, and **finds the Mutant type index by creating its own
mutex and looking up that handle's `ObjectTypeIndex`** - only handles of that type get `NtQueryObject`, because
querying the name of a synchronous named-pipe handle can hang the caller. A match closes the source handle with
`DuplicateHandle(..., DUPLICATE_CLOSE_SOURCE)`. Modes: no argument = close once in every running client,
`-pantau` = stay running and clear each new client (what the .bat does, self-elevating), `-lihat` = report only,
`-nama` / `-proses` to point it at something else. Needs Administrator because the clients run elevated.
Verified on the user's two running clients: one already cleared by hand, the other reported
`\Sessions\2\BaseNamedObjects\PointBlank`, was closed, a re-check showed both clear, and both clients kept running
and responding (the mutex is only read at startup).

Side finding, `BATTLE_PRESTARTBATTLE_REC.cs:46`: `if (p.LocalIP == new byte[4] || ...)` compares `byte[]` by
reference, so it is always false and the `Battle_No_Real_IP` kick has never run. Not related to the multi-client
problem (if it did run it would kick people), left alone.

## Convoy / Escort mode (room type 14) -- 2026-09-20

User: "Saya ingin memperbaiki Convoy Mode. player utama bisa masuk dan player kedua stuck sebagai (ghost). dan di
temukan `[FAIL] Objek ID: 1 tidak memiliki Model data.`". Their own server logs settled the first half.

Where the evidence lives: `Bin\Release\logs\{rooms,errorC,battle,game}\` (one file per server start). The Convoy
attempt is `rooms\2609200007-1048576.log`:
`Room type: Escort` / `Nama Map: 'EH_STILLRAID'` / `Used spawn count: 1` / `End Players count: 1`, with a result
line for slot 0 only - while `errorC` shows **both** players joining (`Room.addPlayer` slot 0 GM_Hyperion, slot 1
GM_HeavyRain). So player 2 joined the room but never spawned.

**`[FAIL] Objek ID: 1 tidak memiliki Model data.` - solved.** `EH_STILLRAID` is map id **106**, and map 106 is not
in `Bin\Release\data\battle\maps.xml` at all: that file holds only **66** of the **125** maps listed in
`data\maps\modes.xml`. `Room.RoundResetRoomF1` does `Map = MappingXML.getMapById(_mapId)`, gets null, and never
attaches an `ObjModel` to any object, so every shot at the convoy (object id 1) hits the `obj._model == null`
branch in `BattleHandler.cs` - logged 40 times in one short match - and **does no damage**, which in Escort means
the objective can never be completed. Fixed by adding to maps.xml (backup `maps._backup.xml`, written once):

    <Map Id="106"> ;Still Raid / EH_STILLRAID - Convoy (Escort)
        <objects>
            <Obj Id="1" NeedSync="false" Anim1="255" Life="12000"/> ;Konvoi - Life masih perkiraan
        </objects>
    </Map>

`Life` 12000 is a guess (the Boss-map helicopters use 12000, Breakdown's objectives 6000, tanks 9000) - it is the
knob to tune. `Anim1="255"` keeps it a plain destroyable; `256`..`259` would instead feed `room._bar1/_bar2`
through `MappingXML.SetObjectives`, which is how Destroy-mode objective bars work and may be what the convoy HUD
bar wants. `NeedSync="false"` is safe: `GetARandomAnim` returns 255 when `_anims` is null.
Also made the failure self-diagnosing: the message now names the map and says whether the **map** is unregistered
or only the **object id** is missing, and `RoundResetRoomF1` logs a warning once per battle when a map is not in
maps.xml. Originals in `_backup_sebelum_perbaikan_convoy\`.
Test: `scratchpad/uji_map/UjiMap.cs` drives the built `PBBattleServer.exe`'s own `MappingXML.Load()` by reflection -
67 maps now, `getMapById(106)` returns the map, `Obj Id 1` has `Life 12000` / `isDestroyable true`, and maps
1/2/35/121 still parse.

**The ghost - NOT solved yet.** `RoomType.Escort = 14` is effectively unimplemented: grepping the whole server it
appears **exactly once**, in `Room.thisModeHaveCD()` (so Escort gets the pre-battle countdown and nothing else).
It is absent from `thisModeHaveRounds()`, from `Net_Room_Death.EndBattleByDeath` (which only handles 1/8/13 and
2/4), and from the battle server entirely. What was ruled out by reading the code: `espectador = true` is set only
for `room_type == 2 || room_type == 4` (`Room.BaseSpawnReadyPlayers`), and the same method's mid-battle branch
sends the spectator `SendUDPPlayerSync(..., 1)` only for those two types, so nothing deliberately makes a type-14
player a spectator. `BATTLE_STARTBATTLE_REC` spawns whenever `room._state == 5` (Battle), which a mid-join should
satisfy. So the mechanism is still unknown - the next step is per-slot logging along
PRESTART -> BATTLE_READY -> BATTLE -> BATTLE_RESPAWN_REC to see where player 2 stops.

## Destroy mode golem bar (map 37 Giran) -- two servers, two different max HP (2026-09-20)

User: "mode destroyer dengan map 37, Giran. Kalau Mode AI ... HP Golem normal dan berfungsi. tapi kalau sudah
bermain dengan player, itu tidak normal dan sinkronisasi animasinya juga salah." They meant the **HP bar on
screen**, not the golem's own attacks.

The golems are objects **0 and 1** of map 37 (`Anim1="256"/"257"` -> `_ultraSYNC` 1/2 -> `room._bar1`/`_bar2`);
the room log calls the map `GIRAN2` (that is the client's stage name for map id 37). Damage itself was never
broken: `logs\battle\*.log` holds **13,185** `[HIT OBJECT] Map: 37` lines and the HP walks down by exactly the
per-bullet damage, e.g. `HP12000(-31), HP11969(-31) ... HP58(-28), HP30(-28), HP2(-28)`.

**Cause: the two servers each had their own idea of the objective's maximum HP.** `Room.SetSpecialStage()` in the
**game** server hardcoded `Bar1/Bar2` per map id, while the **battle** server reads `Life` from
`data\battle\maps.xml`. They had drifted apart:

| map | game server (hardcoded) | maps.xml (battle server) |
|---|---|---|
| 35 Breakdown | 6000 / 6000 | 6000 / 6000 (the only one that matched - and the only one that behaved) |
| **37 Giran** | **12000 / 12000** | **8250 / 8250** |
| 38 Helispot | 6000 / 6000 | 12000 / 12000 (reversed) |
| 39 Defense | 9000 / 9000 | 6000 / 9000 |
| 123 | 6000 / 6000 | map absent from maps.xml |

So the bar opened at 12000, and the first bullet made it **jump down to ~8222** when the battle server's real
value arrived through `SendSabotageSync` -> `Net_Room_Sabotage_Sync` -> `BATTLE_MISSION_GENERATOR_INFO_PAK` (3369).
In **AI mode the battle server never touches objects at all** (`RoundResetRoomF1` and the object sync in
`RespawnSync` both sit behind `!_isBotMode`), so the host client simulates the golem and the bar stays consistent -
exactly why AI mode looked right. The user had been tuning the XML (the logs show 12000, then 8500, now 8250),
which is what pulled the two numbers apart.

Fix: new `pbserver_game\data\xml\ObjectiveXML.cs` reads the same `data/battle/maps.xml` (both servers run from
`Bin\Release`, so the relative path works) and `SetSpecialStage()` takes `Bar1/Bar2` from it, keeping the old
constants only as a fallback for maps with no objective objects - and logging a warning when that fallback is used.
`ObjectiveXML.Load()` is called from `Program.cs` next to `BattleServerXML.Load()`. Tuning a golem's HP is now a
single edit in maps.xml. Test `scratchpad/uji_objektif/UjiObjektif.cs` loads both built servers by reflection and
asserts every objective map now reports identical numbers on both sides (35/37/38/39 all match), that map 37 gives
8250, that `SetSpecialStage()` really produces 8250, and that a non-objective mode leaves the bars alone.

**Still open, reported to the user**: the golem is declared as a *static* object in maps.xml
(`NeedSync="false"`, no `<Anims>`, no `<DestroyEffects>`). `Packet4Creator.getCode4SyncData` sends
`OBJECT_STATIC` (id, life, killer - 8 bytes) when `objSyncId == 0` and `OBJECT_ANIM` (id, life, animId1, animId2,
elapsed - 13 bytes) when it is 1, so the client never receives any animation state for the golem, and
`DestroyState` stays 0 because `_effects` is empty. Map 38 Helispot shows the full pattern for the same kind of
Destroy objective (`NeedSync="true"` + `<Anims>` ids 5/6/7/8 cross-referencing the other helicopter +
`<DestroyEffects>` damaged at 30 %, destroyed at 0). Writing the golem's `<Anims>` needs its real animation ids,
which live in the client's `Siege_Golem.i3Obj` inside `Pack 3.88\Giran2_Scene.i3Pack` - the user approved reading
those packs.

Smaller things found on the way: `SLOT.damageBar1/damageBar2` are **ushort** but accumulate raw damage, so in a
long match they wrap past 65535 and corrupt the objective-damage XP (`earnedXP = damageBar1 / 600`);
`DamageManager.SabotageDestroy` passes `objM._ultraSYNC == 4 ? 2 : 1` as the bar number, so damage to the
`_ultraSYNC == 2` objective is credited to `damageBar1` (display is unaffected - both bar values travel in the same
packet - but the per-player credit is); map 37 repeats `<Obj Id>` 121-128 (harmless copy-paste); and map 36 is
absent from maps.xml entirely.

## Objective HP lives in the CLIENT's `.i3Obj` -- map 37 golems (2026-09-22, IN-GAME PROVEN)

User: "Darah Golem Siege atau Wild Hog pas awal darahnya berkurang jauh dari bar nya ...
dan jika golem nya hancur, harusnya ada animasi hancur, tapi golem nya tidak hancur sama
sekali." Two separate causes, both settled by reading the client's own files.

### The client carries each object's HP and its damage states

`Pack\Object_cgame_<name>.i3Pack` holds a `.i3Obj` = ordinary I3R2 with:

- `CObjectTemplate` = `GND1` ... `OTP1` + **f32 HP**, and its tail is `u32 count` + one
  `u32` raw id per state.
- `CObjectState` = `OST1` + **f32 threshold** (1.00 = intact, 0.30 = damaged, 0.00 = broken)
  + `u32` id of its `i3TimeEventGen` + `u16` scene string index + `i16` anim (-1 = none).
  The generator's `i3TimeEventInfo` list is the actions: `i3ActionBreakObject`,
  `i3ActionPlaySound`, `i3ActionEmitEffect`.

| client object | HP (`OTP1`) | states (thresholds) | maps.xml |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Helispot` (map 38) | 12000 | 3 (1.00 / **0.30** / 0.00) | `Life=12000`, `Effect Id=1 Percent=3600`, `Id=2 Percent=0` |
| `Siege_Golem` | **9000** | 2 (1.00 / 0.00) | was `Life=8250`, no effects |
| `Range_Golem` (= the **Wild Hog**, sounds `WILDHOGCANNON_*.WAV`) | **8000** | 2 | was `Life=8250`, no effects |
| `Tank` | 9000 | 3 | tanks 9000 |
| `Dark_Horror`, `Liviona` | 100 | 1 | the `Life=100` filler entries |

Map 38 proves the rule both ways: `Percent` is an **absolute HP** value (`eff._life >= life`)
that equals threshold x HP (0.30 x 12000 = 3600), and `Effect Id` is the **CObjectState index**.
So `Life` in maps.xml must equal the client's `OTP1`, or the bar starts wrong: the client draws
the bar against its own maximum, and the server only ever sends the current value.

`Giran2_Scene.i3Pack`'s `GINS` (108 objects) gives the id order -- the game objects are numbered
in i3INS order, and **object 0 = `Range_Golem`, object 1 = `Siege_Golem`** (one of each on the map).

### Why the golem never broke

`_destroyState` travels **only** in `STAGEINFO_OBJ_ANIM`, which needs both:

- `NeedSync="true"` -> `objSyncId = 1` (otherwise `OBJECT_STATIC`: id, life, killer only), and
- `objM._updateId == 3`, which `AnimsXML` sets only when some `<Sync Id>` is **not 255**.

With `NeedSync="false"` and no `<Anims>` the client received life reaching 0 and nothing else,
so it never switched to CObjectState 1 (the `Exp_SiegeGolem_02` explosion + `OB_SIEGEGOLEM_DEATH.WAV`).
`RespawnSync` is the exception: it always builds `ObjectHitInfo(3)`, so a respawning player would
have got the state -- but only with `NeedSync="true"`.

Fix applied to `Bin\Release\data\battle\maps.xml` map 37 (backup `maps._backup.xml` already
existed from the Convoy fix and was not overwritten):

    <Obj Id="0" NeedSync="true" Anim1="256" Life="8000">   ;Range_Golem (Wild Hog)
        <Anims><Sync Id="0" Date="0" Next="0" OtherOBJ="0" OtherANIM="0"/></Anims>
        <DestroyEffects><Effect Id="1" Percent="0"/></DestroyEffects>
    </Obj>
    <Obj Id="1" NeedSync="true" Anim1="257" Life="9000">   ;Siege_Golem
        ... the same ...

`Sync Id="0"` follows map 27's `<Obj Id="136">` helicopter, whose own comment reads
"Animacao 0-parado|1-voando"; `Id=0` also sets `_noInstaSync`, so `RoundResetRoomF1` gives the
object `AnimModel{_nextAnim=1}` with duration 0 and the anim never advances. **That id is the one
guess in this fix** -- the golem's CObjectStates carry anim `-1` (none) and the helicopter ids
5..8 are map-scene animations, so if the golem's own animation freezes in game, change it to
`Id="255"` (the destroy state then only reaches players on respawn).

Data only -- no rebuild, the servers read maps.xml at startup. Test
`scratchpad/uji_golem/UjiGolem.cs` drives the **servers' own parsers** by reflection
(`Battle.data.xml.MappingXML` + `Game.data.xml.ObjectiveXML`, with an `AssemblyResolve` handler
pointing at `Bin\Release`): 67 maps still load, both golems read 8000/9000 with ultraSYNC 1/2,
`_updateId == 3`, `_needSync`, one destroy effect each, `CheckDestroyState(0) == 1` and
`CheckDestroyState(1) == 0`, the game server's `GetBars(37)` returns the same 8000/9000, **no
objective map disagrees between the two servers**, and map 38 is untouched.

### The golem's attack animation -- the server must not dictate it (2026-09-22)

In game the HP bar and the destruction were confirmed fixed, and what was left was
"Animasi Serangan golem siege / wild hog, lebih dulu serangan dari pada Serangan HIT nya".

**The golem is simulated entirely by the clients.** The server never interprets it:
`Events.AIDamage` (0x4000, `a4000_BotHitData`) is read and relayed byte for byte, and so is the
client's own `STAGEINFO_OBJ_ANIM` (`code12_StageObjAnim`). The server's only jobs are the
object's life, the objective bar, and the destroy state.

So the only thing the server can get wrong is the animation field it puts in its own packets --
and `<Sync Id="0">` made it get that wrong constantly:

- `Room.SyncInfo(objs, type)`'s object branch (`(type & 1) == 1`, the 2.5 s periodic sync) is
  **dead code**: the one call site, `BattleHandler.cs:529`, passes `type = 2` (players only).
- What does run is the **hit path**: every bullet that lands on the object appends
  `ObjectHitInfo(objM._updateId)` with `_animId2 = obj._anim?._id ?? 255`. In Destroy mode the
  golem is under continuous fire, so with `<Sync Id="0">` every client was told "golem: animation
  0" many times a second, cutting its attack animation short while the damage (relayed from the
  simulating client) still arrived on its own schedule.

Fix, in `pbserver_battle/data/xml/MappingXML.cs` right after `DEffectsXML`:

    if (obj._effects.Count > 0 && obj._needSync)
        obj._updateId = 3;

`_updateId = 3` (= `STAGEINFO_OBJ_ANIM`, the only packet carrying `_destroyState`) used to be
reachable **only** by writing a `<Sync Id>` other than 255, which is exactly what forced the
server to dictate an animation. With this rule an object can have `<Sync Id="255">` (server
dictates nothing, `GetARandomAnim` returns 255) and still deliver its destroy state, so map 37's
golems are now:

    <Anims><Sync Id="255" Date="0" Next="0" OtherOBJ="0" OtherANIM="0"/></Anims>
    <DestroyEffects><Effect Id="1" Percent="0"/></DestroyEffects>

Scope of the rule: an object only changes if it has `<DestroyEffects>` **and** `NeedSync="true"`
**and** no non-255 anim -- across the whole file that is only these two golems. Map 38's
helicopters (anims 5-8) and map 27 Outpost's helicopter (anims 0/1) already had `_updateId = 3`,
and map 38's crane (`<Sync Id="255">`, no effects) stays at 1.

Map 27's helicopter is a third confirmation of the threshold rule from the client files:
`Life="3000"` with `Effect Id=1 Percent=900` (= 0.30) and `Id=2 Percent=0`.

Installed, then **REVERTED the same day at the user's request**. In game the attack animation was
still out of step, and they asked for the original behaviour back: "kembalikan seperti awal lagi,
karena awal itu Attack Animasi nya sudah sinkron. Kalau HUD HP sudah OK sih." So `Sync Id="255"`
was not enough either - with `NeedSync="true"` the hit packet is `STAGEINFO_OBJ_ANIM` (14 bytes:
destroy state, life, **elapsed seconds**, anim1, anim2) instead of `OBJECT_STATIC` (8 bytes), and
the client evidently re-applies the object's state from it, so the golem's animation was still
being disturbed on every bullet even with anim 255.

**Current state of map 37 (what is running):** exactly the stock shape, with only the HP corrected:

    <Obj Id="0" NeedSync="false" Anim1="256" Life="8000"/> ;Range_Golem (Wild Hog)
    <Obj Id="1" NeedSync="false" Anim1="257" Life="9000"/> ;Siege_Golem

`MappingXML.cs` and `Bin\Release\PBBattleServer.exe` were restored from their backups and verified
MD5-identical to the pre-change versions, so the only thing that differs from before this session
is the two `Life` numbers. **The destruction animation is gone again** - that is the trade the user
chose. The backups stay in place (`_backup_sebelum_perbaikan_anim_golem\`,
`Bin\Release\_backup_binari_sebelum_perbaikan_anim_golem\`) and the patch script is
`scratchpad/map/patch_anim_golem.py` if it is ever revisited.

**Then the destruction was put back, death-only (2026-09-22, same evening).** The user confirmed the
attack animation was fine again and asked for the break: "cuma animasi hancurnya saja belum. kan
nanti HP nya sudah habis. lalu Animasi hancurnya langsung bekerja." The working arrangement:

- maps.xml keeps `NeedSync="false"` and **no `<Anims>`**, so every bullet still produces the 8-byte
  `OBJECT_STATIC` packet and the golem's fighting animation is never touched. It only regains
  `<DestroyEffects><Effect Id="1" Percent="0"/></DestroyEffects>` (`_effects` is filled regardless
  of `NeedSync`, and `_updateId` stays 1).
- `BattleHandler.cs`, right after the normal hit packet is queued, appends **one** extra
  `ObjectHitInfo(3)` with `objSyncId = 1`, `_destroyState`, `_animId1/2 = 255`, `_specialUse = 0`,
  guarded by `if (obj._life == 0 && obj.DestroyState > 0 && !objM._needSync)`. The enclosing branch
  is `if (obj._life > 0)`, so it can fire at most once per object per round.

So the golem gets exactly one `STAGEINFO_OBJ_ANIM` in its life - at the moment it dies - instead of
one per bullet. Sources backed up in `_backup_sebelum_hancur_saat_mati\`, binary in
`Bin\Release\_backup_binari_sebelum_hancur_saat_mati\`; only `PBBattleServer.exe` was rebuilt.

**IN-GAME CONFIRMED 2026-09-22** ("Sangat-sangat sempurna"): full bar at the start, attack animation
in step, and the golem explodes when its HP runs out. All three complaints about map 37 are closed.
The rule that came out of it, worth reusing for any other objective: **`Life` in maps.xml must equal
the `OTP1` float in the client's `.i3Obj`**, `<Effect Id>` is the CObjectState index and `Percent` is
threshold x HP - and an object whose own animation the client drives must stay `NeedSync="false"`
with no `<Anims>`, because any packet that carries an animation field interrupts it.

`scratchpad/uji_golem/UjiGolem.cs` asserts all of it and passes against the installed binaries:
NeedSync false, `_updateId == 1`, `_anims == null`, one destroy effect with
`CheckDestroyState(0) == 1` / `(1) == 0`, `GetARandomAnim` -> 255, bars 8000/9000 agreeing on both
servers, maps 27/38 untouched - **plus the packets themselves**, built through the server's own
`Packet4Creator.getCode4SyncData`: a normal hit is sub-head 3 (`OBJECT_STATIC`) in 8 bytes, and the
death packet is sub-head 12 (`STAGEINFO_OBJ_ANIM`) in 14 bytes carrying destroy state 1, life 0 and
anim 255/255. Run it as `UjiGolem.exe <folder binari>` from `Bin\Release`.

### `.i3Pack` reading, corrected

- The marker before the file list is **not** always `0x90713282`: its top byte varies
  (`0x88713282` in `Object_cgame_Siege_Golem`). `i3pack.py` now compares only the low 3 bytes -
  before that it returned an empty listing for those packs. **That top byte is not free-form**: see
  the corrected layout below - its low 3 bits are bits 8..10 of the entry-list length.
- **The file-entry stride is not always 92 bytes**: `Crackdown_Scene` uses 92, the golem packs 76
  (entries still start with a 64-byte name and the whole region is still rotated right 2 bits).
  `i3pack.daftar` still assumes 92, so for a pack it reads as empty, scan for embedded `I3R2`
  images instead (`scratchpad/map/ambil_golem.py`): find `I3R2`, require `s_off == 0xB8`, and take
  the end from the object table. That is how `Siege_Golem.i3Obj` and the 5 `.i3a` were read.

## Session logout log (2026-09-21)

User: "apakah anda bisa membuat log sesi logout di server ?" - the servers logged `[Login Success]` but
nothing when a player left. New `pbserver_data\SesiLog.cs` writes the matching line from both sides, in the
same shape as the login line so the two align in the console:

    [Logout Game  ] [26/09/21 21.50] - ID : [hyperion] IP : [192.168.199.239] SESI : [00:12:00] SEBAB : [keluar normal]

- Tags are padded to the width of `Login Success`: `Logout Auth  ` (`LoginClient.Close`, the player quits at
  the server-select screen) and `Logout Game  ` (`GameClient.Close`, the player leaves the lobby or a battle).
- `SEBAB`: `keluar normal` (the client's own exit packet - `BASE_USER_EXIT_REC` on both servers),
  `pindah server` (game `BASE_SERVER_CHANGE_REC`), `ditendang` (`Close(..., kicked: true)`),
  `koneksi terputus` (anything else). Green in the console for the first two, yellow otherwise.
- Both `Close` methods gained an optional `string sebab`; `LoginClient` keeps the old 2-argument overload so
  its ~40 call sites are untouched. `GameClient.CatatKeluar` runs **before** `RemovePlayer`/`SimpleClear`,
  while `getChannel()`/`_room` are still readable.
- Three destinations: console, `logs/<auth|game>/`, and the new `logs/logout/` (via `Logger.LogLogout`, created
  by `checkDirectorys` for both servers). The logout file adds `NICK`, and `CH`/`ROOM` (game) or `SERVER` (auth).
- **The auth server's soft close is deliberately silent**: `BASE_SERVER_CHANGE_REC` calls `Close(0, false)` when
  the player moves to a game server, which is not a logout. Only `destroyConnection == true` with a logged-in
  account writes a line, so a connection that never logged in writes nothing either.
- Note the timestamp separator follows the Windows locale - Indonesian prints `21.50`, not `21:50` (the existing
  `[Login Success]` line does the same). `SESI` is built by hand so it always uses `:`.
- Test `scratchpad/uji_logout/UjiLogout.cs` loads the built `PBCoreData.dll` / `PBGameServer.exe` /
  `PBAuthServer.exe` and drives the real `Close()` by reflection (`FormatterServices.GetUninitializedObject`,
  with `handle` filled in by hand - `Dispose()` would otherwise NRE outside the try). 8 checks, all pass:
  folder creation, line format, `Durasi` (including > 24 h and a backwards clock), one line per close, the two
  default reasons, nothing for a connection without a login, the auth line, and silence on the soft close.
  Originals in `_backup_sebelum_log_logout\`.

## Server GUI in one window -- `PBPanel.exe` (2026-09-21)

User: "apakah server bisa di buat mode GUI dalam satu tampilan ?". New WinForms project `pbserver_panel`
(`Blacklist_Panel.csproj` -> `Bin\Release\PBPanel.exe`, added to `Blacklist_Server.sln`). **The three servers
are not modified at all**: the panel takes their real console windows and re-parents them into itself.

- `KonsolTerpasang.Pasang()` = `GetWindowLong(GWL_STYLE)`, strip `WS_CAPTION|WS_THICKFRAME|WS_SYSMENU|
  WS_MINIMIZEBOX|WS_MAXIMIZEBOX|WS_POPUP|WS_BORDER`, add `WS_CHILD|WS_VISIBLE`, then `SetParent` into a Panel
  and `MoveWindow` on every resize. Colours, scrollback and mouse all stay native because it is the same
  conhost window - nothing is piped or re-rendered. **Redirecting stdout instead would not work**: all three
  `Program.Main`s call `Console.Clear()` and `Console.SetCursorPosition`, which throw when stdout is a pipe.
- `Lepas()` restores the saved style, parent and rectangle, so the console returns as an ordinary window with
  the server still running. It is called on close, on "Lepas console", from `Application.ThreadException`,
  from `UnhandledException` and from `ProcessExit` - if the panel died without it, the consoles would vanish
  with their parent while the servers kept running.
- **Must run as Administrator.** All three servers carry `requireAdministrator` in their manifests and UIPI
  forbids a lower-integrity process from touching their windows; the panel's manifest matches and it warns at
  startup if it somehow runs unelevated. **Double-clicking is enough** - verified 2026-09-21 by reading
  `RT_MANIFEST` id 1 out of the built `PBPanel.exe` (`FindResource(h, 1, 24)`): 1390 bytes,
  `name="PBPanel.app"`, `level="requireAdministrator"`, so Windows elevates it itself with one UAC prompt.
  The first handover told the user to right-click > Run as administrator, which was wrong and is corrected in
  `Bin\Release\PANEL - BACA INI.txt`. That file also carries the optional Task Scheduler recipe
  (`schtasks /create ... /rl HIGHEST` + a shortcut running `schtasks /run /tn PBPanel`) for skipping the UAC
  prompt entirely - not set up, it adds a permanent task to the machine.
- `Process.MainWindowHandle` only enumerates **top-level** windows, so once a console is attached it returns 0
  and `MainWindowTitle` goes empty. The title is where the auth/game servers write `INCOMING / LOAD ACCS /
  Used RAM` every 100 ms, so `KonsolTerpasang.Judul` reads it straight from the stored HWND with
  `GetWindowTextW` and the pane header shows the bracketed part.
- Player list: `PembacaLog` tails `logs/login/*.log` (`[Login Success]`) and `logs/logout/*.log` (the new

## `.Pef` registry files and the tambourine throw bug (2026-09-18)

(**Corrected 2026-09-24**: that per-block rotation IS the pack's own SECURE V1 "BitRotate" cipher, so
`i3pack.py` already undoes it - a `.Pef` read through `I3Pack` is plain I3R2 with no second layer, and the
block size never has to be guessed. The paragraph below is the pre-`i3pack.py` description, kept for the
record.) `config/*.Pef` inside `Blacklist_Script_*.i3pack` is **not** rotated as one big integer. It is rotated
**right by 3 bits per fixed-size block**, each block independently (`int.from_bytes(blk,'big')`, rotate, back).
For `Weapon.pef` the block is **1024 bytes** - proved by decoding the whole file as one integer first: that
produced ~4300 single-byte anomalies (XOR 0x20/0x40/0x60, i.e. bits 5-6) and 3127 of them sat at offsets
`== 0 (mod 1024)`, the block starts whose wrap bits came from the wrong neighbour. With blocks of 1024 the
anomalies vanish (`AutoFi2eCount2` -> `AutoFireCount2`, `WeapOnThrowKnife` -> `WeaponThrowKnife`). `Goods.Pef`
needs 2048, so **the block size varies per file**: decode with 1024, then check the bytes right after each
multiple of 1024 in a text region; if they are wrong, try 2048/4096. Helper: `pef2.buka(data, blk)` in the
scratch dir. Never trust a lone odd byte in a decoded `.Pef` before checking the block size.

Record layout inside a decoded `.Pef` (it is an ordinary I3R2): each object's data is
`u8 len + name + 'TRN3' + 72-byte header + u32 own_id + 'RGK1' + u32 n_children + 8 zero bytes + n * (u32 id + 4 zero bytes)`.
A weapon record node's children are its **fields**, not other weapons; grouping into tables (`Melee`, `Gun`,
`Bow`, `Grenade`, `Trigger`, `Shield`, `Dual`, `ScopeGun`, `Item`, ...) is by contiguous id range, closed by a
schema node of the same name whose children are the column definitions. Field blobs are separate objects:
`u8 len + name + u32 9 + u32 type + u32 count(15) + values`, type 0 = i32, 1 = f32, 2 = `RGS3 + u32 chars + UTF-16LE`.
The 15 values are the nation columns.

Tambourine (`WeaponDualThrowKnife::_Throw ... Asserted : pNewWeapon != NULL`) - what was ruled out:
- The renumber 262 -> 179 **did** reach the client: the two `Blacklist_Script_Weapon.i3pack` exports differ by
  exactly 75 bytes, at `ThrowItemID` (301262->301179), `_ThrowNumber` and `_Number`. So the "weapon number must
  be <= 255" theory is dead.
- Field-by-field, `Dual_Tambourine_PBIC2024_Neon` matches `Dual_Kunai` (ClassMeta, `_ThrowClass` 1,
  `_ThrowNumber`, `ThrowItemID`, `LeftHandWeaponClass/Num`, `_Extension Throw`, `DoNotThrowLast`), and the
  class-1 record matches `Kunai` #107. Number 179 is in range (the client has throw knives 219/251/254).
- The animation-path fix in `Tambourine_PBIC2024_Neon.I3CHR` (strings 28/35/37 were
  `ResourceChange_Male_Right.i3a`, `Weaponi3a`, `Weapon.i3a`) **is already inside**
  `Pack\Weapon_Tambourine_PBIC2024_Neon.i3Pack`, byte-identical to the rebuilt file. The copy under
  `I3SModeChara\Weapon\...` was still the broken 6703-byte one and was replaced on 2026-09-18.
- The `.i3AnimPack` holds all 16 animations with correct paths; no client-side item/goods table references any
  throw weapon (`Goods.Pef` is gacha boxes, `texture_change_Weapon.Pef` is skin swaps only).

Remaining lead - the **model**, not the registry. `Kunai_Dual.I3S` has an `i3PhysixShapeSet` named `Collision`
plus bones `AnimationDummy`, `EdgeTraceStartFXDummy`, `EdgeTraceEndFXDummy`. `Tambourine_PBIC2024_Neon.I3S`
has none of those - only `GunDummy`, `AniDummy`, `FXDummy` (+ per-jingle bones) and **no collision shape at
all**. A thrown weapon is a physics projectile, so that is the likeliest reason creation returns NULL while the
melee half works. Control tests handed to the user: (a) does stock `Dual_Kunai` throw in this client, and
(b) point the dual tambourine at `ThrowItemID` 301107 / `_ThrowNumber` 107 - if a Kunai flies, the dual entry
and the client path are fine and the fix belongs in the `.I3S`.
