## Mixamo -> `.i3a` -- `i3bvh.py` + I3BVH Convert V3 (2026-09-26)

User: "Mixamo.com itu menyediakan animasi kan ? apakah bisa ambil animasi di jadikan i3a ??" Yes, but
only through a **retarget** - and the reason why is the finding from the section above.

**The route is BVH, not FBX.** BVH is plain text (a skeleton plus euler angles per frame), so the whole
conversion can be written and tested here with no Blender at all; Mixamo -> Blender -> `File > Export >
Motion Capture (.bvh)` is two clicks and everything after that is offline.

### Why the numbers cannot just be copied

- Bone names differ (`mixamorig:Hips` vs `Pelvis`). Of WarDog_Red's **63 bones, 52 have a Mixamo
  counterpart**; the 11 that do not are `Root`, `IK`, `Pivot` and the eight `Twist` bones.
- The hierarchy differs: in PB, **`R Clavicle`'s parent is `Neck`**, while Mixamo parents `RightShoulder`
  to `Spine2`. The same local rotation therefore means a different pose.
- And the decisive one: **`.i3a` stores each bone's FULL LOCAL matrix relative to its parent, not a delta
  from the bind pose** (proved on the golem - see above). Mixamo's angles are relative to Mixamo's own
  rest pose, so copying them onto a PB bone whose rest differs twists the body.

So what is transferred is the **world orientation**, not the local angles:

    R_target_world = R_source_world * inverse(R_source_rest_world) * R_target_rest_world

and the local matrices are then rebuilt down the TARGET's parent chain, keeping the target's own rest
translations so bone lengths never change. A bone with no counterpart simply stays at its rest pose -
the engine matches by name only, so that is safe.

### Decided by measurement, not by asking the user

- **Axis and facing**: all 24 axis-aligned rotations are tried and the one that best matches the rest bone
  directions wins (`cari_putaran`). On a Y-up centimetre BVH it picks the right one with error 0.0000
  against 0.89 for the runner-up. The bone directions are taken to the nearest **paired descendant**, not
  to the first child - `Pelvis`'s first child in PB is `IK`, which does not exist in Mixamo.
- **Scale**: the ratio of the bounding-box diagonals of the paired rest bones (1.971 m vs 197.1 -> 0.01).
  An earlier version used the root bone's height and failed: the root sits on the floor, so it was 0/0.
- **Name scheme**: the own-name pairing and the Mixamo-table pairing are both computed and the one that
  pairs more bones wins, with the loser filling the gaps where it does not clash. Applying the table
  blindly was a real bug - on a BVH that already uses PB names it linked `Spine2` to `Spine1` and tilted
  the whole upper body by 8.5 degrees.
- **Root motion** is anchored on the source root's position **in the first exported frame**, not on the
  BVH rest pose: a Mixamo BVH puts the whole hip height in the position channels and leaves `OFFSET` at
  zero, so using the rest would launch the character a metre into the air.

### The other direction

`ke_bvh()` writes a PB animation out as BVH. BVH joints always have an identity rest rotation, so the
bone's rest orientation has to be folded into the per-frame angles: `OFFSET` = the rest world delta and
`R_bvh = R_world * inverse(R_rest_world)`. Joints whose translation is animated additionally get position
channels (`Salsa_Dance` moves `Root` 23 cm and both clavicles 9 mm), which makes the export exact -
measured joint positions match the PB bone positions to **2 micrometres**.

### Format notes worth keeping

- `BVH.pose(None)` (the rest pose) must keep each joint's `OFFSET` and NOT zero the position channels,
  otherwise the root's rest position comes out as (0,0,0).
- Channel order is the multiplication order in column convention: `Zrotation Xrotation Yrotation` means
  `Rz * Rx * Ry`. `euler_dari` inverts that for all six orders (tested by round trip over 6 x 380 random
  rotations including exact gimbal, worst case 0.000000). The middle angle uses `atan2(sin, |rest|)`
  rather than `asin`, and at gimbal the remaining angle is solved from `R * inverse(R_middle)` - the
  closed-form sign rule is wrong for the odd permutations.

### Proven without Blender

The test builds a **synthetic Mixamo rig out of a real PB animation**: 52 bones only (no Root/IK/Pivot/
Twist), re-parented, `mixamorig:` names, identity rest rotations (so the rest genuinely differs from PB's),
rotated to Y-up and scaled by 100. Retargeting that back onto WarDog_Red reproduces `Salsa_Dance.i3a`:
**rotations within 0.025 degrees** and positions within 8 mm (the 8 mm is the clavicles' own animated
translation, which rotation retargeting deliberately does not carry). Rendering the result in I3Viewer
Editor V3 gives the same four dance poses as the original, pixel for pixel by eye.

`uji_i3bvh.py`: **58 checks** in 8 groups - angle maths, the `.i3a` writer reproducing `Salsa_Dance.i3a`
**byte for byte**, skeleton + name table, `.i3a -> BVH` joint positions, the full retarget round trip
(own names / Mixamo names / Y-up + centimetres), root motion and `--diam`, key compaction, attaching the
result to a character and playing it, four refusals, and the window driven in-process.

**Blender needs no add-on for any of this.** FBX import and BVH export are both shipped and enabled by
default (`io_scene_fbx`, `io_anim_bvh`); Blender is used purely as an FBX-to-BVH translator, and no
retargeting add-on is involved. **Its export dialog needs no particular setting either**: the per-joint
rotation order is read from each joint's own `CHANNELS` line, so "Rotation Mode" (including *Native*,
which may differ per bone) makes no difference - measured over all six orders, the retargeted result is
identical to 0.025 degrees.

**CONFIRMED with a real Mixamo file the same day** (user's screenshot): a Gangnam Style motion taken from
mixamo.com, exported to BVH from Blender and converted here, attached to `WarDog_Red.I3S` as 63 tracks /
742 keys / 12.35 s, with `63 dari 63 trek cocok dengan nama tulang` and the editor's preview dancing. So
the BVH channel convention, Blender's export and the whole retarget hold up outside the synthetic tests.
Note the user's BVH was **60 fps** (742 keys over 12.35 s) because the GUI pre-fills the source's own rate;
PB's own emotes are all 30, and typing 30 into "Kunci per detik" halves the file (63 x 742 x 44 bytes is
about 2.0 MB of key data). **Still not tested in game.**

**Not tested against a real Mixamo file by me** - there is none on this machine, and no Blender either. What
remains unverified is a single convention: that the order the channels are listed in is the order the
rotations multiply (column convention). Writer and reader here share that reading, so the round-trip
tests cannot catch a mismatch with a third-party file - but a wrong convention produces a visibly broken
pose, not a subtle drift.

### FBX read directly -- `i3fbx.py` (2026-09-29)

User: "apakah anda bisa menambahkan fbx to i3a di dalam program I3BVH Convert V3 ?? dari pada
saya convert fbx -> bvh -> i3a." Done, and Blender is now optional: `I3BVH Convert V3` takes a
Mixamo `.fbx` straight.

Sample on the machine: `Desktop\Silly Dancing.fbx` (2,340,240 B, FBX **7700**, written by
"FBX SDK 2020.2") - a Mixamo motion on a rig the user had uploaded a PB skin to, so the file
carries 33 `Model LimbNode` bones, 17 `Model Mesh` nodes, 17 Skin deformers, 171 Clusters and a
`BindPose`.

`i3fbx.baca_gerakan()` returns a **`GerakanFBX(i3bvh.BVH)`** that only overrides `pose()` and
`durasi`, storing each bone's local `(R, t)` per frame instead of channel numbers. So
`i3bvh.retarget()`, the name matching, the axis search and the scale search are reused untouched
- and the BVH route still works exactly as before.

Three things had to be measured, not assumed:

- **`RotationOrder` "XYZ" means `Rz * Ry * Rx`** in this codebase's column convention - the
  reverse of a BVH channel list. This is the one thing that cannot be taken from documentation
  safely, so it is not: the file's `BindPose` holds every bone's world matrix, and
  `_pilih_urutan()` builds the rest pose both ways and keeps the one that matches. On this file
  the right form reproduces all 33 BindPose translations to **0.000000000 m** while the other is
  out by **0.28 m** on average. The measured form is now the fallback when a file has no
  BindPose.
- **A bone is OO-connected to every Deformer Cluster that uses it**, not only to its parent bone.
  Taking "the last OO connection" as the parent shattered the hierarchy - `LeftHandIndex2` came
  out as a root. `Adegan` therefore prefers a parent whose class is `Model`. 28 of the 33 bones
  in this file have more than one OO parent.
- **`Model Mesh` nodes are not bones.** Including them put `LOD0_F_S_SX_HarvestFarmer-Blue...`
  in the skeleton. Filter: `Model` whose subclass is not Mesh/Camera/Light.

Other format notes worth keeping:

- Binary header `Kaydara FBX Binary  \0` + `1A 00` + u32 version at +23; node records use
  **u64** EndOffset/NumProperties/PropertyListLen for version **>= 7500**, u32 below. A record of
  all zeros closes a child list. Array properties (`f d l i b`) are `u32 count, u32 encoding,
  u32 compressed length` with encoding 1 = zlib.
- Local transform is `T * Roff * Rp * Rpre * R * Rpost^-1 * Rp^-1 * S...`, not just T*R*S.
  PreRotation/PostRotation are applied; Mixamo leaves them zero but Max/Maya rigs do not.
- Animation is `Model <-OP- AnimationCurveNode <-OP- AnimationCurve`, the OP property naming the
  channel (`Lcl Rotation` then `d|X`/`d|Y`/`d|Z`). Key times are **ktime, 1/46186158000 s**.
- **The frame step comes from the key deltas, not from `TimeMode`** - this file's keys are 60 fps.
- Axis and scale are NOT converted here: `retarget()` already finds both (this file picked its
  axis rotation with error 0.0811 against 0.8992 for the runner-up, and scale 0.983 because the
  rig is already in metres).
- ASCII FBX 7.x is read by the same code path; FBX 6.x is refused by name ("ekspor ulang sebagai
  FBX 7.x").

Result on the sample: 33 bones -> **28 of the PB skeleton's 63** get motion (the rig has no
thumb/middle/ring/pinky and no twist bones), 230 frames at 60 fps -> 115 at 30, 3.80 s, 150,020 B
of `.i3a`. Every bone length stays constant across frames except `Pelvis`, which carries the body
displacement by design. Rendering the retargeted skeleton beside the FBX's own pose frame by
frame, the poses line up.

GUI: the file row is now "1. Gerakan .fbx (langsung dari Mixamo) atau .bvh", the picker takes
`*.fbx *.bvh`, and the button says "Gerakan -> .i3a". `i3bvh.buka_gerakan(jalur)` does the
dispatch by content (magic / `FBXHeaderExtension`), and the CLI `info` and `ubah` take either.

`uji_i3fbx.py`: **44 checks** - the binary reader's object census, the hierarchy traps above, the
BindPose proof (including that the wrong Euler form really is much worse, so the check means
something), the retarget numbers, bone lengths, a hand-written ASCII FBX exercised end to end,
three refusals, and the window driven in-process through a real conversion. Regression:
`uji_i3bvh.py` 58/58 still pass. Exe rebuilt 2026-09-29 with `--hidden-import i3fbx`
(22,995,599 B; old build in `_backup_sebelum_fbx\`) and smoke-tested in a folder holding no
`.py`. **Not tested in game.**

## `.i3Pack` format, fully decoded -- `i3pack.py` (2026-09-23)

The user asked whether `Desktop\Decode\i3PackEditor.exe` could be decompiled (its source is lost).
It is **native C++ / MFC 32-bit** (`mfc140u.dll`, VS2015+), debug path
`E:\Proyectos\JuegosOnlineproyectos\PB\pbblow\replica\Tools\i3PackEditor\bin\Release\i3PackEditor.pdb` -- i.e. it
belongs to the same "pbblow replica" kit as `I3Tools\`, so its source was never on this machine and native code
cannot be turned back into it. RTTI still names its classes (`CPackEditorApp`, `CMainFrame`, `CNameDlg`,
`pack::I3PackFile` / `PackNode` / `PackFileEntry`). The user chose a **rewrite**; the format below was recovered by
using that exe as an oracle (create/protect/convert-cipher on crafted inputs) plus a sweep of 3,557 client packs.

- Container = ordinary I3R2 (header 0xB8, string table, 28-byte object table), every object an `i3PackNode`.
  String table = `i3PackNode` + each node's name in object order, CRLF-separated, one trailing NUL.
  Objects are written children-first, root last; header 0x34 holds the root's raw id.
- Node data = `u8 len + name` + `TRN3` + 72-byte header (child count at +8) + child ids (u32 each)
  + `u32 marker` + `u32 count field` + file entries + (the exe, and this tool) the node's file bytes.
  Marker = `0x??713282`, and its **top byte is `0x80 | (name code << 3) | (length bits 8..10)`**:
  code 1 (`0x88..0x8F`) -> 48-byte names (entry 76), code 2 (`0x90..0x97`) -> 64-byte names (entry 92),
  code 3 (`0x98..0x9F`) -> the newer-client form below.
- **The entry-list length (= files * 8) is SPLIT ACROSS TWO PLACES** (corrected 2026-09-27; the
  earlier note here said the count field held all of it, and that was wrong):

      bits 0..7   -> low byte of the count field
      bits 8..10  -> the low 3 bits of the marker's top byte
      bits 11..   -> the count field, in place (its own bits 8..10 are ALWAYS 0)
      count field = 0x02000000 | (length & 0xFF) | (length & 0xFFF800)

  So 44 files -> length 0x160 -> marker `0x91713282` + field `0x02000060`. Reading the count from the
  field alone gives **12**, which is exactly what the user reported on `Blacklist_Ingame.i3pack`
  (their old exe showed 44, this tool showed 12). Measured over **24,239 nodes** in the client packs and
  `Pack 3.88` with no exception, and the field's top byte is `0x02` in all 30,732 of them.
  `i3pack.baca_jumlah(atas, medan)` / `tulis_jumlah(jumlah)` are the pair.
- **The break is exactly at 32 files** (32 * 8 = 256 = bit 8). Confirmed against the old
  `i3PackEditor.exe` as an oracle - it writes 31 -> `0x90`+`0xF8`, 32 -> `0x91`+`0x00`,
  44 -> `0x91`+`0x60`, 100 -> `0x93`+`0x20`, 300 -> `0x91`+`0x860` - and this tool now reproduces all
  five **byte-identically**. That 32-file threshold is why it went unnoticed for so long: the exe
  comparison test built a pack of **4** files, and every pack this tool had ever written happened to
  have fewer than 32 files per node (checked: 69 project packs + 3,565 client packs, none affected).
  A node with >= 32 files written by the old code would have been **readable by the client only in
  part** - `(count & 0x1F) | ((count >> 8) << 8)` of it.
  The stock packs hit by the old reader were the big ones: `Airport_Textures` 127, `BlackPanther_Scene`
  116, `Weapon_Common` 1,265, `Effect_High` 658 - 158 nodes in the client folder in total.
  Since every other tool imports `i3pack`, the same undercount was in all 12 of them; the exes that
  bundle it were rebuilt (PyInstaller's FrozenImporter wins over a `.py` next to the exe).
- **Each entry is obfuscated by rotating the whole block right 2 bits as one big-endian integer.** Decoded:
  name[48 or 64], then a 28-byte tail: `+0 u16 cipher mask`, `+2 u16 SECURE flag (0x0800)`, `+4 u16 hash lo`,
  `+6 u16 size lo`, `+8 u16 offset hi`, `+10 u16 size hi`, `+14 u16 hash hi`, `+16 u16 offset lo`, rest unused
  (stock files leave 0xCC/0x33 stack garbage there). Hash = **CRC32 of the upper-cased name** -- that is what the
  old exe writes; stock packs carry some other hash, which the exe overwrites and the engine evidently ignores.
- The entry's flag word at tail+2: **only bit `0x0800` means the content is encrypted**. Reading "flag != 0" as
  SECURE is wrong and was a real bug: `Weapon_AUG_A3_Halloween2026.i3Pack` has a file with flag `0x0001` whose
  content is already plaintext, and "decrypting" it handed i3ImageViewer garbage (the user hit this). A survey of
  Pack 3.88 + the client: flag `0x0000` plain, `0x0800` V1-encrypted, `0x0801` V2-encrypted, `0x0001` plain
  (13 files). `Berkas.bendera` keeps the raw word and `aman` is a property over bit 0x0800, so the other bits
  survive a save.
- **SECURE cipher V1 "BitRotate"**: each **2048-byte block** rotated 3 bits (left to encrypt, right to decrypt);
  a short final block is rotated on its own. All 236 SECURE files in the user's 3,557 packs use it (mask 0).
- **SECURE cipher V2 "PBM"** (mask != 0: type in the high byte, key index in the low byte -- the same encoding as
  IIA2's cipher word) -- **solved 2026-09-23** using the old exe as an oracle (encrypt known patterns, read the
  result back). Its shape, all of it verified against that exe:
  - the content is cut into **65536-byte chunks**, each enciphered independently and restarting at position 0;
  - within a chunk it is **strictly per byte** (a one-byte change in the plaintext changes exactly one output
    byte), and each position `i % 256` has its **own 256-entry substitution table** -- not a keystream, so
    neither XOR nor ADD models it;
  - those tables depend only on **`len(chunk) % 256`** ("class"; a full chunk is class 0), which is why sizes
    44, 300, 556, 16428 all share one keystream;
  - the class-c table is the class-0 table with each row shifted: most positions **+ constant**, the positions
    `7, 9, 12, 15 (mod 16)` **XOR constant**. So one key's whole cipher fits in 64 KB (class-0 tables) + 128 KB
    (operator+constant per class and position).
  `pelajari_v2(exe_lama, tipe, key)` harvests that in ~15 s per key (one 64 KB "value block" file gives the
  class-0 tables, 256x10 constant files give the per-class operators), **verifies it by re-encrypting all 2,561
  probe files byte-identically to the exe**, and writes `Cipher V2\pbm_<type>_<key>.bin` next to the program.
  After that the key needs no exe. CLI: `pelajari-cipher <exe> 2:43` or `--dari-pack <pack>`; the GUI offers it
  automatically when a pack needs an unknown key - in three places: the pack's own entry table (pack will not open),
  a file whose *content* is still encrypted (`mask_mentah()`, offered right after opening, and on the file list's
  right-click as "Pelajari cipher berkas ini..."), and when such a file is sent to an external tool. After a
  harvest, `buka_mentah()` decrypts those blobs in place, so the pack does not have to be reopened.
  `--dari-folder` harvests every key a whole pack folder needs. **All user-visible wording for this says
  "Learning Encrypted Key" and never names the old exe** - the user asked for that so it does not look like an
  external tool is doing the work; the code comments and this file still call it what it is.
  File list also has F2 rename, Delete, Ctrl+A, rubber-band selection by dragging the cursor (`_seret_*`, which
  selects the range between the press row and the row under the cursor), and Ctrl+C/X/V. The clipboard is
  in-process (name, data, mask, flags) so it survives switching packs - that is how a file moves from one pack to
  another - and Ctrl+V also pastes files copied in Explorer by reading CF_HDROP off the Windows clipboard.
  Testing note: `event_generate` for F2/Delete and `bbox`/`identify_row` only work while the window is actually
  mapped, so the GUI test `deiconify()`s for that block.
  **Learning a key that is ALREADY learned used to destroy its table** (found 2026-09-24): `pelajari_v2` read the
  encrypted probe pack back with a plain `I3Pack(...)`, which decrypted it with the existing table, so the
  "measured" substitution came out as the identity and the verification (`tabel.sandi(d) == hasil[n]`) passed
  vacuously. The saved table then "decrypted" every file of that key into garbage with nobody complaining -
  `SweetCrackdown_Col_Hero.I3S` came out not starting with `I3R2`, which is how it surfaced. Two of the user's
  93 tables were like that (2:1D and 2:1E; moved to `Cipher V2\_tabel_rusak\` and re-learned). Fixes:
  `I3Pack(jalur, mentah_v2=True)` skips V2 decryption (what the harvest now uses), `TabelV2.identitas()`,
  `pelajari_v2` refuses to save an identity table or one where every probe came back unchanged, and
  `tabel_v2()` treats an identity file on disk as **not learned** (recording the mask in `_tabel_rusak`) so a
  damaged table can never hand out garbage again. Tests in `uji_i3pack.py` (now 29 checks).
  Harvested so far: 1:00, 1:10, 1:38, 1:90, 2:00, 2:38, 2:3A, 2:43, 2:50, 2:58, 2:8D (the user learned three of
  those from the GUI themselves; by 2026-09-24 the `Cipher V2\` folder holds 93 tables, the rest learned by them). A sweep of `Pack 3.88` (5,516 packs) finds **278 distinct keys** - about an hour
  and 55 MB to harvest them all, so on-demand learning is the default. Keys are NOT derivable from one another:
  across keys ~194 of 256 rows differ by a constant and the rest (positions 7, 9, 12, 15 mod 16) by nothing simple,
  unlike the class relation.
- Packs from a **newer client** (about 3,300 of the 5,518 in `Pack 3.88`) carry marker top byte `0x98..0x9F`:
  after the count field comes a **u16 type/key**, and the 92-byte entries are **not rotated 2 bits** but
  enciphered with V2 as standalone 92-byte buffers (class 92). The key can differ per node inside one pack
  (`Weapon_Tambourine_PBIC2024_Neon`: 2:50 on the node with files, 2:00 on the empty ones), so it is stored on
  `Node`, and a save keeps that format. Proof: reading `Weapon_Tambourine_PBIC2024_Neon.i3Pack` gives all 10
  files byte-identical to what the old exe extracts after its own `convert-cipher --to v1`.
- `i3pack.simpan()` re-reads what it wrote and compares every node path, file path, content and cipher flag before
  replacing the target (write to `<file>.<pid>.tmp`, then `os.replace`). The header's 16-byte hash at 0x3C is zeroed,
  which is what the old exe does too.
- Reading the whole client `Pack\` folder: 3,557 packs, 27,271 files, 0 failures; 3,332 of them rewritten and
  verified. A handful of packs carry junk entries pointing outside the file (`Build by www.fb.com(`,
  `ApexK_Abigail.i3i`) -- those are skipped with a note (the old exe refuses some of those packs outright).

### Tanda pemilik di dalam pack (2026-10-06)

User: "apakah anda bisa menambahkan sisi nama saya di dalam file i3pack ... nanti bisa
di lihat melalui notepad atau hex editor ... kalau ketahuan orang ambil, nama saya ada
di dalamnya untuk pengecekan".

Blok teks ditempel **di ujung file, sesudah isi node terakhir**::

    \r\n[I3PACK-SIGN]\r\n
    Pemilik : HeavyRain
    Alat    : I3Pack Editor V3
    Waktu   : 2026-10-06 22:04:57
    Sidik   : <md5 seluruh byte SEBELUM blok ini>
    Catatan : (opsional)
    [/I3PACK-SIGN]\r\n

**Kenapa di situ aman**: pembaca pack - ini maupun engine - selalu mencari objek lewat
tabel objek di header, dan **tidak ada satu pun medan yang menyebut panjang file**, jadi
byte di belakang isi node terakhir tidak pernah dibaca. Pembacanya cuma memeriksa
`off + size > len(b)`, yang tetap terpenuhi.

**Idempoten tanpa kode tambahan**: `simpan()` menulis ulang file dari nol (header +
string + tabel + isi node), jadi blok lama otomatis tidak ikut tertulis. Menyimpan
berkali-kali tidak pernah menumpuk - ada ujinya (3x simpan, tetap satu blok).

`i3pack.py`: `TANDA_AWAL` / `TANDA_AKHIR` / `blok_tanda()` / `lepas_tanda()` /
`baca_tanda()`, dan `simpan(..., tanda=None, catatan='')`. **Bawaan `tanda=None`**, jadi
seluruh pemanggil dan uji lama tidak berubah artinya - yang menyalakannya jendelanya.
Sidik dihitung sambil menulis (`hashlib.md5` diumpani per potongan), jadi pack 94 MB
tidak perlu masuk memori.

`baca_tanda()` mengembalikan `utuh`: sidik dihitung ULANG dari isi di depan blok, jadi
kalau ada yang menyunting pack-nya sesudah ditandai nilainya False. Itu yang membuat
tanda ini berguna untuk pengecekan, bukan sekadar nama.

GUI: menu `Alat > Tanda pemilik di dalam pack...` (nama + catatan + kotak centang,
disimpan di ini sebagai `tanda_aktif` / `tanda_nama` / `tanda_catatan`, **bawaan AKTIF
dengan nama HeavyRain**), dan `Info pack...` menampilkan tanda yang ada beserta
status utuh/tidak.

**Urutan dengan kode proteksi**: kode di 0x3C itu HMAC-MD5 atas ISI FILE, jadi untuk
pack yang benar-benar diperiksa client (`Pack/<Map>.i3Pack`, `Pack/Script.i3Pack`)
stempelnya harus dipasang **sesudah** tandanya. Menyimpan dulu (tanda ikut), baru
`Alat > Apply the Zepetto.inc Protection Stamp.`

Batasnya disebut terus terang ke user dan tertulis di dialognya: siapa pun yang
menyimpan ulang pack itu dengan program yang sama bisa menimpa tandanya. Ini untuk
pengecekan, bukan kunci.

`uji_i3pack_tanda.py` **26 pemeriksaan** (termasuk: pack tanpa tanda tetap byte-identik,
pack bertanda tetap terbaca utuh isi+cipher, 3x simpan tetap satu blok, menyimpan tanpa
tanda membuang blok lama dan hasilnya byte-identik dengan pack polos, `utuh` jadi False
begitu isinya disunting, dan pack client sungguhan) dan `uji_i3pack_tanda_gui.py` **22**
(jendela digerakkan in-process; `messagebox` DIPATOK sejak awal supaya kotak modal tidak
menggantung uji, dan `BERKAS_ATUR` dialihkan supaya ini milik user tidak tersentuh).
Regresi: `uji_i3pack.py` 49, `uji_i3pack_gui.py` 142, `uji_i3pack_kode.py` 22,
`uji_i3obj.py` 34, `uji_i3vtex.py` 28, `uji_i3pack_jelajah.py` 11.

Sekalian dibetulkan: komentar di `simpan()` yang masih menyebut kode proteksi "opaque,
tidak bergantung isi berkas sama sekali" - itu kesimpulan lama yang sudah terbantah
(lihat bagian "kode proteksi = HMAC-MD5 kunci Zepetto Inc.").

### Tanda pemilik juga di `.I3CHR` -- dan dua jebakan yang khusus ada di situ (2026-10-06)

User: "untuk i3chr maker dan i3chr editor bisa tambahkan juga ?"

Formatnya dipindah ke **`i3tanda.py`** supaya satu bentuk dipakai semua alat
(`i3pack` meneruskan ke situ, nama publik lamanya dipertahankan), plus
**`i3tandaui.py`** berisi dialognya - dipisah supaya pustakanya tetap bebas tkinter.
Setelannya SATU untuk semua alat di **`I3Tanda.ini`** sebelah program, jadi nama cukup
diisi sekali; kunci lama di `I3Pack Editor V3.ini` dipakai sekali sebagai pindahan.

Dua hal yang di `.i3Pack` gratis tapi di `.I3CHR` TIDAK:

1. **`i3chr.I3CHR.simpan()` menyalin seluruh wilayah data sampai EOF apa adanya**
   (`body = f.b[region:len(f.b)]`). Jadi blok tanda lama ikut tersalin dan blok baru
   menumpuk di belakangnya. -> `body` dibersihkan dengan `i3tanda.lepas()`. Di `.i3Pack`
   ini tidak pernah jadi masalah karena penulisnya menyusun ulang berkas dari nol.
2. **`_hitung_ekor()` menghitung ekor objek TERAKHIR sampai EOF.** Kalau objek itu
   kebetulan punya chunk sungguhan (mis. `SND1`), blok tanda ikut terjahit ke dalam
   objeknya waktu disimpan - dan chunk `SND1` yang rusak itulah yang dulu membuat senjata
   "tidak bisa menembak". -> batas akhirnya dipotong sepanjang blok tanda.
   Penyaring `3 huruf + 1 angka` kebetulan sudah menolak blok tanda (`\r\n[` bukan tag),
   tapi itu kebetulan, bukan jaminan: objek terakhirnya berbeda-beda - `i3AI` di
   `SWAT_Female`/`SWAT_Male`, `i3AIContext` di 757 dari 757 berkas senjata.

Jendelanya punya **DUA panel dengan jalur simpan sendiri-sendiri** (`PanelKarakter` lewat
`self.chr.simpan`, `PanelSenjata` lewat `self.s.simpan` -> `i3senjata.Senjata.simpan` ->
`i3chr`), jadi keduanya harus ditambal. Tambalan pertama cuma mengenai panel karakter dan
ujinya tidak menangkapnya - sampai uji panel senjata ditambahkan.

Nilai `TANDA_ALAT` per alat (`I3Pack Editor V3` / `I3CHR Editor V3` / `I3CHR Maker V3`)
ditulis di baris `Alat :`, jadi berkas hasilnya menyebut sendiri ia dibuat program mana.

`uji_i3chr_tanda.py` **32 pemeriksaan** dan `uji_i3chr_tanda_gui.py` **23**. Yang paling
menjaga: simpan tanpa tanda tetap **byte-identik** dengan `Base I3CHR` bawaan, **37 chunk
SND1** utuh sesudah ditandai DAN sesudah 3x simpan, ekor `i3AIContext` tidak berubah, blok
tanda tidak terjahit ke objek mana pun, berkas maker bertanda tetap lolos `periksa()`, dan
ketiga jalur simpan (panel karakter, panel senjata, maker) diuji terpisah.

Dua kesalahan uji yang ikut ketemu dan pantas diingat:

* pemeriksaan "SND1 utuh" versi pertama mencari `b'SND1'` di `o.data` dan selalu memberi
  **0 == 0** - chunk itu memang tersimpan di LUAR ukuran objek. Yang benar daftar
  `I3CHR.ekor`, dan syaratnya ditambah `> 0` supaya "tidak ada yang dijaga" ikut gagal;
* `messagebox` harus dipatok **di `i3tandaui`**, bukan cuma di modul jendelanya - dialognya
  tinggal di sana, jadi tanpa itu kotak modal sungguhan bisa menggantung uji.

### File Browser selalu di atas + ikon program di semua jendela (2026-09-25)

User: "file browser nya buat selalu diatas. jadi kalau di tekan mouse di tidak hilang form nya.
lalu logo nya juga ganti".

- `JendelaJelajah` dapat `tk.BooleanVar` **`atas`** + kotak centang `Selalu di atas` (bawaan ON,
  disimpan di ini sebagai `jelajah_atas`) dan metode `pasang_atas()` yang menyetel
  `attributes('-topmost', ...)`. Diuji sampai lapisan Windows: `WS_EX_TOPMOST` (0x8) benar-benar
  muncul dan hilang di `GetWindowLongW(hwnd, GWL_EXSTYLE)`.
- Ikon: `App.__init__` kini memanggil **`self.iconbitmap(_ike, default=_ike)`**. Argumen `default=`
  memasang ikon untuk SELURUH jendela program, termasuk Toplevel yang dibuat belakangan -
  `iconbitmap()` biasa hanya mengenai satu jendela, itu sebabnya File Browser masih memakai ikon
  bulu tkinter. `pasang_tema_jendela()` juga memanggil `iconbitmap` per jendela sebagai cadangan.
- **Membandingkan HICON antar-jendela adalah uji yang salah**: tiap jendela memuat ikonnya sendiri,
  jadi handle-nya pasti berbeda. Yang benar membandingkan GAMBARNYA (`GetIconInfo` +
  `GetDIBits` lalu hash). Dua jebakan lain di situ: handle 64-bit harus lewat `argtypes`
  (`c_void_p`) atau ctypes melempar `int too long to convert`, dan **ikon root Tk dipasang lewat
  WNDCLASS** sehingga `WM_GETICON` mengembalikan 0 - harus jatuh ke `GetClassLongPtrW(hwnd, -14)`.
- Uji: `uji_i3pack_jelajah.py` (**11 pemeriksaan**). Regresi `uji_i3pack.py` 29,

### Icons, credit and the exe icon (2026-09-24)

User: "Oke tambahkan disini I3Packtool Editor V3 By HeavyRain / ganti icon exe nya di folder
HeavyRain\Icon\IconExe.ico / tambahkan icon didepan nama sesuai ekstensi dalam file i3pack tersebut".

- `Icon\` holds one `.ico` per file extension, **named after the extension** (`I3I.ico` -> `.i3i`,
  `RSC.ico` -> `.rsc`, `Txt.ico` -> `.txt`, `Wav.ico` -> `.wav`, `I3Animpack.ico`, `I3S.ico`, `PEF.ico`).
  `PustakaIkon` walks the folder, so a new type needs only a new `.ico`, no code change. Four names in
  `IKON_KHUSUS` have a job instead of an extension and are skipped by that mapping: `IconExe.ico` (window +
  exe), `Folder.ico` (the left tree, via `untuk_folder()`), `NoIcon.ico` (fallback for any extension with no
  icon of its own - so `untuk()` no longer returns '' once it exists) and `Kunci.ico` (padlock override).
- Tk 8.6 loads PNG but **not** `.ico`, and Pillow is not a dependency, so the `.pyw` converts them itself:
  `ico_ke_png` picks the entry nearest 16x16, `_dib_ke_rgba` decodes the BITMAPINFOHEADER (32/24/8/4/1 bpp,
  bottom-up rows padded to 4 bytes, AND-mask bit 1 = transparent), then `_png` writes an RGBA PNG through
  `zlib` and it goes to `tk.PhotoImage(data=base64)`. All 7 project icons decode; the 24 bpp ones need the
  AND mask or they come out on a black square.
- The file list became `show='tree headings'` with `#0` at width 38 holding only the image (28 put the icon
  right against the name - the user asked for the gap); the `nama` column and every `values` index stayed
  where they were, so the older tests did not move.
- **Padlock overlay** (2026-09-24, "bisa ga tambah icon kunci untuk cipher yang terkunci"): a SECURE file's
  row icon gets a 7x9 padlock composited into its bottom-right corner - **amber** normally, **red** when
  `mentah and mask` (V2 content whose key has not been learned, so it cannot be read yet). A file whose
  extension has no icon shows the padlock alone. The badge is drawn from a small ASCII pixel map
  (`GEMBOK` / `gambar_gembok`) so nothing extra ships, but `Icon\Kunci.ico` overrides it if present.
  `PustakaIkon` therefore keeps raw RGBA per extension in `.rgba` and caches finished `PhotoImage`s in
  `.peta` keyed by `(ext, terkunci, merah)` - tests that looked for an extension in `.peta` must use
  `.rgba` now. `ico_ke_rgba` is the primary decoder (`ico_ke_png` wraps it) and prefers DIB entries;
  an `.ico` holding only PNG-compressed images is refused into `self.gagal` rather than half-handled.
- `folder_ikon()` prefers `HERE\Icon` and falls back to `sys._MEIPASS\Icon`, so the exe is built with
  `--add-data "Icon;Icon"` and still shows icons when moved alone, while a folder next to the exe wins
  (icons replaceable without a rebuild). `--icon Icon\IconExe.ico` sets the exe/window icon; the exe test
  checks RT_ICON id 1 has exactly the size of the image inside `IconExe.ico` (7336 bytes).
- `KREDIT = 'I3Packtool Editor V3 By HeavyRain'` is shown in `Bantuan > Tentang`.
- **Light / dark theme** (2026-09-24): menu `Tampilan`, remembered in the ini as `[umum] tema`.
  `TEMA` holds the two palettes and `terapkan_tema(akar, nama)` sets the ttk Style then walks the widget
  tree with `_warnai_klasik` for the classic widgets (`Menu`, `Text`, `Toplevel`, `Scrollbar`) that
  `ttk.Style` does not reach; `pasang_tema_jendela(induk, jendela)` does the same for each Toplevel as it
  is built. Two things learned: **dark must use the `clam` ttk theme** - Windows' native `vista` theme
  paints its own colours and ignores most `configure`, so a forced dark ends up patchy; and **the classic
  `Scrollbar` stays white on Windows** however you colour it, so `ScrolledText` was replaced by the little
  `teks_bergulir()` helper (`tk.Text` + `ttk.Scrollbar`) for the log and the content viewer.
  Row tags (`diganti`/`baru`) and the accent labels get per-theme colours (`Aksen.TLabel`).
  Testing note: `widget.cget(...)` and `tag_configure(..., 'background')` return Tcl objects, so compare
  with `str(...)` or an obviously-correct colour looks like a failure.

### Cipher type 16 -- a pack nobody's tool can open, recovered by diffing (2026-09-29)

User: "Apakah anda bisa membuka file Script_Encrypt.i3Pack ?? sedangkan Script_Original.i3Pack
nya bisa." Both in `HeavyRain\Script\`, ~94 MB each, same content, one readable.

The container is identical in both - I3R2 header, object table, and the root node `/` (entry key
2:00) match byte for byte. The whole difference is the `config` node's **entry-list cipher**:

    Script_Original   marker 0x98  entry key V2 type 2  key D8   27 files   -> opens
    Script_Encrypt    marker 0x98  entry key V2 type **16** key 45   25 files   -> refused

**Type 16 (0x10) is outside every implementation available.** Across the user's 3,572 client packs
plus `Pack 3.88` only types 1, 2 and 3 ever appear. The newest tool on the machine -
`i3PackEditor.exe` inside `Downloads\Compressed
ew_tools.rar` (403,456 B, May 2026, the Spanish
"PB Latino" build, `i3PackEditor v3.1.lnk` on the desktop points at it) - implements only
`--to v2-1/v2-2/v2-3` and labels anything else `cipher V2 desconocido`, with the giveaway line
**"Necesitas extraer la key con runtime hook (Frida) primero."** So the oracle-harvest route
(`pelajari_v2`) cannot produce this table: the oracle does not have the algorithm.

**A wrong harvested table is worse than none.** `Cipher V2\pbm_10_45.bin` had been produced that
day and `tabel_v2(0x1045)` happily returned it, so `i3pack` "decrypted" the entry list into
garbage and reported "13 dari 25 entri rusak" instead of saying the key was unknown. Tested
against 22 entries whose plaintext is now proven, it reproduces **3 of 1,408 bytes (0.2 %)** -
random. Moved to `Cipher V2\_tabel_rusak\`. Note `TabelV2.identitas()` does NOT catch this kind
of bad table: it is a real permutation, just the wrong one.

**The pack was recovered anyway, without breaking the cipher**, because the file DATA is not
re-encrypted - the blobs are byte-identical to the original's, only shifted (184 bytes at the
start, more later). Three independent levers, all offline:

- **The cipher is a per-position substitution, so byte equality survives it.** `S[i][p] == S[j][p]`
  iff the plaintexts agree at `p`. Feeding the original's names (minus the two that were dropped)
  through that test gives **0 conflicts over 14,784 comparisons** for 22 of the 25 entries - proof
  of the name list AND the order, with no key at all.
- **The layout pins offset and size.** Matching each original blob into the new file, then filling
  the gaps, produces 25 ranges that tile `2656 .. 94,508,570` exactly - no gap, no overlap, ending
  precisely where the root node object starts. The one ambiguous split (GameEffectSoundMapper /
  Goods) was resolved by searching the gap for Goods.Pef's own first 12 ciphertext bytes from the
  original pack: a `.Pef` decrypts to plain I3R2 and its first chunk is a full 65,536 (class 0), so
  the same key gives the identical header ciphertext.
- **Known plaintext then decrypts the tails.** Building the 28-byte tails of the 18 byte-identical
  files (mask/flags/hash from the original, offset/size from the layout) and learning positions
  64..91 gives **0 conflicts**, and reading the other tails back confirms mask, flags, offset and
  size. That is also how the tail layout got re-confirmed: distinct-value counts per position come
  out 21/3/2/2 (mask, flags), 25/25 (hash lo), 23/25 (size lo), 20/3 (offset hi), 12/2 (size hi),
  1/1 (zeros), 25/24 (hash hi), 23/24 (offset lo), then ten zeros.

Delivered `Script\Script_Encrypt (terbaca).i3Pack`: **2,297 bytes differ** from the encrypted
original (the 2-byte key plus the 2,300-byte entry list, re-ciphered with 2:D8); every file blob
untouched. It opens in I3Pack Editor V3 and V3.12, 25 files, and `Script\BACA INI.txt` carries the
findings. Contents vs the original: **2 removed** (`BC.i3Game`, `SubstituteWeaponList.txt`),
**7 changed**, 16 byte-identical.

Two things are NOT recovered, and the readme says so:

- **Three names carry a shared 13-character prefix**: `<13>Character.Pef` (26), `<13>Equipment.Pef`
  (26), `<13>Weapon.Pef` (23). The lengths fit exactly, the three share a 13-byte ciphertext prefix,
  entries 3 and 7 additionally share positions 22..25 (`.Pef`), and the letters that could be read
  land where they should (`a`@17 / `t`@19 for Character; `p`@17 / `e`@19 / `n`@20 for Equipment).
  The prefix itself is unreadable: none of its 13 bytes appears at the same position in any of the
  22 known names, so there is no way into those rows. `pbm` rows are independent permutations - a
  survey of three tables shows `s0` row `i` is neither `row 0 + c` nor `row 0 ^ c` (254 of 255 rows
  unrelated), so one row cannot be extrapolated from another.
- **Quest.Pef's key.** Its mask's type byte reads 0x03 but the key byte does not, and its content
  differs from the original in **every** byte at the same size - which means a different key, since
  a same-key file would keep its I3R2 header ciphertext. Written as 3:F5 (the original's) and
  flagged. The other six changed files are confirmed same-key; for `Emotion.Pef` and
  `GameEffectSoundMapper.textdata` the whole ciphertext differs only because **the size changed and
  the class is `len(chunk) % 256`**, so every substitution row changes - not evidence of a new key
  (`Emotion.Pef` decrypts to I3R2 under 3:09, proving it).

Worth remembering generally: **a pack whose entry list will not decode is not necessarily lost** -
if any sibling build of it exists, the data region is the map back in.

## `.RSC` fully decoded - TWO entry forms - `i3rsc.py` + `I3RSC Editor V3` (2026-09-25)

User: "Buatkan saya RSC Editor yang bisa ambil data dari RSC lain. RSC punya saya tidak biasa."
The "tidak biasa" is real and has three separate causes, all found by surveying the **109 `.RSC`
inside the client's packs**.

### 1. There are two entry forms, and `i3ins.baca_rsc` only knew one

Berkas = `RSCF` + u32 jumlah entri, lalu entri berturut-turut. Kepala entri selalu
`magic | u32 tipe | u32 len(s1) | u32 len(s2) | u32 x` lalu `s1 NUL s2 NUL`, tapi:

| | dipakai di | s1 / s2 | field ke-4 | ekor |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **RSC2** (90 berkas) | RSC per-map `Scene/<Map>/<Map>.RSC` | jalur ditulis **dua kali** | offset entri ini | 72 byte untuk tipe 5 & 7 |
| **RSC1** (19 berkas) | RSC global `Chara/AnimPack.RSC`, `Chara/Character.RSC`, `Weapon/Weapon.RSC`, `Equip/*.RSC`, `Effect/Define/*.RSC`, `Sound/*.RSC` | s1 = **nama**, s2 = **jalur** (backslash) | selalu 0 | **tidak ada** |

`i3ins.baca_rsc` hanya mengenal `RSC2`, jadi 19 berkas itu gagal dengan
"entri 0 (offset 8) tidak dikenal" - itulah yang bikin RSC global tidak bisa dibuka.

### 2. Nomor tipe artinya BEDA antara kedua bentuk

Dihitung dari seluruh 109 berkas (ekstensi vs nomor tipe):

    RSC1: 0 .i3s   1 .I3CHR  2 .i3WRD  4 .i3i   5 .wav  6 .pth  7 .i3AnimPack  8 .i3Obj
    RSC2: 0 .i3a   2 .i3i    4 .wav    5 .i3WRD 7 .i3s  8 .i3Obj 9 .i3Light 11 .i3Path 12 .i3Evt

Jadi **tipe 7 = `.i3AnimPack` di RSC1 tapi `.i3s` di RSC2**. Menyalin entri antar bentuk harus
menghitung ulang nomornya dari ekstensi - `_ubah_bentuk()` melakukan itu.

### 3. Sesudah entri terakhir ada PENUTUP BERKAS, dan sebagian kena cap air tool lain

54 dari 109 berkas punya sisa byte sesudah entri terakhir. Dua hal berbeda bercampur di situ:

- ekor milik entri terakhir (RSC2 tipe 5/7, 72 byte `ff ff ff ff 30` + `cc`...), dan
- **penutup milik berkas**: RSC1 global menyimpan setelan di situ (`Sound/*.RSC` 16 byte =
  2 float + 2 u32, `Weapon/Weapon.RSC` dan `Effect/Define/Effects_*.RSC` 132 byte,
  `Equip/Equip.RSC` dan `Chara/Character.RSC` 189 byte).
- **9 berkas kena cap air `" RSC Reader - By Skript47 (www.LiveToWin34.blogspot..."`**
  (`Chara/AnimPack.RSC`, `Chara/CharaTexture.RSC`, `Effect/Define/EffectImage.RSC`,
  `Equip/EquipTexture.RSC`, `Weapon/WeaponAnimPack.RSC`, `Sound/Character|Interface|Object|Voice.RSC`)
  - sisa dari tool yang pernah menyunting berkas itu.

`FileRSC` memisah keduanya (`entri[-1].ekor` vs `ekor_file`), jadi **menghapus entri terakhir
tidak ikut membuang penutup berkas** - kalau digabung jadi satu, setelan suara/senjata hilang
diam-diam. Ada pemeriksaannya di uji.

**Panjang ekor ditentukan oleh (bentuk, tipe), dan harus diukur - bukan ditebak.** Versi pertama
menebak "72 byte kalau RSC2 tipe 5/7, selain itu 0", dan itu SALAH: user menggeser entri
`Sound/Object/Explosion/OB_SiegeGolem_death.wav` (RSC2 **tipe 4, ekor 16 byte**) ke posisi
terakhir, lalu Simpan berhenti dengan *"verifikasi gagal pada entri ...OB_SiegeGolem_death.wav"* -
entri itu ditulis dengan 16 byte ekor tapi dibaca balik tanpa ekor. Tabel hasil pengukuran atas
seluruh 109 berkas (tiap pasangan hanya punya SATU panjang):

    RSC1: 0 -> 132   1 -> 132   2 -> 132   4 -> 0    5 -> 16   6 -> 0   7 -> 0   8 -> 0
    RSC2: 0 -> 0     2 -> 0     4 -> 16    5 -> 72   7 -> 72   8 -> 0   9 -> 0   11 -> 0   12 -> 0

Jadi catatan "entri RSC1 tidak punya ekor" hanya benar untuk tipe 4/6/7/8; tipe 0/1/2 justru
132 byte. `_panjang_ekor()` memakai **entri lain dengan (bentuk, tipe) sama di berkas itu**
lebih dulu, baru tabel di atas - jadi tipe yang belum pernah terlihat pun ikut benar. Entri baru
juga meniru ekor saudara setipe (`ekor_contoh()`). Uji regresinya menjadikan SETIAP tipe sebagai
entri terakhir lalu menyimpan.

### Alatnya

- **`i3rsc.py`**: `FileRSC` (baca/sunting/`simpan()` dengan verifikasi lewat berkas sementara),
  `Entri` (`nama`/`jalur` menyesuaikan bentuk), `nama_tipe(tipe, magic)`, `tipe_untuk(jalur, magic)`,
  `tambah/hapus/duplikat/pindah`, `normalkan_offset()`, dan **`impor(lain, indeks, posisi,
  lewati_sama, samakan_bentuk)`** - fitur yang diminta. CLI `info` / `daftar` / `impor`.
- **`I3RSC Editor V3.pyw` + `.exe`** (alat ke-13): tabel #/Bentuk/Tipe/Nama/Jalur dengan kotak
  cari, panel sunting, tambah/duplikat/hapus/naik/turun, **Ambil dari RSC lain...** (sumbernya
  boleh `.RSC` lepas ATAU dari dalam `.i3Pack`; entri yang jalurnya sudah ada ditandai abu-abu
  dan dilewati), serta **buka/simpan langsung dari/ke dalam `.i3Pack`**.
- Field offset entri **dipertahankan apa adanya** waktu menulis. Itulah sebabnya ke-109 berkas
  bisa ditulis ulang byte-identik, termasuk `Holiday.RSC` yang 113 dari 175 offsetnya basi
  (`i3ins.isi_rsc` menghitung ulang, jadi berkas itu berubah di sana).
- Uji: **`uji_i3rsc.py` 59 pemeriksaan** - 109 berkas terbaca + identik byte, beda kedua bentuk,
  penutup berkas selamat saat entri terakhir dihapus, sunting, impor (biasa, lintas bentuk,
  tanpa samakan bentuk, dengan posisi, tanpa lewati), dua penolakan, dan jendelanya digerakkan
  in-process sampai Ambil + Simpan.
- Exe dibangun dengan `--icon Icon\RSC.ico --add-data "Icon;Icon" --hidden-import i3rsc
  --hidden-import i3pack`; diuji di folder tanpa satu pun `.py`.

## Moving models between maps -- `i3viewer.py` + I3Viewer Editor V3 (2026-09-26)

User: "Apakah anda bisa membuat i3viewer editor ?? saya ingin ambil isi model di map lain dan memasukannya ke
map crackdown ... Dalam mode 3D dan bisa seret model nya sesuka hati. Ini berlaku terhadap i3s v3 dan v1."

The **fourteenth tool**. `i3viewer.Adegan` reads a scene `.I3S` into a reference graph (like
`pindah_karakter.baca`, but tolerant enough for map scenes), lists the models in it, copies a model's whole
subtree out of another scene, and places it under a new `i3Transform`. The GUI draws the map with `i3gl` and
drags the model with the mouse.

**Read/write gate**: all 51 `.i3s`/`.I3S` on this machine (map worlds, skies, collisions, golem object scenes)
read and rewrite **byte-identically**; the only refusal is `SweetCrackdown_Light.i3s`, a collider set
(`i3CollideeMesh`) that `i3col` does not support either. Tests: `uji_i3viewer.py`, **183 checks**, all pass.

### The find that mattered most: `IIA2 +12` is the INDEX WIDTH

`i3IndexArray` / `IIA2` header: `+4` count, **`+12` u32 index width (0 = u16, 1 = u32)**, `+20` cipher word,
indices at `+32`. Measured across **2,656 IIA2 arrays in 449 client scenes: the flag matches the object size
without a single exception** (1,473 are 16-bit, 1,183 are 32-bit).

`i3gl` had always read u16, so **44 % of index arrays were being drawn from the wrong bytes** - every 32-bit map
rendered as shredded spikes in the 3D tabs of I3Collision / I3INS / I3Path Editor. Fixed in `i3gl._geometri`
(width from the flag, `GL_UNSIGNED_INT` when 4) and in `i3viewer.lebar_indeks`. Proven by rendering
`RothenVillage_World.I3S` (all 32-bit) with the old assumption forced back on: garbage before, the whole
snow-covered village after. Crackdown is 16-bit, which is why this was never noticed on it.

### One vertex array is shared by the whole map

`RothenVillage_World.I3S` has **3 `i3VertexArray` for 976 objects** - the biggest holds 132,714 vertices
(5.3 MB) and is used by 138 meshes; each mesh has its own small `i3IndexArray`. So:

- a model's bounding box must be computed from **only the vertices its triangles reference**, or every model
  reports the bbox of the entire map (the bug the test `kotak batas tiap model berbeda` guards);
- an import must **compact** the arrays (`_padatkan`: union of used vertices, remap, rewrite each IA),
  otherwise copying one snowman drags the whole map along. Measured: 5.0 MB saved per import, so the snowman
  costs **0.22 MB** instead of 5.3 MB.

`i3GeometryAttr` GEO2 (65 B): `GEO2` | u8 primitive type (4 list, 5 strip) | u32 primitive count | u32 0 |
u32 VA | u32 IA | u32 0 | **24-byte bbox (min xyz, max xyz)** | 12 zeros. Only the first `primitive count`
primitives of the IA belong to that mesh. The bbox **must be rewritten after moving vertices**, or the engine
culls the model from view; `_perbarui_kotak` does that for GEO2 and for the 24-byte bbox in a node's `INF2`
(present when `pbound != 0`).

### Textures travel with the model

Every map scene checked (Crackdown 27, RothenVillage 99, Giran2) stores **all** its textures as **embedded**
`i3Texture` objects holding a whole `.i3i` (magic `I3IB`). So copying a model's subtree brings its textures
with it and the result is self-contained - no pack to edit, nothing to copy. That is what makes this feature
practical at all.

### How a copied model is placed

1. the subtree's closure is deep-copied (nodes, attrs, material, VA/IA, textures);
2. V3-only content is converted (`pk.vertex_lama` Platform 8, `MAT2` -> 68-byte material, IIA2 decrypted with
   the `Cipher V2\` tables) when the target is a V1 scene;
3. vertices are **baked** by the source's world matrix and shifted so the model's own origin is the
   centre-bottom of its bbox - which is also what erases the difference between a map whose root is an
   `i3Transform` (RothenVillage, Z-up style) and one that has none (Crackdown);
4. a new `i3Transform` + `i3MatrixObject` wraps it, so moving later is 16 floats, not a vertex rewrite;
5. the new objects are inserted **before the SGI in topological order** (referenced object always first), so
   there is never an `i3GeometryAttr` pointing at a buffer behind it - the
   `i3VertexArrayDX::Lock Asserted : m_pBuffer` trap.

`Adegan.tumpu()` / `set_tumpu()` work in terms of that centre-bottom point, so the X/Y/Z in the panel stay the
spot the model stands on even when it is rotated or scaled. `set_penempatan` must refresh the world matrix of
the **whole subtree** (`segarkan_matriks`) - meshes are read through each `i3Geometry` simpul's own matrix, so
updating only the wrapper made scale and rotation look like they did nothing until the file was reopened.

`bungkus()` wraps a model the map already had in an identity `i3Transform` ("Bisa dipindah" in the GUI) so the
original scenery can be moved too. It deliberately does **not** bake: the vertex array is shared, so baking
would move other models with it.

### Three format details the old readers tripped on

- **Declared sizes overlap.** `i3LuxMapBindAttr` writes 4 bytes but declares 8, so the next object starts 4
  bytes early. `Objek.lebih` remembers the surplus and writes it back, which is why these files round-trip.
  (`pindah_karakter.baca` refuses them with "bertumpuk dengan objek sebelumnya".)
- **`i3AttrSet` has an untagged old form**: no `ATS1`, just `u16 count` + `count x u32` after the INF2 block.
  `i3gl` already knew this; the graph readers did not.
- **External raw ids have an older form**, the same family as `.i3WRD`'s: `0xFFFF0000 | string index`, with the
  object's own id implied by its table position and the reference carrying the full raw id.
  `Object/cgame/Siege_Golem/Siege_Golem_Setting.i3s` is the sample (its texture entry is `0xFFFF0023`, and
  string 35 is `Object\cgame\Siege_Golem/SIEGE_GOLEM.i3i`). `pindah_bone.I3R2` now reads both forms and
  `i3viewer` writes back whichever the object had. **Regression over all 480 i3 files on this machine: 462
  identical, 0 changed, 2 that used to be refused now read** (the two golem scenes). `Adegan.anak_objek` also
  walks `i3Body -> SKN2 -> i3LOD -> shape`, which is what makes those bodied scenes list a model at all.

### The header is never re-laid out

`Adegan.isi()` keeps the source header (**version included**) and every existing object's bytes and order; only
the parent's kid list changes and new objects are appended. That matters: the user's own
`Desktop\Pack\World\Crackdown\Crackdown_World.I3S` had been re-saved by an i3Engine tool - version
0x00070001 -> 0x00090001, 5.7 MB -> 11.2 MB, objects re-laid out - which is exactly the shape the legacy client
rejects (the Dasom_Red case). Output of this tool stays 0x00070001.

Verified against the engine: Crackdown with the snowman, the clock and the cask imported opens in i3Viewer2
with `Cifrado: limpio (sin hits)` and an **empty `i3Viewer2.log`**. **Not tested in game yet.**

### Collision for a placed model (2026-09-26)

User: "Coba tambahkan tabrakan di alat ini." A model dropped into a map is scenery until the map's collision
files get a matching shape, so the editor now drives `i3col` alongside the scene.

- On opening a scene the editor looks for `<Map>_Col_Hero.I3S` (player collision) and `<Map>_Col_Hit.I3S`
  (bullet collision) **next to the scene file**, and - when the scene came from a `.i3Pack` - inside the
  sibling `<Map>_Col*.i3pack` packs. "Buka berkas..." picks them by hand. `i3col.ColFile` gained a `data=`
  argument so a collision file can be read straight out of a pack (round-trips byte-identically from there).
- **"Buat tabrakan untuk model ini"** adds a box to each ticked file. The box is built from the model's
  **local** bounding box times its scale, with the model's yaw - not from the world AABB - so it hugs a
  rotated model instead of swelling around it.
- The link between a model and its box is **only the name**: the box is called `MDL_<model label>`
  (`i3viewer.nama_tabrakan`, sanitised to i3col's 1-31 printable-ASCII rule). Nothing is stored on the side,
  so the pairing survives closing the file, Ctrl+Z, and a later session. To keep that link unambiguous,
  `_tempel` now gives every imported model a label unique within the scene (`..._2`, `..._3`).
- The box **follows the model**: `_ikut_tabrakan` runs after Terapkan and after a mouse drag, and deleting the
  model deletes its box. A rename deletes and re-creates the box, because `i3col` has no rename.
- **Guard**: some "models" in a map scene are one material batch holding many scattered instances -
  `Object_RothenVillage_Ork_Cask` is a single 75 x 1 x 44 m batch of every cask in the village. A collision box
  that size would block the player across the whole map, so anything over `BATAS_KOTAK` (15 m on a side) asks
  first. The model list's Ukuran column shows the same thing before you even import.
- 3D: existing collisions are drawn as thin wireframe and only the selected model's box is filled. Filling
  everything was tried first and is useless - Crackdown's `SM_226` is a ceiling box over the whole map, so the
  entire view turned green. Box edges come from the 8 world corners, paired by edge length (`_rusuk_kotak8`):
  the three shortest distances from one corner are the three sides, and only same-side pairs have exactly those
  distances, so no assumption about PhysX's corner order is needed. Non-box shapes and meshes over 600
  triangles fall back to their AABB, cached per node.
- Saving the scene also saves any changed collision file (`i3col.ColFile.simpan` re-reads and compares every
  collision); a collision file that came from a pack asks for a path, since the base pack must not be
  overwritten.

Regression over every collision file on this machine: **149 read and rewrite byte-identically, 0 differ**
(the refusals in a loose sweep are weapon scenes whose pack name merely contains "Col", plus `_Col_Light.i3s`
collider sets, which `i3col` has never supported).

### Rotate, textures, `.i3a` animation and character scenes (2026-09-26)

User: "bisa di pindahkan dengan mouse ? atas bawah kiri kanan , dan serta memutar kiri kanan atas bawah.
lalu buatkan juga bisa mengganti tekstur. dan bisa menambahkan animasi i3a terhadap object ... kalau bisa
support untuk i3s karakter." Four things, all in place.

**Full rotation.** `matriks_taruh` always composed `S * Ry * Rx * Rz`, but `urai_matriks` only read the yaw
back, so pitch and roll could be written and never seen. It now inverts the composition exactly -
`pitch = asin(R12)`, `roll = atan2(-R10, R11)`, `yaw = atan2(-R02, R22)` on the rows normalised by their own
length (which is the scale) - and returns `(pos, (yaw, pitch, roll), skala)`. Checked over six
yaw/pitch/roll combinations: every angle comes back within 0.01 degrees. `set_penempatan` / `set_tumpu` /
`matriks_taruh` accept the angle either as one number or as that triple (`_sudut3`).

Mouse, on the model: plain drag = slide on the floor, **Shift+drag = up/down**, **Ctrl+drag = rotate**
(horizontal = left/right, vertical = up/down), **Ctrl+Shift+drag = tilt**. The drag now works in
**tumpu space** throughout (`set_tumpu` every frame), which is what makes a model turn on the spot instead
of orbiting its own origin - measured drift over a 60-degree turn: 0.000 m. "Tegakkan lagi" resets all three
angles without moving the model.

`kotak_tabrakan` had to learn about it: i3col can only yaw a box, so a model with pitch or roll gets an
**axis-aligned** box around its world bounding box instead (never smaller than the model), with yaw 0.

**Textures.** `Adegan.tekstur(simpul)` walks the subtree's AttrSets -> bind attrs -> `i3Texture` and reports
role (diffuse / normal / specular / lightmap / ...), name and size; `nama_tekstur` reads the name out of the
embedded `.i3i` header (u16 length at +26, text at +60) and `ukuran_i3i` its width/height/format code.
`ganti_tekstur(tex, data=...)` swaps the embedded bytes (refusing anything not starting `I3IB`) or
`ext=...` points it at an external path. The GUI's **Tekstur** tab lists them, replaces one from a `.i3i`
file (warning first when the pixel size differs, since the model's UVs were made for the old one) and exports
one back to `.i3i`. There is no PNG encoder here, so a new texture has to arrive as `.i3i`.

**Animation from `.i3a`.** A map that really animates (RothenVillage) hangs it off the node:
`i3Transform -> i3TransformSourceCombiner -> i3Animation -> i3TransformSequence`. The decisive find is that
**an `i3TransformSequence` inside a scene is byte-for-byte the same structure as one inside an `.i3a`** -
`u8 len + name | u16 2 | u8 channel flags | 01 01 01 | u32 0 | u32 keys | u32 0 | f32 seconds | the four
channel arrays` - so the track is copied across verbatim, only the name changed.

`set_animasi(simpul, data_i3a, nama_urutan)` therefore: picks a track (the one with the most keys by
default), copies it, appends it to the scene's `i3Animation` (`u8 0 + u32 count + count x (u32 id +
char[32] name)`, creating the object when the scene has none), and builds a 19-byte combiner
`TSC2 + u32 1 + u8 0 + u32 anim + u32 index + u16 1` which the wrapper transform then points at.
`hapus_animasi` reverses it and re-numbers the index inside every other combiner.

**Object order is part of the format here**: RothenVillage has sequences #5-7, animation #8, combiner #9,
node #10 - the combiner is always *before* the node it drives. The first version appended the combiner near
the SGI, i.e. behind the node, which is the same shape as the `i3VertexArrayDX::Lock` forward-reference trap.
`set_animasi` now inserts sequence, animation and combiner ahead of the node.

One `.i3a` holds one track per bone (Air_Kiss: 43), and only ONE is used, because what moves is the whole
model through its node - not bone by bone. A file with several tracks opens a chooser listing keys and
seconds per track. **Whether the V1 client plays a scene animation is untested** - i3Viewer2 accepts the file
with an empty log, and the structure matches a stock animated map, which is as far as offline evidence goes.

**Character `.I3S`.** Three gaps, all closed:

- the reader refused `i3PhysixJointInfoD6` (ragdoll joint, `PJI1` + 404 bytes of float, referencing no
  object - checked across every character scene here) and `i3SkinGeometryAttr` (the 21-byte geometry attr
  plus `SGA1` + u32 palette count + **u32 `i3MemoryBuffer` of the bone palette at +29**);
- `Adegan.mesh` / `_padatkan` / `_perbarui_kotak` only knew `i3GeometryAttr`, so a skinned mesh reported
  zero triangles - `KELAS_GEOATTR` covers both now;
- `i3gl.PetaGL` never walked `i3Body`, so a character drew nothing. It now follows
  `i3Body -> SKN2 -> i3LOD -> BLD1+16 shape` and picks the LOD with the **most triangles** (`_berat_lod`),
  because LOD0 of a PB character is the first-person arms, not the body.

Result: `REBEL_Female.I3S` (283 objects) and `SWAT_Male.I3S` (339) open, rewrite **byte-identically**, list
their parts as models with 14,948 / 17,152 triangles, render textured, and their textures are listed. Note a
character's parts are separate models (`Model_Arms_Material`, `Model_LowBody_Material`, ...), so importing
"a character" into a map brings one part; its external texture paths are reported as missing unless the
`.i3i` files sit alongside.

Tests: `uji_i3viewer.py` grew to **127 checks** (groups 9-13 cover rotation round-trip, textures, animation,
character scenes and the mouse-rotate path in the real window). `uji_i3obj.py` 34, `uji_i3bersih.py` 31,
`uji_i3rsc.py` 59 still pass. A Crackdown carrying a model rotated on three axes, a replaced texture and an
attached animation opens in i3Viewer2 with an **empty log**. **Not tested in game.**

Trap worth keeping: `App._tekan` does a real pick, so a GUI test that drives a drag must stub
`app._tunjuk` or the click silently selects whatever mesh is under that pixel and the drag does nothing.

### Scene tree, bones, and the picking rule (2026-09-26)

User: "ada list direktori nya. lalu menampilkan bone juga untuk karakter ... saya juga mencoba memilih
objek, contoh mobil di crackdown. tapi yang terpilih di cursor malah area tanah atau area sekitarnya."

**The picking rule was wrong.** `_tunjuk` sorted candidates by the distance at which the ray ENTERS their
bounding box and then returned the first one with any triangle hit. A map-wide batch (Crackdown has one whose
bbox is 589 x 17 x 496 m) is entered before a small nearby object, so it won. It now tracks the nearest
**triangle** hit across all candidates and stops early once a candidate's bbox entry is already behind the
best hit - correct and still fast. Measured over 200 random rays into Crackdown: the old rule disagreed with
the true nearest triangle on **64 of them (32 %)**.

**But Crackdown has no car object, and that part is not a bug.** Its world mesh is merged **per material**,
not per object: the 24 models called `Crackdown_1` are batches of 34 x 1 x 35 m (one is 589 x 17 x 496 m), and
`Humvee_Glass` is not a Humvee - it is every glass pane on the map merged into 176 triangles spanning
32 x 0.5 x 40 m. The car body lives inside a batch together with the ground, so selecting it necessarily
selects that batch. A ray into the middle of the car hits exactly two models, both `Crackdown_1`.
RothenVillage is the opposite (`Object_RothenVillage_Snowman_01` and friends are real per-object AttrSets),
which is why picking feels right there. Splitting a batch into separate objects is not something this tool
does.

**The left panel is now the scene graph**, the shape i3Viewer2 calls Grafo de Escena: a `ttk.Treeview` in
`show='tree headings'` mode built from `Adegan.pohon()`, `iid = str(simpul.kunci)`, with Segitiga and
Ukuran filled only for nodes that actually carry mesh. Movable models are green, other mesh models blue,
`i3Body`/`i3LOD`/`i3Skeleton` amber. Picking in 3D opens every ancestor row and scrolls to it; the Cari box
flattens the tree to matching rows. Capped at `BATAS_BARIS` 6000 rows, with the status bar saying so.

**Bones.** `Adegan.kerangka()` returns one entry per `i3Skeleton` reached through `i3LOD -> BLD1+8`, with the
bones already in world space. `tulang_skeleton` reads `BMA1`/`BMA2`: count at +4, `i3MatrixArray` at +8, then
128-byte records - name[32], local matrix at +48, and **depth at +112, which is not a parent index**: the
parent is the nearest earlier bone whose depth is one less. Bone position is the translation row of
`inv4(inverse bind)` from the matrix array.

The catch that cost a probe: those positions are **Z-up**, spanning Y -0.05..0.33 and Z 0..1.61 for
SWAT_Male, while the mesh is Y-up 0..1.67. The i3LOD simpul's own matrix - rows (-1,0,0), (0,0,1), (0,1,0) -
is exactly the Z-up to Y-up conversion, so multiplying by it puts the skeleton on the mesh (1.61 m against a
1.67 m mesh). `kerangka()` does that before returning. Drawn as cyan bones plus yellow joints with the depth
test off, behind the toolbar's **Tulang** checkbox; a map simply has no skeletons and the checkbox does
nothing there.

Tests: `uji_i3viewer.py` group 14 (the suite stood at 141 checks then) - the tree has one root and more rows than models,
selecting a row selects the simpul, Cari filters, a click in the middle of a model returns that model and
**agrees with a brute-force nearest-triangle search**, a map has no skeleton, a character has three (56 / 63 /
25 bones) whose height matches the mesh within 0.4 m, and unticking Tulang really removes them from the
frame (1339 -> 0 cyan pixels in `GLFrame.tangkap()`).

### Skeletal animation lives on the `i3Body`, at `SKN2+12` (2026-09-26)

User: "Animasi di I3Viewer2 harus klik i3Body baru bisa. tapi aplikasi ini tidak bisa. seharusnya
langsung gerak." They were right, and the slot they meant is now decoded.

**`i3Body`'s `SKN2` chunk**: `SKN2` | f32 slope | f32 const | **u32 raw id of an `i3Animation`** |
u32 1 (auto LOD) | 28 zeros | u32 LOD count | LOD ids. The third field is exactly the **Animation**
box in i3Viewer2's i3Body panel, and `i3viewer` was not reading it as a reference at all.

Scanning every `.i3s` on the machine: 634 files carry `SKN2` and **10 have a non-zero animation
slot** - `Siege_Golem_Setting`, `Range_Golem_Setting`, `F_M_Tarantula_Y_LOD2`, the four
`F_S_AD_Santa-CTF` LODs and `Chara\Mermaid_ViperRed\Mermaid_ViperRed.I3S`. Everything else is 0.

**The decisive proof**: Mermaid_ViperRed's embedded animation is **byte-for-byte identical to
`Emote\Salsa_Dance.i3a`** - all 43 tracks, names unchanged. So the recipe a scene needs is simply:

1. every `i3TransformSequence` of the `.i3a` copied verbatim, **its name kept as the bone name**;
2. one `i3Animation` listing them (`u8 0 + u32 count + count x (u32 id + char[32] name)`);
3. that animation's raw id written to `SKN2+12` of the `i3Body`.

**Object order is the same in all five sample files**: the sequences sit contiguously, then the
`i3Animation`, then the `i3Body` - referenced before referrer, as everywhere else in this format.
`set_animasi_badan` inserts exactly there. It deliberately creates a **separate** `i3Animation`
instead of extending an existing one: `SWAT_Male.I3S` already has an `i3Animation` (#315) driven by
six `i3TransformSourceCombiner`s for its dummy bones, and it sits *after* the body - reusing it
would have meant moving it, which would break those combiners.

`Adegan.badan()` / `animasi_badan()` / `set_animasi_badan()` / `hapus_animasi_badan()`. Removal uses
the new `_buang_objek()` and **not `bersihkan()`**: converter output keeps deliberate orphan objects
that `bersihkan()` would throw away.

Round trip proven both ways: stripping Mermaid_ViperRed's animation and re-attaching `Salsa_Dance.i3a`
reproduces the file **byte for byte** (1,569,164 bytes), and attaching/removing on `WarDog_Red.I3S`
returns it byte-identical to the original.

**i3Viewer2 plays it straight from the file** - SWAT_Male + `Air_Kiss.i3a` and WarDog_Red +
`Salsa_Dance.i3a` both open already posed mid-animation, empty `i3Viewer2.log`, "Cifrado: limpio".
**Not tested in game**: whether the V1 client plays a scene animation while the `.I3CHR` state
machine is also driving the character is unknown. Note stock PB does ship skins with one
(`F_S_AD_Santa-CTF`), so the arrangement itself is normal.

### Playing the animation inside the editor -- `i3viewer.Pemutar`

The preview the user asked for ("seharusnya langsung gerak"). It never touches the file.

- **Bone chain**: a bone record's matrix at `BMA+48` is **local to its parent**, and the parent is the
  nearest earlier bone whose depth (`+112`) is one less. Measured: multiplying the local matrices up
  the chain equals `inv4(inverse bind)` to **0.000000** on SWAT_Male, REBEL_Female and
  Mermaid_ViperRed. So posing = replace a bone's local matrix with the sampled TRS and re-multiply.
- **Track layout** (`kunci_urutan`): after the 22-byte sequence header come FOUR arrays of `n` keys -
  position 3f, rotation 4f, scale 3f, time 1f (44 bytes per key). The engine's `.i3a` loader ignores
  the channel flags and always reads all four, which is why `i3anim.ekspor_i3a` must write flag 0x0F.
- **Quaternion is `xyzw`, row-vector convention, no transpose.** Picked by measurement, not guesswork:
  of the four candidates only that one puts `Idle_Stand.i3a`'s first frame near the bind pose
  (mean 28.9 degrees vs 76 / 158 / 155 for the others).
- **`i3SkinGeometryAttr` bone palette**: `SGA1` holds the palette count at +25 and an `i3MemoryBuffer`
  at +29. The buffer is `u32 byte count` then, per palette, `u32 first index | u32 triangle count |
  u32 bone count | that many bytes of skeleton bone numbers`. Proven on REBEL_Female: the ranges are
  0/1048, 3144/782, 5490/1140 - each start is exactly the previous start + 3 x its triangle count.
  Vertex blend indices are numbers **into that palette**, so `_palet()` walks the index array to map
  them back to skeleton bones. Files from the converter (`WarDog_Red`, `Mermaid_ViperRed`) use plain
  `i3GeometryAttr` and index the skeleton directly.
- **Speed** (user asked for 60 fps, 2026-09-26 - and the GPU was never the limit, the skinning is pure
  CPU work). Measured on WarDog_Red + Salsa_Dance, the 3 meshes the renderer actually draws
  (7,367 vertices): bone matrices **5.1 -> 1.2 ms** by opening out the 4x4 multiply into `kali_affine`
  (the bottom row of a bone matrix is always 0,0,0,1, so the generic `pb.mat_mul` does 64 multiplies for
  nothing) and by skipping skeletons no drawn mesh uses; skinning **19.7 -> 3.1 ms** through an optional
  numpy path. Whole frame **23.8 ms (42 fps) -> 13.9 ms (72 fps)**, so 60 fps now has headroom.
  Micro-optimising the Python loop was tried first and is not the answer: a fast path for the 38 % of
  vertices bound to a single bone bought 7 % (28.0 -> 26.2 ms). numpy is bundled in the exe
  (`--hidden-import numpy`, 8.7 -> 23.0 MB); without it `pose(cepat=False)` still works, just at ~33 fps.
  `pose_np` writes through a **strided numpy view** of the interleaved vertex buffer
  (`np.dtype({'names': ['p'], 'formats': [('<f4', 3)], 'offsets': [0], 'itemsize': stride})`), so there
  is no copy and no per-vertex `pack_into`. Both paths agree to 0.2 micrometres.
- **Two scheduling traps cost the other half of the frame rate**, and both had to go before the
  measured rate matched the measured work:
  1. `_pose_sekarang` only SCHEDULES a redraw, so `SwapBuffers`' vsync wait (16.7 ms on a 60 Hz screen)
     happened outside the tick and the timer delay was stacked on top of it - 30 ms per frame, 33 fps.
     The loop now calls `gl.segera()` inside the tick, so the remaining budget is ~0 and the pace is
     set by vsync.
  2. Windows' default timer resolution is **15.6 ms**, so `after(1)` really waits a whole tick and the
     stacking came back at ~42 fps. `_jam_halus()` raises it with `winmm.timeBeginPeriod(1)` while
     playing and releases it on stop/close (it is a process-wide setting).
  Measured in the real window after both: **58-59 fps**, i.e. vsync. The Animasi tab shows the achieved
  rate beside the time, computed from the **interval between ticks** - measuring the work inside a tick
  reported an impossible 138 fps, because the draw was not part of it.
- **Drawing**: display lists COPY client vertex data when compiled, so an animated batch cannot use
  one. `PetaGL.hidupkan({va idx: bytearray})` makes those batches draw immediately from a ctypes view
  **sharing memory with the player's bytearray** (`from_buffer`), so a new pose costs no copy at all.
  Everything else keeps its display list.
- Normals are not posed: a character mesh is always textured and `PetaGL.gambar` turns lighting off
  while a texture is bound, so a static normal never shows.
- The editor gained a toolbar checkbox **Gerakkan**, a **Pratinjau gerak** box in the Animasi tab
  (Jalankan / Berhenti plus a time slider), and the **Tulang** overlay follows the animation. Playback
  starts by itself as soon as an animation is attached or a scene carrying one is opened.
- `_gambar_isi` now sets up `GL_LIGHT0` like the collision editor does: `PetaGL.gambar` enables
  `GL_LIGHTING` for untextured batches and expects the caller to have prepared a light, which this
  editor never did - a scene whose textures are missing used to render pitch black.

Tests: `uji_i3viewer.py` groups 15 and 16 (**183 checks total**) - the byte-identical Mermaid round
trip, object order, save/reload, bone lengths staying constant across time, a 100%-weighted vertex
matching its bone matrix exactly, the posed mesh staying human-sized, two refusals (a map scene has
no `i3Body`; an emote is refused on the golem's `Bone01` skeleton), and the window driven in-process
until 27,717 pixels change between two frames.

### What is actually inside a standalone `.i3a` (measured, 2026-09-26)

Asked when the user wanted to know whether `.i3a` can be round-tripped through Blender. Measured over
the 25 files in `Emote\` (1,223 tracks) plus the two golem scenes.

An `.i3a` is a plain I3R2 holding only **N x `i3TransformSequence` + 1 x `i3Animation`** (the root, id
in header 0x34). No skeleton, no hierarchy, no mesh - **only bone NAMES**, so the armature has to come
from the `.I3S`.

One sequence = `u8 len + name` + a 22-byte header + four key arrays:

    u16 2 | u8 channel flags | 01 01 01 | u32 0 | u32 key count | u32 0 | f32 duration (s)
    then  N x float3 position, N x float4 rotation (quaternion XYZW), N x float3 scale, N x float time (s)

so exactly **44 bytes per key** and `object size == 1 + len(name) + 22 + 44*N` (checked on every file).

- **Channel flags are 0x0F in all 1,223 tracks.** The loader ignores them and always reads four arrays,
  which is why `i3anim.ekspor_i3a` must write 0x0F and fill every channel.
- **A key holds the bone's FULL LOCAL transform relative to its parent - not a delta from the bind
  pose.** Proof: `Siege_Golem_Setting.i3s`'s own animation is a static pose, and each of its 41 first
  keys reproduces the bone's `BMA+48` local matrix to **0.000001**. (A delta encoding would have
  stored identity.)
- **Quaternion XYZW, unit length** in all 5,614 samples checked; row-vector convention, no transpose
  (measured separately - see the Pemutar section).
- **Scale is (1,1,1) in 1,222 of 1,223 tracks.**
- **Position is constant in 1,161 of 1,223 tracks.** In `Salsa_Dance.i3a` only three tracks translate:
  `Root` (up to 0.232 m - the root motion) and the two clavicles by ~9 mm.
- **Key count is per track, and 315 of 1,223 tracks have exactly ONE key** (a bone that never moves).
  So `Air_Kiss.i3a` has 43 tracks of which 5 hold a single key.
- Times are explicit seconds per key. Where they are evenly spaced it is **exactly 30 keys per second**
  (`Salsa_Dance` 181 keys / 6.00 s, `UI_IdleB` 291 / 9.67); 461 tracks are unevenly spaced.
- Space is the skeleton's own: **Z-up, metres** (a 1.8 m character spans Z 0..1.8). The `i3LOD` node
  matrix - rows (-1,0,0), (0,0,1), (0,1,0) - is what turns it Y-up for display. Blender is Z-up and
  metric too, so no axis conversion is needed if the armature is imported from the `.I3S`.
- 65 distinct bone names across `Emote\`; names carry spaces (`R Clavicle`, `L Little1`) and matching
  is by name only, so the names must equal the `.I3S` skeleton's exactly.

**Sequence names can be EMPTY.** In both golem scenes every `i3TransformSequence` has a zero-length
name and the bone names live only in the `i3Animation` list (`u8 0 + u32 count + count x (u32 id +
char[32] name)`). That list is the authority: `i3viewer.nama_animasi(anim)` reads it, and
`animasi_badan()` / `Pemutar` fall back to the sequence's own name only when the list entry is blank.
Before this, the golem's animation looked like 41 tracks all named "" and could not be played.

**No Blender bridge exists yet.** Everything needed for one is decoded: armature from the `.I3S`
(names, depth->parent, `BMA+48` local matrices, `i3MatrixArray` inverse binds) and the action from the
`.i3a` as above. The reverse direction is `pose_bone` local = `parent.matrix.inverted() @ bone.matrix`,
baked per frame, written as the four arrays with flag 0x0F.

### The GUI

`I3Viewer Editor V3.pyw`: toolbar (Buka / Dari pack / Simpan / Simpan sebagai / **Ambil model dari map lain...** /
Duplikat / **Bisa dipindah** / Hapus / Tekstur / Kotak pilihan / **Tulang** / **Gerakkan** / Pas ke layar), the **scene tree** on the left
(hierarchy, segitiga, ukuran; green = movable, blue = has mesh), the `i3gl` 3D view in the middle, and a **notebook** on the right
with four tabs - Penempatan (nama, X, Y, Z, three rotation angles, skala, Terapkan, Tegakkan lagi), Tekstur,
Animasi (including the Pratinjau gerak player) and Tabrakan. Mouse: click = pick (ray vs bbox then vs triangles), drag = slide on the floor
plane, Shift+drag = up/down; right-drag orbit, middle-drag pan, wheel zoom, WASDQE walk, F focus, Home fit.
Ctrl+Z is exact - each undo entry is the whole file image.

While dragging, the placement matrix is written straight into the batches `PetaGL` already uploaded
(`batch['ga']` carries the `i3GeometryAttr` object number, which matches `Adegan.objs` because the map is
uploaded from `Adegan.isi()`), so the model moves at frame rate without rebuilding anything.

A scene opened **from a `.i3Pack`** can only be saved with "Simpan sebagai..."; putting it back is done in
I3Pack Editor V3, into a `" (2)"` copy, never over the base pack.

`I3Viewer Editor V3.exe` rebuilt 2026-09-26 (8.72 MB, 8,723,965 bytes; the 8,724,612-byte build that adds `nama_animasi` is staged in `_perbarui\` because the user had the program open, `--icon Icon\I3S.ico`, `--hidden-import i3col`), smoke-tested in a folder holding no
`.py` at all (6 checks: window opens on a scene given as an argument, closes cleanly).

**The index-width fix needed four other exes rebuilt.** PyInstaller's FrozenImporter wins over `sys.path`, so
`I3Collision Editor V3.exe`, `I3INS Editor V3.exe` and `I3Path Editor V3.exe` kept drawing from their BUNDLED
copy of the old `i3gl`, and `I3Pack Editor V3.exe` from the old `i3obj` (its OBJ export had the same u16
assumption). All four were rebuilt 2026-09-26 and open/close cleanly; the previous binaries plus the pre-fix
`i3gl.py` / `i3obj.py` / `pindah_bone.py` are in `_backup_sebelum_indeks32\`.

Regression after all of it: `uji_i3viewer.py` 53, `uji_i3rsc.py` 59, `uji_i3pack.py` 29, `uji_i3pack_gui.py` 147,
`uji_i3pack_format.py` 39, `uji_i3pack_jelajah.py` 11, `uji_i3pack_exe.py` 10, `uji_i3obj.py` 34,
`uji_i3bersih.py` 31, `uji_i3vtex.py` 28 - all pass.

Noticed while re-running those: the **user's installed `Crackdown_Scene.i3pack` now holds a 66-entry
`Crackdown.RSC` whose two path copies disagree** - the first uses `/`, the second `\` - on 62 of 66 entries.
Every stock RSC2 entry writes the two copies identically (1,110 entries in Pack 3.88, 3,188 in the client, no
exception), so this file is the only deviation on the machine; it most likely came from the i3LevelDesign export.
Reported to the user, not changed. `uji_i3rsc.py`'s check now compares the paths with the slash direction
normalised and reports how many still match exactly.

## Menjatuhkan `.obj` ke dalam map -- `i3objin.py` + `i3map.py` (2026-09-30)

User: "Apakah anda bisa membuat Program map editor ??" lalu dipertegas: "saya hanya drag dan
drop obj, dan juga path teksture nya juga ngikut, itu nanti dalam format i3s map nya".

### Objeknya TIDAK disusun dari nol - cetakan di scene itu sendiri yang dikloning

Satu mesh i3 butuh selusin objek saling merujuk (`i3Texture`, `i3TextureEnableAttr`,
`i3TextureBindAttr`, `i3MaterialAttr`, `i3AttrSet`, `i3VertexArray`, `i3IndexArray`,
`i3GeometryAttr`, `i3Geometry`, node), tiap kelas punya byte tak-bertabel dan medan yang belum
semuanya dipecahkan. Jadi caranya sama seperti `pindah_senjata`: **kloning satu model CONTOH
yang sudah ada di scene itu, lalu timpa verteks, indeks dan data teksturnya.** Format word,
descriptor, dan 46 byte kepala `.i3i` yang belum dikenali dijamin sah karena datang dari berkas
itu sendiri.

`Adegan.contoh_obj()` memilih cetakan: subtree tepat satu mesh, set UV paling sedikit
