## "Musuh melayang saat kaca pecah" -- state RETAK memang masih bisa dipijak (2026-10-02)

User: "kadang-kadang musuh melayang saat kaca nya pecah, kadang normal. itu kenapa ya ??"

### Terjawab dari log user sendiri, bukan dari tebakan

`logs/battle` memberi angkanya langsung: `[HIT OBJECT] Map: 73 | ID: 205 | HP: 120 |
Damage: 24`, jadi satu panel perlu **lima** tembakan. Dengan tabel state di `.i3Obj`
(1,00 / 0,50 / 0,00) dan HP 120:

| tembakan | HP | pecahan | state client | bisa dipijak? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| - | 120 | 1,00 | utuh | ya |
| 1 | 96 | 0,80 | utuh | ya |
| 2 | 72 | 0,60 | utuh | ya |
| 3 | 48 | 0,40 | **retak** | **YA** <- melayang |
| 4 | 24 | 0,20 | **retak** | **YA** <- melayang |
| 5 | 0 | 0,00 | bolong | tidak -> jatuh |

Jadi bukan bug: scene retak SENGAJA masih punya tabrakan pemain ("kaca retak, masih
bisa dipijak"), hasil permintaan user sendiri "Retak 50% bolong 0%". Dua dari lima
tembakan meninggalkan panel yang TERLIHAT hancur tapi masih menahan orang.
"Kadang normal" = beruntun cepat sampai tembakan ke-5, tahap retaknya tidak terlihat.
Di log itu panel 53 malah cuma kena 2 kali lalu ditinggal di HP 72 - tidak pernah retak.

### Yang disingkirkan sambil memeriksa

Dugaan yang lebih menarik dan ternyata SALAH: bahwa server menyuruh client memakai
state 1 (yang sekarang = RETAK) saat HP 0, lewat `<Effect Id="1" Percent="0"/>`.
Diperiksa: **map 72 dan 73 TIDAK punya `<DestroyEffects>` sama sekali**, jadi
`_effects` kosong, `MappingXML.CheckDestroyState` selalu mengembalikan 0, dan
`_updateId` tetap 1 - server hanya mengirim `OBJECT_STATIC` (nilai nyawa), tidak
pernah nomor state. Jadi state dipilih client sendiri dari pecahan nyawanya.

Bandingkan map 38 Helispot yang objeknya juga 3 state: ia memang punya DUA entri,
`<Effect Id="1" Percent="3600"/>` (= 0,30 x 12000) dan `<Effect Id="2" Percent="0"/>`.
Jadi untuk objek 3 state yang memang mau dikendalikan server, dua entri itu yang benar.

### Pembanding kalau nanti terulang dengan sebab lain

Saat musuh melayang, lihat panelnya:
  * masih KELIHATAN (retak) -> sebabnya tabel state di atas, ambangnya yang disetel;
  * sudah HILANG total -> bukan ini. Tersangkanya controller PhysX 2.8 yang menyimpan
    penunjuk shape yang diinjaknya, jadi gravitasi baru berlaku begitu dia bergerak.
    Ambang tidak akan menolong di kasus itu.

### Yang dikerjakan: ambang retak 0,50 -> 0,25 (pilihan user)

6 template di `Object_Glass_Mode.i3Pack`, **2 byte per berkas**, semuanya di medan
ambang; HP, scene tiap state, aksi dan jumlah objek tidak disentuh. Pack distempel
ulang (`CHECK ok`). Dengan damage 24 jendela melayang jadi satu tembakan (0,20 saja).

Kenapa ambang RENDAH lebih baik daripada setengah: ia selalu berarti "hampir jebol"
apa pun senjatanya. 0,50 berarti "separuh", yang bisa selebar beberapa tembakan untuk
senjata berdamage kecil. Konsekuensi yang disebutkan ke user: senjata berdamage besar
bisa MELEWATI tahap retak sama sekali - itu wajar, berarti pecahnya cepat.

`Map BSP\ambang_retak_025.py` (`--ambang` bisa diberi nilai lain). Cadangan pack di
`Map BSP\cadangan_glass_lab\Object_Glass_Mode.sebelum_ambang025_*.i3Pack`.
`periksa_retak_bolong.py` 18/18 terhadap pack TERPASANG.

Dua jebakan skrip di ronde ini:
  * state yang disasar ditentukan lewat **nama scene** (`break` tapi bukan `hole`),
    bukan nomor indeks. Skrip lama `perbaiki_ambang_pecah.py` menyasar "state ber-scene
    selain state 0" dan sekarang menolak sendiri karena ada DUA - penjaganya benar,
    tapi skripnya memang sudah tidak berlaku sejak objeknya jadi 3 state.
  * medan scene di tabel state berbentuk `0x80060008`: bit31 eksternal, nomor string di
    bit 16..30, **nomor objek di 16 bit bawah**. Yang dipakai nomor OBJEKNYA, lalu
    `.ext`-nya dibaca - tidak perlu menebak bentuk raw id. Dan `try/except` di sekitar
    pencarian nama sempat membuat SEMUA nama jadi kosong karena satu salah-nama atribut
    (`s.strs` vs `s.strings`); yang menangkapnya cuma assert di bawahnya. Pencarian nama
    sekarang dibiarkan meledak terang.

Data saja - tidak ada binari server yang dibangun ulang dan tidak perlu restart server.
Client perlu keluar-masuk map supaya `.i3Obj`-nya dibaca lagi. **Belum diuji di game.**

## Kaca MIRING Glass_Updown dikembalikan -- dan cara menghitung jatah objeknya (2026-10-02)

User: "Di glass_updown itu object glass nya masih ada kan ?? tapi yang miring kok ga ada ??"

### Yang miring itu kaca UNGU, dan memang saya yang memangkasnya

Diukur dengan membandingkan `.i3INS` cadangan (389 objek) dengan yang terpasang: objek
yang kuaternionnya BUKAN yaw murni (|qx| atau |qz| > 0,01) ada **25** di cadangan dan
**1** di yang terpasang. Yang satu itu lampu (Y 96, miring 83 derajat); 24 sisanya hilang
semuanya.

Ke-24 itu `P_GLow_GlassMode_GLASS_01` - kaca **ungu**, miring tepat **28 derajat**
(`qz = +-0,242`, jadi memiringnya di sumbu Z), skala X 1,13-1,14, empat-empat di enam
ketinggian **35,30 / 36,90 / 38,50 / 40,10 / 41,70 / 43,30** pada X +-9 atau +-12 dan
Z +-12 atau +-15. Scene utuhnya punya tabrakan pemain, jadi panel itu **bisa dipijak** -
bentuknya tanjakan penghubung antar lantai, yang masuk akal untuk map bernama "Updown".

Catatan lama di berkas ini menyebut lapis yang dibuang sebagai "24 panel (kaca ungu)"
tanpa menyebut bahwa itu panel MIRING - itulah yang membuat hilangnya tidak kelihatan
dari catatan sendiri. Sekarang disebut eksplisit.

### Cara menghitung jatah objeknya ADA TIGA, dan bedanya +-6

Ini yang perlu diingat supaya angka di catatan tidak saling bertabrakan:

| aturan | yang dihitung | Glass_Updown sebelum | sesudah |
|---|---|---|---|
| hanya `.i3Obj` | kaca + dinding | 214 | **200** |
| semua `punya_resource()` | + World, lampu, 4 `.i3Evt` | 220 | **206** |
| pemeriksa `periksa_glass_updown.py` | aturannya sendiri | 216 | **202** |

Jatahnya ~221 (bukti Glass_Lab: 572 objek, tepat 351 baris `AddObject : Static Object
count overflow`). Aturan mana yang client pakai BELUM dipastikan - jadi yang aman adalah
menjaga ketiganya di bawah 221, dan menyebut aturannya setiap kali mengutip angka.
Sebelum ronde ini sisa jatahnya cuma 1-7 tergantung aturan; sesudahnya 15-21 di ketiganya.

### Yang ditukar (pilihan user)

Satu lapis dinding **Y 43,20** (Wall_B 19 + Wall_W 19 = 38) dibuang untuk memberi ruang
24 kaca ungu. Hasilnya lebih AMAN dari sebelumnya di ketiga aturan di atas, bukan cuma
cukup. Lantai kaca utama (73 panel Y 40,90), kaca kuning (49 di Y 37,70), kaca hijau atas
(16 di Y 44,10) dan lapis dinding Y 41,70 semuanya utuh, dan ke-16 respawn terbukti masih
berdiri di atas lantai kaca Y 40,90.

Cara mengerjakannya seperti ronde pemangkasan: `.i3INS` dibangun ulang dari CADANGAN 389
objek (supaya lapis yang dulu dibuang bisa kembali) lalu ditulis ke pack yang SEKARANG -
jadi `.RSC` yang sudah dilengkapi scene pecah dan ambang retak 0,25 tidak ikut mundur.
Template ungunya sudah terdaftar di `.RSC` dan `maps.xml` map 73 sudah punya 256 slot,
jadi keduanya tidak disentuh sama sekali.

`Map BSP\kembalikan_kaca_miring.py` - diturunkan dari `penuhkan_glass_updown.py`, bedanya
HANYA daftar `SIMPAN` plus tiga penjaga baru: kaca ungu harus tepat 24, nol di antaranya
boleh tidak miring, dan dinding harus tepat 38 (satu lapis). Pack distempel ulang (SAH).
Cadangan `cadangan_glass_updown\Glass_Updown_Scene.sebelum_ungu_*.i3Pack`.

`periksa_glass_updown.py` **14/14** dan `periksa_retak_bolong.py` **18/18** terhadap pack
TERPASANG. Data saja - tidak ada binari server yang dibangun ulang dan tidak perlu restart
server; client cukup keluar-masuk map. **Belum diuji di game.**

Jebakan skrip yang terulang: `\n` di dalam heredoc Bash tertelan jadi baris baru
sungguhan, sehingga tiga pesan `sys.stderr.write('... %d\n')` menjadi string tak tertutup
(`SyntaxError`). Diganti `print(..., file=sys.stderr)` yang tidak butuh escape sama sekali,
dan skrip pembetulnya memanggil `compile()` untuk membuktikan sintaksnya lolos sebelum
berhenti. Untuk isi yang memuat backslash: pakai berkas lewat Write, jangan heredoc.

## `.i3VTexImage` (UI atlas images) -- `i3vtex.py` (2026-09-24)

User: "tambahkan menu konversi I3VtexImage -> TGA dan Juga sebaliknya", samples in
`G:\Games\PB Deluxe\Locale\Russia\UI_V12\VTexList` (495 files). Decoded from those files alone.

- Header 2048 bytes: `+0` magic **`VTIH` or `HAZE`** (same layout, both appear; the other VTex tool writes
  VTIH even for a HAZE source), `+4` u32 version 1, `+8`/`+12` width/height (always a multiple of 128,
  128..1024), `+16` 0, `+20` u32 slot number (19..39, meaning unknown, preserved), `+24` u32 flag 0/1,
  `+0x80` the source `.tga` path as ASCII (`Image/Avatar/Belt_1.tga`). Payload at 2048.
- Payload = **BGRA8888, 4 bytes/pixel, stored as 128x128 tiles** in row-major tile order, size exactly
  `w*h*4` with no mips. Read linearly it looks like the image repeated 8 times across and squashed - that
  is the tell that the tiles have not been unswizzled. 14 of the 495 files are 128/160-byte placeholders
  with width/height 0.
- `tulis_tga` writes 32-bit uncompressed TGA **bottom-up (descriptor 0x08)**: with that, our `.tga` is
  **byte-identical to the other VTex tool's output** (checked against 4 `.tga` files it left in that folder
  while the user was working there). `baca_tga` also accepts top-down, 24-bit and RLE (type 10).
- `dari_tga` reuses the **old file's header** (magic, slot, flag, source path) when a `contoh` is given or
  the target already exists, and refuses a size that differs from the old image or is not a multiple of 128.
  132 plain files round-trip file -> TGA -> file **byte-identical**.
- **354 of the 481 real payloads are encrypted** with the PBM family (per-position substitution, 64 KB
  chunks) - the same family as the `.i3Pack` V2 cipher but **a different key table, and a different key per
  file** (354 distinct keystreams in 354 files). Confirmed not in the old exe: a zero-block oracle probe over
  all 768 keys (`type 1/2/3` x 256; the CLI accepts type 3, which the pack format never uses) matched none.
  What does hold: 192 of the 256 rows follow `((x ^ (i+1)) + (K[i] - (i+1)))` where `K[i]` is the ciphertext
  in an all-zero region - verified by predicting `E(255)` at positions 3 and 7 of a real encrypted file. The
  other 64 (`i mod 16` in {8, 9, 12, 15}) have no closed form yet; decrypting them with the same formula gives
  a mean error of 131/255, so encrypted files are **refused**, not half-opened. The other VTex tool fails on
  exactly the same files (its `.tga` output for them is the same garbled stripes), so this is a shared wall.
- Detector `tersandi()`: fraction of alpha bytes (position 3 mod 4) equal to 0x00 or 0xFF. Across the sample
  folder plain files score 0.585-1.000 and encrypted ones 0.000-0.201, so the 0.40 threshold has a wide gap.
  Tail periodicity alone is NOT enough - a constant fill colour is also 256-periodic (Belt_1's empty area is
  `22222200`), which is what made an earlier classification call clean files encrypted.
- GUI: `Alat > Konversi gambar i3VTexImage` (both directions, file picker or whole folder) plus, on a
  `.i3VTexImage` **inside a pack**, right-click `Simpan sebagai TGA...` / `Ganti isi dari TGA...`.
  CLI: `python i3vtex.py info|ke-tga|dari-tga|folder-ke-tga|folder-dari-tga`.
- Tests: `uji_i3vtex.py` (28 checks: tiles, TGA 24/32-bit and RLE, header preserved, refusals, plus the whole
  sample folder) and the VTex block in `uji_i3pack_gui.py`. Test images must use alpha 0/255 only, or
  `tersandi()` correctly calls them encrypted.
- Note `UIRe\*.i3VTex` / `.i3VTexSub` in the user's own V1 client are a **different** thing (the virtual
  texture atlas + its subsets, what `i3VTexUI.exe` edits); `i3vtex.py` does not touch those.

## `.i3i` -> PNG -- `i3i.py` (2026-09-27)

User: "Untuk I3Pack Editor V3, buatkan Extract i3i nya ke format png ya". `.i3i` is the ordinary game
texture (the pack editor could already hand one to i3ImageViewer, but not export it).

Header I3IB: `+6` u16 width, `+8` u16 height, `+10` u8 format code, `+24` u16 mips, `+26` u16 name
length, pixels at `60 + name length`. **Format codes measured over 6,836 `.i3i` in the client**, by
bytes per pixel across the whole mip chain - not guessed:

    0x80, 0x81        0.5 B/px    DXT1  (8-byte blocks)          4,695 files
    0x04              1.0 B/px    DXT5  (16-byte blocks)         2,024 files
    0x01, 0x05, 0x06  4.0 B/px    uncompressed 32-bit, B,G,R,A      61 files
    0x02              1.6 B/px    inconsistent - NOT solved         56 files

`0x02` and `0x07` are **refused with a message naming the code**, never guessed: a PNG written from a
wrong reading is worse than a refusal. The supported codes cover 99.2 % of the client's `.i3i`.

- Channel order for the 32-bit codes is **B,G,R,A** (D3D `A8R8G8B8` little-endian). Confirmed by
  decoding `mini_BankHall.i3i`: grey walls with **khaki** outlines plus a blue/red spawn pair - swap
  R and B and the khaki turns blue. The DXT path is unambiguous (RGB565) and was checked against
  `BB_P90_Ext_Bike_Diff.i3i`, which comes out red exactly as i3Viewer2 renders that model.
- DXT1 has two block modes: when `c0 <= c1` index 3 is **transparent**, so alpha 0 is written there.
  DXT5 alpha is the usual 8-byte block (two endpoints + 3-bit indices, 6- or 4-value table).
- `tulis_png` writes RGBA8 (colour type 6) through `zlib` - no Pillow, nothing new to install.
- API: `baca(path or bytes)` -> `Gambar`, `ke_rgba(g, mip=0)` -> `(w, h, bytearray)`,
  `tulis_png(path, w, h, rgba)`, `ke_png(sumber, tujuan=None, mip=0)`.
  CLI: `python i3i.py info|png|folder`.
- **I3Pack Editor V3**: right-click a `.i3i` -> **"Simpan .i3i sebagai PNG..."** (several selected at
  once go into one folder), plus `Alat > Ekspor gambar .i3i ke PNG` for loose files and for a whole
  folder tree. The row is greyed for anything that is not `.i3i`, and the module is imported behind
  `try/except` like `i3vtex`/`i3obj`/`i3bersih`, so a missing `i3i.py` only disables the menu.
- `uji_i3i.py`: **42 checks** - four refusals, one real file per format code decoded and written, the
  PNG re-read with its IDAT row count verified, the mip-1 half-size rule, and the editor window driven
  in-process through both the single-file and the multi-file path.
- Regression: `uji_i3pack.py` 50, `uji_i3pack_gui.py` 147, `uji_i3pack_jelajah.py` 11 all pass
  (`uji_i3pack_format.py` now skips itself - its sample pack `CakeCrackDown_Scene` is no longer in the
  client).
- The `.exe` was rebuilt 2026-09-27 with `--hidden-import i3i` added to the documented command
  (8,699,076 bytes; old build in `_backup_sebelum_png\`). **The exe uses its bundled modules, so
  dropping `i3i.py` next to it does nothing until it is rebuilt.**

## I3Pack Editor **V3.12** (versi ringkas) -- `buat_v312.py` (2026-09-28)

User: "buatkan saya i3Pack Editor V3 versi Lite nya. tapi jangan ganggu yang bawaan aslinya atau full
fitur, ini untuk teman saya", then "Kata lite nya hapus aja ya, Buat aja namanya I3Pack Editor V3.12".
So V3.12 is a **separate program** and the full `.pyw` is not touched at all.

`I3Pack Editor V3.12.pyw` is **generated**, not hand-copied: `buat_v312.py` applies 26 exact string
edits to the full source, and **every edit must match exactly once** or the script stops and names the
edit. That is the whole point - when the full editor changes, regenerating either works or fails loudly;
it can never quietly produce a half-broken copy.

    python buat_v312.py          # 132,467 -> 138,303 byte

**The name is a trap.** `NAMA = os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(_SENDIRI))[0]` splits at the LAST dot,
so `I3Pack Editor V3.12.pyw` would read as `I3Pack Editor V3` - the window title would be wrong and,
worse, `BERKAS_ATUR = HERE + NAMA + '.ini'` would make it share the **full version's settings file**.
One of the 26 edits therefore pins `NAMA = 'I3Pack Editor V3.12'` literally. Verified: the exe writes
`I3Pack Editor V3.12.ini`, next to but separate from `I3Pack Editor V3.ini`.

Removed (per the user's marked-up screenshots): Pack baru, Import folder jadi pack, Ganti nama, Hapus,
Alihkan flag SECURE, Cari dan ganti teks, Ganti nama massal, Convert + bersihkan .i3s (menu and
right-click), Atur alat luar per jenis file, Ganti isi dari TGA, and the `.i3i -> PNG` export - plus the
Ctrl+N / Ctrl+H / F2 / Delete bindings, or the removed items would still be reachable by key.

Kept: buka/simpan, extract, copy-paste, File Browser, light/dark theme, drag & drop, **both** OBJ export
modes, i3VTexImage <-> TGA, bulk SECURE protect, Info pack.

Three behaviours differ on purpose:

- **`.i3i` export goes to TGA, not PNG.** `i3i.ke_rgba` gives RGBA and `i3vtex.tulis_tga` wants BGRA, so
  `_rgba_ke_bgra` swaps the two channels in place (`b[0::4], b[2::4] = b[2::4], b[0::4]`).
- **Saving never asks for a format.** `Simpan sebagai...` calls `_simpan_ke(f)` with no `pilihan`, which
  is the existing "keep the pack's own format" path - so a V3 pack stays V3 and a V1 pack stays V1.
- **Learning Encrypted Key does not harvest.** This build has no oracle exe; `pelajari_cipher` now calls
  `_minta_tabel_cipher`, which names the missing keys **and the exact file each needs**
  (`i3pack.jalur_tabel` -> `pbm_<tipe>_<kunci>.bin`), offers a picker, and copies the chosen `.bin` into
  `Cipher V2\`. It then **clears `i3pack._tabel_terbuka` and `_tabel_rusak`** - without that, a table that
  failed to load earlier stays cached and the file just copied in is never looked at. The old harvesting
  body is kept as `_pelajari_cipher_penuh`, unused.

`uji_v312.py`: **57 checks** - the full version still contains everything V3.12 drops (so the generator
cannot have edited the wrong file), every removed label absent and every kept label present across the
menu bar, submenus and both context menus, the theme menu, `WS_EX_ACCEPTFILES` on the window, `.i3i` ->
TGA for one file and for a whole selection (header type 2 / 32 bpp, size exactly `18 + w*h*4`, dimensions
equal to the `.i3i`), `Simpan sebagai` not calling `_tanya_format`, the saved pack keeping its source
format, and the cipher menu routing to the file-supply flow. Note the test's menu walker must accept
`radiobutton` entries or the theme menu reads as empty.

Regression after all of it: `uji_i3pack_gui.py` 147, `uji_i3i.py` 42, `uji_i3pack.py` 50 - all pass.
Exe built 2026-09-28 `--onefile` as **I3Pack Editor V3.12.exe** (8,700,684 B) with only
`i3pack i3vtex i3i i3obj pindah_bone` as hidden imports - `i3bersih`, `pindah_karakter` and
`pindah_senjata` are dropped because nothing in this build reaches them, and the `try/except` import
guards already handle their absence. Its window title and its own `.ini` were both checked.

## One menu for every tool -- `I3Tools V3` + `i3tema.py` (2026-09-29)

User: "apakah anda bisa menggabungkan semua alat saya ... jadi satu menu ... Lalu buatkan
desain UI nya lebih moderen. bukan kaku seperti sekarang."

`I3Tools V3.exe` (**23,953,682 B**) is one binary holding the menu **and all 14 tools**.
Against roughly 160 MB of separate exes that is also a big saving, because the shared
libraries (tkinter, numpy, the i3* modules) are stored once.

### Each tool runs as its own PROCESS, and that is the whole design

The alternative - turning 14 `tk.Tk` applications into frames of one window - means rewriting
14 proven programs. They each own a `tk.Tk`, several hold an OpenGL context, and at least one
(`I3Pack Editor V3`) sets the ttk theme globally. So the menu **launches**, it does not embed:

    frozen :  I3Tools V3.exe --alat <id>      (subprocess of the same exe)
    sumber :  pythonw.exe "<Tool>.pyw"

Not one line of any tool's logic changed, and a tool that crashes takes nothing else with it.
`--daftar` lists the ids; `--alat <id> [argumen]` passes the rest through to the tool.

**The trap that had to be handled: ten of the fourteen tools name themselves after the exe.**

    _SENDIRI = sys.executable kalau frozen, kalau tidak __file__
    NAMA     = os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(_SENDIRI))[0]

and `NAMA` becomes the window title, the `.log` name and - the dangerous one -
`BERKAS_ATUR = HERE + NAMA + '.ini'`. Inside the combined exe all of them would read
"I3Tools V3", so **I3Pack Editor would read and write `I3Tools V3.ini` instead of its own
settings** (external tools per file type, File Browser state, theme). `jalankan_alat()`
therefore fakes `sys.executable` and `sys.argv[0]` to `<folder exe>\<Nama Alat>.exe` for the
life of that tool: the folder stays right, the name comes out right, and nothing in the tools
had to be touched. The exe test asserts both halves - every window title starts with its own
tool's name, and `I3Pack Editor V3.ini` (not `I3Tools V3.ini`) is what appears on disk.

Note `I3BVH I3a Convert V3.exe` is **not** a separate tool - its strings show it is an older
build of `I3BVH Convert V3` - so the menu lists 14, not 15.

### The menu itself

A dark (or light) sidebar with category filters, a search box, and a grid of cards drawn on a
`tk.Canvas` - rounded corners via `create_polygon(smooth=True)`, a coloured 3-letter badge per
tool, hover that lifts the card and turns its border the accent colour, and a dot marking tools
used before (last-used sorts first, kept in `I3Tools.json`). Cards reflow to the window width.
Closing the menu does not close the tools, and it says so when any are still open.

### The icon

The menu shipped with tkinter's feather at first - the window icon is `iconbitmap()`, which
nothing had called. `Icon\I3Tools.ico` is now generated by `scratchpad/buat_ikon.py`: a dark
rounded tile holding the four category colours in a 2x2 grid, drawn at 4x and downsampled, in
**seven sizes (16/20/24/32/48/64/256)**. The 16/20/24 versions drop the tile and let the four
squares fill the icon, or they turn to mush.

Written as **DIB entries, not PNG**: the icon reader inside I3Pack Editor V3 refuses an `.ico`
whose images are all PNG-compressed, so this keeps the project's own tools able to read it.
`jalur_ikon()` prefers `Icon\I3Tools.ico` beside the program over the copy bundled in the exe,
so it can be swapped without rebuilding, and `iconbitmap(p, default=p)` covers dialogs too.
Verified two ways: `GetIconInfo` on the live window reports the tile colour plus the four
category colours, and all seven images appear verbatim inside the exe while `IconExe.ico`'s do
not.

### `i3tema.py` - one theme, deliberately shy

Applied by one guarded line at the top of every tool's `App.__init__`:

    if i3tema:
        i3tema.pasang(self)

What it changes: colours, flat relief, hover/selection states, `Text`/`Listbox`/`Menu`/
`Scrollbar` (which `ttk.Style` never reaches), and the Windows title bar via
`DWMWA_USE_IMMERSIVE_DARK_MODE` (attribute 20, falling back to 19, followed by a
`SWP_FRAMECHANGED` because the frame only repaints on demand).

What it deliberately does **not** change, and why:

- **No font or padding anywhere.** These windows are sized to the pixel (the I3CHR editor's
  height was cut 1146 -> 1026 so its buttons would not be clipped); a button one pixel taller
  can break a row. An early draft set `TButton padding=(10, 4)` and `TNotebook.Tab
  padding=(12, 5)` - both removed.
- **`Canvas` is never touched.** The map editors paint the 2D denah and the 3D preview on one.
- **A widget whose `background` is `''` is skipped** - that is the frame `i3gl` hangs its
  OpenGL context on.
- `i3tema.lewati(w)` marks a subtree as off limits. The menu's sidebar uses it: `pasang()`
  re-sweeps classic widgets on `after_idle` (it runs at the START of `__init__`, before the
  widgets exist), and without the mark that sweep wiped the accent colour off the active
  category a frame after it was drawn.
- `bilah_judul()` must **not** call `update_idletasks()` - idle work run too early can hang
  the OpenGL context creation in the tools that have a 3D tab (the `iconbitmap` deadlock
  recorded above is the same family). `winfo_id()` alone creates the window.

Base theme is `clam`, not the Windows `vista` theme, for the reason already recorded under
I3Pack Editor: `vista` paints its own colours and a forced dark comes out patchy.

### First in-game result: the client does NOT react to the extra bit

With `SoundFlag=MassKill` the user reported: the weapon award works, the "Reach kill ... Equip :"
chat line appears - **and no sound**. That chat line is sent from `Load_Weapon_Ranked` itself, so
the ranked path definitely ran and `frag.killFlag` really was `Intercept|MassKill = 258`.

And the flag really does reach the client: in both callers `RegistryFragInfos` runs *before* the
packet is built (`Game_SyncNet.cs` 417 then 434; `BATTLE_DEATH_REC.cs` 77 then 102), and the frag
objects are the same ones `BATTLE_DEATH_PAK` writes.

So the working hypothesis is now: **the client reads `killFlag` as ONE value, not as a bitmask**.
258 matches nothing it knows. That also means the `|=` "fix" is only safe if the client really is
bit-aware - on a headshot it now sends 264, and a single-value client would show no notice at all
where it used to show WEAPON UPDATE.

Because that cannot be settled from here, `SoundFlag` now has **four forms**, all switchable by
editing the ini alone (it hot-reloads, so one match can test several):

    None             killFlag |= Intercept                 (bawaan)
    lama             killFlag  = Intercept                 (persis perilaku sebelum 2026-09-29)
    <Bendera>        killFlag |= Intercept | <Bendera>     (butuh client bit-aware)
    only:<Bendera>   killFlag  = <Bendera>                 (suara + notice-nya, WEAPON UPDATE hilang)

`only:` is the decisive experiment: if it produces the MASS KILL notice **and** its voice while
WEAPON UPDATE disappears, the client is single-value and the trade is permanent - sound or the
WEAPON UPDATE HUD, never both, unless the exe is patched. If even `only:` is silent, then this
client does not play announcer voices off `killFlag` at all and the whole route is dead.

Two log lines were added to make any future round readable without guessing:
`[Room] Ranked (BattleAce): True/False` in every room log (needed because `RNK` turns Ranked on
without touching `room.special`, so the existing "Room special" line cannot tell), and one
`[Ranked] <nama> kill ke-N -> senjata X, killFlag A |= B (SoundFlag ...)` per weapon award.

### SOLVED in game: single-value killFlag, and the streak byte is the way in

`SoundFlag=only:MassKill` (killFlag = 2) -> **the notice became MASS KILL and its voice played**.
Together with `Intercept|MassKill = 258` producing nothing, that settles two things:

- the client **does** drive announcer voices from `killFlag`, and
- it reads `killFlag` as **one value, not a bitmask**.

So the `|=` form can never work on this client, and `Intercept` simply has **no sound bound to
it**. That is not an inference: `BC.log` from the session logs **zero** attempts to load any
`Sound/Voice/Announce/*.wav`, while it happily logs every other missing resource in the same run
(`Could not load a header of Gui/WeaponShape/Weapon_Kill23.i3i`, `LRU Sound Resource NULL Name :
WM_BB_PinkDragon_Reload.wav`). The client never even asks for a sound for that notice, so adding a
`.wav` under any guessed name cannot help - the pairing is hardcoded in the packed exe.

**But the death packet has a SECOND, independent field that the client also turns into a notice
AND a voice**: the streak byte at the end of `BATTLE_DEATH_PAK`, normally
`killsOnLife == 2 -> 1, == 3 -> 2, > 3 -> 3` (Double Kill / Triple Kill / Chain Killer - the
starred notices). Because it is separate from `killFlag`, forcing it gives **WEAPON UPDATE and a
sound in the same packet**.

`StreakSound` in `rankedweaponlist.ini` (0 off, 1/2/3) does exactly that, for the weapon-award
packet only:

- `Room.AceStreak` (new field, Game project only - `PBCoreData.dll` is untouched) is set by
  `Load_Weapon_Ranked` through `player._room`,
- `BATTLE_DEATH_PAK.write()` uses it instead of the real streak and clears it, so it fires once.

Cost, stated plainly: the streak notice appears too, and it is a lie about the streak.

Settings now in the ini, both hot-reloaded:

    SoundFlag=None     StreakSound=3      WEAPON UPDATE + Chain Killer voice   <- terpasang
    SoundFlag=only:X   StreakSound=0      X's notice + voice, no WEAPON UPDATE
    SoundFlag=lama     StreakSound=0      exactly the behaviour before 2026-09-29

### Third in-game round: the streak byte produced NO sound either (2026-09-29)

`SoundFlag=None` + `StreakSound=3` -> the user reports **"UI WEAPON UPDATE muncul, tapi tidak
ada suara"**, and no MEAT CHOPPER notice was mentioned either.

The server side was verified to be correct before touching anything, and this elimination is
worth keeping so it is not redone:

- the ranked path ran - `logs/game` holds
  `[Ranked] GM_HeavyRain kill ke-3 -> senjata 200004006, killFlag 0 |= 256 (SoundFlag None,
  StreakSound 3)` for all four awards;
- `Room.AceStreak` was written to the **same Room object** the packet uses: `Room.cs` sets
  `p._room = this` when a player joins, `BATTLE_DEATH_REC` takes `room = player._room`, and
  `AccountManager.getAccount(id, true)` returns the live cached Account, never a copy;
- `write()` runs **exactly once** per packet (`Room.SendPacketToPlayers` calls
  `GetCompleteBytes` once and broadcasts the bytes), so the one-shot `AceStreak` cannot be eaten
  by the first recipient;
- `lastKillState` is server-internal and never transmitted, so the trailing byte really is the
  only streak field in 3355.

So either the trailing byte does not drive a notice/sound at all, or **the client draws only ONE
notice per kill and WEAPON UPDATE won**, taking the streak sound down with it. That second model
fits every observation so far (`only:MassKill` -> MASS KILL + voice; `Intercept|MassKill = 258`
-> nothing; `Intercept` + streak 3 -> WEAPON UPDATE, nothing else).

Guessing further is what the previous two rounds already cost, so the build now measures instead.

### `SapuSuara=1` - one match tests fourteen hypotheses

`Weapon_List_Ranked.SAPU` is a 14-row table of `(killFlag, streak byte)`, one row per weapon
award. A match has exactly **14 kill thresholds** (3, 6, 9, 11, 14, 17, 21, 25, 28, 33, 37, 43,
50, 55), so one full round walks the whole table. The row number is written into the player's own
chat line - `Reach kill 3   Equip : XXX   << UJI 1/14 flag - beruntun 3` - so the result can be
read off the screen without opening a log.

Rows: streak 3/1/2 alone with killFlag untouched (does the streak byte do anything?), then
killFlag 512 / 1024 / 2048 / 4096 / 8192 / 16384 (the bits above `Intercept`, which
`KillingMessage` simply has no names for - the field is written as a `short`, so bits 9..14 are
unexplored), then 256 + streak 3 as the control that reproduces tonight, then streak 4 and 5,
then killFlag 3 (two bits at once), then 0 as the silent control.

Three smaller changes went in with it:

- **`SoundFlag=off`** leaves `frag.killFlag` completely untouched, which is what makes it
  possible to test the streak byte with no other notice competing with it. `only:0` could not do
  this - 0 falls back to `Intercept` by design.
- **`StreakSound` now accepts 1..255**, not 1..3.
- `Load_Weapon_Ranked` gained a **4-argument overload taking the `Room` directly**, and
  `Net_Room_Death` passes its own `room`. Relying on `Account._room` happened to be correct, but
  the packet is built from the caller's `Room` and that is the one the byte must land in; the
  3-argument overload is kept so nothing else had to change.
- `BATTLE_DEATH_PAK` now logs `[Ranked] paket 3355: byte beruntun dipaksa = N` whenever it
  overrides the byte, so "did it leave the server" is never a question again.

Tests: `srv/UjiSapu.cs` **30 checks** (the 14 sweep rows in order and wrapping at 15, sweep
beating `SoundFlag`/`StreakSound`, `SoundFlag=off`, the widened range incl. 256 -> ignored, the
explicit-Room overload with `Account._room` null, and a non-threshold kill touching nothing).
Regression `UjiSuara.cs` 26 and `UjiIniAsli.cs` pass; `UjiSiap.cs` (10 checks) runs against the
**installed** binary reading the real ini. Two test-side traps: a second `Load_Weapon_Ranked`
overload makes a plain `GetMethod` throw `AmbiguousMatchException` (same as `BenderaSuara`
earlier), and **`UjiSapu` rewrites the ini it points at**, so it must never be run against
`Bin/Release`.

Installed 2026-09-29 with all three servers stopped: `PBGameServer.exe` 587,264 B, md5
`3ae8ec6d1feaeb295f13c713929868f1`; `PBCoreData.dll` untouched. Rollback in
`Bin/Release/_backup_binari_sebelum_sapu_suara/` (586,240 B + the previous ini), sources in
`_backup_sebelum_sapu_suara/`.

**The option that already works** if the sweep finds nothing: `SoundFlag=only:MassKill` gives a
real announcer voice, at the price of showing MASS KILL instead of WEAPON UPDATE. The ini

### `only:MassKill` confirmed in game - sound yes, WEAPON UPDATE no

User: "Ketika ganti senjata, notice HUD Masskill dan suaranya muncul, tapi tidak dengan HUD UI
WEAPON UPDATE." Exactly as predicted, and it closes the question the previous rounds opened:
**killFlag is a single value and one value can only mean one notice**, so WEAPON UPDATE and a
voice can never come from that field together.

Everything below is about getting them from **different fields, or different packets**.

### `HudGanda` - five ways to send both at once

Three independent mechanisms exist in packet 3355, and the build now implements all of them so
one match can decide between them:

- **`killingtype`** - `frag.killFlag = Intercept` while `FragInfos.killingType` (the byte right
  after the opcode, `CharaKillType` DEFAULT/PIERCING/MASS) is set to MASS. This is a genuinely
  separate field and the **client itself normally fills it** - `BATTLE_DEATH_REC.cs:37` reads it
  from the client and the server just echoes it back - so the client definitely parses it. The
  other death path (`Net_Room_Death.Load`) hardcodes it to 0 and derives MassKill into `killFlag`
  instead, which is why it has never been exercised from the server side here.
- **`frag` / `frag-balik`** - one packet, **two frags for the same victim**: one carrying the
  sound flag, one carrying `Intercept`. A multi-kill genuinely produces several frags in one
  packet, so the client is built to render more than one notice from a single packet.
- **`paket` / `paket-balik`** - the death packet sent **twice** with different `killFlag`. Safe
  from double counting because **every number in 3355 is absolute, not incremental**: team
  scores, all 16 slots' `allKills`/`allDeaths`, and `Score` are final values, so re-sending
  restates them rather than adding to them.

`SapuHud=1` cycles the five, one per weapon award, and writes the mode into the player's own chat
line (`Reach kill 3   Equip : XXX   << HUD 2/5 frag`). A match has 14 thresholds, so each mode
gets about three tries. Expected side effect of the frag/paket modes: **the kill appears twice in
the kill feed** - that is the price, not a fault.

Two implementation points that matter:

- **The extra frag must NOT be appended inside `Load_Weapon_Ranked`.** That function is called
  from inside `RegistryFragInfos`'s `for (i = 0; i < kills.frags.Count; i++)` loop, so appending
  there would make the new frag be scored as a real kill. It is appended by
  `Weapon_List_Ranked.SiapkanPaket(room, kills)`, called from both death call sites immediately
  before the packet is built - i.e. after `AllUtils.CompleteMission` has already read
  `GetAllKillFlags()`, so mission cards are untouched. `PerluPaketKedua(room, kills)` runs after
  the send, flips the flag and says whether to send again, and clears the room state.
- **`kills.killsCount` must be updated with the list.** The packet writes `killsCount` and then
  iterates `frags`; the client reads that many frags and then reads the team scores, so a
  mismatch of one shifts the entire rest of the packet. `UjiHud` checks this at byte level: a
  2-frag packet must be exactly `99 + 17 * n` bytes with `killsCount` at offset 5 and the two
  `killFlag`s at 26 and 43.

State lives on `Room` (`AceHud`, `AceSuara`, `AceFrag`) next to `AceStreak`, so `PBCoreData.dll`
stays untouched - `Frag` is already visible there through `using Core.models.room`.

`srv/UjiHud.cs`: **52 checks** - `ModeHud` parsing (names, numbers, bad values), all five modes
end to end including which frag gets which flag and that the extra frag is a new object, the
sound flag coming from `SoundFlag` with MassKill as the fallback, `PerluPaketKedua` refusing to
fire twice, the byte-level packet checks above, `SapuHud` cycling 1,2,3,4,5,1,2, and the
untouched paths (HudGanda off, non-threshold kill). Regression `UjiSapu` 30, `UjiSuara` 26,
`UjiIniAsli` pass; `UjiSiap` (15 checks) runs against the installed binary and the real ini.

Test-side traps met: `GetCompleteBytes` writes `stream length - 2` into the header, which is
**four** less than the complete array (the header itself plus the opcode are not counted); and a
test that reads `Room.AceHud` to see which sweep mode ran must read it **before**
`PerluPaketKedua`, which clears it.

### The sweep answered it: the client keeps ONE notice, and the LAST one wins

All five `HudGanda` modes ran twice in one match (kills 3/17, 6/21, 9/25, 11/28, 14/33, all
logged). The user's report:

| mode | sent | seen |
|---|---|---|
| `killingtype` | killFlag 256 + `killingType` = MASS | no sound - the field does nothing for notices |
| `frag` / `frag-balik` | one packet, two frags (32 and 256) | one notice only; **kill listed ONCE** |
| `paket` | 32, then 256 immediately | not both |
| **`paket-balik`** | **256, then 32 immediately** | **CHAIN SLUGGER notice + its voice; WEAPON UPDATE gone** |

Three facts fall out of that last row, and they are what everything now rests on:

- **the second packet really is received and processed** - its notice is the one that survived;
- **the client holds one notice at a time and the later one replaces the earlier**, taking the
  sound with it (the first packet's voice never played);
- **the kill feed does not duplicate**, because every counter in 3355 is absolute - so sending
  the packet twice is safe, exactly as predicted.

Two frags for one victim inside a single packet are **merged**, so that route is dead. So is
`killingType`: despite being a separate field the client fills itself, it drives no notice.

### `JedaPaket` - the remaining lever is TIME, not a different field

If the later notice wins, then the order that works is **sound first, `Intercept` last**, with
enough of a gap that the first notice has already rendered and started its voice:

    paket 1   killFlag = sound flag   -> notice + voice start
    (jeda)
    paket 2   killFlag = Intercept    -> WEAPON UPDATE replaces the notice, voice keeps playing

`JedaPaket=<ms>` (1..10000, anything else = 0) delays the second packet; `SapuJeda=1` sweeps
150 / 300 / 600 / 1000 / 1500 / 2000 / 3000 ms one per weapon award, forcing mode `paket`, with
the value written into the player's chat line (`<< JEDA 600ms`).

Implementation notes worth keeping:

- **The delayed packet is built at send time, not frozen now.** Every number in 3355 is absolute,
  so a packet whose bytes were built before the delay would briefly roll the scoreboard back if
  another kill landed during the gap. `KirimPaketKedua` keeps the `Room`/`FragInfos`/`SLOT`
  references and constructs `BATTLE_DEATH_PAK` inside the timer callback.
- **The timer callback must catch everything.** An unhandled exception on a `System.Threading.
  Timer` thread kills the whole process in .NET 4.x. It is wrapped, and it re-checks
  `room._state == RoomState.Battle` first so a finished round is never sent to.
- The `Timer` object is held in a one-element array captured by its own callback, otherwise the
  GC can collect it before it fires.
- Both death call sites now end with a single `Weapon_List_Ranked.KirimPaketKedua(room, kills,
  killer, isBotMode)`; `PerluPaketKedua` survives as the decision half and is what the tests
  drive.

`srv/UjiJeda.cs`: **29 checks** - `JedaPaket` reaching `Room.AceJeda` only for the two `paket`
modes, clamping of negative and oversized values, `SapuJeda` cycling all seven and overriding
`SapuHud`, immediate send at 0, a 3000 ms delay returning in **0 ms** (non-blocking), the delayed
send genuinely firing after the gap (measured 431 ms for a 400 ms setting) **with its exception
contained so the process survives**, a room out of `Battle` never being sent to, and
`HudGanda=off` leaving the old paths untouched. Regression `UjiHud` 52, `UjiSapu` 30, `UjiSuara`
26, `UjiIniAsli` all pass.

### IN-GAME CONFIRMED, and the last knob is how long the borrowed notice shows

that CHAIN SLUGGER is visible for those 2.5 s first.

That duration IS `JedaPaket`: the first notice only disappears when the second packet overwrites
it. So the flash is tunable to nothing in principle - and needs **no rebuild and no restart**,
because `JedaPaket` takes any value 1..10000 and the ini is re-read on timestamp change. It can
even be changed mid-match; it applies from the next weapon award.

The one thing that decides how low it can go cannot be measured from the server: **does replacing
a notice also cancel the sound it started?** One award answers it -

- voice still complete at 150 ms -> not cancelled; keep going down (100, 66, 50) until it is, and
  the notice becomes a few frames;
- voice cut or silent -> cancelled; the notice must stay on screen for as long as the voice runs,
  so `JedaPaket` has to be the voice length (2500 for ChainSlugger) and the flash is unavoidable.

Set to **150 ms** and left running. Note `0` is known to fail outright (both packets land in the
same frame; the first notice never renders and its sound never starts), so the floor is somewhere
above it.

### HOT KILLER: the streak byte was never actually disproven

The user sent a screenshot of a **HOT KILLER** notice with one star and "Waspada di area ini",
seen naturally during play, **with sound**. That is the trailing streak byte of 3355 doing its
job - the second notice channel, the one `StreakSound` drives.

So the 2026-09-29 conclusion that the streak byte "produced no sound" was wrong in its reasoning:
it was tested in the same packet as `killFlag = Intercept`, and the client keeps only ONE notice,
so WEAPON UPDATE simply overwrote it. Every negative result in this whole investigation has the
same shape.

How to test it cleanly, with no rebuild (the installed binary already supports it):
`HudGanda=off` + `SoundFlag=off` (leaves `killFlag` untouched, so nothing competes) +
`StreakSound=1`, then 2, then 3. If it sounds, wiring it into the working two-packet arrangement
is one line - `Load_Weapon_Ranked` currently forces `beruntun = 0` whenever `HudGanda` is active,
deliberately, so two experiments could not mix.

**`UI_HUD_Revenge_Effect.wav` IS reachable - the filename lies.** The user watched the sequence
in game: the streak notice fires CHAIN KILLER with `MV_Ann_Chain_Killer.wav` (2.52 s), and then
**HOT KILLER follows with `UI_HUD_Revenge_Effect.wav` (2.30 s)**. It is the hot-killer sound, not
a revenge sound; an earlier note here called it unreachable by grepping for "revenge", which is
the wrong word - the server has no "hot" concept either (the only `hot` hits are an `ITEM_TAG`
and a shop flag byte), so the whole chain is the client reacting to that one streak byte.

Two consequences, both important:

- **The client QUEUES its own notices** - two notices with two sounds, one after the other, from a
  single packet. So "the client keeps one notice" is only true of notices we push: two packets
  landing in the same frame overwrite each other, which is a delivery artefact, not a display
  limit.
- The streak byte reaches roughly **4.8 s of announcements** (2.52 + 2.30) at its top level, and
  HOT KILLER appears to come only *after* CHAIN KILLER. Whether a lower value (`StreakSound=1`
  or `2`) yields the hot-killer sound on its own is untested.

### Tools open INSIDE the hub now - tabs by window reparenting (2026-09-30)

User: "buka nya di tab I3Tools V3, tanpa membuka layar baru." Done, and **not one line of any
tool changed**. Each tool still runs as its own process; the hub takes over its window - the same
`SetParent` trick `PBPanel.exe` uses on the three server consoles - so crash isolation, the whole
reason the separate-process design was chosen, is kept.

**The risky assumption was settled first, by measurement**: does a GL context survive `SetParent`?
It does. All five GL tools (Viewer, Collision, Path, INS, Bone Weight) were reparented into
another process's Tk frame, resized, captured and detached; the Viewer's 3D area went from 3,400
distinct colours before to 3,809 after a reparent **plus** a resize, so it genuinely re-rendered
at a new viewport rather than showing a stale framebuffer. Had this failed, the whole plan would
have needed a different shape.

Three things had to be solved:

- **Finding the window.** A onefile exe shows its window from a **grandchild** process, so the pid
  `Popen` returns owns nothing (the test confirms `cucu:True`). Enumerating by process name is
  unreliable and injecting a wndproc into Tk is what produced `0xC0000409` in the pack editor's
  drag & drop. Instead the **child reports its own HWND**: `jalankan_alat` is given `--dok <token>`
  and, once the App exists, writes `GetAncestor(winfo_id(), GA_ROOT)` into
  `%TEMP%\i3tools_dok_<token>.txt`, which the hub polls. It deliberately does **not** call
  `update_idletasks()` first - idle work run too early can hang GL context creation.
- **Menu bars.** Windows forbids a child window from having one, so `root.config(menu=...)` would
  silently vanish. Measured: only **2 of the 14** tools use a menu bar (I3Pack Editor, I3RSC
  Editor) and both lay their root out with `pack`. `pasang_adaptor_menu()` - installed in the
  child, before the tool is imported - intercepts `config(menu=)` and rebuilds the menu as a row
  of `ttk.Menubutton` inside the window, reusing the tool's own `Menu` widgets so every entry and
  command still works. Verified: with the adapter the pack editor has no native menu
  (`GetMenu == 0`) and gains File/Edit/Alat/Tampilan/Bantuan with 11/16/15/2/1 entries; the RSC
  editor gains Berkas/Entri/Bantuan. Without it, the native bar is still there - so standalone
  launches are untouched.
- **The tools are bigger than the hub.** They were designed to own a window; the Collision editor
  wants ~1400 px and its right-hand panel was clipped. `Dok._tempel` measures the window's natural
  size **before** stripping its frame (afterwards there is no way to ask) and `App.pastikan_muat`
  grows the hub by the shortfall, bounded by the screen.

Shape of it: `Dok` per tool, each with a `Frame` placed full-size in `App.wadah`; switching tabs is
`lift()`, so nothing is rebuilt. Closing a tab posts `WM_CLOSE` to the tool - its own save prompts
still run. **Closing the hub detaches every docked tool back into a normal window** rather than
taking them down with it (`Dok.lepas`, same as PBPanel's `Lepas`). A sidebar toggle "Buka di dalam
tab" (remembered in `I3Tools.json`) switches back to the old separate-window behaviour, and
`jalankan()` now always goes through `--alat` so the frozen and source paths are identical.

Tests: `uji_i3tools_tab.py` **17 checks** driving the real hub - all **14 tools** dock (parent,
size and process verified for each) and close cleanly, three at once with tab switching, opening an
already-open tool just selects its tab, the tool resizes with the hub, and detaching leaves the
processes alive as top-level windows. `scratchpad/uji_exe_dok.py` **11 checks** against the built
exe in a folder holding no `.py` at all - the grandchild HWND report, docking for a menu tool, a GL
tool and a plain one, the menu adapter working frozen, and each tool still writing its own
`.ini`. Regression `uji_i3tools.py` **35** (its "click a card launches the tool" check had to learn
about `app.doks`).

Built 2026-09-30: `I3Tools V3.exe` 23,959,756 B, md5 `cd1f28c1cafedf81d6ac54c94e5eaa64`.

### REVERTED the same day - it crashed in real use

User: "Kalau di kembalikan saja bagaimana?? crash jadinya. biarlah seperti sebelumnya aman."
Restored immediately: `I3Tools V3.exe` is back to **23,953,682 B**, md5
`8ee466cf09ec2b50ec332573be8c5fa2` and the `.pyw` to `c67784396a8bd9769dee7d62bd15e7c4`, both
byte-verified against `_backup_sebelum_tab/`; `uji_i3tools_tab.py` was removed and
`uji_i3tools.py` put back to its original form (34 checks, all pass). Nothing of the tab feature
remains in either file - grep for `dalam_tab` / `class Dok` / `pasang_adaptor_menu` returns 0.

**So docking is not safe in practice, whatever the tests said**, and that is the finding worth
keeping. Every automated check passed - 14/14 tools docked, the frozen exe path, the GL contexts,
the menu adapter - yet it crashed when actually used. The tests only ever drove a *fresh* tool:
open, verify, close. What they never exercised is a tool being **worked in** while reparented -
dialogs owned by a window that is now a child, nested `mainloop`s inside those dialogs, drag &
drop (`WM_DROPFILES` goes to the window the shell hit-tests, and the pack editor's subclassed
wndproc is documented as fragile), and the GL tools' own `update_idletasks()` re-entrancy. Any of
those is a better suspect than the reparenting itself.

The whole implementation is preserved in `_hasil_tab_dibatalkan/` (the tab `.pyw` and `.exe`, plus
`uji_i3tools_tab.py`, `uji_exe_dok.py`, `uji_menu.py`, `uji_varian.py`, `win.py`). If it is ever
revisited, the thing to establish FIRST is which tool crashed and at what action - and the tests
must drive a docked tool through real work, not just open and close it.

### killFlag values ABOVE 256 are live - the server's enum stops too early (2026-09-30)

`KillingMessage` in `pbserver_data` ends at `Intercept = 256`, but the client knows more. Two
independent proofs:

- **`Helmet Protection` has both a notice image and `MV_Ann_HelmetProtection.wav` (2.54 s) yet no
  entry in the enum at all.** The enum is hand-maintained, exactly like `WeaponList`.
- **Tested in game** with `SoundFlag=only:<number>` (the parser already takes raw numbers, so this
  needs no rebuild and no restart):

      512   -> CHAIN KILLER notice + its voice
      1024  -> MASS KILL notice + its voice

`512 = ChainKiller` is a value the server never had a name for. `1024` landing on MASS KILL again -
a notice already reachable as `2` - suggests either a duplicate mapping (a variant, e.g. by
explosion vs by shotgun) or a wrap in the client's lookup; not settled.

The field is `writeH((short)frag.killFlag)`, i.e. **16 bits**, so `2048, 4096, 8192, 16384` are
still untried, and `32768` is reachable too (it casts to -32768 and goes on the wire as u16
32768). Non-bit values look dead - `258` produced nothing.

**Why this is being swept at all**: `MV_Ann_Kill.wav` (1.61 s) exists in
`Sound_voice_Announce.i3pack` but **no notice image matches it** - all 40 images in
`kill_message.i3i` + `kill_message1.i3i` were checked. A killFlag value that plays a voice with no
notice art would give sound with **nothing** extra drawn on screen, which removes the whole
"hide the borrowed notice" problem instead of merely shortening it. That is what the remaining
values are being looked for.

Testing costs nothing: with `HudGanda=paket` still on, packet 1 carries the value under test and
packet 2 still delivers WEAPON UPDATE, so the working behaviour is never lost while sweeping.

| Dino `.i3AnimPack` | **0**, in packs or loose |

The baseline makes it unambiguous: **50 of the client's characters do have
`Chara\<name>\<name>.I3CHR`** loose beside their pack; the Dino group is the only one that does
not. So `pNewChara` is NULL because the file that *creates* the character does not exist.

A sweep of **9,218 packs** across five locations (the client, `Update v1.15.42\Pack`,
`Pack 3.88`, `Change Logs`, `Dev\Chara`) plus a loose-file search finds **no Dino character
`.I3CHR` anywhere on this machine**. The only Dino `.I3CHR` that exist are the four *weapons*

### Joining motions: main animation + idle in one `.i3a` (2026-09-30)

User: "buatkan saya file fbx nya bisa di gabungin ke file fbx yang lain (untuk animasi idle
setelah animasi utama dibuat) atau bisa di gabung i3a jika animasi fbx idle nya tidak ada."

`i3bvh.sambung(daftar, silang, fps, lanjut)` concatenates several motions into one track set.
It works at the **retargeted** level - `trek = [(bone name, [(time, pos, quat, scale)])]` - which
is the one place every source already meets: FBX, BVH and `.i3a` all reduce to it, so a Mixamo
main motion and a stock `.i3a` idle join without any special case.
`muat_bagian(path, kerangka)` picks the route: `.i3a` is used as-is (already in PB skeleton
space), `.fbx`/`.bvh` go through `retarget` first.

Four things it has to get right, none of them obvious:

- **Bone ORDER differs between files.** `Salsa_Dance.i3a` and `Air_Kiss.i3a` both have 43 tracks
  but not in the same order, so parts are reordered by NAME onto the first part's list
  (`_samakan_urutan`); a bone the later part lacks simply holds its previous pose. A test that
  compares by index instead of name reports a 119-degree error that is not there - that happened.
- **Every part is resampled at one fps.** Stock `.i3a` key spacing is often uneven (461 of 1,223
  tracks in `Emote\`), so joining raw key lists would produce a lumpy timeline. `_sampel` does
  linear interpolation for position/scale and **slerp** for rotation, clamped at both ends.
- **Body displacement must continue, not snap back.** `lanjut=True` shifts a later part's
  positions so it starts where the previous one ended. It is applied **only to bones whose
  position actually varies** - every other bone carries the same bind translation in all parts, and
  shifting those would deform the skeleton. Measured on `Salsa_Dance` joined to itself: the seam
  jump on `Root` is 0.0000 m with it, 0.1868 m without.
- **`silang` seconds of crossfade** insert interpolated keys between the parts. Measured: the
  largest per-frame rotation step at the seam drops from 11.0 to 3.1 degrees with 0.5 s.

CLI: `ubah ... --sambung BERKAS` (repeatable) `--ulang N` `--silang DETIK`.
GUI: a fourth file row "Gerakan lanjutan / idle - .fbx, .bvh atau .i3a (boleh kosong)" plus
"Idle diulang" and "Silang antar gerakan (detik)". The duration passed to `tulis_i3a` is taken
from the joined track, not from the first part's `ket['durasi']`.

`uji_i3bvh_sambung.py`: **22 checks** - two `.i3a` joined (duration, uniform key count, strictly
increasing times), the second part genuinely present (pose right after the seam matches its first
pose to **0.0 degrees**, by name), crossfade key count and smoothness, root continuity, idle
repeated 3x, write/read round trip, `muat_bagian` routing, three refusals, and the window driven
in-process through a real conversion (BVH generated from an `.i3a` via `ke_bvh`, so the test needs
no Mixamo file; comma decimals accepted). Regression `uji_i3bvh.py` 58, `uji_i3anim_i3a.py` 43.

Rebuilt 2026-09-30: `I3BVH Convert V3.exe` **23,013,222 B** and `I3Tools V3.exe` **23,958,490 B**
(the merged menu bundles its own copy of `i3bvh`, so it needs the rebuild too - and it was rebuilt
from the **restored pre-tab** source, so the reverted docking feature stays out). Previous exes and
the pre-change `i3bvh.py` / `.pyw` are in `_backup_sebelum_sambung/`. Both smoke-tested: window
opens and closes clean, and the frozen CLI lists `--sambung` / `--silang`.

**Not tested in game.**
