### The build venv lives in a temp folder, and Windows empties that

Mid-session the scratchpad's PyInstaller venv lost **its `.py` files while every `.pyc` in
`__pycache__` survived** - `PyInstaller/__init__.py` gone, `pyinstaller.exe --version` dying with
`ImportError: cannot import name '__version__' from 'PyInstaller' (unknown location)`. Defender
had logged nothing; a temp-folder cleanup is the likeliest cause. Worth knowing because the venv
sits under `%TEMP%`, which is NOT inside the user's Defender exclusion and is fair game for
Storage Sense.

Two recoveries, both offline:

- **Copying `X/__pycache__/Y.cpython-310.pyc` to `X/Y.pyc`** makes Python import the modules
  again (420 of them here) and `--version` works. But it is **not enough to build**: PyInstaller
  finds hooks by globbing `hook-*.py` and copies runtime hooks in as SOURCE, so with only the
  `.pyc` present the hooks silently vanish - the exe came out 704 KB smaller. Do not ship a build
  made this way.
- **The real fix, still with no download**: every wheel needed is already in pip's HTTP cache.
  `scratchpad/ambil_wheel.py` walks `%LOCALAPPDATA%\\pip\\cache\\http`, finds each cached body
  that starts with `PK\x03\x04`, reads `*.dist-info/{METADATA,WHEEL}` for the name, version and
  tag, and writes a properly named `.whl`; then
  `pip install --no-deps --no-index <wheels>` restores the venv exactly (pyinstaller 6.22.2,
  hooks-contrib 2026.7, pefile, packaging, altgraph, pywin32-ctypes, numpy). Two traps: pip
  refuses a wheel whose filename does not follow the convention, and altgraph's WHEEL lists
  `py2` first so it must be renamed `py2.py3-none-any` to be accepted.

Check after any such repair: `PyInstaller/hooks` should hold ~363 `.py`, `hooks/rthooks` 20, and
`_pyinstaller_hooks_contrib/stdhooks` ~684. Four `.py` in `hooks/rthooks` means the venv is still
broken even though `--version` answers.

Sources of the 14 `.pyw` before the theme line was added are in `_backup_sebelum_tema\`.

## Mesh `.i3s` -> one `.obj` with groups -- `i3obj.py` (2026-09-24)

User asked whether the pack editor could "extract file obj seperti PBSDK", then chose **one OBJ holding
every mesh, each as a `g` group**. PB SDK's own `I3S.ExportOBJ` writes one file per mesh instead.

- `Adegan(jalur)` walks from the `i3SceneGraphInfo` root through `i3Node` / `i3AttrSet` / `i3Transform(2)` /
  `i3BoneRef` / `i3Geometry`, multiplying `i3MatrixObject` matrices along the way (so mesh positions are
  already world space), **plus `i3Body` -> `SKN2` -> `i3LOD` -> `BLD1+16` shape** which `i3gl.PetaGL` does not
  do - without that branch a character `.I3S` yields nothing, because its meshes hang off the body, not off
  plain nodes. Group name = `[LOD<n>_]<nearest named ancestor>_<GeometryAttr object index>`; the index makes
  it unique and matches PB SDK's block numbering.
- VA30 layout from the format word (`pos12`, `+12 nrm` if bit 0x2, `+4` colour if bit 0x8, then UV). Primitive
  4 = list, 5 = strip (unrolled, alternate winding flipped). Only the vertices a mesh's triangles actually
  reference are written, remapped to a local 0-based range.
- `vt` is written as `u -v`, matching PB SDK both ways (its importer calls `BuildVertexArray(g, flipUV=true)`
  which does `uy * -1`, and its exporter writes `-v`), so a round trip through PB SDK keeps UVs.
- **Encrypted IIA2 index arrays are decrypted with the existing `Cipher V2\` tables** (see the I3R2 notes:
  same PBM cipher as the pack V2 one). A mesh whose key is not harvested is skipped, its mask collected in
  `Adegan.kunci_perlu`, and the GUI then offers "Learning Encrypted Key" for exactly those masks and re-exports.
  `IF_S_Dajeong-Red_LOD1.i3s` is the sample: 6 meshes, 6 different keys, one of which (2:05) is already in the
  folder. **Read the scene before writing**: `App._obj_tulis` builds the `Adegan` first so the missing keys are
  still reported when `tulis_obj` then fails with "tidak ada mesh yang bisa diekspor".
- Guard that matters: after decryption `max(idx) >= vertex count` rejects the mesh. That is what stops a wrong
  or missing key from producing a plausible-looking but garbage mesh.
- Two modes: `tulis_obj` (one file, `g` per mesh) and **`tulis_obj_per_mesh`** (one file per mesh named
  `<i3s stem>_<group>.obj`, PB SDK's shape - added 2026-09-24 on request). `ekspor(..., per_mesh=True)`
  switches; the per-mesh path reuses `tulis_obj` on a one-mesh `Adegan` built with `__new__`.
- GUI: `Alat > Ekspor mesh .i3s ke OBJ` (cascade: one file / per mesh; multi-select + output folder)
  and, on a `.i3s` inside a pack, right-click `Ekspor mesh ke OBJ (satu file)` / `(per mesh)`
  (content written to the temp dir first, since `i3obj` reads files).
  CLI: `python i3obj.py info|obj|obj-pisah`.
- Tests: `uji_i3obj.py` (32 checks). Beyond counts it verifies the SHAPE - height 1.5-2.2 m, width < height,
  and vertices present in all ten height bands - because a wrong face/index mapping still produces the right
  counts. Rendering the exported points and triangles of `F_S_AR_Priest-Red_LOD1` gives a proper standing
  T-pose character. `REBEL_Female.I3S` exports 22 meshes / 14,941 triangles, matching a direct count of the
  `GEO2` primitive counts.

## Convert + clean `.i3s` -- `i3bersih.py` (2026-09-24)

User: "buatkan langsung convert i3s nya seperti I3Scene Convert v3, nanti i3s nya hasil clean atau
bersih (wajib dengan bone)". Asked what "clean" and "wajib dengan bone" meant; they chose
**convert AND decrypt IIA2**, and **refuse the result if bones are lost**.

- `konversi(src, out)` = `pindah_karakter.jenis_file()` routing (same as I3Scene Convert v3) ->
  `pindah_karakter.convert_karakter()` for new-client characters, `pindah_senjata.convert_mandiri()`
  for new-client weapons, plain copy for a file already in the old format -> `bersihkan_iia2()` ->
  bone check.
- **`bersihkan_iia2` patches IN PLACE.** Decrypting an index array does not change its length, so the
  bytes at `obj.off + 32 .. +2n` are overwritten and the cipher word at `+20` is zeroed; nothing else
  moves. That matters: i3Viewer2's "Quitar IIA2" + Save re-lays out the whole file (header version,
  BMA1->BMA2, objects reordered, orphans dropped) and the legacy client then rejects it - the
  Dasom_Red case in this file. The test asserts byte-for-byte equality outside the index regions,
  plus identical object count, string table and per-object offsets.
- Bone rule: `info_bone()` counts BMA1/BMA2 bone entries and VAs whose `(fmt>>14)&7` is non-zero.
  If the source had either and the result has none, the output file is **deleted** and `GalatBersih`
  raised. Overwriting the source is refused outright.
- Keys that are not harvested are never forced: those arrays are left encrypted, their masks come back
  in `kunci_perlu`, and the GUI offers "Learning Encrypted Key" then re-runs. Verified end to end on
  `F_S_SX_HarvestFarmer-Blue_LOD1.i3s` (new client, 5 encrypted arrays, keys 2:AF/2:B6/2:B7/2:BA):
  after harvesting those four, all 5 arrays come out plain, bones stay 67/4, `pb.lod_entries` still
  reads it, and the exported OBJ renders as a correct standing character.
- GUI: `Alat > Convert + bersihkan .i3s (client baru -> V1)...` and, on a `.i3s` inside a pack,
  right-click `Convert + bersihkan .i3s ini...` which then offers to **put the result back into the
  pack**. CLI: `python i3bersih.py info|convert|bersih`.
- **Multi-mesh weapons** (user hit this on `Weapon_Kar98k_TSR_Carnaval.i3Pack`, 2026-09-24):
  `pindah_senjata.weapon_lods` walks a LOD depth-first and stops at the FIRST `i3AttrSet`, then demands an
  `i3Geometry` among its kids - it only ever handled ONE mesh per LOD. Kar98k has 23 meshes hung off nested
  `i3BoneRef`s under AttrSets named `NewOpt` whose kids are more AttrSets, so it died with
  "LOD0: i3Geometry tidak ditemukan". `i3bersih.konversi` now **falls back to the generic
  `pindah_karakter.convert_karakter` rebuild** when the weapon route raises (`jenis` becomes
  `senjata (rute umum)`), which handles arbitrary scene trees. Result: 227 objects, 3 LODs, 14,198 vertices,
  23/23 index arrays cleaned, 14 bones kept, and the exported OBJ renders as a correct scoped Kar98k.
- That fallback needs `pb.mesh_refs` to descend into `i3BoneRef` (same shape as `i3Node`), which
  `pindah_karakter.periksa` reaches through `pb.lod_entries`. It is behind the module switch
  **`pindah_bone.IKUT_BONEREF`, default False**, and `i3bersih` flips it only around that one call
  (try/finally). Measured: with the flag on or off the HarvestFarmer-Red character conversion writes a
  **byte-identical** file, and `lod_entries` over all 281 project `.i3s` is unchanged - but the switch stays
  off by default so the in-game-proven character path can never be affected by a file we have not tried.
  **Trap when checking that**: `convert()` embeds the OUTPUT PATH in the `i3SceneGraphInfo` name, so two runs
  written to different filenames always differ in size and bytes. Compare runs written to the SAME path, or
  you will chase phantom non-determinism (this cost a detour).
- Tests: `uji_i3bersih.py` (31 checks; the "all arrays clean" one for the character sample is skipped when the
  needed keys are not in `Cipher V2\`, which is honest rather than a failure).

## `BC.i3Game` -- the client's stage list -- `i3game.py` (2026-09-24)

User: "Apakah anda bisa membuat Tool untuk edit file BC.i3Game ??" (they dropped a copy in `BCI3Game\`).
This is the file that decides **which maps the client knows**, i.e. what their `PBStage.dll` /
`InsertStageInfo` hack was working around - editing it here needs no DLL.

Plain I3R2 v9, four classes, no encryption. `BC.i3Game` = 113 stages / 340 instances / 9 layers,
`BCNewUI.i3Game` (V1.15.42 Blacklist_Script) = 111 / 336, start stage `NewLogin` instead of `Login`.

- **`i3StageInfo`** (one per map/screen) = `u8 len + name` then
  `STG1` | **class name, 67 bytes NUL-padded** | `ff` + f32 0.4 + 3 zeros + `ff` + f32 0.4 (13 bytes,
  identical in all 113) | `u32` raw id of another stage (`Lobby`->`ReadyRoom`, `Login`->`Lobby`,
  `CI`->`Login`, `Inven`/`Server`->...; 0 in 108 of 113) | u32 0 | **u32 length of the RSC text** |
  **u32 number of instances** | 60 zeros | the RSC text | per instance `u32 id + u32 0`.
  Stage classes seen: `CStageBattle` x102, plus one each of `CStageLobby`, `CStageReadyRoom`,
  `CStageReady`, `CStageLogin`, `CStageInven`, `CStageCI`, `CStageServer`, `CStageExit`,
  `CStageMapEditor`, `UILogin`, `UIMainFrame`. Only **2 stages carry an RSC path**
  (`Training` -> `World\Training\Training.RSC`, `MapEditor` -> `MapEditor/UserMap.RSC`); everything else
  gets its resources elsewhere.
- **`i3StageInstanceInfo`** = name of the C++ class to spawn + `u32 | u32 | f32 |` 20 zeros. Only four
  classes appear: `CGameCharaBase` (108), `WeaponBase` (107), `CTracerBullet` (102, normally `300, 1, 0`),
  `CGameCharaEquip` (23). A battle stage is normally those first three. Each instance belongs to exactly
  one stage and always sits **before** it in the object table.
- **`i3SgLayer`** = name + 36 bytes; byte 2 is 1 for the UI layers (`HudRoot`, `UIRoot`, `GuiRoot`,
  `UIRoot2`, `MessageRoot`) and 0 for `WorldRoot`, `ObjectRoot`, `CharaRoot`, `EffectRoot`.
- **`i3Framework`** (`LastWarfare`, the SGI root) = `GND1` + 28 zeros | `FRW1` | `cccccccc` |
  **u32 start stage** | 124 zeros | **u32 stage count + that many stage ids** | **u32 layer count + ids** |
  **u32 length + the global RSC list** (CRLF-separated, 13 paths: `Sound\Weapon.RSC`,
  `Chara\AnimPack.RSC`, `Weapon/Weapon.RSC`, ..., ending in 2 NULs).
  **The last 12 bytes of that list lie OUTSIDE the object's declared size** - the same trap as the `SND1`
  chunk in `.I3CHR`. Drop them and the client's resource list ends mid-path at `Weapon/`. `GameFile`
  remembers how much fell inside (`frw_dalam`) so an unchanged save is byte-identical.
- The string table follows the usual rule (class name then object name, in object order, ending in 2 NULs);
  **stage class names are NOT in it**, they live inline in the object data.
- `i3game.py`: `GameFile` (read/edit, objects as Python references), `Stage` / `Instance` / `Layer`,
  and `simpan()` which rewrites the whole file with fresh ids, re-reads it and compares every stage.
  Object order written = per stage its instances then the stage, then the layers, then the framework -
  which reproduces the stock layout exactly. Operations: rename, class, RSC path, stage link, instance
  add/edit/delete, `tambah` (new stage copying a normal battle stage), `gandakan`, `hapus` (refused while
  another stage links to it or it is the start stage), `pindah` (order in the framework list),
  `set_stage_awal`, and the global RSC list. CLI `--daftar --info --tambah --gandakan --ganti-nama
  --hapus --stage-awal --out`.
- `I3Game Editor V3.pyw`: stage table (number, name, class, the objects it spawns, RSC, link) with a
  search box, right-hand panel for the selected stage, a second table for its instances, "Jadikan stage
  awal", "Daftar RSC global...", undo (Ctrl+Z), and Simpan / Simpan sebagai. The start stage is green.
- Tests: `scratchpad/game/uji_i3game.py` (35 checks: both files byte-identical on rewrite, the 12 untabled
  bytes surviving, add/duplicate/rename/delete/undo, class+RSC+start stage+instances round-tripping,
  stage links staying valid after a duplicate, 8 refusals, the CLI) and `scratchpad/game/uji_gui.py`
  (24 checks driving the real window). All pass. **Not tested in game yet** - the obvious next step is
  adding a stage here and seeing whether the client accepts the map.

## Renaming a map safely -- `map_nama.py` (2026-09-24)

User, after noticing that dropping SweetCrackdown's `_World.I3S` into `Crackdown.i3pack` works
while a full copy named CakeCrackdown does not: "aneh bukan ?". It is not: overwriting one slot
changes only bytes (a mesh does not carry its own name and nothing resolves by it), while a
renamed copy has to agree in **four independent layers**, each a chance to break, each breaking
with a different assert:

    1. .i3Pack file names            <Map>.i3Pack, <Map>_Scene.i3Pack, ...
    2. member paths inside the pack  World/<Map>/..., Scene/<Map>/...
    3. the five paths in .i3WRD      -> i3World::OnLoad2 : pInfo != NULL
    4. the .RSC entries (path1+2)    -> the light / box references
    5. the MD5 resource hashes in <Map>.i3INS  -> i3World::BindSgRes kind_of<i3GameResWorld*>  (added
       2026-09-24; this is the one that was missing and it is what actually crashed the client)

**The rename rule that makes this safe**: only touch the map's own namespace - `World/<Map>/` and
`Scene/<Map>/`, plus file names inside them where `<Map>` stands as a whole token (delimited by
start/end, `_` or `.`). `Object/billboard/Crackdown_Glass01.i3i` is a **shared asset name** that
stock Crackdown also references (and that exists in no pack at all), so it must stay. The token
boundary is also what stops `Crackdown` matching inside `CakeCrackdown` - without it the result is
`CakeCakeCrackdown`.

Commands: `periksa` (health report), `perbaiki --map B --dari A` (fix a half-renamed map in place),
`salin --dari A --ke B` (clone). `--cadangan` is required for `perbaiki` and is **refused if it
points inside `Pack\`** - the client loads every `.i3Pack` there, so a backup beside the original
shadows it (the user hit exactly that earlier in the project).

`periksa` makes two passes, and the second is the one that matters:

- **missing references** - every RSC path against an index of the whole `Pack\` folder, minus the
  set a working comparator map (`--banding Crackdown`) is also missing. Stock Crackdown is missing
  **35** references of its own (all `Object/billboard/...`), so a raw count is meaningless; only the
  difference is. Comparator paths are mapped through `ganti_jalur` first, or every renamed path
  looks new.
- **cross-map references** - any `World/<other>/` or `Scene/<other>/` path inside this map's packs.
  These **resolve** (the other map's packs provide them), so an existence check alone passes a
  half-renamed map. This is the most common real failure and was invisible until the check was
  added: a half-renamed copy of Crackdown scored 0 problems, then 85 once the check existed.
  A path with no map folder at all (`World/<file>.i3s`, 2 segments) is reported too - that is the
  shape of the earlier SubData bug.

Applied to the user's live client: CakeCrackdown went from **42 cross-map references to 1**
(41 RSC entries in `Scene/Crackdown/_Generated/` repointed at its own folder), and its
missing-reference profile now matches stock Crackdown exactly. The remaining 1 is a stray leftover
member `World/CakeCrackdown_Light.i3s` - a misplaced file, not a naming error, so the tool reports
it and does not touch it. Backup written to `D:\Data C\BlacklistPB\_cadangan_map\<map>_<stamp>\`.

Note `i3ins.isi_rsc` recomputes each entry's stored offset field. Stock `Crackdown.RSC` has all 56
correct; the user's hand-edited `CakeCrackdown.RSC` had **55 of 56 stale** (left over from the
shorter original paths) and stock `Holiday_Scene` has 113 of 175 wrong, so the engine evidently
ignores the field - but a rewrite normalises it to the stock convention. 86 of 88 client Scene RSCs
round-trip byte-identically through `baca_rsc`/`isi_rsc`; the 2 that differ are exactly those two.

Test `scratchpad/col4/uji_mapnama.py` (30 checks): 10 rename-rule cases incl. the shared-asset and
`CakeCakeCrackdown` traps, pack-name mapping, then real work on a **copy** of the Pack folder -
a deliberately half-renamed map (85 problems -> 0), the live CakeCrackdown case (42 -> 1 with the
leftover correctly reported), backup contents byte-identical and the inside-`Pack\` backup refused,
only `.i3WRD`/`.RSC` bytes changing, and a full `salin` producing a map that checks clean.

## V3 collision -> V1 -- `ColFile.ke_v1()` (2026-09-24, PROVEN in i3Viewer2)

User: "Apakah anda bisa membuat Alat convert CakeCrackdown_Col_Hit.I3S bisa di baca oleh
I3Viewer2.exe ??? Atau anda perlu buat menu baru di I3Scene Convert v3 untuk Colision nya".
Their `BC.log` showed the exact failure:

    i3ResourceFile::FindObjectByID(32287) ... object list size 76
    i3PhysixShapeSet::OnLoad : Asserted : pBuff != NULL
    i3ResourceFile::FindObjectByID(1065353215) ... object list size 76

`1065353215` = `0x3F7FFFFF`, the bit pattern of the float 0.99999994 - the client is reading
**float data as an object id**, i.e. the shape-set header is being read at the wrong offsets.

**Two things separate a V3 collision from a V1 one**, and a survey of 140 client collision
files (59,894 shapes) against the V3 SweetCrackdown files pins both down:

| shape | V1 client | build V3 |
|---|---|---|
| box | PXA3 flags **0** | PXA3 flags **5** |
| convex | PXA3 flags **0** | PXA3 flags **3** |
| triangle mesh | PXA3 flags **4** | **PXA4** flags 4 |

`SweetCrackdown_Col_Hero.I3S` is the Rosetta stone: 228 PXA3 **and** 2 PXA4 written by the same
V3 tool in one file, which is how the two layouts were lined up.

`ColFile.ke_v1(ubah_flags=True)` does both, and `ColFile.perlu_v1()` reports what a file needs:

- **PXA4 (56-byte header) -> PXA3 (68)**. The layouts agree except that PXA3 carries three extra
  u32 between the "1" and the three floats: face-buffer id, face count, i3Vector3Array id. So
  PXA3+36 == PXA4+28 for the floats, and PXA4's second-blob size at +16 is replaced by the terrain
  id (PXA4 keeps terrain at +20).
- **The two objects PXA4 does not have are rebuilt** from the cooked mesh inside the NXUSTREAM
  (`Collision.geometri_lokal()`): `i3Vector3Array` = u32 count + 12 B per vertex,
  face buffer (`i3MemoryBuffer`) = u32 byte count + 16 B per face (u32 x3 + u16 terrain index +
  u16 junk). They are inserted immediately before the shape set, which reproduces the stock object
  order (terrain, face, vec, shapeset, matrix, combiner, transform2).
- **Counts match the cooked mesh exactly** in stock files (i3 vec count == cooked nv, i3 face
  count == cooked nt; only MET_00 and TH_MET_90 in Crackdown differ, where cooking added
  vertices), and the **order legitimately differs** - the i3 copy is the pre-cook order. So
  rebuilding in cooked order is fine.
- Per-face u16 fields: the first is the terrain index (0 in 6.1M of 6.2M stock faces, and one
  shape set has exactly one terrain buffer, so 0 is written); the second is **uninitialised
  memory** - 52,428 = `0xCCCC` is its most common value across the client - so 0 is written.
- PXA4's **second cooked mesh copy is dropped** (PXA3 has nowhere to put it). It is the same
  triangles in another coordinate space; the NXU copy is the one `_cooked()` already reads.
- Files that are already V1 are left **byte-identical** (`ke_v1` reports 0/0 and does not touch
  `self.ubah`).

**Proven against i3Viewer2** (`scratchpad/col4/uji_viewer.py`, which deletes `i3Viewer2.log` first
and waits for the title to become `<file> - i3Viewer2`, because the title only gains the filename
~3.5 s in, after the load finishes):

| file | window title | exit code | log |
|---|---|---|---|
| SweetCrackdown_Col_Hit.I3S (PXA4) | stays `i3Viewer2` | **0x80000003** (assert) | - |
| the same file after `ke_v1()` | `Sesudah_Col_Hit.I3S - i3Viewer2` | 0 | empty |
| stock Crackdown_Col_Hit.I3S | `Crackdown_Col_Hit.I3S - i3Viewer2` | 0 | empty |

Front ends: CLI `python i3col.py --file X --ke-v1 --out Y` (plus `--biarkan-flags`), and
**I3Scene Convert v3** routes collision files automatically - new `i3col.adalah_collision()` is
checked **before** `pindah_karakter.jenis_file()`, because a collision file has no vertex array
and no new-client class, so `jenis_file` calls it "sudah format lama" and skips it.
`kenali()` in the `.pyw` is that wrapper; `jenis_file` itself was deliberately left alone since
`i3bersih` depends on its current answers.

Tests in `scratchpad/col4/`: `uji_kev1.py` (20 checks: both SweetCrackdown files converted, world
geometry identical node by node, counts/flags/tags, face indices inside the vertex list, the
result rewriting byte-identically, and two already-V1 files staying byte-identical),
`uji_viewer.py` (5), `uji_gui_scene.py` (15, the Scene Convert window driven in-process).
Regression after the change: of the collision files on this machine **146 rewrite byte-identically,
0 differ** (the refusals are `_Col_Light.i3s` collider sets, which `i3col` has never supported).
Bug the GUI test only caught once a check was added after the "BERHASIL" line: `_finish` reads
`r['vertices']` and `r['size']`, so a converter's result dict must carry them or the status line
raises inside the Tk callback.
**Not tested in game yet.**

## `.i3WRD` -- a map's table of contents -- `i3wrd.py` (2026-09-24)

User: "File SweetCrackdown.i3WRD itu apa ya ??" then "Buatkan saya alat untuk mengedit alat tersebut, termasuk
juga full edit." This is the file the client reads **first** when loading a map; every other map file is reached
through it. Decoded from **192 stock `.i3WRD`** pulled out of the client `Pack\` and `Pack 3.88`.

Plain I3R2, 3-9 KB, 8 objects (7 or 6 when a table is absent), no encryption:

    #0..#4  i3SceneGraphInfo   EXTERNAL, size 0 -> World / Sky / Col_Hero / Col_Hit / Light
    #5      i3WorldSectionTable   optional (167 of 192 have it)
    #6      i3MapSectorTable      optional (189 of 192)
    #7      i3World               always, always 276 bytes

- **The order of the five SGIs never varies** - 0 exceptions in 192 files. The fifth is usually named
  `<Map>_Col_Light.i3s`, sometimes `<Map>_Light.i3s`.
- **External raw ids use TWO different encodings** and each file must be written back in its own:
  `0xFFFF0000 | objid` (37 files, the older ones) and the normal `bit31 | strindex<<16 | objid` (155 files).
  The first form is why `pb.I3R2` refuses these files (it reads string index 0x7FFF).
- The five external objects all carry **the offset of the first real object**, not their own - the same trap as
  `i3Animation` in `.I3CHR`.
- **6, 7 or 10 zero bytes sit OUTSIDE the last object's declared size** (all 192 files have some). Same family as
  the `SND1` chunk in `.I3CHR` and the RSC-list tail in `BC.i3Game`: drop them and the file is malformed.
  `WrdFile.ekor` keeps them verbatim.
- String table = class name then object name, in object order, ending in 2 NULs; the five paths land at indices
  1..5. Layout is header(0xB8) | strings | object table | data | tail.
- `i3WorldSectionTable` = `WST1` + u32 count + 32 zeros, then **176-byte** records: `name[128]` (cp949) +
  `u32 mask` + 44 bytes. `i3MapSectorTable` = `MST1` + the same 40-byte header, then **148-byte** records:
  `name[128]` + 20 bytes. Sizes are exactly `40 + count * rec`, which is the parser's check.
- `i3World` = `u8 len + name` + `GND1` + 44 zeros + `WRD2` + body:
  `+0..39` five `(u32 external raw id, u32 0)` slots, in the same order as the objects (equal to the object
  table's ids in all 192 files); `+40` and `+68` two **28-byte fog blocks**; `+96` and `+104`
  `(u32 raw id of WST, u32 0)` and the same for MST (**0 when that table is absent**, verified in all 192);
  `+112..` zero padding. The padding absorbs the name length, so **the object is 276 bytes whatever the node is
  called** (`World0` x133, `World` x54, `World1` x3, `StillRaid` x2).
- **Fog block** (28 B): `u8 enable`, `u8 mode` (D3DFOGMODE: 1 EXP, 2 EXP2, 3 LINEAR), 2 bytes, RGBA colour
  (alpha always 0xFF), then f32 **density**, **start**, **end**, and two floats that are 0.0 in every file.
  Block 1 ends at 1..500 m, block 2 at 50..3000 m, so they are presumably world fog and sky fog - **not proven
  in game**, which is why the tool just calls them Kabut 1 and Kabut 2.
- The tool: `WrdFile` (read/edit, `simpan()` re-reads and compares every value before replacing the target via a
  temp file, `cadangan=True` writes `<name>._backup.i3WRD` once), `Sektor`, `Seksi`, `Kabut`, and
  **`ganti_nama_map(lama, baru)`** which rewrites the map name in all five paths case-insensitively.
  Names keep their original bytes when unedited, so cp949 text that does not round-trip through Unicode is safe.
  CLI: `--ganti-nama-map --set PERAN JALUR --nama-world --tambah-sektor --nama-sektor --hapus-sektor --out
  --cadangan`. `main()` calls `reconfigure(errors='replace')` on stdout first: the stock sector names are Korean
  and this machine's console is cp1252, so without it every listing died with `UnicodeEncodeError`.
- GUI: five tabs (Berkas map / Sektor map / Seksi dunia / Kabut / Lain-lain), undo (Ctrl+Z, snapshots of
  `isi()` so undo is exact to the byte), a colour picker, and **"Periksa berkas di folder Pack..."** which scans a
  whole `Pack\` folder in a worker thread and reports each of the five paths as ada / HILANG / GANDA - the check
  that catches a missing or shadowed map file before the client crashes on it. The sector tab permanently shows
  the rule that the sector count must equal the `<Map>_0..n` line count in `World_<Nation>.txt`.
- Tests in this session's scratchpad (`wrd/`): `uji_i3wrd.py` **58 checks** (all 192 files rewritten
  **byte-identical**, fields, rename, sector/section edits, fog, the 276-byte rule, dropping and re-adding a
  table with the WRD2 reference following, 4 refusals, backup-once, CLI), `uji_gui.py` **39 checks** driving the
  real window in-process, `uji_exe.py` **13 checks** in a folder holding no `.py` at all. All pass.
- **Not tested in game yet.** The obvious first use is re-pointing a copied map pack's five paths instead of
  hand-editing bytes.

## A map is SIX packs -- making a new one (2026-09-24)

> **READ THE "ROOT CAUSE" SECTION BELOW FIRST.** Everything in this section between the file list and the
> "standing rule" at the end is a record of hypotheses that were all **disproved**. The real cause of every
> crash described here is the MD5 resource hash inside `<Map>.i3INS`. In particular the final conclusion -
> "a made-up map name is a dead end, reuse a name the client already ships" - is **not** established: it was
> inferred from crashes that had a different cause. Reusing a known name is still the lower-risk choice
> (`BioLab` is in all four `.i3Game`), but a new name may well work once the hashes are right.

User: "Buatkan saya i3pack map baru bisa ambil base dari file dari crackdown ... Dari tadi saya ga bisa
buat map baru. kena crash melulu." Their `CakeCrackdown` (a candy re-skin of Crackdown, world/sky/col_hit
in `MapBaru\CakeCrackdown\`) crashed the client. Result is in `MapBaru\hasil\` with `BACA INI.txt`.

**The file set of one map**, taken from `Crackdown` (30 files, and the new map must match it exactly):

| pack | contents |
|---|---|
| `<Map>.i3Pack` | `World/<Map>/` : `<Map>.i3WRD`, `<Map>_Ref.dds`, `<Map>_Sky.i3s`, `<Map>_World.I3S`, `Path.i3Path` |
| `<Map>_Col.i3Pack` | `<Map>_Col_Hit.I3S` (bullet collision) |
| `<Map>_Col_Hero.i3Pack` | `<Map>_Col_Hero.I3S` - **SECURE (flag 0x0800, V1 BitRotate)** in the stock pack |
| `<Map>_Scene.i3Pack` | `Scene/<Map>/` : `.i3INS`, `.RSC`, `_Generated/Box*.i3s` |
| `<Map>_SubData.i3Pack` | `<Map>_Light.i3s`, `Images/` : `load_<Map>_Blue.i3i`, `load_<Map>_Red.i3i`, `mini_<Map>.i3i`, `mini_<Map>_text.i3i`, `minfo_<Map>.txt`, `Light/<Map>_Light0.i3Light` |
| `<Map>_TabMinimap.i3Pack` | `TabMinimap/` : `info_<Map>.txt`, `tab_mini_<Map>.i3i` |

Plus the stage must exist in **`BC.i3Game`** (see the `i3game.py` section) - theirs was already there, in
`Blacklist_Script_Config.i3pack` (114 stages; `Script.i3pack` still has the old 113, and the Config one wins).

**CORRECTION (same evening): neither defect below was the crash.** The user installed the fixed set and
it still died. The client's own `BC.log` says what actually happens:

    LoadRSC --- RSC : Scene/CakeCrackdown/CakeCrackdown.RSC
    LoadRSC TRUE
    (13x) Could not load resource : Scene/CakeCrackdown/_Generated/Box_*.i3s
    i3Framework::OnUpdate() - STATE_LOAD_END Enter
    i3World::BindSgRes(...) : Asserted : i3::kind_of<i3GameResWorld*>(pRes)

then `PointBlank.exe` dies in `i3FrameworkDx.dll`, `0xC0000005`, **fault offset 0x00115224 - identical on two
runs**, so it is deterministic. Read `BC.log` and `Get-WinEvent Application` FIRST next time; both were there
before I started guessing. The 13 "Could not load Box_*.i3s" lines are noise: Crackdown's own RSC names the
same 13 files, they are absent from the client too, and Crackdown works.

**Everything checked against the other 88 maps and RULED OUT** (each was a plausible-looking difference):

| looked wrong | reality |
|---|---|
| world mesh is I3R2 **version 9** | 21 other maps in this client are version 9 too |
| scene root is `i3Transform`, Crackdown's is `i3Node` | 70 of 88 are `i3Transform` |
| `.i3WRD` external SGI ids `0x80010001..5` vs Crackdown's `0xFFFF0001..5` | 68 of 89 use the `0x8001` form |
| `i3World` object named `World0` | 58 of 89 use `World0` |
| world path in `.i3WRD` not upper-cased | 73 of 89 are mixed case |
| the `.RSC` | re-derived from Crackdown's and came out **byte-identical to theirs** |
| `.i3INS` + the 13 `Box*.i3s` | byte-identical to Crackdown's |

Current state: everything non-mesh is now **derived from Crackdown byte for byte**
(`scratchpad/map/turunkan.py` rewrites only the path strings in the `.i3WRD` and `.RSC` and asserts every
object's data is unchanged), and `scratchpad/map/buat_varian.py` also builds four bisection sets in
`MapBaru\uji\` - all meshes from Crackdown, then one new mesh at a time - so the next in-game test says
which file is at fault. **Trap found while doing this**: the rename must NOT touch
`Object/billboard/Crackdown_Glass01/02.*` in the `.RSC` - those are shared assets many maps use, and renaming
them to `CakeCrackdown_Glass01` makes them disappear. Restrict renaming to paths starting `World/<Map>/` or
`Scene/<Map>/`.

**IN-GAME RESULT: the packs are NOT the problem.** The variant where **every mesh is Crackdown's own bytes**,
only renamed, crashes with the identical assert. So `_World`, `_Sky` and `_Col_Hit` are all innocent, and so is
every file I rebuilt. What the map's content is does not matter - what matters is how the map is registered.

The comparison that finally narrowed it: **SpacePort is also a DLL-added map and it WORKS**, so diff the two.
Everything matches - `.i3WRD` external SGI ids `0x8001xxxx`, `i3World` named `World0`, 8 objects, the same pack
set. One difference is left:

| | UID | exe slot | family | result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SpacePort | 118 | `TD_JUNKYARD` | 1 = `TD_` Death Match | **works** |
| CakeCrackdown | 108 | `BB_BIOLAB` | 2 = `BB_` | **crashes** |

`PBStage.dll` registers new maps by reusing a UID the packed exe already knows
(`STAGEID_INFO_LIST::InsertStageInfo`, see `BACA INI - PBStage.txt` in the client); `STAGE_ID =
(family << 24) | UID`, and the family comes from the slot being reused. The working theory now is that a
`BB_` slot makes the engine build a different stage/world kind, so `BindSgRes` gets a resource that is not an
`i3GameResWorld`. Next test handed over (`MapBaru{BS}uji{BS}5_PBStage_tukar_slot{BS}`): a `PBStage.ini` that
**swaps the two slots** - CakeCrackdown to 118/TD_, SpacePort to 108/BB_ - which settles it either way in one
launch and touches no pack at all.
Worth knowing for later: of the 61 `TD_` slots in the exe, **only `TD_JUNKYARD` (118) has no packs in this
client**, and SpacePort already occupies it; the other free slots are 108 `BB_BIOLAB` and 103 `ES_DINORUINS`.
The server's `data/maps/modes.xml` is positional (125 entries, index = map id) and has 103/108/118 all
`enable="false"` - yet SpacePort works on 118, so that flag is not what gates a map.

**SLOT-SWAP RESULT: the family theory was WRONG too.** `PBStage.log` confirms the swap was applied
(118 = CakeCrackdown 0x01000076, 108 = SpacePort 0x0200006C) and `BC.log` shows **SpacePort loading fine on
the BB_ slot 108**. So: SpacePort works on either slot, CakeCrackdown fails on either slot. The slot and its
family decide nothing.

**The mistake underneath all of this**: I kept deriving the new map from **Crackdown**, which is a map the exe
has known since forever. The right template is **SpacePort** - the only DLL-added map in this client that
works, i.e. the same situation as CakeCrackdown. Next tests handed over:
`MapBaru{BS}uji{BS}6_klon_spaceport{BS}` (SpacePort cloned byte for byte under the name CakeCrackdown - 26
files verified identical apart from the path strings in `.i3WRD`/`.RSC`) and `7_klon_spaceport_world_kue{BS}`
(same plus the cake world mesh). If 6 crashes, the NAME/registration is at fault, not any file.
**Do not clone the `_Textures` / `_Images_NoText` packs**: `SpacePort_World.i3s` names its textures with the
absolute in-pack path `World{BS}SpacePort{BS}Textures/...`, so those packs must stay under the original name
(`scratchpad/map/klon.py` skips them).

**ROOT CAUSE (found from the user's hint "SpacePort dan DeadTown namanya sudah terdaftar dalam
PointBlank.exe v1"): `config/BC.i3Game` is shipped by TWO packs, and the new stage was only in one of them.**

| file | pack | stages | CakeCrackdown |
|---|---|---|---|
| `config/BC.i3Game` | `Blacklist_Script_Config.i3pack` | 114 | yes |
| `config/BC.i3Game` | `Script.i3pack` | 113 | **no** |
| `config/BCNewUI.i3Game` | `Blacklist_Script_Config.i3pack` | 111 | **no** |
| `config/BCNewUI.i3Game` | `Script.i3pack` | 111 | **no** |

`SpacePort` and `DeadTown` are in all four (they ship with the client - the exe knows the names, only the
packs were missing, which is why converting those maps from V3 works). A made-up name added to just one of
the four is invisible to whichever copy the client actually reads, so the stage never becomes a world
resource and `i3World::BindSgRes` gets the wrong kind. **That is why every pack variant failed, including the
one built from Crackdown's own bytes and the byte-faithful SpacePort clone - the map packs were never the
problem.**

Fix built with the new `i3game.py`: `scratchpad/map/daftar_stage.py` walks every `.i3Game` in every pack and
adds the stage (duplicating the `Crackdown` entry) wherever it is missing, then verifies that **nothing else
in those packs changed** - same file count, same bytes, same cipher flags (`MapBaru{BS}hasil_daftar_stage{BS}`,
`Script.i3pack` 18 files / `Blacklist_Script_Config.i3pack` 15 files, only the `.i3Game` entries differ).
**Rule for any new map: register the stage in EVERY `.i3Game` the client ships, not just one.** Awaiting the
in-game result.

**`Script.i3pack` IS ANTI-TAMPER PROTECTED - never edit it.** Replacing it makes the client pop
`STR_TBL_GLOBALDEF_GAMEINTERFACE_DATA_CRACKED1/2`. The user restored it themselves and said to keep additions
to `Blacklist_Script_Config.i3pack` only. So the 113-stage `BC.i3Game` inside `Script.i3pack` can never gain a
new stage name - **a made-up map name is a dead end in this client.**

**The way that works is the user's own, and it is now the standing rule: reuse a map NAME the client already
ships.** Requirements, all checkable offline:
1. the name is in all four `.i3Game` files (so nothing needs editing),
2. the exe's own stage table knows it (`PBStage - daftar stage di exe.txt`), which also fixes its UID and family,
3. no main pack for it exists in `Pack{BS}`, so nothing is lost.
Free names in this client: **`BioLab`** (BB_, UID 108 - the slot already configured), `DinoRuins` (ES_, 103),
`Holiday2` (EH_); `Junkyard` (TD_, 118) is taken by SpacePort. That is exactly how SpacePort and DeadTown were
added - their names shipped with the V1 client, only the packs were missing, so the V3 maps were converted in
under those names.
Delivered `MapBaru{BS}hasil_BioLab{BS}`: the cake meshes under the name BioLab, 6 packs / 33 files, the
existing `BioLab_SubData.i3pack` contents carried over intact plus `BioLab_Light.i3s`; verified that all five
`.i3WRD` references resolve inside the set, every `.i3i` is a power of two and every `.i3s`/`.i3Path` parses
(`scratchpad/map/buat_biolab.py`, `periksa_biolab.py`).

One more thing learned from `BC.log`: `PBStage.dll` injects at 21:10:17 but the exe builds its own stage table
at 21:10:31 and then logs `InsertStageInfo : Asserted : "Stage Id is an already-registered number"` **twice** -
once for each DLL entry whose UID the exe also owns (118 Junkyard, 108 BioLab; 37 Giran has no exe entry, which
is why it does not collide). The DLL's entry wins, so this is benign - but it shows the DLL registers *before*
the exe, and that a UID the exe knows is always double-inserted.

**Two real defects fixed on the way**, found by comparing against every other map in the client (worth keeping
as rules even though neither was the crash):

- **The loading screens were not a power of two.** `load_CakeCrackdown_Blue.i3i` was 1600x1200 and
  `_Red.i3i` 1920x1080. Of the **242** `load_*.i3i` in the client, 240 are 1024x1024 and the other two are
  512x1024 and 1024x256 - every single one a power of two, and those two were the only exceptions. The
  loading screen is the FIRST thing loaded when entering a map, so a texture the device refuses kills the
  client right there. Rebuilt at 1024x1024 DXT1 (code 0x81), 524,348 bytes - byte-size identical to
  `load_Crackdown_*.i3i` - artwork scaled into the **top 768 rows with the bottom 256 transparent**, the
  layout every stock loading screen uses (same finding as the Giran2 work).
- **`CakeCrackdown.dds` instead of `CakeCrackdown_Ref.dds`.** 78 of the 87 `.dds` in the client are
  `<Map>_Ref.dds` (the rest are absolute dev paths with the same basename, plus one stock typo
  `Airportr_Ref.dds`); theirs was the only one with no `_Ref` at all. Nothing in the `.i3WRD` or `.RSC`
  names it, so the client builds the name by convention.

Also worth knowing before chasing ghosts:

- **35 of the 56 `.RSC` entries point at files that are not in the client at all** - the glass billboards
  (`Object/billboard/Crackdown_Glass0*.i3i/.I3S/.i3Obj`) and every `_Generated/*.i3Evt`. **Crackdown's own
  RSC has exactly the same 35 missing**, and Crackdown works, so a missing RSC entry is normal here and is
  not the bug. Compare counts against a working map instead of reading the list.
- The `i3World` object name (last string in the `.i3WRD`) is `World0` in 58 of 89 maps, `World` in 29 -
  so `World0` is fine, not a rename artifact.
- Pack FILE names are case-insensitive on Windows: `CakeCrackDown.i3Pack` and `CakeCrackdown.i3Pack` are
  the same file, so a new set overwrites the old one instead of shadowing it.
- Their `_Col.i3Pack` still held **Crackdown's** `_Col_Hit.I3S` (985,866 bytes) - the new one from
  `MapBaru\` is 3,025,286 with its own materials (GND_, PAP_, PLASTIC_, GLASS_, TH_*).
- `_Col_Hero.I3S` in the delivered set is still Crackdown's 89 collisions; the matching 230-collision one
  for this mesh is in `Desktop\SweetCrackdown\SweetCrackdown_Col_Hero.i3Pack` (offered, not swapped in).
- Build + check scripts: `scratchpad/map/buat_pack.py`, `buat_load.py` (the DXT1 encoder, 1-bit alpha),
  `periksa.py` (30 checks: file list identical to Crackdown's, every `.i3WRD` reference present, RSC
  misses no worse than Crackdown, every `.i3i` a power of two, and every `.i3s`/`.i3Path` actually parsing
  through `i3gl`/`i3col`/`i3path`). **Not tested in game yet.**

## ROOT CAUSE of every failed map copy: the `.i3INS` stores an **MD5 of the resource path** (2026-09-24)

Every earlier theory in this file about why a renamed map crashes was wrong. The real cause was read out of
the **i3Engine SDK source** the user owns (`D:\My Project\Point Blank Developer Tools\Full Source I3Engine
Tool 2007.zip`; the extracted `Desktop\I3Engine Tool` folder is gone, read it straight from the zip).

`i3::pack::GAME_INSTANCE` (`include/i3Framework/i3GameResDefine.h`) names the two fields this file used to call
"kode A" and "the 12-byte hash":

    UINT32 nHashCodeResPath;   // .i3INS body +0   <- the object's RESOURCE, not a flag
    UINT32 nHashCodeInstClass; // .i3INS body +4   <- class_crc() of the C++ class to spawn
    UINT32 HashCode[3];        // .i3INS body +80

Together `+0` then `+80` are a **128-bit MD5 of the resource path**, built exactly as
`i3LevelRes::setPath` does it (`i3TDK/i3Level/i3LevelRes.h`): `make_unix_path` (backslash -> `/`), then
`to_upper`, then `i3MD5::Gen` over `strlen` bytes (no NUL). `i3GameSceneInfo.cpp` splits it into the struct
(`l & 0xFFFFFFFF` -> `nHashCodeResPath`, then `l >> 32`, `h`, `h >> 32` -> `HashCode[0..2]`) and looks the
resource up by that value alone:

    UINT128 hash( HashCode[2], HashCode[1], HashCode[0], nHashCodeResPath);
    pInstInfo->_pRes = m_pResManager->FindResourceByHash( & hash);

**The client never matches a resource by its path text.** So a map copied under a new name still carries the
MD5s of the OLD paths, `FindResourceByHash` misses, and `i3World::BindSgRes` (`src/i3Framework/i3World.cpp:156`,
`I3ASSERT( i3::same_of<i3GameResWorld*>(pRes))`) gets something that is not the world:

    i3World::BindSgRes : Asserted : i3::kind_of<i3GameResWorld*>(pRes)

Proven on the user's own files before any in-game test:

| map | hash check |
|---|---|
| `Crackdown` (stock, works) | 76 objects, **all** resolve against its RSC |
| `SpacePort` (added by PBStage.dll, works) | 69 objects, **all** resolve |
| `CakeCrackdown` (crashes) | **29 objects resolve to nothing** - `World`, `Element`, `Path`, 26 `Box*` |

and byte-exactly: `MD5("WORLD/CRACKDOWN/CRACKDOWN.I3WRD")` = `020d1d7a a9f840e89e8ae8bddef12386` = the `World`
object's 16 bytes in `Crackdown.i3INS`. Same for SpacePort.

This retro-explains everything that made no sense: overwriting one slot works (nothing is renamed, the hashes
stay valid); a variant holding **Crackdown's own bytes** still crashed; a byte-faithful **SpacePort clone**
still crashed; and the `.i3Game` stage-list theory, the slot/family theory and every pack-content theory were
all dead ends. **`Script.i3pack` never had anything to do with it** - it is still anti-tamper protected and
must still not be edited, but a new map does not need it.

Which objects carry a hash: the `World` root (the map's `.i3WRD`), the light (`.i3Light`), `Path`
(`.i3Path`), every trigger `Box*` (its `.i3Evt`) and every glass / i3Obj instance (its `.i3Obj`). Respawns
have `nHashCodeResPath == 0xFFFFFFFF` and no resource (`i3LevelPrim_Respawn.cpp` writes exactly that).
**Shared assets keep their hash**: `Object/billboard/Crackdown_Glass01.i3Obj` is named Crackdown but belongs
to many maps, so renaming its path (or its hash) breaks it - the same rule as `map_nama.ganti_jalur`.

In the tools now:
- `i3ins.md5_jalur(jalur)`, `Objek.hash_res` / `set_hash_res()` / `punya_resource()`, `HASH_KOSONG`,
  `peta_hash_rsc()`, `ganti_hash_resource(ins, entri_lama, entri_baru)` and `periksa_hash_resource(ins, entri)`.
  The rename needs the RSC entry list **before and after** the rename, in the same order, because MD5 is
  one-way - the old path is recovered by hashing the old RSC, never by parsing the object.
- `map_nama.py`: `salin` and `perbaiki` now update the hashes (`_olah_ins`, and `olah_pack` processes the
  `.RSC` before the `.i3INS` so the mapping exists), and `periksa` reports a map whose `.i3INS` hashes do not
  resolve - the check that would have found this on day one. Verified: cloning Crackdown to a scratch Pack
  folder now reports **0 problems**, stock Crackdown/SpacePort report "semua cocok", CakeCrackdown reports the
  29.
- Regression: **87 of the 88 `.i3INS` in the client** read and rewrite byte-identically. The one refusal,
  `RushHour.i3INS` ("objek 34 susunannya tidak dikenal"), is a pre-existing parser gap unrelated to this.

Delivered `MapBaru\hasil_BioLab\` (6 packs / 33 files, 29 hashes fixed) and
`MapBaru\perbaikan_CakeCrackdown\CakeCrackdown_Scene.i3Pack` (the user's own installed pack with only the
`.i3INS` hashes corrected; the other 14 files byte-identical).

### The map picture in the room UI -- `Stage.Pef` (same day, cosmetic)

`BC.log` also carries, once per UI refresh and **not** fatal:

    CEquipShapeManager::SetMapShape : unknown Stage name [ BioLab ] (see Stage.pef)

`config/Stage.Pef` ships in **both** `Blacklist_Script_Config.i3pack` (193,176 B, 109 stage keys) and
`Script.i3pack` (166,949 B, 105). After the pack's own V1 BitRotate it is a plain I3R2 of `i3RegKey` nodes -
no second cipher layer, so the older note in this file about "3 bits per 1024/2048-byte block" was describing
the pack cipher itself. Node layout: `u8 len + name + 'TRN3' + 72-byte header (sub-key count at +8) +
sub-key ids + 'RGK1' + u32 value count + 8 zeros + n x (u32 id + u32 0)`; a value object is
`u8 len + name + u32 9 + u32 type + u32 15 + values` (type 0 i32, 1 f32, 2 `RGS3` + u32 chars + UTF-16LE),
15 = the nation columns. A stage key holds `_UIShapeIndex`, `StageUID`, `CamFar`, `Shader_BloomIntensity`, ...

The key exists but is spelled **`Biolab`** while the exe's stage table, all four `.i3Game`, the pack names and
every in-pack path spell it **`BioLab`** - a stock typo. (Engine `i3Registry::FindKey` -> `i3TreeNode::
FindNodeByName` uses `generic_is_iequal`, i.e. case-INsensitive, so the 2007 engine would have found it; the
2020 client's `CEquipShapeManager` evidently does not.) Shipped as an optional
`hasil_BioLab\opsional_gambar_map\Blacklist_Script_Config.i3pack`: **exactly 2 bytes** differ in
`config/Stage.Pef`, the other 14 files are byte-identical with unchanged cipher flags. If the message survives
it, the client reads `Script.i3pack`'s copy instead - which stays untouched, so the map picture stays blank.

Also worth knowing from that log: the client reached the lobby and the ready room fine and logged
`GotoNextStage( BioLab )` + `LoadRSC Scene/BioLab/BioLab.RSC` + `LoadRSC TRUE` before dying, so a `[F]`
SetMapShape line is noise, and the 13 `Could not load resource : Scene/<Map>/_Generated/Box_*.i3s` lines are
the same ones stock Crackdown produces.


## NEVER edit a base pack in place -- the `" (2)"` override convention (2026-09-24)

The user's rule, and the client proves it: **an original pack must stay byte-intact.** A change goes into a
SECOND pack whose name is the base name plus `" (2)"`, and that copy wins because **a space (0x20) sorts
before the dot (0x2E)**, so `BurningHall (2).i3pack` is read before `BurningHall.i3pack`.

Two stock examples in `BlacklistPB V1 Remake\Pack`, both maps, both exactly this shape:

| pack | files | vs base | differs |
|---|---|---|---|
| `BurningHall (2).i3pack` | 5 | **the same 5 paths** as `BurningHall.i3pack` | `_Sky.i3s`, `_World.I3S` |
| `Octagon (2).i3Pack` | 4 | the same 4 paths as `Octagon.i3pack` | `_Sky.i3s` |

So a `" (2)"` pack is a **full copy of the base with a few members swapped**, not a partial overlay.
Related but different: a `_2` / `_New` suffix (no space, e.g. `Weapon_Common_2.i3Pack`,
`Weapon_Common_New.i3pack`, `Blacklist_Hud_2.i3pack`) sorts AFTER the base (`.` 0x2E < `_` 0x5F), so those
packs only ADD new paths - they cannot override. Confirmed by content: `Weapon_Common_2` holds all 1041 base
paths plus 248 new ones, and for the shared ones the base copy is what the client actually uses.

**Why it matters**: the user reports that modifying a base pack's contents produces the in-game notice
`STR_TBL_INGAME_HUD_NOTICE_GAME_DATA_DAMAGED` ("Game data file rusak ... akan segera keluar dari game",
logged as `Exit From Msg CallBack / File:.\StageBattle.cpp / Line:1889`). That is **not** the anti-tamper
dialog - anti-tamper is `STR_TBL_GLOBALDEF_GAMEINTERFACE_DATA_CRACKED1/2`, which is what editing
`Script.i3pack` triggers. Two different checks, two different messages.

Deliveries were rebuilt accordingly: `MapBaru\perbaikan_CakeCrackdown\CakeCrackDown_Scene (2).i3Pack` plus
`kembalikan_pack_dasar\CakeCrackDown_Scene.i3Pack` (the base restored to its original bytes),
`MapBaru\hasil_BioLab\BioLab_SubData (2).i3Pack`, and
`hasil_BioLab\opsional_gambar_map\Blacklist_Script_Config (2).i3pack`.

Restoring that base was possible because the pre-fix `CakeCrackdown.i3INS` is **byte-identical to
`Crackdown.i3INS`**, and `i3ins.ganti_hash_resource` is exactly reversible: renaming Crackdown's hashes to
CakeCrackdown reproduces the installed file, and renaming them back reproduces Crackdown's file.
