### I3INS Editor V3: the "Resource" column (2026-09-24)

The object tree gained a third column showing **which file each object's MD5 resolves to**, because the
`.i3INS` stores only the hash and nothing readable (see the ROOT CAUSE section). `_muat_resource()` reads the
`<Map>.RSC` sitting next to the `.i3INS` (`i3ins.cari_pendamping`) and builds `i3ins.peta_hash_rsc()`; the
hash can only be turned back into a path by hashing every RSC entry, since MD5 is one-way.

Per object: the basename when it resolves, `-` when the object has no resource (`0xFFFFFFFF`, the respawns),
`?` when there is no `.RSC` to compare against, and **`TIDAK KETEMU` with the row tagged red** (`putus`) when
the hash is not in the RSC. The detail panel gained a `Resource:` row with the full path, red when broken,
and opening a file logs a summary plus the `map_nama.py salin` fix line.

Verified on two real files: the installed `CakeCrackDown_Scene.i3Pack` (64 hashed objects, **0 red**) and the
pre-fix copy in `MapBaru\perbaikan_CakeCrackdown\kembalikan_pack_dasar\` (**29 red** - World, light, path,
26 boxes), with respawns correctly showing `-` and never red. Test: `scratchpad/uji_kolom_resource.py`.
Note the app's `__main__` runs `batch()` when given any argument, so the exe cannot be handed a file path to
screenshot - drive the `.pyw` in-process instead (`scratchpad/potret_ins.py`, PrintWindow flag 2 on
`GetAncestor(winfo_id(), GA_ROOT)`).
### A `0x98` pack marker makes the V1 client ignore the pack entirely (2026-09-25)

Symptom: `CGameCharaManager::_GetRespawnPosition : "team 1 has no Respawn Position" (1:Red 2:Blue 3:R_NPC
4:B_NPC)` and, on the server, `Used spawn count: 0` / `End Players count: 0`. The tell in `BC.log` is what is
**missing**: 13 other `.RSC` files load and `RSC : Scene/<Map>/<Map>.RSC` never appears at all, so the stage
goes `JumpStage()` -> (2 s, no loading) -> `Recv battle packet Protocol ID(3349)` -> `STATE_LOAD_END Enter`
instead of the normal `LoadRSC` + ~11 s.

Cause: the pack's node marker. The u32 `0x??713282` before each node's file list has a top byte that picks the
layout - `0x88..0x8F` 48-byte names, `0x90..0x97` 64-byte names (both plain, entries rotated 2 bits), and
**`0x98..0x9F` = newer-client format where a u16 type/key follows the count field and the entry list is
V2-enciphered**. The V1 client cannot read `0x98`; the pack behaves as if it were empty, so no `.i3INS`, so no
respawn objects. Every stock pack in this client is `0x88`/`0x90`/`0x91`/`0x92` - **none is `0x98`**.

`i3pack.py` deliberately PRESERVES a `0x98` node's format on save (so newer-client packs are not corrupted),
which means editing such a pack and saving it keeps it unreadable to V1. To convert, set
`node.kunci_entri = 0` and `node.penanda_atas = 0x90` on every node and save - contents, order and per-file
cipher flags are untouched; the file shrinks by 2 bytes per node. Script:
`scratchpad/map/turunkan_format.py`; delivered as `MapBaru{BS}perbaikan_format_pack{BS}`.

`map_nama.py periksa` now reports every pack's marker and counts `>= 0x98` as a real problem - it previously
said "0 masalah nyata" for a map whose scene pack the client could not read, which was a genuine hole. This
needed `i3pack` to record `node.penanda_atas` for ALL nodes (it used to set it only on the `0x98` branch).

Timeline that proved it: the same map loaded fine at 00:38 with a `0x90` scene pack (`LoadRSC` + 11 s + battle),
the user rewrote that pack at 00:53, and from then on the scene was never loaded. The map's own data was
provably fine throughout - `periksa` reported all five `.i3WRD` paths present, 56 RSC entries, no cross-map
references and every `.i3INS` hash resolving.

Also worth keeping: respawn team comes from `GAME_INSTANCE.nParam1` at body **+60** (`i3LevelPrim_Respawn.cpp`:
`pInfo->nParam1 = m_nRespawnStyle`), the field this file calls "bendera". Crackdown 6x0 + 6x1, BurningHall and
SpacePort 8x0 + 8x1 - so 0/1 map to Red/Blue and a working map never needs more.

**It happened again on SweetCrackdown (2026-09-25)**, same tell: `GotoNextStage( SweetCrackdown )`
at 20:53:33 with **no** `--- RSC : Scene/SweetCrackdown/SweetCrackdown.RSC` anywhere after it, then
`_GetRespawnPosition : 1 team has no Respawn Position` 13 s later. **All seven** of the map's packs were
`0x98`. The `.i3INS` itself was fine (9 respawns, 5 `TT_RED` + 4 `TT_BLUE`, `A=FFFFFFFF B=4CE77B33`,
every hash resolving). Converting all seven to `0x90` shrinks each by 2 bytes per node with the file
list, contents and cipher flags byte-identical; delivered as
`MapBaru{BS}perbaikan_format_SweetCrackdown{BS}` with `cadangan_pack_asli{BS}`. The source packs came from a
newer client, and I3Pack Editor V3 deliberately preserves that format on save - so **an edited copy of a
`0x98` pack stays `0x98` however many times it is saved**; only a pack created from scratch defaults to
`0x90`. Converter kept at `scratchpad/lvl/turunkan_format.py` (it re-reads the output and compares every
file before reporting success).

**Third recurrence, 2026-09-27: "player jatuh dari dunia" on SweetCrackdown.** Same cause, narrower
scope - the user installed 5 of the 7 fixed packs on 25 Sep but not the two collision ones, then
re-copied the V3 originals as `" (2)"` overrides on 27 Sep. `BC.log` says it outright, and this is the
signature to look for when collision is missing:

    Could not load resource : World/<Map>/<Map>_Col_Hero.I3S
    Could not load resource : World/<Map>/<Map>_Col_Hit.I3S
    i3World::OnLoad2 : Asserted : pInfo != NULL      (once per missing SGI)

Note the map still renders and the RSC still loads - only the packs holding the collision are ignored,
so the symptom is falling through the floor rather than a black screen or a spawn error. The collision
FILES were already V1 (`perlu_v1()` -> 0 PXA4, 0 non-V1 flags), so `ke_v1()` was not needed; it really
was only the pack marker.

**A `<Map>_Col_Hero.I3S` must also carry cipher V1 BitRotate, not V2.** Sweep of all 3,572 packs in the
user's client: **291 SECURE files, every one of them mask 0 (V1 BitRotate)** - every stock
`<Map>_Col_Hero.i3pack` included. The only two exceptions on the machine were the two SweetCrackdown
Col_Hero copies (`V2.2:1E`), which came in with the V3 packs. So when downgrading a pack to V1, also set
`berkas.mask = 0` on every SECURE file; `ubah_format` alone does not touch file ciphers.
Delivered `MapBaru{BS}perbaikan_collision_SweetCrackdown{BS}` (three `" (2)"` packs +
`cadangan_pack_terpasang{BS}`).

### The `.i3INS` object `World` MUST sit at (0, 0, 0) (2026-09-27)

Measured over the map `.i3INS` in the client: **the `World` object is at exactly (0,0,0) in every stock
map** (89 checked, no exception). The `Path` object's position is meaningless (CakeCrackDown's is at
-335.39, 0, 27.81) and the light sits wherever it belongs.

A level rebuilt in **i3LevelDesign** breaks that rule silently: dropping `<Map>.i3WRD` on the viewport
creates the `i3LevelWorld` element **at the cursor**, not at the origin, and the export writes that
position into the `.i3INS`. SweetCrackdown's rebuilt file had `World0` at (3.98, 4.14, 6.87), and
because the respawns were then placed against that shifted world, all nine sat ~4.2 m above the floor
with four of them outside the map footprint entirely - nothing under them at all.

Subtracting the World offset from the respawns lands all nine on the collision floor at Y 1.59..1.98,
which is exactly `CakeCrackDown`'s working respawn band (1.60..1.93) on the same cake mesh, position
for position (Respawn8 -1.27/16.37 vs CakeCrackDown -1.51/16.31). **The fix is right whichever way the
client treats the World transform**: honoured, world and respawns both move to zero and stay
consistent; ignored, the respawns are only now correct. So there is nothing to bet on - just put World
at the origin and shift the respawns by the same amount.

How to check any map offline: raycast straight down from each respawn against the Col_Hero triangles
(`i3col.Collision.geometri_dunia`). Start the ray **just above the respawn (+0.3 m), not +2 m** - a
respawn under an arch or platform otherwise reports the overhead surface as its floor (Respawn7 sits
below a 3.82 m platform over a 1.79 m floor). Official respawns sit 0.01-0.2 m above the floor.

**The exported `.RSC` is GENERATED from the level's elements, never copied from the old one.**
`CExportThread::BuildUsedResList` walks `m_pScene->GetElementCount()`, skips anything hidden or
disabled, then calls `pRes->OnQueryDependancy(m_ResList)` per element (which pushes the resource's
`m_RefResList` then itself). So the RSC only ever lists what the level actually contains.
Stock `Crackdown.RSC` measured: **56 entries = 8 map files + 41 from the 26 trigger boxes**
(15 `.i3Evt` + 26 `_Generated/Box*.i3s`) **+ 7 from the 2 glass objects**. A level rebuilt with only
world + path + a few respawns therefore exports 7-13 entries, and that is not a bug.

**A Level Primitive contributes NOTHING to the RSC** - the source says so
(`// Level Primitive Class들은 Resource를 저장할 필요가 없다.`) and it was verified live: dropping a Box,
exporting, and reading the result gives `Box0` in the `.i3INS` (`A=FFFFFFFF B=AA49F4C5`) while the RSC
gains no entry and **no `_Generated/Box0.i3s` file is written**. Only a box marked **Trigger**
(checkbox `IDC` 1061 in its property page) contributes, and only its **event** resource (`.i3Evt`).
So recreating the sector boxes in the tool can restore the `.i3Evt` entries but never the 26
`_Generated/Box*.i3s` ones.

Worth knowing before worrying about those: of stock Crackdown's 56 RSC entries only **21 resolve to a
file that exists anywhere in the client** - the 8 map files and 13 `_Generated/Box*.i3s`. **None of its
15 `.i3Evt` are shipped at all** (`Crackdown_Scene.i3pack` holds 15 files: `.i3INS`, `.RSC`, 13
`Box*.i3s`), so a missing `.i3Evt` entry is normal here. The practical route for adding respawns or
objects to an existing map is therefore **I3INS Editor V3 on the original `.i3INS` + `.RSC`**, which
keeps both in step, rather than rebuilding the level from scratch in i3LevelDesign.

**Read the right client.** The user runs `D:{BS}Data C{BS}BlacklistPB`, not `C:{BS}Users{BS}HYPERION{BS}Documents{BS}BlacklistPB V1 Remake`
(which CLAUDE.md named). Both exist with their own `Pack{BS}` and `BC.log`; several rounds were wasted analysing
the wrong one. Check `BC.log` timestamps across both before reading either.


### A rebuilt level loses the map's LIGHT, and nothing complains (2026-09-27)

User: "di map lain aman, cuma di map SweetCrackdown aja bermasalah" - the melee weapon
`Leviathan_Axe` renders as gloves with no model. Ruled out by measurement first, all of it
worth reusing as a checklist: the weapon pack is V1 with 9 intact files; `Leviathan_Axe.i3s`
**loads in i3Viewer2 with an empty log**; the map's 32 textures are all embedded with 0 missing
external references; the map is not heavy (21.2 MB of texture, 10th of 86; 32 MB of packs
against WestStation 59 and DeadTown 104); and its `Stage.Pef` key is identical to Crackdown's.

What IS wrong, and it is unique to this map:

    SweetCrackdown.RSC   :  7 entries   <- no .i3Light entry
    Crackdown.RSC        : 66 entries   <- "type 9  Light/Crackdown_Light0.i3Light"
    SweetCrackdown.i3INS : 11 objects   <- World, Path, 9 respawns. No Element.

**Of the 86 maps in the client, 84 have a light object in their `.i3INS`.** The only two that
do not are SweetCrackdown and DeadTown - both converted maps. The `.i3Light` file itself is
present and valid in `<Map>_SubData.i3Pack` (507 bytes, `i3LightAttr` + `i3LightObject`, same
shape as Crackdown's); it is simply never declared in the RSC and never instantiated.

Direct consequence of the rule already recorded above - **the exported `.RSC` is GENERATED from
the level's elements** - so a level rebuilt in i3LevelDesign from just `.i3WRD` + `Path` +
respawns exports no light. The map mesh still looks right because it is lightmapped; what loses
its light is the character and the weapon in hand. **Nothing in `BC.log` reports this.**

Fix (`MapBaru{BS}perbaikan_lampu_SweetCrackdown{BS}`, a `" (2)"` Scene pack): add the type-9 RSC entry
right after the `.i3WRD` (Crackdown's own order) and append an `Element` object whose 92-byte body
is **copied verbatim from Crackdown's** (position -10.86 / 27.02 / -9.99, rotation, scale, class
code `D966C30D`), rewriting only `nHashCodeResPath`/`HashCode[3]` with `md5_jalur` of the new
light path. Crackdown is the right template because its play area is the same +-18 m, so a light
27 m up lands in the same relative spot. World, Path and all 9 respawns stay byte-identical.

Two API traps met while building it: `i3ins.impor()` **refuses lights** ("kotak, lampu, World,
Path, dan respawn terikat file map asalnya"), so the object is constructed directly -
`Objek(badan, ekstra, 'Element', sisa)` with `sisa` = name[64] + u32 layer + u32 extra size +
36 zeros - and appended; and `i3ins.peta_hash_rsc()` expects `i3ins.EntriRSC` (`.path1`), not
`i3rsc.Entri` (`.s1`/`.jalur`), so build the hash map by hand when the RSC came from `i3rsc`.

**IN-GAME CONFIRMED 2026-09-27** ("Ternyata benar lampunya"): adding the light back makes the melee
model render again. So on this client a map with NO light instance does not merely look flat - a
first-person weapon model can fail to draw entirely. The original note below was written before that
test and is kept for the reasoning.

**Was not proven at the time**: that the missing light is what hides the weapon model. It is the only
map-specific defect found, and it is worth fixing either way. The cheap decisive test handed to
the user is equipping a STOCK melee (Mini_Axe 161 KB / AXE_Berserker 1.4 MB, textures 256-512 px)
on the same map - `Leviathan_Axe` is 7.4 MB with 208,320 vertices and a 2048x2048 diffuse.

**`BC.log` is overwritten on every client launch**, so a log is only readable if the user exits
and reports before relaunching - the gameplay log for this session was already gone, replaced by
a later lobby session. Ask for that timing explicitly when a log is needed.

Reading a Bandicam recording is a practical way to diagnose these: `ffmpeg` is installed at
`C:{BS}ffmpeg-9.0.1{BS}bin`. `-vf "fps=1,scale=470:-1,tile=4x4"` gives a one-image contact sheet -
but **judge colour and texture only at full resolution**: in the downscaled sheet the map's Oreo
stacks looked like untextured grey slabs, and at 1:1 they are perfectly textured.

### A weapon re-saved by an i3Engine tool loses its glow (2026-09-27)

User: "ada pisau Apex Mercury ... Effect glow nya hilang, itu di semua map, sedangkan Mercury Mars
muncul glow nya". Pack `Weapon_ApexK_Saber.i3pack`.

Found by diffing against the **official V1.15.42 release** the user already has on disk -
`D:{BS}Data C{BS}Downloads{BS}Point Blank Dev{BS}Update v1.15.42{BS}Pack{BS}` (also `Change Logs{BS}V1.15.42{BS}`, and the
V3 original in `Pack 3.88{BS}Weapon_Mercury_Saber.i3Pack`, which needs cipher key 2:1:50 to open).
**Check there first whenever a stock weapon or map file misbehaves** - it is a clean reference copy.

Of the pack's 10 files, **only the model differs**: 376,728 B / 127 objects installed against
376,427 B / 122 objects official; the 7 textures, the `.i3CHR` and the `.i3AnimPack` are byte-identical.
The emissive texture is healthy too - `Mercury_Saber_Emessive.i3i` has the same content as Mars's
`Mars_Saber_Effect_Emessive.i3i` (32x128, mean RGB 141/24/17; only the format byte differs, 0x80 vs 0x81).

The five extra objects are all duplicated state attributes - `i3TextureEnableAttr` 5 vs 3,
`i3ReflectMaskMapEnableAttr` 5 vs 3, `i3MaterialAttr` 7 vs 6 - and the attribute order inside the
AttrSets shifted. At LOD0, the one a first-person weapon uses:

    official   [parent] AlphaTest=1 Blend=1 AlphaFunc BlendMode Material(emissive 0.00)
               [blade ] EmissiveMapEnable=1  TextureBind  EmissiveMapBind
    installed  [parent] Material(emissive 0.40) AlphaFunc AlphaTest=1 Blend=1 BlendMode EmissiveMapEnable=1
               [blade ] TextureBind  EmissiveMapBind  Material(emissive 0.40)

i.e. the blade AttrSet lost its own `EmissiveMapEnable` (pushed up to the parent) and gained a
material. "Enable attrs multiply, order shifts, object count grows" is the **signature of a file
re-saved by an i3Engine tool / PB SDK** - the same shape as the Dasom_Red case. Delivered
`MapBaru{BS}perbaikan_glow_ApexK_Saber{BS}` (the official pack as a `" (2)"` override).

Comparison material worth keeping: `Weapon_Mars_Saber.i3Pack` still names its trail AttrSet
`Mercury_Saber_Trail_LOD0_Material`, so Mars is a derivative of Mercury - the same model, which is
why it is the right A/B partner. Its body also binds `Mars_Saber_Emissive.i3i`, a file that exists in
**no** pack, and it glows anyway - so a missing emissive bind on the body is not what drives the glow;
the blade AttrSet is.

Parser notes for this kind of dig (all met while writing the dumps):
- an `i3AttrSet`'s attribute list is `ATS1` **after** the name AND the INF2 block - locate it with
  `data.find(b'ATS1')`, never at a fixed offset; count at `+4`, ids from `+16`.
- a weapon/character scene's root is the `i3Body`, not a node: follow `SKN2+48` count / `SKN2+52` ids
  to the `i3LOD`s, then `BLD1+16` to each shape node. Walking only INF2 kids prints nothing at all.
- the 68-byte `i3MaterialAttr` as 17 floats is `ambient[4] diffuse[4] **emissive[4]** specular[4] shininess`,
  so the emissive colour is at **byte offset 32**.
- `sys.stdout.reconfigure(errors='replace')` before dumping node names: these files carry cp1252-hostile
  bytes in unnamed nodes and the dump dies on the first one otherwise.

Reading a Bandicam clip to locate the moment: the HUD weapon name sits at roughly x 1500-1580,
y 828-842 in a 1608x932 capture - crop that, not the middle of the screen.

### A part that must glow needs MATERIAL emissive, not an emissive map (2026-09-27, bisected in game)

**CORRECTION, same evening - the heading above is the corrected one; the paragraphs below record
how it was reached, including a wrong turn.** The blade was never missing: in the user's last
screenshot it IS drawn, as a dark brown bar. What is missing is its LIGHT. The real cause is the
**material emissive colour**:

    Mercury hilt material   emissive 1.35 1.35 1.35   -> bright
    Mercury blade material  emissive 0.00 0.00 0.00   -> dark
    every Mars material     emissive 0.40 0.40 0.40   -> glows

Mercury's blade relies on the emissive MAP (`Mercury_Saber_Emessive.i3i`) to light itself. **This
client does not apply the emissive map**; it uses the material's emissive colour. Mars glows
because all its materials carry 0.40 and it does not depend on the map at all.

The bisection that proved it was already in hand and I read it wrongly: drawing the blade through
the HILT's AttrSet made it bright, which means the hilt's MATERIAL has something the blade's does
not - not that blending was broken. Fix shipped as `MapBaru{BS}perbaikan_emissive_ApexK_Saber{BS}`:
raise the three blade materials (one per LOD) from 0.00 to 1.35. **Nine floats in the whole file** -
blend, alpha test, textures, bones and geometry untouched, file size unchanged, 3 of 122 objects
changed. In i3Viewer2 the blade glows orange-white with blending intact.

**Rule for any weapon whose glow is missing on this client: check the material's emissive colour
first.** 0.00 with an emissive map bound is the broken shape; give it 0.40 (Mars's value) to 1.35.
Note `struct.pack_into('<3f', ...)` of 1.35 reads back as 1.3500000238, so compare float32 with a
tolerance - an exact `==` check reports a false failure.

User: "pisau Apex Mercury, effect glow nya hilang, di semua map; Mercury Mars muncul glow nya."
Four in-game rounds to pin down, and **three of my diagnoses were wrong** - the elimination is
the valuable part:

| tried | result |
|---|---|
| installed model differed from the official V1.15.42 release (127 vs 122 objects) - restored it | still missing |
| copied the parent's blend attrs onto the blade's own AttrSet (Mars's shape) | still missing |
| blade mesh is skinned to `AniDummy_Blade`, whose scale `Change.i3a` animates 0 -> 1; rebound it to `AniDummy` (the hilt's bone) | still missing |
| **drew the blade geometry through the HILT's AttrSet** | **blade APPEARS, solid** |

That last one is the bisection that settled it: geometry, vertex array, index array and bone are
all healthy. (I first read it as "the client will not draw the blended mesh" - **wrong**, see the
correction above.) The hilt (no blend) draws; the
blade and the trail (both under an AttrSet carrying `i3BlendEnableAttr` + `i3AlphaTestEnableAttr`)
do not. Mars Saber glows in the same client because **every one of its meshes is rigid and its
blade AttrSet is reached differently** - so a working comparison weapon does not prove the feature
works in general.

Everything else was eliminated by measurement first, and this is the checklist worth reusing:
no other pack shadows the files (3,564 scanned); the `.I3CHR` points at the right `.i3s`;
`Weapon/Weapon.RSC` has the entry; **`BC.log` from the very run shows no warning at all**;
blend mode and alpha func are byte-identical to Mars (SRCALPHA -> INVSRCALPHA, ADD; ref 0 GREATER);
emissive enable + bind present on all three LODs; the GEO2 bboxes are right (blade z 0..0.70);
all seven textures resolve and `Mercury_Saber_Emessive.i3i` has the same content as Mars's;
and **i3Viewer2 renders the glowing blade correctly from the same file** - so the viewer is not a
proxy for the client on transparency.

Superseded attempt, kept because it is a working technique: `MapBaru{BS}bilah_opaque_ApexK_Saber{BS}` moves the blade and trail AttrSets **out** of
the blended parent and attach them to each LOD's top AttrSet, so they keep their own
`TextureBind` + `EmissiveMapBind` but lose AlphaTest/Blend. Only INF2 kid lists change - no object
created or deleted, 116 of 122 objects byte-identical. In i3Viewer2 the blade comes out bright
orange with a halo. Cost: the trail is opaque too and always visible.

It does not need a "DirectX DLL patch" either way - the model just has to light itself through the
material.

Tools note: `pb.build_inf2(inf, kids)` + `pb.parse_inf2` are all that is needed to reparent a node -
rewrite the object as `name + build_inf2(...) + data[q:]` and re-lay out the file (header, strings
unchanged; object table offsets/sizes recomputed; keep each object's untabled tail by slicing to the
NEXT object's offset, or `i3SoundNode`-style trailing chunks are lost).

### Per-tool exe icons (2026-09-24)

The user moved from one shared `Icon\IconExe.ico` to **one `.ico` per tool**, named after the tool:
`I3WRD.ico`, `I3INS.ico`, `I3Collision.ico`, `I3Game.ico` (plus the older `Scene.ico` for I3Scene Convert v3).
Each `.pyw`'s icon lookup now tries its own name first and falls back to `IconExe.ico`, so a tool whose icon
has not been drawn yet still gets one - and dropping a new `<Tool>.ico` into `Icon\` is enough for the window
icon, while the exe's own icon needs a rebuild because it is baked into the binary.

`I3INS Editor V3.pyw` had no window icon at all; it gained `jalur_ikon()` plus a **deferred** `_pasang_ikon()`
(`after(300, ...)`, re-scheduled until `self.gl.ctx` exists) because it has an OpenGL tab - `iconbitmap` before
the GL context hangs `update_idletasks()` inside `i3gl._buat_konteks`, the same trap as the collision editor.

Rebuilt 2026-09-24 with PyInstaller 6.22.2 (old exes in `_backup_sebelum_ikon_baru\`). **In Git Bash write the
`--icon` / `--add-data` paths with FORWARD slashes**: `"$H\\Icon\\$ico.ico"` silently loses the variable
(bash reads `\$` as a literal `$`) and PyInstaller then dies with `Icon input file ...Icon$ico.ico not found`.

Verification that avoids the Windows resource API entirely (`EnumResourceNamesW` callbacks kept raising
`OverflowError: int too long to convert` on the module handle): parse the `.ico` directory yourself and check
that **each image's raw bytes appear verbatim inside the exe**. All four pass, and the old `I3WRD` exe does not
contain `I3WRD.ico`'s bytes - a clean before/after. Windows were also opened and closed from a folder holding
no `.py` file at all.

## i3LevelDesign.exe tested for real -- it DOES open a shipped map (2026-09-25)

User: "menguji alat I3LevelDesign.exe ... coba di uji dengan file yang ada didalam folder
`Uji I3LevelDesign`" (an exported SweetCrackdown: `World\SweetCrackdown\` + `Scene\SweetCrackdown\`
side by side, i.e. a proper Media root). The 2026-09-13 note above ("the tool is too old for their
client") is **wrong and is superseded**: the map loads, renders and exports. What was missing was the
setup, not the tool.

**Read the source, it is in the SDK zip**: `Tools/i3LevelDesign/` (201 files) and `i3TDK/i3Level/`
(257) inside `Full Source I3Engine Tool 2007.zip`, and it matches this exe (same `pbblow/replica`
debug paths, and every behaviour below was predicted from it and then confirmed live).

### How it really works

- **The project file is a LEVEL, not the exported map.** `Ci3LevelDesignDoc::LoadLevel` takes an XML
  (`i3XMLFile` whose key object is an `i3LevelScene`) or an I3R2 holding an `i3LevelScene`. There is
  **no importer for `.i3INS`/`.RSC`** - `AddRes` only knows I3CHR, I3OBJ, I3WRD, I3S, I3A, I3I, TGA,
  WAV, i3Light, i3Evt, i3Path. So "Load Level" on anything in a shipped map folder cannot work.
- **`MediaPath.ini` is dead** (the string is in no binary). Folders come from
  `HKCU\Software\Zepetto\i3LevelDesign\OPTION`: `ResPath` (resource root, all paths are relative to
  it) and `WorkDir` (**the export destination** - `CDlgExport::OnOK` does
  `setDestPath(m_szWorkingDir)`). Set them in `Tools > Options`, never point WorkDir at the folder
  holding the original map or Export overwrites it.
- **"Add Resource" and "ReScan Resource" are dead code in this build.** `_AddNewResource()` is
  commented out entirely and `_RescanResourceList()` has its `Scan(szPath)` call commented out
  (it only calls `CreateCommonResource()`). `CMainFrame::OnShowWindow`'s auto-load of
  `RES.i3RESDB` is commented out too, and `i3Level::LoadDB` is never called. Confirmed live: the
  menu item runs and nothing happens. (That is also why posting those command ids "did nothing" in
  2026-09-13 - the popup uses `TPM_RETURNCMD`, so its commands never travel as WM_COMMAND either.)
- **The only way in is Explorer drag & drop.** `CMainFrame::OnDropFiles` -> `DropRes` -> `AddRes` +
  `DropObject` at the cursor. A synthesised cross-process `WM_DROPFILES` does NOT work (the HDROP is
  a global handle of the sending process); a **real** SendInput drag does. Click the file once to
  select it first, then drag - a drag that starts with the Explorer window unfocused grabs nothing.
- Ribbon/menu commands DO travel as WM_COMMAND, so `PostMessage(frame, WM_COMMAND, id, 0)` works:
  `1075` Export, `57601` File Open, `57604` Save As.

### What the test proved (all on a scratchpad copy; the user's folder was never touched)

1. Dropping `SweetCrackdown.i3WRD` on the viewport loads the **whole map, fully textured** (wafers,
   gift box, cookies) and places a `i3LevelWorld` element. `Path.i3Path` drops in the same way.
2. Save Level -> the file holds 5 external `i3SceneGraphInfo` + `i3WorldSectionTable` +
   `i3MapSectorTable` + `i3World` + the elements + `i3LevelScene`, i.e. **the `.i3WRD` content,
   sector and section tables included, is embedded in the project**.
3. Export -> "Complete...", writing `WorkDir/Scene/<SceneName>/<SceneName>.i3INS` (**GINS v4**, with
   the layer table) + `.RSC`. The scene name comes from the **level file name** (`SaveLevel` does
   `SetName(filetitle)`), so save the level as `<Map>` or the export lands in the wrong folder.
4. **The exported hashes are exactly what `i3ins.md5_jalur` predicts** -
   `MD5("WORLD/SWEETCRACKDOWN/SWEETCRACKDOWN.I3WRD")[0:4]` = `8A092B19` = the World object's
   `nHashCodeResPath`, same for `Path.i3Path`. Independent confirmation of the ROOT CAUSE section.
5. **What is lost**: the original `.i3INS` has 42 objects / 35 RSC entries (12 respawns, the trigger
   boxes with their `.i3Evt`, glass, light); a rebuilt level exports only what you put in it
   (2 objects / 7 entries here). The tool cannot read the old `.i3INS` back, so respawns, triggers,
   glass and lights have to be placed again by hand.

### Two traps that cost real time

- **Save Level as `.i3s` produces a file the tool cannot reopen.** The file dialog appends the
  document template's `.i3s`, and the binary branch of `SaveLevel` only does `file.SetObjects(...)` -
  it never sets the key object, so the header's key-object id stays 0 and reopening asserts
  `i3ResourceFile::FindObjectByID : ((idx) >= 0) && ((idx) < m_ObjList.size())` and then crashes.
  **Type the extension `.XML` (or `.i3LevelDesign`, which `OnSaveDocument` converts to XML).** The
  XML branch writes `KeyObject=`, and reopening it works - proven: title becomes
  `SweetCrackdown.XML - i3s` and the map renders again. The XML is readable text
  (`<Object8 Class="i3LevelWorld" Res="World/SweetCrackdown/SweetCrackdown.i3WRD" ...>`).
- **`PointBlank_ForLevelTool.i3Exec` could never load**, and that is what the Korean startup box
  says ("...i3Engine으로 컴파일되지 않아 사용이 불가합니다. **툴재빌드를 위해**..." = the
  `hModule == NULL` branch, i.e. LoadLibrary failed, NOT the version check - the version matches,
  both sides are `0x82030001`). `CLevelDesignProfile::Apply` looks for `*.BIN`/`*.i3Exec` **in the
  ResPath root only** (`LookForFiles(..., Type = 0)`, no subdirectories), so a copy of the i3Exec
  must sit there. Then LoadLibrary still failed with 126/127 because the module statically imports
  `twitchsdk_32_Debug.dll`, `S2MO_32bit.dll` and `BugTrap.dll` (plus `libmp3lame-ttv`,
  `swresample-ttv-0`, `avutil-ttv-51` behind the Twitch one) which ship with the game client, not
  with the tool - **and the decisive one is that it imports `?S2MOReadPublicKey@@YAHPADAAH@Z`, which
  only the `Client Point Blank v3.16` build of `S2MO_32bit.dll` exports** (the v388 Russia and
  PB Deluxe copies do not). With those six DLLs in `I3Tool\` the module loads: the startup box is
  replaced by a harmless `HitMapDBConnect 실패` (a Zepetto-internal SQL data link, `HItmap.udl`,
  from `CHitMapManager::Init`) and the Export dialog's **Stage Type list gains `CStageBattle`,
  `CStageExit`, `UIFramework`, `UILogin`** - proof the PB metas registered. The saved XML then names
  the world's game instance `CGameWorld` instead of `i3World` (the exported `nHashCodeInstClass`
  is `5EAB4A90` either way, so for the world it changes nothing).
  **`Stage Type` in the Export dialog affects nothing that is exported.** Its only use is
  `DlgExport.cpp:197`, building the "Launch Game" command line
  `sprintf(szCmd, "%s %s %s(%s)", szApp, szBinName, g_pScene->GetName(), m_szStageType)`; the value is
  remembered in the registry as `StageType`. The list is `i3Stage` plus everything derived from it, so
  it is another tell that the PB module registered. Note "Launch Game" can never work here anyway -
  `szApp` is hardcoded to `D:\i3bin\i3Viewer.exe`, a Zepetto-internal path. The stage class that
  actually matters for a map is the one in `BC.i3Game` (`CStageBattle` for all 102 battle maps).

### Adding respawns in i3LevelDesign (2026-09-25, tested)

`Respawn` is a **built-in Level Primitive** (`i3LevelResDatabase` registers Box / Sphere / Capsule /
Respawn under the "Level Primitive" root, path `Level_Primitive_Respawn`). Expand that node in the
Resouces panel and drag `Respawn` into the viewport - it lands on the map surface under the cursor
and is created already selected, with the move gizmo on it.

What the Properties panel then shows is exactly what ends up in the `.i3INS`:

| panel field | exported field | value seen |
|---|---|---|
| Name | `m_szName` | `Respawn0`, `Respawn1` - same names the stock maps use |
| Resource | `nHashCodeResPath` | `0xFFFFFFFF` (no resource), as `i3LevelRespawn::OnSetInstanceInfo` writes |
| Instance Class | `nHashCodeInstClass` | `i3RespawnObj` -> `0x4CE77B33`, **identical to the stock respawns** |
| "Specific..." combo | `nParam1` (body +60) | `TT_RED`(0) `TT_BLUE`(1) `TTN_RED`(2) `TTN_BLUE`(3) `TTN_NEUTRAL`(4) |

That maps straight onto the client's own legend `1:Red 2:Blue 3:R_NPC 4:B_NPC` (the message is
1-based, the field is 0-based), and matches the stock 0/1 split.

Two things worth knowing:

- **The team combo only exists because the PB module loads.** The TDK's own respawn property page
  (`CProp_LvElm_Prim_Respawn`, `IDC_CB_TEAM`) has **no items at all** - the two `AddString("Red Team")`
  / `("Blue Team")` calls are commented out and the `.rc` declares an empty `CBS_DROPDOWN` - so
  `OnCbnSelchangeCbTeam` (which reads `GetCurSel()`) can never fire. The working TT_RED/TT_BLUE combo
  is the PB-specific page served by `g_pInterface->OnQueryPropertyDlg`, i.e. it is there only with the
  six client DLLs in place (see above).
- **The combo applies to EVERY selected respawn**, not just the last one (`OnCbnSelchangeCbTeam`
  loops over `GetSelectedElements`). Select exactly one before changing the team, or all of them flip.
  The safe alternative: the level XML stores it per object -
  `<Object9 Class="i3LevelRespawn" Name="Respawn0" ... RespawnStyle="0" Transform3="4.99 4.18 5.17 1">` -
  so team and position can be edited there by hand, or afterwards in **I3INS Editor V3** (which already
  edits the +60 field).

Verified end to end: two respawns dropped on SweetCrackdown, exported, and read back with `i3ins` as
`Respawn0` / `Respawn1`, `A=FFFFFFFF B=4CE77B33`, positions on the cake surface, team field written
from the combo.

### Adding a Siege Golem (or any PB game object) in i3LevelDesign (2026-09-25, tested)

Drag `Object/cgame/Siege_Golem/Siege_Golem.i3Obj` onto the viewport (extract
`Object_cgame_Siege_Golem.i3Pack` into the ResPath first, keeping the in-pack paths) and the golem
appears on the map as an `i3LevelObject`, `Object` and `Texture` gain resources, and Export writes
the `.i3INS` entry plus the RSC group.

**The one step that matters: set `Instance Class`.** `i3LevelObject` defaults to `i3Object`, and
`i3LevelElement3D::OnSetInstanceInfo` writes `nHashCodeInstClass = CRC32(0xFFFFFFFF, m_szInstanceClass)`,
so a golem left on the default exports as `B713F4D9` - a generic object the client will not treat as a
golem. Select it, open the **Instance Class** combo in Properties, pick `CGameObjectSiegeGolem`, and
the exported code becomes **`52C6CD57`** - exactly the value Giran2's own golem carries. Verified by
exporting twice and reading both with `i3ins`.

The combo is the element's game class plus everything derived from it (`get_all_derived_metas`), so it
only has content **when the PB module is loaded** (the six client DLLs, see above). With it, the full
catalogue is offered: `CGameControledObject`, `CGameObjectBattleUseItem`, `CGameObjectEvent`,
`CGameObjectGiftbox`, `CGameObjectHatchling`, `CGameObjectHelicopter`, `CGameObjectJumper`,
`CGameObjectJumpHold`, `CGameObjectMark_OutPost`, `CGameObjectPowerGenerator`,
`CGameObjectRespawnHelicopter`, `CGameObjectRidingHelicopter`, **`CGameObjectSiegeGolem`**,
`CGameObjectStormTubeRepairTrain`, `CGameObjectTextSpeaker`, `CGameObjectWeaponBox`,
**`CGameObjectWildHogCannon`** (= the Range Golem), `CTargetInTutorial`, `GachaObject`,
`GameScreenObject`, `i3Object`, `TargetObject`. The "Specific..." page adds **Object Type**
(`Normal` / `MissionObject` / `BreakdownObject` / `JumperObject` / `LadderObject`) and **Team**
(`Red Team` / `Blue Team` / `All`), saved in the level XML as `ObjType=` / `TeamType=`.

Two notes:

- **The golem's two sounds do not exist in this client.** Its `.i3Obj` names
  `SOUND/OBJECT/EXPLOSION/OB_SIEGEGOLEM_WAIT.WAV` and `..._DEATH.WAV`; a scan of all 3,557 packs in
  `D:\Data C\BlacklistPB\Pack` finds neither. Dropping the object therefore raises two
  `i3FileStream::Open : Failed to CreateFile(...) err code = 3` asserts - press **Continue**, the
  object is still added, and the exported RSC simply omits them (11 entries, no wav). That is the same
  harmless situation as stock Crackdown's 35 missing `Object/billboard/...` references.
- Placing the golem is only the client half. For it to be destructible the **server** still needs its
  entry in `data/battle/maps.xml` with `Life` equal to the `OTP1` float in the `.i3Obj`
  (Siege_Golem 9000, Range_Golem 8000) - see "Objective HP lives in the CLIENT's `.i3Obj`" above.

Proven end to end on SweetCrackdown: golem dropped, class set, exported, and read back as
`Siege_Golem0  A=2D2C5B11 B=52C6CD57`, with the RSC listing `Siege_Golem.i3Obj` (type 8),
`SIEGE_GOLEM_SETTING.I3S` (type 7) and the `.i3i` textures (type 2).

Scripts from this session's scratchpad (`lvl/`): `potret.py` (PrintWindow one window), `klik.py` /

## Working on this machine

- Check outputs in the viewer with `I3ToolsViewer\i3Viewer2.exe "<file>"`. Capture only that window (PrintWindow on
  its HWND), never the full screen: the user has private apps open. Leave viewer windows the user opened alone.
- A successful load shows a window titled `<file> - i3Viewer2`; a reject shows an `i3Engine Event Log` dialog (or the
  process is simply gone). The dialog's Where/Message text is in Edit controls that need `WM_GETTEXT` (cross-process
  `GetWindowText` returns ""). Better still: **delete `I3ToolsViewer\i3Viewer2.log` first** - the viewer only creates
  it when it does not exist, and the fresh log names the object it choked on. Crashes also land in
  `Get-WinEvent Application`.
- `D:\Data C\Downloads\Point Blank Dev\Chara` holds the user's other converted characters: read-only unless asked.
- Driving a running Tk exe without touching the real mouse (2026-09-14): Tk takes mouse buttons from `GetKeyState`, so a
  posted WM_LBUTTONDOWN alone does nothing. Attach to the Tk thread (`AttachThreadInput`), set VK_LBUTTON / VK_RBUTTON /
  VK_SHIFT with `SetKeyboardState`, and send WM_MOUSEMOVE (twice, ~50 ms apart, so a ttk.Button is "active" before the
  press - with one move the I3Scene "Pilih..." button ignored the click) + button messages to the widget's `TkChild` HWND with
  `SendMessageTimeout`, a whole press-drag-release within ~200 ms (Tk's 250 ms pointer timer re-reads the real cursor).
  Every Tk widget is a `TkChild` window, so find widgets structurally with `GetParent` (the OpenGL frame is the largest
  visible leaf; `GetPixelFormat` across processes returns 0). Tk file dialogs: WM_SETTEXT on the Edit inside control
  1148, then WM_COMMAND IDOK; message boxes: WM_COMMAND IDYES/IDNO. Never answer a save prompt with Yes on user data.

## Membuat map dari nol -- `i3map.py` + "Map DinoRuins" (2026-10-01)

User: "Apakah anda bisa buat satu map untuk saya ??" Hasilnya `HeavyRain\Map DinoRuins\`
(6 pack / 31 berkas, kerangka Crackdown + 17 bangunan baru dari OBJ + tabrakannya).
`i3map.py` adalah pustakanya: `Peta.baru/bungkus/periksa/cari/semua_berkas`, `nama_bebas()`,
`tabel_stage_exe()`.

### Aturan nama map ternyata DUA syarat, bukan satu -- dan syarat kedua itu yang bikin crash

Penyerahan pertama memakai nama **Cemetery** dan client langsung mati waktu masuk ready room:

    CPhaseReadyRoom::OnEntranceStart  event:145
    STAGEID_INFO_LIST::GetStageName(int) : Asserted : 0 && "Stage Id 가 존재 하지 안습니다."
    [ CRASH_TRACE ] Crash Occured

Perhatikan **crash-nya bukan saat memuat map** - `GetStageName` dipanggil jauh sebelum itu,
waktu client menyusun layar ready room dari id stage. Jadi assert ini tidak ada hubungannya
dengan isi pack sama sekali; sudah benar semua pack-nya dan tetap mati.

Aturan yang lengkap:

    syarat 1  nama ada di KEEMPAT berkas .i3Game
              (BC.i3Game + BCNewUI.i3Game, masing-masing di Script.i3pack dan
               Blacklist_Script_Config.i3pack)
    syarat 2  nama ada di TABEL STAGE DI DALAM PointBlank.exe
              (D:\Data C\BlacklistPB\PBStage - daftar stage di exe.txt, 106 entri)

Catatan lama di berkas ini cuma menyebut syarat 1 secara eksplisit; syarat 2 tersirat di
kalimat "the exe's own stage table knows it" tapi tidak pernah diperiksa oleh kode.
`i3map.nama_bebas()` sekarang menuntut keduanya (plus "belum punya pack"), lewat
`tabel_stage_exe()` yang mengurai berkas dump itu dengan

    re.match(r'\s*[0-9A-Fa-f]{8}\s+([A-Z]{2}_[A-Z0-9_]+)\s+(\S+)\s*$', baris)

**Hasil setelah dikoreksi: di client user hanya tersisa DUA nama yang boleh dipakai** -
`DinoRuins` (ES_DINORUINS) dan `Holiday2` (EH_HOLIDAY). Sembilan nama yang tadinya lolos
cek-satu-syarat (C_Point, Downtown_Show, Downtown_Test03, Giran, Lasvegas,
Library_Test01/02/03, MerryWhiteVillage) semuanya akan crash persis seperti Cemetery -
mereka ada di `.i3Game` tapi tidak ada di exe.

### Indeks `modes.xml` = UID stage di exe

Temuan baru, dan ini yang membuat nama bisa dipilih dengan yakin. `data/maps/modes.xml`
posisional (125 entri `<map>`, indeks 0..124) dan indeks itu **sama dengan UID stage di exe**.
Tiga bukti silang dari komentar di berkas itu sendiri:

    entri 103  "[NoStageName] Dinoruins"   <->  ES_DINORUINS  UID 103
    entri 108  "CakeCrackdown"             <->  BB_BIOLAB     UID 108
    entri 118  "[NoStageName]Junkyard"     <->  TD_JUNKYARD   UID 118

Jadi untuk map baru: cari UID-nya di tabel exe, itulah nomor baris di `modes.xml`.
`MapsXML.parse` mengemas yang `enable="true"` jadi 4 mask 32-bit (`maps1..maps4`) yang
dikirim di `BASE_USER_INFO_PAK` (pbserver_auth), jadi **`enable="false"` = map tidak pernah
muncul di layar buat-room**; mask 4x32 itu juga yang membatasi id ke 0..127. `mode="..."`
adalah mask mode tambahan per map (6573 = AI+Sniper+Eliminate+Headhunter+Shotgun+AIStronger+Chaos,
4524 dipakai kebanyakan Death Match, 132 Bomb Mission, 0 = tanpa mode tambahan). Label
seksi di berkas itu ("Dino Mode", "Bomb Mission Mode", ...) cuma komentar - entri 108
CakeCrackdown ada di seksi Bomb Mission tapi `mode="6573"` dan dipakai normal.
`modes.xml` hanya dibaca sekali waktu start (`MapsXML.Load()`), jadi mengubahnya perlu
restart server - dan menyalakan/mematikan server itu keputusan user.

Untuk DinoRuins: baris 153, entri 103, sekarang `enable="false" mode="0"`; perlu jadi
`enable="true" mode="6573"` (atau 4524) supaya muncul di daftar map.

### Yang masih belum pasti soal DinoRuins

Tag-nya `ES_`, keluarga Dino/Escape (cuma 4 map: DinoRuins, D_BreakDown, D_Uptown,
BreedingNest). Teori "keluarga slot menentukan kegagalan" sudah terbantah untuk crash
(lihat SLOT-SWAP RESULT di atas), tapi **belum diuji** apakah client mau menampilkan map
ber-tag ES_ di daftar map untuk room Team Death biasa. Kalau ternyata tidak, pindah ke
Holiday2 - dan UID Holiday2 belum ketemu, jadi barisnya di `modes.xml` harus dicari dulu.

Peringatan yang ikut diserahkan ke user: **jangan buat room mode Boss/Dino di map ini**.
Bukan karena map-nya, tapi karena karakter Dino di client ini memang tidak lengkap
(22 `.I3CHR` didaftarkan di `Chara/Character.RSC`, nol ada di disk) - lihat bagian
"Boss / Dino mode crashes the client" di atas.

+ 17 bangunan dari OBJ (1 Tugu marmer, 6 Nisan, 6 Tembok, 4 Peti), simetris terhadap Z=0.
Sembilan di antaranya digeser otomatis waktu dibangun supaya tidak menimpa respawn atau
titik jalur AI. Tiga tekstur (batu/marmer/kayu) dibuat sendiri dan **ditanam sebagai i3Texture
internal**, jadi tidak ada berkas tekstur tambahan. Tabrakan ikut: 17 kotak `MDL_*` di
Col_Hero dan 17 di Col_Hit.

`periksa_dinoruins.py` **membongkar PACK-nya, bukan folder kerja** - yang diperiksa harus
yang benar-benar dikirim. 16 pemeriksaan, semuanya lolos: 31 berkas, Col_Hero SECURE V1
(mask 0), tidak ada node `0x98`, 17 bangunan tegak dengan alas menempel lantai di dalam
+-17 m, ketiga tekstur tertanam, 43 tekstur bawaan utuh, tiap bangunan punya kotak tabrakan
di kedua berkas, tidak ada yang menimpa respawn atau jalur AI. i3Viewer2 membuka
`DinoRuins_World.I3S` dengan judul benar dan **tidak membuat `i3Viewer2.log` sama sekali**.

Jebakan yang ditemui waktu menulis pemeriksanya: translasi aktor PhysX ada di **kolom ke-4**
(`Collision.posisi`, indeks 3/7/11), bukan `pose[12]/[14]` - versi pertama memakai indeks

### Aturan " (2)" JAUH lebih luas dari yang tercatat: berlaku untuk tiap NAMA MAP BAWAAN (2026-10-01)

User, sesudah map DinoRuins memunculkan notice "Game data file rusak" di tengah pertandingan:
**"Intinya nama Map Original itu ketika di ubah isi dalamnya. pasti notice nya muncul itu.
Kecuali di buat (2) dibelakangnya."**

Catatan lama di berkas ini menyebut aturan `" (2)"` hanya untuk **menimpa pack bawaan yang sudah
ada**. Itu terlalu sempit. Yang diawasi adalah **NAMA**-nya: `DinoRuins` dikenal exe (slot
`ES_DINORUINS`, UID 103), jadi sebuah `DinoRuins.i3pack` ikut diperiksa **walaupun client
sebelumnya tidak punya pack bernama itu sama sekali**. Map baru yang memakai nama bawaan - yang
memang satu-satunya rute yang lolos `STAGEID_INFO_LIST::GetStageName` - karena itu HARUS dikirim
sebagai `<Nama> (2).i3pack`.

Keenam pack DinoRuins diganti namanya jadi `DinoRuins (2).i3pack`, `DinoRuins_Col (2).i3pack`,
`DinoRuins_Col_Hero (2).i3pack`, `DinoRuins_Scene (2).i3pack`, `DinoRuins_SubData (2).i3pack`,
`DinoRuins_TabMinimap (2).i3pack` - isinya tidak diubah sama sekali, dan `periksa_dinoruins.py`
tetap 16/16.

#### Yang diawasi = ISI pack map UTAMA (i3WRD, _Sky, _World, Path)

User: "Yang di awasi itu didalam nya yang ada i3wrd, i3s sky dan world atau path". Jadi bukan
seluruh enam pack - yang diperiksa isi `<Map>.i3pack`: `<Map>.i3WRD`, `<Map>_Sky.i3s`,
`<Map>_World.I3S`, `Path.i3Path`.

**Kedua pack `" (2)"` BAWAAN di client membuktikannya**, dan bukti ini kuat karena dibuat Zepetto
sendiri, bukan oleh user:

| pack | isi | yang BEDA dari base |
|---|---|---|
| `BurningHall (2).i3pack` | 5 berkas, jalur identik | `_Sky.i3s` **dan** `_World.i3s` |
| `Octagon (2).i3Pack` | 4 berkas, jalur identik | `_Sky.i3s` saja |

Di kedua pack itu `.i3WRD`, `Path.i3Path` dan `_Ref.dds` identik dengan base-nya. Artinya Zepetto

dan Octagon menunjukkan mengganti sky saja pun sudah perlu rute itu. Catatan lama di berkas ini
hanya menyebut `" (2)"` sebagai "salinan penuh dengan beberapa anggota ditukar"; alasan KENAPA
salinan itu ada baru jelas sekarang.

Kelima pack lain (`_Col`, `_Col_Hero`, `_Scene`, `_SubData`, `_TabMinimap`) tidak punya contoh
`" (2)"` bawaan sama sekali, yang konsisten dengan "tidak diawasi". Untuk DinoRuins kelimanya tetap
diberi `" (2)"` karena nama berkas pack hanya menentukan urutan baca (tidak ada base yang
ditimpa), jadi biayanya nol dan risikonya lebih kecil daripada menebak batas pengawasan.

#### Notice itu TIDAK menuduh map-nya rusak - bacanya harus hati-hati

Percobaan pertama (1 Okt 01:14) terbaca begini di `BC.log`, dan semuanya sehat:

    GotoNextStage( DinoRuins )
    --- RSC : Scene/DinoRuins/DinoRuins.RSC        <- RSC-nya dimuat
    START BATTLE STAGETYPE 1 STAGESLOT 0 STAGEORD 103
    (16 detik tanpa satu baris pun)
    -- Exit From Msg CallBack  File:.\StageBattle.cpp  Line:1889

`Line:1889` = `STR_TBL_INGAME_HUD_NOTICE_GAME_DATA_DAMAGED`, yang di tabel string duduk di
keluarga `STR_TBL_INGAME_HUD_NOTICE_*` (team balance, game end, remove helmet) - **notice HUD
dalam pertandingan, bukan galat memuat berkas**. Jadi "map berhasil dimuat" dan "notice data
rusak" bisa terjadi bersamaan, dan pemuatan yang sukses BUKAN bukti packnya sah.

Semua ini diperiksa lebih dulu dan **bersih**, jadi tidak usah diulang kalau terjadi lagi:

| diperiksa | hasil |
|---|---|
| nama sektor `DinoRuins_0..13` di `Script/String/Turkey/World_Turkey.txt` | ada 14 baris, isinya sama dengan Crackdown |
| kunci `DinoRuins` di `Stage.Pef` | ada - nol baris `CEquipShapeManager::SetMapShape` di log |
| material tabrakan 17 bangunan baru | Col_Hit terrain `(2,-1,0)` = besi, Col_Hero `(0,-1,0)` - dua-duanya nilai bawaan |
| isi pack | 31 berkas, semua format V1, `_Col_Hero` SECURE mask 0 |
| sisi server | `Nama Map: 'ES_DINORUINS'`, `Used spawn count: 2`, nol galat |

#### `maps.xml` yang tidak memuat map itu TIDAK ada hubungannya

`logs/battle` mencatat `[MappingXML] Map 103 tidak ada di data/battle/maps.xml`. Menggoda untuk
dikejar, tapi salah: **map 9 (Crackdown), 108 (CakeCrackdown) dan 118 (SpacePort) juga tidak ada
di maps.xml**, dan ketiganya dimainkan user tiap hari. `Room.cs:183` pun sudah menjaganya
(`Map != null ? Map._objects : null`). Jadi entri maps.xml cuma perlu untuk map yang punya objek
bisa ditembak; untuk Team Deathmatch biasa tidak perlu sama sekali - jangan restart server untuk itu.

#### `PBStage.ini` masih memuat `129=2,Cemetery` - UID di luar jangkauan

Sisa percobaan Cemetery yang gagal. `PBStage.log` bilang "OK" untuk keenam entri, tapi exe-nya
sendiri protes dua kali di awal tiap sesi:

    getStageCodeName(char *,int) : Asserted : (ord > STAGE_ORD_NA) && (ord < STAGE_ORD_MAX)
    setStageName(int,char *)     : Asserted : (ord > STAGE_ORD_NA) && (ord < STAGE_ORD_MAX)

Tepat **satu** dari enam UID yang terdaftar berada di luar jangkauan (37, 68, 77, 108, 118 aman;
129 tidak), dan assert-nya juga tepat dua - jadi pasangannya jelas. Terpisah dari itu,
`InsertStageInfo : Asserted : 0 && "Stage Id sudah terdaftar"` muncul **empat** kali = keempat UID
yang exe-nya sudah punya sendiri (118, 108, 77, 68); 37 dan 129 tidak bertabrakan. Barisnya tinggal
dihapus - ditawarkan ke user, belum dikerjakan.

#### Jebakan diagnosis yang terbukti mahal di ronde ini

Pack bawaan `UI_WeaponShape.i3pack` memang diubah user jam 00:54 malam itu (satu berkas:
`weapon_select20.i3i`, stub 17 byte -> gambar 1.048.636 byte), dan itu sempat jadi tersangka utama
karena cocok dengan catatan lama soal "mengubah pack bawaan". **Tersangka yang salah** - user
menolak menyentuhnya dan menyebutkan aturan nama map di atas, yang ternyata memang penjelasannya.
Dua hal yang ikut ketahuan dan layak dicatat:

- **38-39 berkas `Weapon_Kill*.i3i` yang isinya cuma 17 byte ASCII `Modified by VIDEL` itu BAWAAN
  rilis resmi 1.15.42**, bukan kerusakan di client user - rilis resminya punya kerusakan yang sama
  persis. Jadi baris `Could not load a header of Gui/WeaponShape/Weapon_Kill23.i3i` di log adalah
  derau normal di client ini. Catatan lama yang menyebutnya sebagai pack rusak khas client user
  perlu dibaca dengan itu.
- Membandingkan pack terpasang dengan `Update v1.15.42\Pack\` berkas-per-berkas (md5) langsung
  menunjuk satu berkas dari 82. Itu rute tercepat untuk tahu apa yang pernah disentuh di sebuah
  pack bawaan.

**Belum diuji di game** dengan nama " (2)".

### Kode proteksi pack - kenapa map baru kena "Game data file rusak" (2026-10-01, TERPECAHKAN)

Ini menutup pertanyaan yang sudah berkali-kali salah tebak di berkas ini. **Bukan** soal mengubah
pack bawaan, **bukan** nama map, **bukan** maps.xml, **bukan** keluarga ES_/EH_.

`BC.log` menyebutkannya terang-terangan - dua baris `[W]` yang muncul TEPAT sebelum notice:

    i3ResourceFile.cpp(1440) _CalcFileChecksum        : Pack/DinoRuins.i3Pack 파일을 열 수 없습니다
    i3ResourceFile.cpp(1568) CheckProtectionCode      : Pack/DinoRuins.i3Pack ... Encription Code를
                                                        가져올 수 없습니다
    (5 detik kemudian)  -- Exit From Msg CallBack  File:.\StageBattle.cpp  Line:1889

Jadi untuk stage `<Map>`, client **mewajibkan berkas bernama persis `Pack/<Map>.i3Pack`**, menghitung
checksum-nya, dan membaca sebuah "Encription Code" dari dalamnya. Kodenya = **16 byte di header 0x3C**.

#### Sifat kodenya - diukur, bukan ditebak

| | |
|---|---|
| pack berkode di client user | **3.440 dari ~3.572** |
| `BurningHall.i3pack` 6.976.175 B vs `BurningHall (2).i3pack` 9.793.538 B | isi beda total, **kode SAMA** |
| `DSquad_Scene.i3pack` 110.474 B vs `DSquad_Scene (2).i3pack` 98.995 B | isi beda, **kode SAMA** |
| md5 seluruh berkas / berkas dengan kode dinolkan / header saja / isi sesudah header | **tidak satu pun** menghasilkan kodenya |
| md5 nama berkas (21 varian: huruf besar/kecil, dengan/tanpa `Pack/`, garis miring dua arah) | tidak cocok |
| dua pack tak berhubungan berbagi kode | ada, 44 kelompok |

**Kodenya OPAQUE**: tidak bergantung isi berkas, tidak bergantung nama. Jadi tidak perlu dihitung -
tinggal DISALIN dari pack map bawaan mana pun. Itu juga persis yang dilakukan tooling Zepetto sendiri:
keempat pack `" (2)"` bawaan (`BurningHall`, `DSquad_Scene`, `DSquad_SubData`, `DSquad_TabMinimap`)
membawa kode base-nya.

#### Yang diperiksa CUMA pack map utama - dibuktikan berkas user sendiri

| pack | ditulis ulang user? | kode | notice? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Crackdown.i3pack` 2013, `DeadTown.i3pack` 2012, `SweetCrackdown.i3Pack` Agu | tidak | ada | - |
| `Crackdown_Col`, `_Col_Hero`, `_Scene` (26-27 Sep) | ya | **NOL** | tidak ada |
| `DeadTown_Col_Hero`, `DeadTown_Scene` (27 Sep) | ya | **NOL** | tidak ada |
| `SweetCrackdown_Col/_Col_Hero/_Scene/_SubData/_TabMinimap/_Images_NoText` | ya | **NOL** | tidak ada |
| semua pack `" (2)"` buatan alat | ya | **NOL** | tidak ada |

Jadi: `_Col`, `_Col_Hero`, `_Scene`, `_SubData`, `_TabMinimap`, `_Textures` bebas ditulis ulang -
**tidak usah dibikin `" (2)"`**. Hanya `<Map>.i3pack` yang harus ada dan berkode.

Ini sekaligus menjelaskan kenapa aturan `" (2)"` bekerja: bukan karena nama `" (2)"` ajaib, tapi karena
namanya BUKAN `<Map>.i3pack` sehingga tidak pernah diperiksa - dan base yang asli (berkode) tetap di
tempatnya. Nama pack sendiri tidak menentukan apa pun soal isi: client mencari sumber daya lewat jalur
di DALAM pack, dan nama berkas cuma menentukan urutan baca (spasi 0x20 sebelum titik 0x2E, jadi
`" (2)"` menang).

#### Di `i3pack.py`

`simpan()` dulu menolkan 0x3C ("hash header tidak dipakai game; exe lama juga menolkannya") - itulah
yang membuat pack map utama buatan alat ini SELALU ditolak. Sekarang ada properti
**`I3Pack.kode_proteksi`** (baca/tulis 16 byte itu): pack yang dibaca dari berkas mempertahankan
kodenya sendiri, pack baru mulai nol dan tinggal diisi. Akibatnya **pack map utama bawaan sekarang
boleh ditulis ulang** - kodenya ikut terbawa.

Regresi: `uji_i3pack.py` **49 lolos 0 gagal**, termasuk uji byte-identik lawan exe lama (pack ujinya
dibuat dari nol, jadi kodenya nol dan hasilnya tidak berubah).

#### Dua percobaan gagal yang membentuk kesimpulan ini

1. `DinoRuins.i3pack` buatan alat, kode NOL -> notice muncul 16 detik sesudah battle mulai, **tanpa satu
   pun baris galat di BC.log**. Ini yang bikin salah arah: map-nya terbaca sempurna (`LoadRSC` sukses,
   `START BATTLE ... STAGEORD 103`), server pun bersih.
2. Keenam pack diganti jadi `" (2)"` dan base dihapus -> notice muncul lagi, **tapi kali ini dua baris
   `[W]` di atas ikut tercetak** karena berkasnya benar-benar tidak ada. Justru kegagalan kedua yang
   memunculkan buktinya.

**Pelajarannya**: notice ini TIDAK menuduh isi map, dan pemuatan map yang sukses bukan bukti packnya
sah. Kalau muncul lagi, yang dibaca pertama adalah `_CalcFileChecksum` / `CheckProtectionCode` di
`BC.log` - dua baris itu menyebut nama berkas yang dipermasalahkan.

Terpasang 2026-10-01: `DinoRuins.i3pack` (6.306.201 B, kode `af41a554...` disalin dari
`Crackdown.i3pack`) + lima pack pendukung bernama biasa berkode nol. `periksa_dinoruins.py` 16/16.
**Belum diuji di game.**

#### Kode proteksi di I3Pack Editor V3 (2026-10-01)

User: "itu kamu terapkan kemampuannya di i3pack editor v3 saya?" - awalnya belum, cuma di
`i3pack.py`. Sekarang ada tiga bagian:

- **Otomatis**: `simpan()` mempertahankan kode pack yang dibaca dari berkas (properti
  `I3Pack.kode_proteksi`). Jadi **pack map utama bawaan sekarang boleh ditulis ulang** - sebelumnya
  selalu rusak diam-diam.
- **`Alat > Kode proteksi pack (map baru)...`**: menampilkan kode pack yang terbuka, lalu menawarkan
  menyalin kode dari pack lain (file picker). Sumber berkode nol ditolak dengan pesan yang menyebut
  contoh pack bawaan.
- **`Info pack...`** dapat baris `Kode pack`, dengan keterangan "NOL - hanya jadi masalah kalau ini
  pack map utama".

`uji_i3pack_kode.py`: **16 pemeriksaan** - sisi pustaka (kode bertahan saat tulis ulang, isi berkas
tidak berubah, pack baru mulai nol lalu bisa diisi, dua penolakan ukuran) dan jendelanya digerakkan
in-process (menu ada, kode tersalin, pack ditandai berubah, kode ikut tersimpan, isi tetap utuh,
sumber berkode nol ditolak, Info pack menampilkan barisnya). Regresi `uji_i3pack.py` 49,
`uji_i3pack_gui.py` 142 - lolos.

**Bukti sebelum/sesudah di exe**, lewat `replace-file --save` dari folder tanpa satu pun `.py`:

    exe BARU : sumber 0a28d383... -> hasil 0a28d383...   kode dipertahankan
    exe LAMA : sumber 0a28d383... -> hasil 00000000...   kode dinolkan

Dibangun ulang 2026-10-01: `I3Pack Editor V3.exe` **8.730.146 B** dan `I3Tools V3.exe`
**23.980.784 B** (hub membundel salinan `i3pack` sendiri - kalau tidak ikut, membuka Pack Editor
dari dalam I3Tools masih memakai perilaku lama). Yang lama di `_backup_sebelum_kode_proteksi\`.
Catatan jujur soal cakupan uji: bukti byte-level di atas dijalankan pada exe editor yang berdiri
sendiri; `I3Tools V3.exe` hanya diuji sampai "jalan dan melisting 14 alat" - jalur `--alat pack
<perintah CLI>` ternyata tidak meneruskan ke CLI alatnya, jadi tidak bisa dipakai untuk uji itu.

**Yang TIDAK berubah**: nama map tetap harus lolos dua syarat (ada di keempat `.i3Game` DAN di tabel
stage exe). Sesudah DinoRuins dipakai, di client user tinggal **Holiday2** yang tersisa - jadi
"bebas bikin map baru" masih dibatasi nama, bukan lagi dibatasi pack.

`I3Pack Editor V3.12.pyw` (versi ringkas buatan `buat_v312.py`) BELUM ikut - ia dibangkitkan dari
sumber penuh, jadi regenerasi akan membawa fitur ini, tapi 26 suntingannya perlu dicek dulu terhadap
menu Alat yang bertambah satu baris.

### TERPECAHKAN: kode proteksi = HMAC-MD5 kunci `"Zepetto Inc."`, dan engine sendiri bisa memasangnya (2026-10-01)

Rangkaian tebakan di bagian sebelumnya (kode opaque, kode = checksum isi, dsb.) semuanya
**terlampaui**. Jawabannya dibaca langsung dari binari, bukan dikira-kira.

#### Jalan menemukannya

1. **`BC.log` menyebut fungsinya**: `i3ResourceFile.cpp(1440) _CalcFileChecksum` dan
   `i3ResourceFile.cpp(1568) CheckProtectionCode`. Itu kode ENGINE, jadi ada di
   `i3BaseDx_Cli.dll` - dan DLL itu **tidak terbungkus di client V1 pun**. (Exe-nya terbungkus;
   exe `Client Point Blank v3.16` milik user tidak - itu yang membuka jalan berikutnya.)
2. **Kedua fungsi DIEKSPOR** oleh `i3BaseDx*.dll`:

       ?CheckProtectionCode@i3ResourceFile@@SA_NPBD0H@Z   RVA 0x55970
       ?SetProtectionCode@i3ResourceFile@@SA_NPBD0H@Z     RVA 0x555C0   <- PENULISNYA

   Keduanya `static bool (const char*, const char*, int)` dan memanggil satu inti bersama di
   `0x100551A0`; yang membedakan cuma nomor baris log (1514 Set / 1568 Check).
3. **Nama fungsi internal ikut diekspor** - itu yang memecahkan artinya:

       10023A50 = i3FileStream::i3FileStream()
       10023C40 = i3FileStream::Open(const i3::rc_basic_string<char>&, int, uint)
       1004BE10 = i3MD5::HMAC_Start(md5_context*, char* key, int keyLen)   <<<

   Jadi argumen ke-2 = KUNCI HMAC, ke-3 = panjang kunci.
4. **Kuncinya dibaca dari exe v3.16 yang tidak terbungkus.** `PointBlank.exe` v3.16 mengimpor
   `CheckProtectionCode` dari `i3BaseDx.dll`; menelusuri `FF 15 <slot IAT>` di `.text` ketemu
   **dua** tempat panggil, dan `push` sebelumnya membuka semuanya:

       CheckProtectionCode("Pack/Script.i3Pack", "Zepetto Inc.", 12)   <- anti-tamper Script
       CheckProtectionCode("Pack/%s.i3Pack",     "Zepetto Inc.", 12)   <- tiap map

   **Kunci = `Zepetto Inc.` (12 karakter, cocok dengan `push 0Ch`).**

#### Memakainya: panggil fungsi engine, jangan hitung sendiri

HMAC-MD5 standar atas berbagai daerah byte (seluruh berkas, kode dinolkan, tanpa header, potongan
awal) **tidak** menghasilkan kodenya - `_CalcFileChecksum` jelas membaca berkas dengan caranya
sendiri. Jadi rumusnya tidak diturunkan; yang dipakai **fungsi engine itu sendiri**.

`HeavyRain\Kode Proteksi\KodeProteksi.exe` (C# `/platform:x86`, sumbernya `KodeProteksi.cs`):

    KodeProteksi.exe <folder client> <pack pembanding> [pack yang distempel]

    contoh: KodeProteksi.exe "D:\Data C\BlacklistPB" Pack/NStation.i3pack Pack/DinoRuins.i3pack

Yang WAJIB, dan ini yang bikin percobaan pertama gagal:

- **32-bit.** DLL-nya x86; Python di mesin ini 64-bit jadi tidak bisa memuatnya. Dibangun dengan
  `C:\Windows\Microsoft.NET\Framework\v4.0.30319\csc.exe /platform:x86`.
- **`i3Pack::Init()` harus dipanggil dulu** (`?Init@i3Pack@@YA_NXZ`, juga diekspor). Tanpa itu
  `i3FileStream::Open` gagal dan fungsinya cuma mencetak "파일을 열 수 없습니다" - persis pesan
  yang muncul di game waktu berkasnya memang tidak ada. `i3Pack::Bind()` tidak perlu (mengembalikan
  False dan tidak berpengaruh).
- **`arg2` tidak boleh NULL** - kalau NULL, prosesnya langsung AccessViolation.
- Jalur boleh relatif (`Pack/X.i3pack`), pakai backslash, atau absolut - ketiganya diterima, asal
  direktori kerja = folder client.

Hasilnya, diverifikasi pemeriksa engine sendiri:

    Check("Pack/NStation.i3pack", "Zepetto Inc.", 12)   -> TRUE   (pack bawaan)
    Set  ("Pack/DinoRuins.i3pack", ...)                 -> TRUE   kode 5c649190...
    Check("Pack/DinoRuins.i3pack", ...)                 -> TRUE   (pack buatan alat)

Keenam pack DinoRuins distempel dan lolos Check. **Pack `" (2)"` dan base donor tidak diperlukan
lagi** - `DinoRuins.i3pack` sekarang berisi map yang sebenarnya dan sah.

#### Akibatnya untuk aturan-aturan di berkas ini

- Catatan "pack map utama tidak boleh ditulis ulang" **tidak lagi mutlak**: boleh, asal kodenya
  distempel ulang sesudahnya.
- Konvensi `" (2)"` tetap berguna (base asli utuh sebagai cadangan), tapi bukan lagi satu-satunya
  jalan.
- **Map benar-benar baru di bawah nama bawaan kini mungkin** - syarat namanya (ada di keempat
  `.i3Game` DAN di tabel stage exe) tetap berlaku.
- `Script.i3pack` dilindungi mekanisme yang SAMA, bukan mekanisme lain - dan sekarang bisa
  distempel juga. Tetap jangan disentuh tanpa alasan kuat: isinya basis data item V1.

**IN-GAME CONFIRMED 2026-10-01** (user: "Oh iya benar bisa"): map DinoRuins - map yang dibangun
dari nol oleh alat ini, di bawah nama bawaan, dengan keenam packnya ditulis `i3pack.py` lalu
distempel `SetProtectionCode` - **jalan di client**. Tidak ada pack `" (2)"`, tidak ada base donor,
tidak ada berkas Zepetto asli di antara keenamnya.

Jadi seluruh rantai map baru sekarang terbukti ujung ke ujung: nama yang lolos dua syarat ->
`i3map` membangun 6 pack dari kerangka map lain -> `i3objin` menjatuhkan model OBJ -> `i3col`
membuat tabrakannya -> `KodeProteksi.exe` menstempel - dan client menerimanya.

#### Koreksi: `enable` di `modes.xml` BUKAN yang menggerbangi sebuah map

Waktu menyerahkan DinoRuins saya menulis bahwa `enable="false"` berarti client tidak pernah
melihat map itu, dan menyuruh user mengubahnya jadi `enable="true"` lalu merestart server.
**Itu salah.** Sesudah map DinoRuins terbukti jalan di game, baris 153 (entri ke-103) diperiksa
lagi dan masih persis apa adanya:

    <map mode="0" tag="0" enable="false" /> <!-- [NoStageName] Dinoruins DC 10/04/18 -->

Server tidak pernah diubah dan tidak pernah direstart. Jadi mask 4x32-bit di
`BASE_USER_INFO_PAK` tidak menentukan map muncul atau tidak di layar buat-room - apa pun
fungsinya, bukan itu. Catatan lama di berkas ini sudah benar sejak awal ("SpacePort works on 118,
so that flag is not what gates a map"); klaim yang lebih baru itulah yang keliru.

Rangkumannya, untuk map Team Deathmatch biasa **sisi server tidak perlu disentuh sama sekali**:
tidak `modes.xml`, tidak `maps.xml` (map 9 Crackdown, 108 CakeCrackdown dan 118 SpacePort
sama-sama absen dari maps.xml dan ketiganya jalan).

tersebut jika tersedia animasi / bone. include dengan teksture nya juga ... buatkan juga daftar
LOD nya ... buatkan UI nya lebih keren dan menarik." Alat **ke-16**.

Rutenya sama dengan `pindah_senjata`/`i3objin`: **kloning senjata V1 bawaan lalu timpa isinya**,
bukan menyusun `.i3s` dari nol. Format word, descriptor, dan medan `.i3i` yang belum dipecahkan
dijamin sah karena datang dari berkas itu sendiri.

- `i3senjatain.py` - `baca_sumber` (OBJ lewat `i3objin.baca_obj`, FBX lewat `i3fbx.baca_mesh`),
  `cari_orientasi`/`matriks_pas`, `tulis_va_senjata`, `kotak_lod`/`sisakan_mesh`,
  `pasang_tulang_fbx`, `blend_per_titik`, `ganti_nama_simpul`, `tulis_tertata`, `bangun`

  `bangun|info|sumber`.
